name: Residual Adapters
full_name: Residual adapter modules for multi-domain ResNets
paper_title: Learning multiple visual domains with residual adapters
formula_latex: g(x;\alpha) = x + \alpha * x,\quad \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C\times 1\times 1}\ (\text{bank of }1{\times}1\text{ filters, wrapped with domain-specific BN});\quad \text{frozen: domain-agnostic }3{\times}3\text{ filters } w_1,w_2;\ \text{trained per domain: } \alpha,\ \text{BN scale/shift}
trainable_params: 2(C^2+5C)\ \text{per residual block (vs. } 2(h^2C^2+hC)\text{ shared, } h=3)
locus: inside every ResNet residual block, in series after each 3x3 convolution (with batch-norm)
structure: Serial insertion of a linear near-identity endomorphism \(I+\alpha\) of the \(C\)-channel feature space (a per-pixel \(C\times C\) matrix, i.e. 1x1 conv) composed with domain-specific BN affine maps; full-rank, no bottleneck, no nonlinearity. The CVPR 2018 follow-up (Rebuffi et al., arXiv:1803.10082) moves the 1x1 adapter in parallel to the 3x3 convolution.
mergeable_reason: At inference every piece is linear or affine: BN, the 1x1 adapter \(I+\alpha\) and the BN that follows sit between a frozen 3x3 convolution and the ReLU (Fig. 2). They therefore fold exactly into a domain-specific 3x3 filter bank plus bias (per tap \(W' = D_2(I+\alpha D_1)W\)). The paper keeps them unmerged so that one backbone is shared across domains.
identity_at_init: Exactly the identity when \(\alpha=0\) (residual form); in the paper adapters are first co-trained with the backbone on ImageNet, then only domain-specific parameters (with strong weight decay on \(\alpha\)) are trained per domain.
key_idea: Split a multi-domain ResNet into frozen domain-agnostic filters plus tiny domain-specific residual 1x1 adapters that collapse to the identity at zero, so one network can be steered across very different visual domains; this is the origin of the term 'adapter' later imported to NLP by Houlsby et al.
results_note: On the Visual Decathlon (10 image domains) residual adapters adding ~11% parameters per domain are close to or better than full per-domain fine-tuning while avoiding forgetting.
categorical_reading: A linear pointed extension that descends along the merge to the R-action object \(W_0\mapsto G\,W_0\), the orbit closure of \(GL_C\) acting on output channels. It is LoRA-FA whose frozen down-projection is \(W_0\) itself, and the full-matrix ancestor of the diagonal methods (IA)\(^3\) and SSF.

name: Adapter (Houlsby)
full_name: Bottleneck adapter modules (serial, two per layer)
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
formula_latex: y = F(x)\quad \text{(frozen sublayer, up to its output projection)};\quad y \leftarrow y + W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,y + b_{down}) + b_{up};\quad \text{then } \mathrm{LN}(x+y);\quad W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained};\quad \text{LayerNorm and head also trained};\quad \text{all pretrained weights frozen}
trainable_params: 2\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{per layer (two adapters)} + \text{LayerNorm parameters}
locus: two serial adapters per Transformer layer: after the attention output projection and after the FFN, each before the residual add and LayerNorm
structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with an internal residual connection: each frozen sublayer \(F\) is post-composed with the near-identity endomorphism \(\mathrm{id}+W_{up}\sigma W_{down}\) of \(\mathbb{R}^d\) (rank-\(r\) bottleneck, nonlinear).
mergeable_reason: The nonlinearity inside the bottleneck prevents folding the adapter into the frozen linear weights, so inference keeps the extra sequential modules and latency.
identity_at_init: Near-identity, not exact. Projection weights are drawn from a zero-mean Gaussian with std \(10^{-2}\) truncated at 2 std, and biases are zero, so the adapter output is close to 0 and the internal skip makes the module approximately the identity. The paper's init-scale sweep finds performance robust for std \(\le 10^{-2}\) and degrading for larger scales.
key_idea: Insert small bottleneck modules with a skip connection into every Transformer layer and train only them (plus LayerNorms), so one frozen BERT serves many tasks with a few percent new parameters per task.
results_note: On GLUE with BERT-Large, adapters reach a mean score of 80.0 vs 80.4 for full fine-tuning while adding 3.6% parameters per task, and remain competitive across 26 text-classification tasks.
categorical_reading: A pointed extension that post-composes each frozen sublayer with the near-identity endomorphism \(\mathrm{id}+U\sigma(D\,\cdot)\), so it is of action type on the extension, and other methods meet it only through the realisation. The non-affine \(\sigma\) is exactly the M∞ obstruction of Thm VI.3(c); with \(\sigma=\mathrm{id}\) it would be the serial linear adapter of Prop VI.4(b), isomorphic to LoRA when \(W_0\) is invertible.

name: Pfeiffer Adapter
paper_title: AdapterFusion: Non-Destructive Task Composition for Transfer Learning
formula_latex: a = \mathrm{LN}\big(x + F(x)\big)\ (F = \text{frozen FFN sublayer, LN its frozen post-LayerNorm});\quad y = W_{up}\,\mathrm{ReLU}(W_{down}\,a + b_{down}) + b_{up} + F(x);\quad h = \mathrm{LN}(y + x);\quad W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained; backbone frozen}
trainable_params: 2rd + r + d\ \text{per layer (one adapter; default reduction factor } d/r = 16)
locus: one adapter per Transformer layer, only after the feed-forward block
structure: Same algebraic shape as the Houlsby adapter (serial residual bottleneck MLP) but inserted once per layer, after the FFN, with the residual taken from the FFN sublayer; found by an architecture search over positions, residuals, LayerNorms, reduction factors and nonlinearities.
mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottleneck in series with the FFN cannot be absorbed into frozen weights.
identity_at_init: Approximate only. The paper adds 'randomly initialized' adapters, and the AdapterHub default (init_weights='bert') is \(N(0, 0.02^2)\) weights with zero biases. The bottleneck output is small but not zero, and there is no exact zero-init guarantee.
key_idea: A single adapter after the FFN performs on par with Houlsby's two adapters per layer while halving the inserted modules and compute; it became the default sequential adapter (SeqBnConfig) of AdapterHub and the building block of AdapterFusion and MAD-X.
results_note: In the paper's architecture search on SST-2, CommonsenseQA and argument mining, the single post-FFN adapter matched the Houlsby configuration with half as many adapters.
categorical_reading: The same serial bottleneck extension as Houlsby, at one site per layer, but it reads the post-LN block output \(\mathrm{LN}(x+F(x))\) and writes into \(F(x)\). That is a different wire, so it is Houlsby's sibling in VIII.B rather than a sub-object: no freezing of Houlsby's coordinates produces it.

name: MAD-X
full_name: Multiple ADapters for Cross-lingual transfer (language, task and invertible adapters)
paper_title: MAD-X: An Adapter-Based Framework for Multi-Task Cross-Lingual Transfer
formula_latex: \mathrm{LA}_l(h_l,\rho_l) = U_l\,\mathrm{ReLU}(D_l h_l) + \rho_l,\quad \mathrm{TA}_l(h_l,\rho_l) = U'_l\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(D'_l\,\mathrm{LA}_l(h_l,\rho_l)\big) + \rho_l;\quad A_{inv}:\ o_1 = F(e_2)+e_1,\ o_2 = G(o_1)+e_2,\ \ A_{inv}^{-1}:\ e_2 = o_2 - G(o_1),\ e_1 = o_1 - F(e_2);\ \ F,G\ \text{bottleneck MLPs};\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: \underbrace{2r_Ld}_{\text{language}} + \underbrace{2r_Td}_{\text{task}}\ \text{per layer} + \underbrace{\tfrac{d^2}{2}}_{\text{invertible (once)}}\ (\text{+ biases; paper: } r_L = d/2,\ r_T = d/16)
locus: language and task adapters stacked after the FFN in every layer; invertible adapter on the input embeddings with its inverse before the tied output embeddings
structure: Serial composition (stacking) \(\mathrm{TA}\circ\mathrm{LA}\) of two bottleneck adapters that share the FFN residual, plus an invertible NICE additive-coupling bijection \(A_{inv}\) on token embeddings whose exact inverse is applied before the tied output embedding; language modules are swappable at inference (zero-shot transfer by replacing \(\mathrm{LA}^{src}\) with \(\mathrm{LA}^{tgt}\)).
mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottlenecks and coupling layers must be executed at inference; swapping modules is the point of the design.
identity_at_init: Not explicitly enforced: adapters use the standard small random init of Pfeiffer adapters; the coupling \(A_{inv}\) equals the identity only when \(F=G=0\).
key_idea: Factor cross-lingual transfer into separately trained, swappable language adapters (MLM on unlabeled text), task adapters stacked on top, and invertible embedding adapters, so a task adapter trained in one language transfers zero-shot to another by swapping the language adapter.
results_note: With XLM-R Base, full MAD-X improves over XLM-R by more than 5 F1 on average for cross-lingual NER (largest gains on low-resource and unseen languages) and is competitive on XQuAD.
categorical_reading: A word in the composition monoid of serial extensions: \(\mathrm{TA}\circ\mathrm{LA}\) is two composition stages, and swapping \(\mathrm{LA}^{src}\) for \(\mathrm{LA}^{tgt}\) re-bases the task adapter on a different language stage. The invertible adapter conjugates the whole network by a NICE coupling, \(E^\top A_{inv}^{-1}\circ\mathrm{body}\circ A_{inv}E\), an honest group element whose coordinate split is imposed structure.

name: AdapterFusion
full_name: AdapterFusion: attention-based composition of task adapters
paper_title: AdapterFusion: Non-Destructive Task Composition for Transfer Learning
formula_latex: s_{l,t} = \mathrm{softmax}_{n}\big(h_{l,t}^{\top}Q_l \cdot z_{l,t,n}^{\top}K_l\big),\quad z'_{l,t,n} = z_{l,t,n}^{\top}V_l,\quad o_{l,t} = \sum_{n=1}^{N} s_{l,t,n}\,z'_{l,t,n};\quad \text{frozen: backbone and } N \text{ trained task adapters } \Phi_n;\ \text{trained: } Q_l,K_l,V_l\ (\text{and head})
trainable_params: 3d^2 + 3d\ \text{per layer}\ (Q_l,K_l,V_l\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d})
locus: a fusion layer after the \(N\) parallel task adapters at the FFN position of every layer
structure: Input-dependent convex combination: a dot-product attention whose query is the FFN output and whose keys/values are the outputs of \(N\) frozen adapters, i.e. a context-dependent point of the simplex \(\Delta^{N-1}\) mixing \(V\)-projected adapter outputs (two-stage: knowledge extraction, then composition).
mergeable_reason: All \(N\) adapters and the attention mixer run at inference; the mixing weights depend on the input.
identity_at_init: No: \(Q\) and \(K\) are random; \(V\) is initialized to an identity diagonal plus 1e-6 noise (and L2-regularized toward it), so at init the layer outputs an attention-weighted average of adapter outputs, not the base model.
key_idea: Separate knowledge extraction (train one adapter per task, non-destructively) from knowledge composition (learn a small attention layer that mixes the frozen adapters per token for a target task), avoiding catastrophic forgetting and task interference of multi-task fine-tuning.
results_note: Across 16 NLU tasks with BERT-base, AdapterFusion improves over full fine-tuning and over single-task and multi-task adapters on the target task.
categorical_reading: A family over inputs: \(x\mapsto s(x)\in\Delta^{N-1}\) picks, per token, a point of the simplex over \(N\) frozen adapters, a \(T\)-point of the \(N\)-fold adapter extension with \(T=X\), not an object of \(\mathsf{Meth}\). It separates knowledge extraction (the frozen adapters) from composition (the \(T\)-point), and its only continuous gauge is the query–key slide.

name: AdapterDrop
full_name: AdapterDrop: dropping adapters from lower Transformer layers
paper_title: AdapterDrop: On the Efficiency of Adapters in Transformers
formula_latex: h^{(l)} = \begin{cases} F_l\big(h^{(l-1)}\big) & l \le n \\ A_l\big(F_l(h^{(l-1)})\big) & l > n \end{cases},\qquad n \text{ fixed (specialized) or } n\sim\mathcal{U}\{0,\dots,11\}\ \text{per batch (robust)};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters } A_l \text{ trained}
trainable_params: (L-n)\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{for specialized AdapterDrop (adapters only in the top } L-n \text{ layers)};\ L\,(2rd+r+d)\ \text{for robust AdapterDrop (all adapters trained, } n \text{ resampled per batch)}
locus: adapters kept only in the upper \(L-n\) layers; the first \(n\) layers are the unmodified backbone
structure: Restricts the set of insertion sites to a final segment of the layer chain, so the composite factors as (adapted top) \(\circ\) (shared frozen bottom); the shared prefix can be computed once for many tasks. The robust variant samples \(n\) per batch (stochastic depth over adapters). Also prunes AdapterFusion to its most-attended adapters.
mergeable_reason: Remaining adapters are ordinary nonlinear bottleneck adapters.
identity_at_init: Inherited from the underlying adapter initialization (approximate identity); the first \(n\) layers are exactly the backbone.
key_idea: Lower layers matter little for adapters, so removing their adapters (during training and/or inference) speeds up training and multi-task inference with small accuracy loss; one robustly trained model can be run with any number of dropped layers.
results_note: With RoBERTa-base on GLUE, dropping adapters from the first five layers keeps 97.1% (specialized) / 95.4% (robust) of performance and makes simultaneous inference on 8 tasks 39% faster; pruning AdapterFusion from 8 to 2 adapters keeps performance.
categorical_reading: Specialised AdapterDrop is the sub-object of the adapter extension obtained by freezing the bottom-\(n\) adapters at their neutral point (A2). That also truncates the backprop cone (Obs IV.4) and makes the frozen bottom segment shared across tasks. Robust AdapterDrop is a family over the drop depth \(n\in\{0,\dots,11\}\), trained jointly.

name: K-Adapter
paper_title: K-Adapter: Infusing Knowledge into Pre-Trained Models with Adapters
formula_latex: a_k = \mathcal{A}_k\big([\,h_{l_k}\,;\,a_{k-1}\,]\big),\ \ \mathcal{A}_k = \text{down-proj} \to N\ \text{Transformer layers} \to \text{up-proj (skip across the projections)},\ \ l_k\in\{0,11,23\};\quad \text{output } [\,h_L\,;\,a_K\,];\quad \text{knowledge pre-training: backbone frozen, } \mathcal{A}\text{ trained}
trainable_params: \approx 42\text{M per knowledge adapter during knowledge pre-training (RoBERTa-Large frozen; } K=3 \text{ adapter layers at backbone layers } \{0,11,23\},\ N=2,\ H_A=768,\ H_d=768,\ H_u=1024);\ \text{downstream fine-tuning updates RoBERTa with the adapters frozen}
locus: outside plug-in (side network) reading hidden states of backbone layers \(\{0, 11, 23\}\); its output is concatenated with the backbone's final hidden state
structure: Side network: a separate small Transformer stack that reads (by concatenation) intermediate backbone states and never writes back into the backbone; the final representation is the concatenation (a product) of backbone and side-network features, and multiple knowledge adapters are combined by further concatenation.
mergeable_reason: A separate network with its own Transformer layers runs alongside the backbone.
identity_at_init: No: adapters are randomly initialized; the backbone representation is left untouched (outputs are concatenated, not added), so original features stay available but the head sees a new concatenated feature.
key_idea: Inject different kinds of knowledge (factual relations from Wikidata, dependency syntax) into independent side adapters trained with the backbone frozen, enabling continual, non-interfering knowledge infusion. Note: for downstream tasks the paper keeps the adapters fixed and fine-tunes RoBERTa, so it is a modular knowledge-infusion method rather than a downstream PEFT method.
results_note: K-Adapter (factual + linguistic) improves RoBERTa-Large on entity typing (OpenEntity +1.38 F1), relation classification and question answering.
categorical_reading: A side extension that never writes back: the representation is the product \(h_L\times a_K\), so the base function survives as the projection \(\pi_1\), and knowledge sources are added by further products. Downstream the paper fine-tunes the backbone with the adapters frozen, so only the knowledge-infusion stage is a PEFT method in this framework.

name: Compacter
full_name: Compacter (Compact Adapter with low-rank PHM layers)
paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(s_i^{D}t_i^{D\top}),\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(s_i^{U}t_i^{U\top}),\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{shared by all adapters and layers},\ s_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\rho},\ t_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\rho},\ s_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\rho},\ t_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\rho}\ (\rho=1\ \text{default});\ d=\text{hidden size},\ r=\text{bottleneck};\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: 2\rho(d+r)\ \text{per adapter} + n^{3}\ \text{shared};\ \text{model total } 4L(d+r)+n^{3}\ (\rho=1)
locus: bottleneck adapters after attention and FFN sublayers (Compacter++: after the FFN only)
structure: Adapter projections are sums of \(n\) Kronecker products of shared 'slow' \(n \times n\) matrices \(A_i\) with layer-specific rank-\(\rho\) 'fast' matrices \(s_i t_i^{\top}\) (low-rank PHM, LPHM).
mergeable_reason: Serial bottleneck adapter with a nonlinearity; adds inference latency and cannot be folded.
identity_at_init: Not specified as an exact zero-init; relies on the adapter residual connection as in Houlsby adapters.
key_idea: Combine hypercomplex (Kronecker-sum) layers, cross-layer sharing of the slow factors, and rank-one fast factors to bring adapter cost from \(O(kd)\) to \(O(k+d)\).
results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, Compacter (0.073%) and Compacter++ (0.047% of parameters) perform on par with full fine-tuning and outperform it on SuperGLUE and in low-resource settings.
categorical_reading: Compacter is a method on the Houlsby extension \(\Theta\times\Theta'\), obtained from the PHM adapter by tying the slow weights \(A_i\) across all boxes and restricting the fast weights to rank \(\rho\). It maps by A3 into the PHM adapter and into the dense Houlsby adapter, but no weight-space method simulates it, because its box function is non-affine.

name: HyperFormer
full_name: HyperFormer / HyperFormer++: shared hypernetworks for task-conditioned adapters
paper_title: Parameter-efficient Multi-task Fine-tuning for Transformers via Shared Hypernetworks
formula_latex: (U_{\tau}^{l},D_{\tau}^{l})=\big(W^{U^l},W^{D^l}\big)I_{\tau},\ \ I_{\tau}=h_I(z_{\tau})\ \ (\text{HyperFormer++: }I_{\tau}=h'_I(z_{\tau},l_i,p_j)\text{ with one hypernetwork shared by all layers});\quad A_{\tau}^{l}(x)=LN_{\tau}^{l}\big(U_{\tau}^{l}\operatorname{GeLU}(D_{\tau}^{l}x)\big)+x;\ \text{trained: hypernetworks, task/layer/position embeddings, layer norms; T5 frozen}
trainable_params: \text{HyperFormer++ (whole model, }T\text{ tasks): }t(T+4+2L)+8te+2t(2rd+2d)\ \ (t=64,\ e=128;\ \text{task/layer/position embeddings, two task projectors, adapter and LayerNorm hypernetworks for encoder and decoder}),\ \text{a new task adds }t;\ \text{HyperFormer: one hypernetwork per layer with }t(2rd+2d)\ \text{weights; T5 LayerNorms also trained; 0.29\% added parameters per task reported}
locus: adapters after the attention and feed-forward blocks of every T5 layer, plus conditional layer norms
structure: Linear hypernetwork mapping a (task, layer, position) embedding to the down/up projections of a residual bottleneck adapter and to layer-norm parameters; knowledge shared through the hypernetwork, specialization through task embeddings.
mergeable_reason: The generated modules are non-linear bottleneck adapters inserted into the computation graph.
identity_at_init: No explicit guarantee; generated adapters sit in a residual branch \(A(x) = \mathrm{LN}(\dots) + x\).
key_idea: Instead of separate adapters per task, generate all adapters from shared hypernetworks conditioned on task and position embeddings, sharing information across tasks while keeping task-specific modules.
results_note: Improves multi-task GLUE performance with only 0.29% added parameters per task and gives substantial gains in few-shot domain generalization.
categorical_reading: HyperFormer is a \(T\)-point \(a:T\to Q_{\rm adapter}\) of the adapter extension, given by a linear hypernetwork whose \(GL_t\) slide on the task-embedding wire is its gauge. Tasks share \(a\) and specialise through \(z_\tau\). Unlike Text-to-LoRA, each fibre \(a(z_\tau)\) is a non-linear adapter with an output LayerNorm, so no task's model lifts to \(\Theta\).

name: Parallel Adapter
paper_title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
formula_latex: h \leftarrow F(x) + s\cdot W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,x),\quad x = \text{input of the frozen sublayer } F\ (\text{FFN or attention});\ \ s=1\ (\text{PA}),\ s>1\ \text{fixed (scaled PA, e.g. } s=4);\ \ W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: 2rd\ (+\,r + d \text{ biases})\ \text{per adapted sublayer}
locus: in parallel to the FFN (preferred) or attention sublayer, reading the sublayer input
structure: Additive parallel composition: the frozen sublayer map \(F\) is replaced by \(F + s\,g\) with \(g = W_{up}\sigma W_{down}\) a bottleneck MLP of the same input (a sum of two morphisms with common domain), versus the serial post-composition \((\mathrm{id}+g)\circ F\) of sequential adapters.
mergeable_reason: The bottleneck is nonlinear and \(F\) (an FFN) is nonlinear, so \(F+sg\) cannot be rewritten as the original architecture; with \(\sigma = \mathrm{id}\) around a single linear map it collapses to LoRA, which is mergeable.
identity_at_init: Exact for the scaled PA as implemented: LoRA-style init (\(W_{down}\) Kaiming-uniform, \(W_{up} = 0\)), so the parallel branch outputs 0 at init.
key_idea: Viewing prefix tuning as a gated parallel adapter on attention outputs suggests moving adapters from serial to parallel insertion, placing them at the FFN, and borrowing LoRA's scaling; parallel insertion beats serial at equal budget (a similar parallel adapter was proposed concurrently by Zhu et al., 2021 for MT).
results_note: On XSum summarization and WMT16 en-ro translation, the FFN parallel adapter outperforms the FFN sequential adapter by 1.7 ROUGE-2 and 0.8 BLEU at the same parameter budget.
categorical_reading: The additive dual of the serial adapter: \(F+s\,U\sigma(D\,\cdot)\) is a Minkowski sum on an extension, so at function level its stages add like LoRA's. Around a single linear map, \(\sigma=\mathrm{id}\) gives LoRA (Prop VI.4(a)), and with ReLU \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\to\mathrm{PA}_{2r}\) via \(h(B,A)=([B,-B],[A;-A])\), since \(\mathrm{ReLU}(t)-\mathrm{ReLU}(-t)=t\). A GELU parallel bottleneck would embed by freezing (A2) in AIM's joint MLP adapter and in Res-Tuning's FFN Res-Adapter, but He et al.'s PA is ReLU, so those are not arrows out of this object.

name: MAM Adapter
paper_title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
formula_latex: \text{attention: } \mathrm{head} = \mathrm{Attn}\big(xW_q,\ [P_k; CW_k],\ [P_v; CW_v]\big),\ P_k,P_v\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d/n_h}\ (\ell=30);\quad \text{FFN: } h \leftarrow \mathrm{FFN}(x) + s\cdot W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,x),\ r=512;\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: 2\ell d + 2rd\ \text{per layer at inference }(\ell = 30,\ r = 512;\ \text{prefix trained through an MLP reparameterization})
locus: prefix vectors at every attention layer (small budget) plus a scaled parallel adapter at every FFN (large budget)
structure: Sum of two of the unified-view instances in each layer: a softmax-gated parallel modification of attention heads (prefix tuning) and a scaled parallel bottleneck on the FFN, with the parameter budget deliberately allocated mostly to the FFN.
mergeable_reason: Prefixes add attention slots and the FFN adapter is nonlinear.
identity_at_init: Partial: the scaled parallel adapter starts at 0 (\(W_{up} = 0\)), but prefixes change attention from the first step (prefix tuning has no exact identity init).
key_idea: Transfer the favourable design choices found by the unified analysis: parallel insertion, FFN modification with large capacity, scaling composition, and multi-head attention modification with a tiny prefix.
results_note: With 6.7% tuned parameters, MAM matches full fine-tuning on XSum and en-ro and is the best of the compared PEFT methods; with RoBERTa-base and 0.5% parameters it reaches 87.4 MNLI / 94.2 SST-2 vs 87.6 / 94.6 for full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: A sum, on an extension, of a prefix on attention and a scaled parallel adapter on the FFN. Because the prefix summand is unpointed, the sum is an unpointed extension, and not a \(\oplus\)-word in \(\mathsf{Meth}\) (Exposé I). Prefix tuning embeds in it by freezing the adapter at \(U=0\) (A2), but the parallel adapter does not embed, since no prefix value is neutral.

name: UniPELT
full_name: UniPELT: unified, gated parameter-efficient language model tuning
paper_title: UniPELT: A Unified Framework for Parameter-Efficient Language Model Tuning
formula_latex: h'_A = \mathcal{G}_A\,W_{up}\,\phi(W_{down}\,h_{FN}) + h_F;\quad K' = [\mathcal{G}_P P_K;\,K],\ V' = [\mathcal{G}_P P_V;\,V];\quad W = W_0 + \mathcal{G}_L\,\Delta W_{\text{LoRA}};\quad \mathcal{G}_m = \mathrm{sigmoid}\big(\mathrm{FFN}_m(\cdot)\big)\in(0,1),\ m\in\{A,P,L\};\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: 2rd\ (\text{adapter}) + 2\ell d\ (\text{prefix}) + 2\,r'(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\text{LoRA on } W_q,W_v) + O(d)\ \text{gates, per layer}
locus: sequential adapter after the FFN, prefixes at attention keys/values, LoRA on \(W_q\) and \(W_v\), each with its own gate in every layer
structure: Input-dependent sigmoid-gated sum of three heterogeneous submodules inside each layer (serial adapter, prefix, LoRA): a learned, per-example mixture over PEFT 'experts', with each gate able to switch its submodule off.
mergeable_reason: Adapter and prefix branches are not mergeable and the LoRA gate depends on the input.
identity_at_init: Not exact: inherits submodule initializations (LoRA \(B = 0\) and near-zero adapters, but prefixes perturb attention from the start).
key_idea: Rather than choosing one PEFT method per task, include adapter, prefix tuning and LoRA as submodules and learn gates that activate whichever combination suits the data and task.
results_note: On GLUE, UniPELT gains 1-4 points over the best individual submodule in low-resource settings, often exceeds the upper bound of its submodules, and matches or beats fine-tuning with more data.
categorical_reading: An input-gated combination of three summands (serial adapter, gated prefix, LoRA): a family over inputs \(X\) of points of \(\mathrm{Ad}\oplus\mathrm{Prefix}\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}\) on an extension. Gating the prefix keys and values does not gate its softmax mass, so no gate value is neutral and the object is unpointed. Input-dependence also costs LoRA its mergeability.

name: AdaMix
paper_title: AdaMix: Mixture-of-Adaptations for Parameter-efficient Model Tuning
formula_latex: \text{train: } x \leftarrow x + f\big(x\,\mathcal{W}^{down}_{i,k}\big)\,\mathcal{W}^{up}_{i,j},\ \ (j,k)\ \text{sampled uniformly per step};\ \ \mathcal{L} = \mathrm{CE} + \tfrac12\big(\mathrm{KL}(z^{\mathcal{A}}\Vert z^{\mathcal{B}}) + \mathrm{KL}(z^{\mathcal{B}}\Vert z^{\mathcal{A}})\big);\quad \text{inference: } \mathcal{W}'^{up}_{i} = \tfrac1M\sum_{j}\mathcal{W}^{up}_{ij},\ \mathcal{W}'^{down}_{i} = \tfrac1M\sum_{j}\mathcal{W}^{down}_{ij}
trainable_params: (M+1)\,rd\ (+\text{biases})\ \text{per adapter during training in the default setting (} M \text{ down-projections, one shared up-projection, Sec. 3.4)},\ 2Mrd \text{ without sharing};\ 2rd\ \text{per adapter after merging (default } M=4)
locus: Houlsby adapter positions (or LoRA matrices when the underlying method is LoRA)
structure: A sparse mixture of \(M\) adapter 'experts' per layer with random (parameter-free) routing during training, consistency-regularized between two stochastic routes, and collapsed by weight averaging into a single adapter of the original size for inference (a model-soup within one layer).
mergeable_reason: The averaged adapter is still a nonlinear bottleneck (mergeable into \(W\) only when the underlying method is LoRA).
identity_at_init: Inherits the underlying PEFT initialization (approximate identity for adapters; exact for LoRA with \(B = 0\)).
key_idea: Train several adaptation modules per layer with stochastic routing (same FLOPs as one), then average them into one module, gaining ensemble-like benefits at the cost and size of a single adapter.
results_note: Tuning 0.1-0.2% of parameters, AdaMix outperforms full fine-tuning on all GLUE tasks with RoBERTa-large (0.23%) and beats LoRA and adapters on E2E NLG with GPT-2.
categorical_reading: At training time AdaMix is a family over random routes \((j,k)\in[M]^2\) of adapters; for inference it is collapsed by the factor-wise averaging map, an A3 arrow into a single adapter. Like LoraHub's factor-wise rule, the average depends on the gauge. Sharing one up-projection pins the hidden-unit permutations of all experts to a common gauge, which is why weight averaging is meaningful here.

name: LLaMA-Adapter
full_name: LLaMA-Adapter (adaption prompts with zero-initialized gated attention)
paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
formula_latex: S_l = \tfrac{Q_lK_l^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}},\ \ K_l = [P_l;T_l;t_l]W_k,\ V_l = [P_l;T_l;t_l]W_v;\quad S^{g}_l = \big[\mathrm{softmax}(S^{K}_l)\cdot\tanh(g_l);\ \mathrm{softmax}(S^{M+1}_l)\big];\quad t^{o}_l = W_o\,S^{g}_l V_l;\ \ P_l\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{and per-head gates } g_l\ \text{trained (top } L' \text{ layers)};\ W_{q,k,v,o}\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: L'\ell d + L' n_h\ \ (\ell = 10,\ L' = 30 \Rightarrow \approx 1.2\text{M for LLaMA-7B})
locus: self-attention of the topmost \(L'\) layers: learnable adaption prompts used as extra keys/values (through the frozen \(W_k\), \(W_v\)) with a gated, separately normalized softmax
structure: Learned prompt tokens prepended at each upper layer and attended through their own softmax whose output is multiplied by a zero-initialized tanh gate; because the word-token softmax is kept separate, the layer equals the original attention plus an additive gated prefix branch. In He et al.'s unified view this is a zero-gated parallel attention branch, whose softmax bottleneck has width \(\ell\) and whose projections are tied to the frozen \(W_{q,k,v,o}\).
mergeable_reason: The adaption prompts add attention slots in the top layers at inference.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(g_l = 0\) gives \(\tanh(g_l) = 0\), so the prompt branch contributes nothing and the separately normalized word-token attention is unchanged.
key_idea: Prefix-like prompts in the upper layers combined with a zero-initialized gate inject instruction-following ability progressively without disturbing the pretrained model at the start of training; the same zero-init attention also injects image tokens for multimodal reasoning.
results_note: Fine-tunes frozen LLaMA-7B on 52K self-instruct demonstrations with 1.2M parameters in under one hour on 8 A100s, giving instruction-following comparable to fully fine-tuned Alpaca-7B; also extends to ScienceQA and other multimodal benchmarks.
categorical_reading: A separately normalised prefix, \(\mathrm{Attn}_q(C)+\tanh(g)\,\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)\), uses two perspective maps (Thm VI.5(d)): content attention is untouched, and \(g=0\) is a neutral point. So its categorical contribution over prefix tuning is pointedness. At \(g=0\) only the gate moves to first order.

name: LLaMA-Adapter V2
full_name: LLaMA-Adapter V2: parameter-efficient visual instruction model
paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter V2: Parameter-Efficient Visual Instruction Model
formula_latex: y = W_0x \;\to\; y = s\cdot(W_0x + b),\ \ b\ \text{init } 0,\ s\ \text{init } 1\ \text{(every linear layer; released code applies } s \text{ to the input: } y = W_0(s\odot x) + b);\ \ +\ \text{zero-gated adaption prompts in the last } L' \text{ layers and visual tokens with zero-init attention in early layers; norms unfrozen; } W_0 \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: (d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per linear layer (scale + bias)} + \text{norm gains} + L'\ell d + \text{gates} + \text{early visual prompts/projection}\ \ (\text{paper: bias/scale/norm part} \approx 5\text{M} = 0.04\%;\ \approx 14\text{M new parameters over LLaMA in total})
locus: every linear layer (bias + scale), all normalization layers, adaption prompts in the last layers, visual prompts in early layers
structure: Composite of (i) affine reparameterization of every linear map by a diagonal scale and bias (a BitFit/SSF-like action, mergeable), (ii) LLaMA-Adapter zero-gated prefix attention in the upper layers, and (iii) early fusion of visual tokens, with disjoint parameter groups trained on image-text vs instruction data.
mergeable_reason: The scale/bias part can be folded into \(W_0\), but the gated adaption prompts and visual-token attention cannot.
identity_at_init: Exact: bias 0, scale 1 and zero-initialized attention gates leave the model unchanged at init.
key_idea: Unlock more capacity cheaply (bias + scale on all linear layers, unfrozen norms), inject visual tokens early and instruction prompts late, and train the two parameter groups on disjoint data to avoid interference between image-text alignment and instruction following; expert captioning/OCR models can be plugged in at inference.
results_note: Adds about 0.04% (~5M) new parameters to LLaMA for language instruction tuning and obtains open-ended multimodal instruction following trained only on image-text pairs plus language instruction data.
categorical_reading: A pointed extension that sums an R-part (a per-layer torus-and-translation action of (IA)\(^3\)/BitFit type, which merges) with LLaMA-Adapter's zero-gated prefix (which does not). The norm gains and the consumers' input scales are related by a diagonal slide, which is its torus gauge. The disjoint parameter groups trained on different data are a training recipe, not a change of object.

name: Side-Tuning
paper_title: Side-Tuning: A Baseline for Network Adaptation via Additive Side Networks
formula_latex: R(x) = \alpha\,B(x) + (1-\alpha)\,S(x),\quad B\ \text{frozen base},\ S\ \text{trainable side network},\ \alpha\ \text{learned or scheduled (e.g. } \alpha(N) = \tfrac{k}{k+N})
trainable_params: |\theta_S| + 1\ \ (\text{side network of any size: a copy of } B, \text{ a distilled small net, or a tiny MLP})
locus: representation level: late fusion of base and side features before the task decoder
structure: Late-fusion side network: an \(\alpha\)-blend (convex combination) of frozen base features and side-network features computed from the same input, with no access to intermediate backbone activations; \(\alpha = 1\) is feature extraction, \(\alpha = 0\) with \(S\) a copy of \(B\) is fine-tuning.
mergeable_reason: The side network is a separate forward computation that must run at inference.
identity_at_init: Exact when \(S\) is initialized as a copy of \(B\) (the paper's default when architectures match): \(R(x) = B(x)\) for any \(\alpha\); otherwise \(S\) is initialized by distillation from \(B\) (approximate).
key_idea: Adapt a frozen network by learning a residual side network whose output is blended with the base representation; it never degrades the base task and treats the base as a black box (it can even be a non-network).
results_note: Competitive with fine-tuning on transfer and incremental-learning benchmarks (iCIFAR, iTaskonomy, Habitat RL, SQuAD v2 with BERT) without forgetting, often with side networks much smaller than the base.
categorical_reading: A late-fusion side extension \(R=\alpha B+(1-\alpha)S\), pointed at \(\alpha=1\). With \(S\) a copy of \(B\) and \(\alpha=0\) it contains full fine-tuning at the function level: Full FT \(\to\) side-tuning pointed at \((0,B)\), \(h(\theta)=(0,\theta)\). So it sits above the terminal object of \(\mathsf{Meth}\) and is not an object of it.

name: LST
paper_title: LST: Ladder Side-Tuning for Parameter and Memory Efficient Transfer Learning
formula_latex: h^{g}_{i} = \mathrm{Layer}^{g}_{i}\big(\mu_i\,\mathrm{Down}_i(h^{f}_{i}) + (1-\mu_i)\,h^{g}_{i-1}\big),\ \ \mu_i = \mathrm{sigmoid}(\alpha_i/T),\ \alpha_i\ \text{init } 0,\ T=0.1;\quad \hat y = \mathrm{LMHead}\big(\mathrm{Up}(h^{g}_{N})\big);\ \ \text{backbone } f \text{ frozen and run forward-only; side network } g,\ \mathrm{Down}_i,\ \mathrm{Up}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: \approx |\theta_f|/r^{2} + O(L\,d^{2}/r)\ \ (\text{side Transformer with all widths divided by the reduction factor } r,\ \text{plus ladder projections})
locus: a separate thin side network fed by shortcut ('ladder') connections from every backbone layer (and the embeddings); predictions come from the side network through the frozen LM head
structure: Side network = \(1/r\)-width pruned copy of the backbone receiving, at each depth, a gated convex combination of a linearly down-projected backbone activation and its own previous state; information flows only backbone -> side, so no gradient enters the backbone.
mergeable_reason: The side network is extra computation at inference (it produces the prediction).
identity_at_init: No: the output is produced by the side network, so the model does not equal the backbone at init; instead the side network is initialized by structural pruning of backbone weights (Fisher-information row importance) and gates start at \(\mu = 0.5\).
key_idea: Parameter efficiency is not memory efficiency: by never backpropagating through the backbone (gradients only flow through a small ladder-connected side network), training memory drops far below adapters or LoRA.
results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, LST saves 69% of full fine-tuning memory (2.7x more savings than Adapter/LoRA at similar parameter usage) and beats Adapter and LoRA in the low-memory regime; it also scales to T5-3B and CLIP-T5 vision-language tasks.
categorical_reading: An extension whose prediction factors through a side network of width \(d/r\). By the cut-rank bound, \(\mathrm{LMHead}\circ\mathrm{Up}\) has rank \(\le d/r\), so no parameter value reproduces \(f\): LST is unpointed, not merely near-pointed. Its contribution is on the cotangent side: the ladders cut the backprop cone, so the backbone's backward pass never runs (Obs IV.4).

name: Res-Tuning
full_name: Res-Tuning / Res-Tuning-Bypass: tuners unbound from the backbone
paper_title: Res-Tuning: A Flexible and Efficient Tuning Paradigm via Unbinding Tuner from Backbone
formula_latex: x' = \mathrm{OP}(x) + \text{Res-Tuner}(x),\ \ \mathrm{OP}\in\{\mathrm{MHA},\mathrm{FFN},\text{block}\}\ \text{frozen};\quad \text{Bypass: } x^{b}_{0} = x_0,\ \ x^{b}_{l} = \lambda\,\text{Res-Tuner}_{h}(x_l) + (1-\lambda)\,\text{Res-Tuner}_{v}(x^{b}_{l-1}),\ \lambda = \mathrm{sigmoid}(\cdot)\ \text{init } 0.5
trainable_params: \sum_{\text{tuned ops}} |\theta_{\text{tuner}}|\ \ (\text{tuner-dependent, e.g. } 2rd \text{ per bottleneck tuner})
locus: tuners in parallel to MHA, FFN and whole blocks (Res-Tuning), or a detached bypass network fed by every block output (Res-Tuning-Bypass)
structure: 'Unbinding': prefix, prompt and adapter tuning are rewritten (with empirical equivalence) as frozen operation plus a parallel residual tuner, so tuners become free-standing modules added to backbone operations; the Bypass variant assembles horizontal (backbone \(\to\) bypass) and vertical (bypass \(\to\) bypass) tuners into a ladder-like side network.
mergeable_reason: Tuners are generally nonlinear (attention or MLP) modules, and the Bypass variant is a separate network.
identity_at_init: Depends on the tuner instantiation (zero-initialized output projections give the identity in the attached form); the Bypass variant does not reproduce the backbone at init.
key_idea: Decoupling tuner design from the backbone structure lets any tuner be attached anywhere and combined freely, and detaching the tuners into a bypass avoids backpropagating through the backbone and allows one backbone pass for many tasks.
results_note: State-of-the-art VTAB-1K accuracy among PETL methods at similar parameter counts; Res-Tuning-Bypass cuts training memory by 49.7% and multi-task inference time by 80.9% on discriminative tasks, and by 70.7% / 83.6% for Stable Diffusion generation.
categorical_reading: 'Unbinding' rewrites every tuner as a parallel summand \(\mathrm{OP}+\mathrm{Tuner}\), moving it into the additive, parallel-adapter form. For prefix and prompt tuning this replaces the single softmax by a separately normalised branch, which is a different object (Thm VI.5(b) against (d)), not an equivalent one. The Bypass variant is an LST-type ladder.

name: ControlNet
full_name: ControlNet: trainable-copy side network with zero convolutions
paper_title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
formula_latex: y_c = \mathcal{F}(x;\Theta) + \mathcal{Z}\big(\mathcal{F}(x + \mathcal{Z}(c;\Theta_{z1});\Theta_c);\Theta_{z2}\big),\quad \Theta\ \text{frozen},\ \Theta_c \leftarrow \Theta\ \text{(trainable copy)},\ \mathcal{Z} = 1{\times}1\ \text{conv with zero weights and bias}
trainable_params: |\Theta_c| + |\Theta_{z}| + |\mathcal{E}|\ \ (\text{trainable copy of the 12 encoder blocks and the middle block of the SD U-Net, the zero convolutions, and a tiny 4-layer conv encoder } \mathcal{E} \text{ mapping the } 512^2 \text{ condition to } 64^2)
locus: trainable copy of the U-Net encoder and middle block; its outputs are added through zero convolutions to the skip connections and middle block of the frozen U-Net
structure: Side network = trainable copy of the encoder that additionally receives the condition \(c\), connected to the frozen network at both ends through zero-initialized 1x1 convolutions; it extends the input object from \(x\) to \((x, c)\) and adds residual corrections to the frozen decoder's skip features.
mergeable_reason: The copy processes the extra condition input and must run at inference.
identity_at_init: Exact: both zero convolutions output 0 at the first step, so \(y_c = F(x; \Theta)\) and the trainable copy starts as the pretrained encoder.
key_idea: Reuse the deep pretrained encoder as a backbone for learning a new conditioning signal by training a copy of it and connecting it with zero convolutions, which protects the frozen model from harmful gradients early in training.
results_note: Adds spatial controls (edges, depth, segmentation, human pose, etc.) to Stable Diffusion, with training robust on both small (<50k) and large (>1M) datasets.
categorical_reading: A pointed side extension over the enlarged input \(X\times C\): a copy of the encoder joined at both ends by zero convolutions. At initialisation the copy is dead to first order, and only the outer zero convolution moves. Its corrections are additive residuals on skip features, so several ControlNets compose by \(\oplus\).

name: T2I-Adapter
full_name: T2I-Adapter: lightweight condition adapters for text-to-image diffusion
paper_title: T2I-Adapter: Learning Adapters to Dig out More Controllable Ability for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
formula_latex: F_c = \mathcal{F}_{AD}(C),\quad \hat F^{\,i}_{enc} = F^{\,i}_{enc} + F^{\,i}_{c},\ i\in\{1,2,3,4\};\quad \text{multi-condition: } F_c = \sum_{k=1}^{K}\omega_k\,\mathcal{F}^{k}_{AD}(C_k);\ \ \text{SD frozen, } \mathcal{F}_{AD}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: \approx 77\text{M per adapter (18M small, 5M tiny variants)}
locus: external condition encoder whose four multi-scale features are added to the frozen U-Net encoder features
structure: Additive feature injection from a small external network (pixel-unshuffle, convolutions and residual blocks): each condition defines a translation of the frozen encoder's intermediate states at four scales, and several adapters compose by weighted sum without retraining.
mergeable_reason: The adapter processes the extra condition input at inference.
identity_at_init: Not guaranteed by construction (no zero-init is described); the original model is recovered exactly when no adapter is attached or its weight \(\omega_k = 0\).
key_idea: Align the internal knowledge of a frozen text-to-image model with external control signals using small, composable condition encoders that only need one pass per generation.
results_note: Supports sketch, depth, segmentation, keypose and color-palette control of Stable Diffusion with ~77M parameters, and multi-condition control by composing adapters without extra training.
categorical_reading: An additive feature-injection extension over the condition object \(C\). The correction \(F_c\) is independent of the latent and the timestep, so for fixed \(C\) it is a constant, spatially varying translation of four encoder states, and multi-condition use is the \(\oplus\) of adapters weighted by \(\omega_k\). It is not zero-initialised, so it starts with a pointing defect.

name: IP-Adapter
full_name: IP-Adapter: image prompt adapter with decoupled cross-attention
paper_title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
formula_latex: Z^{new} = \mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V) + \lambda\cdot\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K',V'),\quad Q = ZW_q,\ K = c_tW_k,\ V = c_tW_v\ \text{(frozen)},\ \ K' = c_iW'_k,\ V' = c_iW'_v\ \text{(trained, init from } W_k,W_v)
trainable_params: 2\,d_{c}\,d\ \text{per cross-attention layer } (W'_k,W'_v) + \text{image-embedding projection}\ \ (\approx 22\text{M for SD 1.5, 16 layers})
locus: a parallel image cross-attention branch added to every cross-attention layer of the U-Net, sharing the frozen query
structure: Decoupled cross-attention: a second attention over new image-prompt tokens (with its own key/value projections and its own softmax) is added to the frozen text cross-attention output; \(\lambda\) scales the branch. Structurally this is the same decoupled-softmax parallel attention branch as LLaMA-Adapter's gated prompts, but its keys/values come from an input (the image embedding) through new trainable projections.
mergeable_reason: The image branch attends over extra tokens derived from the image prompt at inference.
identity_at_init: Not at init (\(W'_k, W'_v\) are copied from \(W_k, W_v\) so the branch is active from the start); the original model is recovered exactly with \(\lambda = 0\).
key_idea: Instead of concatenating image and text features into the frozen cross-attention, add a separate cross-attention for image features so a small adapter gives strong image-prompt control while remaining compatible with text prompts and structural controls.
results_note: A ~22M-parameter IP-Adapter is comparable to or better than fully fine-tuned image-prompt models and remains compatible with text prompts and ControlNet-style controls.
categorical_reading: Structurally LLaMA-Adapter's separately normalised branch, \(\mathrm{Attn}(Q,K,V)+\lambda\,\mathrm{Attn}(Q,K',V')\), but with keys and values computed from an auxiliary input: an extension over \(X\times C_{\rm img}\). \(V'=0\) is neutral, but the copy initialisation starts it with a defect.

name: AdaptFormer
paper_title: AdaptFormer: Adapting Vision Transformers for Scalable Visual Recognition
formula_latex: \tilde x_\ell = W_{up}\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(W_{down}\,\mathrm{LN}(x'_\ell)\big),\quad x_\ell = \mathrm{MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(x'_\ell)\big) + s\cdot\tilde x_\ell + x'_\ell,\ \ s = 0.1;\ \ \text{ViT frozen, } W_{down},W_{up}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: 2rd + r + d\ \text{per block}
locus: in parallel to the MLP (FFN) block of every ViT layer
structure: Scaled parallel bottleneck adapter on the FFN (AdaptMLP), i.e. the vision instance of the scaled parallel adapter with \(s < 1\).
mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottleneck in parallel with a nonlinear MLP.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(W_{up}\) and all adapter biases are zero-initialized (\(W_{down}\) Kaiming-normal), so the branch outputs 0 at init.
key_idea: Adapt ViTs through a lightweight parallel branch next to the MLP rather than through token-space prompts, which scales to the many tokens of video.
results_note: With ViT-B, ~1.5% extra parameters give about 10% and 19% relative improvement over full fine-tuning on Something-Something v2 and HMDB51, and it beats VPT on image benchmarks.
categorical_reading: The scaled parallel adapter at the FFN with \(s=0.1\), isomorphic to He et al.'s parallel adapter by rescaling \(W_{up}\). It is the vision instance of the additive extension.

name: Convpass
paper_title: Convolutional Bypasses Are Better Vision Transformer Adapters
formula_latex: X' \leftarrow X + \mathrm{MHSA/MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(X)\big) + s\cdot\mathrm{Convpass}\big(\mathrm{LN}(X)\big),\quad \mathrm{Convpass} = \mathrm{Conv}^{\uparrow}_{1\times1}\circ\mathrm{GELU}\circ\mathrm{Conv}_{3\times3}\circ\mathrm{GELU}\circ\mathrm{Conv}^{\downarrow}_{1\times1}\ \text{on tokens reshaped to the patch grid ([cls] as a } 1{\times}1 \text{ image)}
trainable_params: 2L\big((2r+1)d + 9r^2 + 2r\big)\ \text{in total (two Convpass per layer; paper } r = 8)
locus: in parallel to both MHSA and MLP in every ViT block
structure: Parallel convolutional bottleneck (ResNet-style 1x1-3x3-1x1 block on the reshaped token grid) that injects spatial-locality inductive bias; unrolled, each layer becomes an ensemble of transformer, CNN and hybrid paths.
mergeable_reason: The 3x3 convolution mixes neighbouring tokens and the block is nonlinear, so it cannot be absorbed into per-token frozen weights.
identity_at_init: Exact in the official code: up-projection weights and biases are zero-initialized (down-projection Xavier; 3x3 conv initialized to identity at its centre tap).
key_idea: Language-oriented adapters lack visual inductive bias; a convolutional bypass restores 2D locality during fine-tuning and works especially well in the low-data regime.
results_note: With under 0.5% extra parameters, Convpass outperforms language-oriented PETL modules (Adapter, LoRA, VPT, NOAH) on VTAB-1K and few-shot fine-grained classification.
categorical_reading: A parallel extension whose bottleneck contains a \(3\times3\) convolution over the patch grid, so its correction at a token depends on the token's neighbours: a token-mixing edit outside every per-token method. With the convolution frozen at its centre-tap identity init it becomes a per-token parallel adapter with activation \(\mathrm{GELU}\circ\mathrm{GELU}\) (an A2 sub-object).

name: ST-Adapter
paper_title: ST-Adapter: Parameter-Efficient Image-to-Video Transfer Learning
formula_latex: \mathrm{ST\text{-}Adapter}(X) = X + f\big(\mathrm{DWConv3D}(XW_{down})\big)\,W_{up},\quad X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times N\times d}\ \text{reshaped to } T\times h\times w\times r \text{ before the depth-wise } 3{\times}1{\times}1 \text{ convolution};\ \text{image backbone frozen}
trainable_params: 2rd + k_Tk_Hk_W\,r + O(d + r)\ \text{per adapter } (k = 3{\times}1{\times}1)
locus: one adapter before the MHSA of every ViT block (operating on the \(T\) frames' patch tokens)
structure: Serial residual bottleneck with a depth-wise spatio-temporal convolution in the compressed space, i.e. a token-mixing linear operator across neighbouring frames inserted between down- and up-projection; it gives an image model temporal reasoning. (The official code has no activation between the depth-wise convolution and \(W_{up}\), and adapts only the patch tokens, leaving [CLS] unchanged.)
mergeable_reason: The 3D convolution mixes tokens across frames and positions, so it cannot be folded into per-token frozen weights.
identity_at_init: Exact in the official code: depth-wise 3D-conv weights and all biases are zero-initialized, so the adapter outputs \(X\) at init.
key_idea: Turn a frozen image transformer into a video model by inserting cheap adapters whose bottleneck contains a depth-wise 3D convolution for temporal modelling.
results_note: With CLIP ViT-B/16, ST-Adapter matches full fine-tuning on Kinetics-400 (82.0 vs 81.7) and SSv2 (66.3 vs 66.1) while updating 7.2M vs 121.6M parameters.
categorical_reading: A serial bottleneck extension whose bottleneck contains a depthwise temporal convolution: a linear, token-mixing operator in the compressed space. It is M∞ because it is not a per-token edit, not because of an activation. The per-channel convolution privileges only the bottleneck basis (a torus gauge), not the residual wire.

name: AIM
full_name: Adapting Image Models (spatial, temporal and joint adaptation)
paper_title: AIM: Adapting Image Models for Efficient Video Action Recognition
formula_latex: z^{T}_{l} = z_{l-1} + \mathrm{Ad}_T\big(\text{T-MSA}(\mathrm{LN}(z_{l-1}))\big),\ \ z^{S}_{l} = z^{T}_{l} + \mathrm{Ad}_S\big(\text{S-MSA}(\mathrm{LN}(z^{T}_{l}))\big),\ \ z_l = z^{S}_{l} + \mathrm{MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(z^{S}_{l})\big) + s\cdot\mathrm{Ad}_J\big(\mathrm{LN}(z^{S}_{l})\big);\ \ \text{T-MSA} = \text{S-MSA frozen, applied along time};\ s = 0.5
trainable_params: 3\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{per block } (r = d/4)
locus: three adapters per ViT block: after the reused temporal attention (no skip), after spatial attention (with skip), and parallel to the MLP (no skip, scaled by \(s\))
structure: Reuses the frozen spatial self-attention as a temporal attention by re-indexing tokens (the same frozen operator acting along a different axis), and adds serial adapters after both attentions plus a scaled parallel adapter at the MLP.
mergeable_reason: Nonlinear adapters and an additional (reused) attention pass at inference.
identity_at_init: Exact. The second FC layer of every adapter is zero-initialized, and the temporal and joint (MLP-parallel) adapters have no internal skip connection, so both branches output 0 while the spatial adapter (with skip) is the identity. The model equals the image model at init.
key_idea: Equip a frozen image transformer with spatio-temporal reasoning without new attention weights: reuse its attention over time and train only lightweight adapters.
results_note: Achieves comparable or better accuracy than fully fine-tuned video models with far fewer tunable parameters on four action-recognition benchmarks (Kinetics-400/700, Something-Something v2, Diving-48).
categorical_reading: An extension that inserts a new box, temporal attention, with weights tied to the frozen spatial attention and neutralised by a zero-initialised adapter, together with a serial spatial adapter and a scaled parallel MLP adapter. A GELU parallel adapter embeds in AIM by freezing the temporal and spatial adapters at zero (A2); He et al.'s ReLU PA does not, since AIM's adapters are GELU (official vit_clip.py).

name: RepAdapter
paper_title: Towards Efficient Visual Adaption via Structural Re-parameterization
formula_latex: \mathrm{Ad}(x) = x + s\big(W_u(W_dx + b_d) + b_u\big),\ \ W_d\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\ \text{dense},\ W_u\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{group-wise (block-diagonal, } k \text{ groups)};\quad \text{placed before a frozen projection } W_0:\ W_0' = W_0\,(I + sW_uW_d),\ \ b_0' = b_0 + sW_0(W_ub_d + b_u)
trainable_params: rd + \tfrac{rd}{k} + r + d\ \text{per adapter (two adapters per block)}

Token mixing makes it M∞, and the per-channel blend fixes the standard basis of the wire (coordinate geometry). The default up-projection is not zero, so it starts with a pointing defect.

name: CLIP-Adapter
full_name: CLIP-Adapter: residual feature adapters for CLIP
paper_title: CLIP-Adapter: Better Vision-Language Models with Feature Adapters

name: PreFT

formula_latex: h_i=W_0x_i+m_i\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx_i\ \ (\text{LoRA}_P),\qquad h^{(l)}_i\leftarrow h^{(l)}_i+m_i\,s_r\,W_2^{\top}\big(W_1h^{(l)}_i+b\big)\ \ (\text{DiReFT}_P),\qquad m_i=\mathbf{1}[\,i\le\ell\,];\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ W_1,W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{r},\ s_r=1/\sqrt{r},\ \alpha=32;\ \ \text{decode positions } i>\ell \text{ run the frozen model and see the adapter only through the KV cache of positions } \le\ell;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B)\ \text{or}\ (W_1,W_2,b)\ \text{trained}

Generated tokens reach the adapter only through the keys and values cached at prompt positions.
structure: A position mask placed on an existing adapter. Writing an adapter as \( \langle\Phi_\phi,\mathcal F,\mathcal P\rangle \) (intervention, target modules, target positions), PreFT keeps \( \Phi_\phi \) and \( \mathcal F \) and shrinks \( \mathcal P=\{1,\dots,\ell+T\} \) to \( \mathcal P=\{1,\dots,\ell\} \). For \( \text{LoRA}_P \) the per-token update is the rank-\( r \) matrix \( m_i\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \), so the effective weight depends on the token: \( W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \) on prompt tokens and \( W_0 \) on generated tokens. For \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) the per-token update is a rank-\( r \) affine edit \( s_rW_2^{\top}(W_1h+b) \) of the residual stream at prompt positions. Attention is causal, so the whole effect on token \( i>\ell \) is carried by the adapted \( (K,V) \) entries of positions \( \le\ell \) at every layer. No KV entries are added, unlike prefix or KV-cache tuning.
mergeable_reason: The update is gated by position, so no single matrix \( W' \) reproduces it: prompt tokens need \( W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \) and generated tokens need \( W_0 \). A single-adapter deployment could prefill with a merged copy and decode with \( W_0 \), but that doubles weight memory and defeats multi-adapter batching. The design goal is that decode runs the bare base model, so no adapter weights are touched at decode.
identity_at_init: Yes. \( \text{LoRA}_P \) keeps LoRA's init (Kaiming-uniform \( A \), \( B=0 \), scaling \( \alpha/r \)). \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) uses the paper's zero-delta init \( W_1=0 \), \( b=0 \), \( W_2 \) with orthonormal rows (App. C.1 and the released preft/adapters/direft.py), so \( \Phi(h)=h \) at step 0. key_idea: Multi-adapter serving is throughput-bound at decode, where each request's adapter matmul is memory-bound, so PreFT applies the adapter only to the \( \ell \) prompt tokens processed at prefill and runs every decode step on the frozen base model. results_note: Serving 512 adapters on Llama 3.1 70B (4 H100s, Punica workload, vLLM fork), prefill-only DiReFT reaches 1.9x and prefill-only LoRA 1.87x the throughput of all-position multi-LoRA, while on RLVR (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval) prefill-only adapters trail all-position ones by a mean of about 2 points.
categorical_reading: PreFT is LoRA (or DiReFT) pulled back along the prompt-position gate, the mirror image of aLoRA's gate: a family \(T\to Q\) that sits at \(q\) on positions \(\le\ell\) and at \(q_0\) afterwards. Under causal attention the generated tokens see the adapter only through the prompt's \((K,V)\) cache, so the realised map is not \(\Phi_f(\theta)\) for any single \(\theta\). Being pointed after \(\ell\) is what lets decoding run on the frozen weights, and also what blocks merging.

name: OrthoMerge
paper_title: Orthogonal Model Merging
formula_latex: \text{OFT experts: } W_i=W_0R_i^{\top},\ R_i=(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i^{\top}=-Q_i;\ \ \text{other experts: } R_i^{\top}=U_iV_i^{\top},\ U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}=\mathrm{SVD}\big(W_0^{\top}W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}\big)\ \big(\text{Procrustes } \min_{R^{\top}R=I}\|W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}-W_0R^{\top}\|_F\big),\ Q_i=(R_i-I)(R_i+I)^{-1};\ \ Q_m=\frac{\sum_i\|Q_i\|_F}{\|\sum_iQ_i\|_F}\cdot\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}Q_i,\ \ R_m=(I+Q_m)(I-Q_m)^{-1};\ \ W_m=W_0R_m^{\top}+\mathrm{EuclidMerge}\big(\{\rho_i\}\big),\ \rho_i=W_i-W_0R_i^{\top}\ (\rho_i=0\ \text{for OFT experts});\ \ W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}\in\{W_i,\ W_0+\tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}}\};\ \text{training-free, all weights frozen}

locus: Weights of every linear layer of the merged experts: the input-side rotation of OFT-adapted layers, or, through orthogonal-residual decoupling, every layer of LoRA or fully fine-tuned experts (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B MergeBench experts, Qwen2.5-VL-7B). Post hoc, no training.
structure: Merging in the Cayley chart of the orthogonal group. Each expert contributes a rotation \( R_i\in O(d_{in}) \), read off an OFT checkpoint or obtained by orthogonal Procrustes from \( W_0 \) to a target weight. The inverse Cayley map sends it to a skew-symmetric generator \( Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in}) \); the generators are averaged linearly and rescaled by \( c=\sum_i\|Q_i\|_F/\|\sum_iQ_i\|_F\ge1 \) to undo norm loss from cancellation, then mapped back by the Cayley map. The merged multiplicative factor is exactly orthogonal, so \( W_0R_m^{\top} \) keeps the singular values of \( W_0 \) (hence its spectral norm and hyperspherical energy) for any number of experts. For non-OFT experts each weight is split as \( W_i=W_0R_i^{\top}+\rho_i \) (orthogonal plus residual), and the residuals are merged by a Euclidean rule (TA, TIES or TSV-M). The Procrustes target is \( W_i \) (OrthoMerge-G) or \( W_0+\tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}} \), where \( \tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}} \) keeps only the output-neuron rows of \( \tau_i=W_i-W_0 \) whose cosine with the mean task vector is negative (OrthoMerge-C). The Cayley chart covers only orthogonal matrices without eigenvalue \( -1 \), so a reflection returned by Procrustes would fall outside it; the paper does not discuss this case.
mergeable_reason: The output is an ordinary weight matrix \( W_m=W_0R_m^{\top}+\rho_m \) in the base architecture (the merged OFT rotation can be multiplied into \( W_0 \)), so the merged model has no inference overhead.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free merge). Trivially consistent: if every expert equals \( W_0 \) then \( Q_i=0 \), \( R_m=I \), \( \rho_i=0 \) and \( W_m=W_0 \) (taking \( c=1 \) when \( \sum_iQ_i=0 \)).
key_idea: Average OFT rotations in their Lie algebra rather than in weight space: map each \( R_i \) to \( Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in}) \) with the inverse Cayley transform, average with a norm-restoring factor, and map back, so the merge stays on \( O(d_{in}) \) and preserves the spectrum of \( W_0 \). categorical_reading: OrthoMerge is task arithmetic in the Cayley chart of the orbit \(W_0\cdot SO(d_{in})\) rather than in \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\). The merged point \(W_0C(Q_m)^{\top}\) stays in the \(K_{\rm out}\) level set that every OFT expert preserves, which no linear merge of OFT experts does. For non-OFT experts it first splits each weight into an orbit point and a residual, merges the two parts by the orbit rule and by a Euclidean rule, and adds them.

locus: Any LoRA-adapted linear layer (experiments: \( W_q,W_k,W_v,W_{up},W_{down} \) of Gemma-3-4B-pt, Gemma-2-9B, Gemma-3-12B-pt). The method changes how per-example gradients are clipped and noised and how the factors are updated, not the adapter shape.
structure: Plain LoRA on the fixed-rank manifold \( \mathcal M_r \), with DP-SGD moved from the factors to the base of the gauge bundle \( (B,A)\mapsto BA \), whose fibres are the orbits \( (B,A)\sim(BR,R^{-1}A) \), \( R\in GL(r) \). Per-example gradients are projected onto the tangent space \( T_{BA}\mathcal M_r=\{\delta B\,A+B\,\delta A\} \) (dimension \( r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r) \)) by \( \mathcal P_{B,A} \), which depends only on \( \mathrm{col}(B) \) and \( \mathrm{row}(A) \) and is therefore gauge invariant. The projection is lifted to the factors canonically as \( \Delta B=g_B(AA^{\top})^{\dagger}-\tfrac12\Pi_Bg_B(AA^{\top})^{\dagger} \), \( \Delta A=(B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}g_A-\tfrac12(B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}g_A\Pi_A \) with \( g_B=GA^{\top} \), \( g_A=B^{\top}G \), so that \( \Delta B\,A+B\,\Delta A=\mathcal P_{B,A}(G) \). Clipping uses the intrinsic Frobenius norm summed over all modules. The noise is the tangent projection of an isotropic Gaussian, sampled through factor lifts \( \Xi_B=(I-\Pi_B)\Omega_B(AA^{\top})^{-1/2} \), \( \Xi_A=(B^{\top}B)^{-1/2}\Omega_A^{\top} \); it is isotropic on \( T_{BA}\mathcal M_r \) with \( \mathbb E\|\mathcal P(\Xi)\|_F^2=r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r) \), independent of \( \|A\|_F,\|B\|_F \). The noisy step is post-processed by right/left rank-space preconditioners \( (V+\lambda I_r)^{-1/2} \) built from \( r\times r \) second moments, with floors \( \lambda\asymp(\sigma C/b)^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\cdot^{-1})/r \), and then retracted to rank \( r \) by truncated SVD. Because the step is additive in the tangent space, the bilinear noise term \( \eta^2\xi_B\xi_A \) of factor-space DP never appears, and the retraction error is \( O(\eta^2) \).
mergeable_reason: The released adapter is an ordinary low-rank product and merges like LoRA; privacy follows from post-processing. Because the official code trains on a spectrally re-based base \( W_{res}=W_0-U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top} \), it saves the adapter re-expressed against the original \( W_0 \) as the rank-\( 2r \) pair \( [B,\,B_0]\,[A;\,-A_0] \) (PiSSA-style conversion in spectral_rebase_adapter_inplace), which merges into \( W_0 \) the same way.
identity_at_init: The paper does not state an init. The tangent projectors and noise sampler need full-column-rank \( B \) and full-row-rank \( A \), which rules out LoRA's \( B=0 \). The official code uses a PiSSA-style spectral residual init, \( W_0\leftarrow W_0-U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top} \), \( B=U_r(\Sigma_r/s)^{1/2} \), \( A=(\Sigma_r/s)^{1/2}V_r^{\top} \) with LoRA scale \( s \), so \( W_{res}+sBA \) equals the original \( W_0 \) at step 0 (function-preserving with non-degenerate factors).
key_idea: LoRA factors are defined only up to \( (B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A) \), so DP-SGD on the factors clips and noises a gauge-dependent quantity and injects a bilinear \( \eta^2\xi_B\xi_A \) term whose energy can be made arbitrarily large without changing \( BA \). PRISM clips and noises the projection of per-example gradients onto the tangent space of the rank-\( r \) manifold at \( BA \), which gives gauge-invariant updates with closed-form intrinsic noise \( \tfrac{\sigma C}{b}\sqrt{r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r)} \).
results_note: On GLUE8 and Math-10K with Gemma-3-4B-pt, PRISM has the best average utility under DP (0.690 at epsilon=6 and 0.680 at epsilon=3, delta=1e-5) against FFA-LoRA, LoRA-RITE, AdamW, LoRA+ and LAMB, while LoRA-RITE is best without DP.
categorical_reading: PRISM keeps PiSSA's object and moves DP-SGD from \(Q\) to the base \(\mathcal M_r\) of the gauge bundle \((B,A)\mapsto BA\). Clipping and noise act on the tangent projection \(\mathcal P_{B,A}(G)\), so the whole randomised step, noise included, is a function of \(BA\), and the bilinear \(\eta^2\xi_B\xi_A\) term of factor-space DP disappears. It is the stochastic counterpart of the descended cometrics of Exposé III (LoRA-Pro's projected gradient, Riemannian preconditioning).

key_idea: General knowledge sits in the principal singular subspace of the pre-trained weights and task knowledge in the residual subspace, so KeepLoRA initialises each task's LoRA from the SVD of the first-step gradient projected away from both that principal subspace and past-task feature directions, then freezes \( A_t \). categorical_reading: KeepLoRA is LoRA-FA re-based once per task. Its frozen frame comes from the SVD of the first-step gradient after the principal input subspace of \(W_0\) and past-task features have been projected out. By the degree-one collapse each stage is full fine-tuning projected onto \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\), so \(\Delta W\,[P_W,M_{t-1}]=0\) by construction. The nonzero \(B_t^{(0)}\) is a split pointing of a linear method, so it changes only the parametrisation.

name: LoRA-Pre
full_name: LoRA-Pre: low-rank online-linear-regression compression of optimizer momenta
paper_title: Taming Momentum: Rethinking Optimizer States Through Low-Rank Approximation

trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{per matrix (full-parameter training)};\ \text{optimizer state } 2r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(Adam) or } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(Muon) instead of } 2d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{or } d_{out}d_{in}
locus: Optimizer states of all attention and MLP weight matrices (other parameters use standard Adam): Llama pre-training from 60M to 1B parameters on C4, and full fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B and Llama-3.1-8B on MetaMath100k.
structure: No adapter: the weight step is the usual full-rank Adam (or Muon) step, but the EMA momenta are stored as rank-\( r \) factors. The EMA update \( m\leftarrow\beta m+(1-\beta)g \) is one gradient step with learning rate \( 1-\beta \) on \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2 \), so momentum is the weight of an online linear regressor. LoRA-Pre replaces \( m \) by \( m_Bm_A \) and takes one exact Newton step per factor on \( \tfrac12\|m_Bm_A-g\|_F^2 \) (Hessians \( m_Am_A^{\top}\otimes I \) and \( I\otimes m_B^{\top}m_B \)). The result is a simultaneous (Jacobi-style) EMA of each factor toward the least-squares fit of the new gradient given the other factor's previous value, with \( 1-\gamma_1=\sqrt{\beta_1} \) so that the product decays at Adam's rate \( \beta_1 \). The second moment stays positive through the Hadamard-square parametrisation \( v=(v_Bv_A)^{\circ2} \), with \( v_Bv_A \) regressed onto \( |g| \). For Muon the regression target is \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2-\tfrac{\mu}{1-\mu}\langle m,g\rangle \). Since the Adam ratio \( \hat M_t/\sqrt{\hat V_t} \) is elementwise, the weight update is full-rank even though the state is rank-\( r \). LoRA's update is rank-\( r \), and GaLore's step lies in a rank-\( r \) projected subspace. Adafactor's rank-1 factored second moment is an earlier instance of factoring optimizer state.
mergeable_reason: There is no auxiliary module: updates are written straight into W, so the result is an ordinary dense checkpoint with the original architecture and unchanged inference cost.
identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparametrisation, training starts at \( W_0 \) (random init for pre-training). The factored states start at \( m_B=v_B=0 \), \( m_A,v_A\sim\mathcal N(0,0.02) \), so the reconstructed momenta start at 0 as in Adam. Theorem 3.1 assumes full-rank factors and Algorithm 1 writes plain inverses, which are singular at the first step because \( m_{B,0}=0 \). Appendix C.1 defines the update with Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses \( (m_B^{\top}m_B+\lambda_d I)^{-1}m_B^{\top} \) and \( m_A^{\top}(m_Am_A^{\top}+\lambda_d I)^{-1} \), \( \lambda_d>0 \), which are well defined at \( m_B=0 \); the value of \( \lambda_d \) used in experiments is not reported and the code is not released.
key_idea: An EMA momentum update is one step of online gradient descent on \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2 \), so momentum is an online linear regressor and can be compressed like any model. LoRA-Pre factors \( m \) (and \( v=(v_Bv_A)^{\circ2} \)) into rank-\( r \) matrices updated by closed-form Newton steps, which cuts optimizer memory for Adam and Muon in both pre-training and fine-tuning.
results_note: Pre-training Llama-1B on C4 at rank 512, LoRA-Pre Adam reaches 13.53 validation perplexity versus 15.64 for GaLore and 15.56 for full-state Adam, and fine-tuning on MetaMath100k at rank 8 it beats LoRA by 3.14 points on Llama-3.1-8B and 6.17 points on Llama-2-7B (GSM8K/MATH-500 average).
categorical_reading: LoRA-Pre is Full FT with a compressed optimiser state. Its object is the terminal \((\Theta,\theta_0,\mathrm{id})\); the low rank lives only in the momenta, which are themselves trained as an online low-rank regressor of the gradient stream. Unlike GaLore, whose step is confined to a moving rank-\(r\) period, nothing confines its update, and every difference from Adam lies in the induced cometric.

full_name: StructLoRA: information-bottleneck direction filtering with graph-based layer coordination

locus: \( W_q \) and \( W_v \) of every Transformer layer (LLaMA-7B/13B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, ViT-B/16, LLaVA-1.5-7B; RoBERTa-base on GLUE). The coordinator acts across depth on the stack of per-layer updates.
structure: LoRA with a learned diagonal gate between the factors, \( B\,\mathrm{diag}(m)\,A \): a sparsifying selector over the \( r \) rank-one directions, like SoRA's gate but trained with a variational-IB KL to a Bernoulli prior. A training-time map across layers is added on top: the vectorised filtered updates \( U=[u_1;\dots;u_L] \) pass through a shallow residual GCN on a depth graph (adjacent layers plus semantic edges between layers with highly aligned updates or gradients). To first order this is a Laplacian smoothing step \( U\leftarrow U-\eta(\mathbf L\otimes I)U \), which lowers the drift energy \( \sum_l\|u_{l+1}-u_l\|^2 \). Section 3.3 and the released code merge the coordinated \( \Delta\tilde W_l^{\mathrm{final}} \), which in general no longer has rank \( \le r \) because the GCN mixes and nonlinearly maps updates from several layers. Appendix E.7 says instead that the gated \( \Delta\tilde W \) is merged. The released code's coordinator is a dense linear encoder on \( \mathrm{vec}(\Delta\tilde W_l) \) of width \( d_{out}d_{in} \), which does not match the stated \( <0.05\% \) overhead at LLaMA scale.
mergeable_reason: Whichever update is deployed, the gated \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}B\,\mathrm{diag}(m)\,A \) (Appendix E.7) or the coordinator output \( \Delta\tilde W^{\mathrm{final}} \) (Sec. 3.3 and the code's merge_structlora), it is a fixed matrix added to \( W_0 \), so inference cost equals the base model's.
identity_at_init: The gated LoRA path is the identity at init (\( B=0 \), Kaiming-uniform \( A \), gate logits 2.0 in the code). The coordinated update is not guaranteed to be: in the released code the coordinator returns \( u+\mathrm{dec}(\mathrm{enc}(u)) \) with default nn.Linear biases, so \( \Delta\tilde W^{\mathrm{final}}\ne0 \) at step 0 whenever it is active. The paper does not discuss this.
key_idea: Not all \( r \) LoRA directions carry task signal, and layers adapted independently drift apart. StructLoRA gates the rank-one directions with an information-bottleneck filter and, during training only, smooths the per-layer updates across depth with a shallow GCN (a Laplacian smoother), then merges the result so inference costs the same as LoRA.
results_note: On GLUE with RoBERTa-base, StructLoRA reports an 86.5 average, 0.5 points above Sensitivity-LoRA, the strongest dynamic-rank baseline.
categorical_reading: As released, StructLoRA is not a low-rank method. The training-only coordinator's decoder is a dense trainable map back into weight space, and its output is what gets merged, so the deployed update ranges over every adapted box and starts at a defect. Only with the coordinator off (App. E.7, or merge_structlora called without a coordinator) is the object SoRA's gated cone \(W_0+\{B\,\mathrm{diag}(m)A\}\) pointed at the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex. In that reading the GCN smoothing is a training device that \(\rho\) does not see.

full_name: Federated LoRA with rotational alignment of client factors

locus: LoRA-adapted linear layers in federated fine-tuning (RoBERTa-Large on GLUE; Llama 3-8B on GSM8K and HumanEval), implemented in FederatedScope-LLM
structure: Each client trains a rank-\(r\) LoRA \(\Delta W=BA\). The contribution is the aggregation map: before uploading, each client picks a representative of its factor pair's orbit under the \(SO(r)\) subgroup of the \(GL(r)\) gauge action \((B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A)\). The representative is chosen by orthogonal Procrustes against last round's global factors, aligning \(A\) and \(B\) in alternate rounds. The server then averages factors, so the global adapter stays rank \(r\) and \(\bar B\bar A\) approximates \(\tfrac1N\sum_iB_iA_i\) up to the aggregation error \(E^t=\bar B\bar A-\tfrac1N\sum_iB_iA_i\).
mergeable_reason: The global adapter \(\bar B^t\bar A^t\) is an ordinary rank-\(r\) LoRA product and folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(\Delta W_0=\bar B^0\bar A^0=0\) (Algorithm 1, line 2; the scalar example in Fig. 2 starts from \(\bar B^0=0\)), so training starts at \(W_0\). Each alignment preserves every client's update exactly, since \(\tilde B_i\tilde A_i=B_iRR^\top A_i=B_iA_i\).
key_idea: Because \((BR)(R^\top A)=BA\) for every rotation \(R\), clients can reach equivalent but rotated factors, and averaging them gives a \(\bar B\bar A\) far from \(\tfrac1N\sum_iB_iA_i\). Fixing this gauge with a closed-form Procrustes rotation toward last round's global factors (softened by \(\lambda\); \(\lambda=0\) is plain FedIT averaging) shrinks the aggregation-error term in the nonconvex convergence bound. It costs \(O(dr^2+r^3)\) per client and adds no communication.
results_note: On GLUE with RoBERTa-Large (\(r=4\), Dirichlet \(h=0.5\), \(N=50\) clients; Table 1), FedRot-LoRA averages 87.34% accuracy versus 82.44% for RoLoRA and 76.80% for FedIT.
categorical_reading: FedRot-LoRA is FedIT with a partial gauge fixing: before uploading, each client replaces \((B_i,A_i)\) by the representative of its \(SO(r)\)-orbit closest to the previous global pair. This removes the rotational part of the aggregation error \(\bar B\bar A-\tfrac1N\sum_iB_iA_i\), but not the part coming from the non-compact half of \(GL_r\). That is why Prop V.4 needs a shared factor (FFA-LoRA), stacking (FLoRA) or a gauge-invariant statistic (FLoRG) for exactness.

A row-orthonormal \(A_0\) attains this minimum and also caps the first update at full fine-tuning's (\(\|\Delta W_1\|_F\le\eta\|G_0\|_F\), Proposition 5.3). The minimum is not unique: any \(A_0\) whose singular values are at most \(\sqrt2\) attains it, including, with high probability, the \(\mathcal N(0,1/n)\) LoRA baseline in Table 1, so the bound alone does not separate orthonormal from Gaussian \(A_0\). categorical_reading: LoRA-RLPO/RLMO is LoRA pointed in the \(\mathrm T_A\) stratum at the top or bottom right singular subspace of \(W_0\): PiSSA's and MiLoRA's subspaces with their Type II split removed. That puts the start back at the apex and keeps \(\|I-A_0^\top A_0\|_2=1\), the quantity in the paper's bound on the LoRA-to-full-FT gap. Every \(A_0\) with singular values \(\le\sqrt2\) attains that bound, so the orthonormal frame is one point of a large set of equally good pointings.

name: NaRA
paper_title: NaRA: Noise-Aware LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Diffusion LLMs
