locus: q, k, v, o attention projections of masked-diffusion LLMs (LLaDA-8B-Base and LLaDA-8B-Instruct); one image-diffusion experiment (SDXL, DreamBooth) in Section 6.6
structure: \(\Delta W(\lambda)=BC(\lambda)A\). Static per-module factors \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\) and \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\) sandwich a dynamic \(r\times r\) core that is a smooth function of the scalar noise level \(\lambda\). One Fourier-feature MLP, shared by every adapted module, produces the core once per denoising step. The update therefore moves continuously along the denoising trajectory inside fixed rank-\(r\) column and row spaces.
mergeable_reason: For a fixed \(\lambda\), \(W_0+BC(\lambda)A\) is a dense matrix. But \(\lambda\) changes at every denoising step (and can differ across sequences in a batch), so no single merged weight exists. The paper lists non-mergeability as a limitation (Appendix, Table 10); re-merging at every step is possible in principle (catalogue's inference, not the paper's).
identity_at_init: \(B=0\) gives \(\Delta W(\lambda)=0\) for every \(\lambda\). The hypernetwork's last layer is zero-initialized, so \(C(\lambda)=I_r\) and the initial gradients equal LoRA's.
key_idea: Masked-diffusion LLMs see very different inputs at different noise levels, so a static \(\Delta W\) helps mostly at mid noise. NaRA sandwiches a noise-conditioned core \(C(\lambda)=I_r+\eta\mathcal F_\phi(e_\lambda)\) between static LoRA factors, giving a continuous family \(\Delta W(\lambda)\). Theorem 4.1 shows this family can represent any finite set of updates whose combined column and row spaces have dimension \(\le r\); the extra parameters are under 0.01% of the model. Timestep-conditioned LoRAs already existed for image diffusion (TC-LoRA, TimeStep Master); NaRA is the first noise-aware PEFT for diffusion LLMs.
results_note: On LLaDA-8B-Instruct commonsense reasoning (\(r=32\), Table 1), NaRA averages 84.09% versus 80.18% for LoRA and 82.73% for HiRA, with 0.425% versus 0.417% trainable parameters.
categorical_reading: NaRA is a section of LoRA over the noise-level line: a smooth map \(\lambda\mapsto W_0+BC(\lambda)A\) whose fibres move inside one fixed pair of rank-\(r\) column and row spaces, with an \(r\times r\) core produced by one hypernetwork for all modules. Static LoRA is the constant section (\(\eta=0\)). Fibrewise it is MoSLoRA with the mixer generated, and tied across modules.

locus: q, k, v, o attention projections in both the SigLIP vision encoder and the Qwen2 LLM of LLaVA-OneVision-Qwen2-7B (216 target layers; 0.5B model for ablations; also Molmo2-8B); wraps LoRA, DoRA, LoRA-FA, SliceFine (\(r=2\), \(\alpha=4\)) or prompt tuning (10 virtual tokens); \(E=4\) experts, n-gram routing window 3
structure: The output \(\hat z\) of one shared PEFT module is rescaled element-wise by a convex combination of \(E\) expert vectors. A parameter-free softmax router chooses the combination from normalized slices of \(W_0x\) and \(\hat z\), with confidence-adaptive top-\(k\) and one decision per n-gram window. For LoRA this is \(\Delta W(x)=\mathrm{diag}(\mathcal P(x)+\gamma p_s)\,BA\): a token-dependent diagonal rescaling of the rows of one rank-\(r\) update.
mergeable_reason: \(\mathcal P(x)\) depends on each token (or n-gram window) through the router, so \(\Delta W(x)=\mathrm{diag}(\mathcal P(x)+\gamma p_s)BA\) varies per token. Only with \(E=1\) does it collapse to a static, mergeable \(\mathrm{diag}(p_1+\gamma p_s)BA\).
identity_at_init: With LoRA, the released code zero-initializes \(B\), so \(\hat z=0\) and \(h=W_0x\) exactly. Initialization is \(p_i\sim\mathcal U(0.9,1.1)\), \(p_s\sim\mathcal N(0,0.1^2)\), \(\gamma=0\), so LiME also starts close to the plain shared PEFT module.
key_idea: MoE-PEFT methods normally keep \(E\) adapter copies plus a learned router. LiME keeps one PEFT module and lets \(E\) vectors \(p_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\) rescale its output, so expert cost becomes \(E\,d_{out}\) and works with any PEFT method. Routing logits come for free from the first \(E\) coordinates of the frozen output and the PEFT output. Theorem 2 states that the optimal-risk gap to expert-specific PEFT is \(O(\bar\varepsilon)\) if the modulation approximates it within \(\bar\varepsilon\); the approximation error itself is assumed, not bounded.
results_note: On MMT-47 with LLaVA-OneVision-Qwen2-7B (Table 2), LiME-LoRA has the best commonsense-reasoning average (84.98%), with 3.49M trainable parameters versus 10.79M for MoELoRA. In the GLUE efficiency study (one epoch on one H100, about 894M total parameters), LiME-LoRA trains 0.52M parameters versus 1.97M for MoELoRA and runs 23% faster.
categorical_reading: LiME is an \(X\)-point of row scalings of one shared LoRA update: MoV's routed scaling vectors, moved from \(W_0\) to the adapter's output. Per token its weight \(W_0+\mathrm{diag}(v(x))BA\) lies in LoRA\(_r\) with a fixed row space and a token-dependent column space \(\mathrm{diag}(v(x))\,\mathrm{col}\,B\). The router borrows coordinates of \(W_0x\) and \(\hat z\) as logits. That is what makes it parameter-free, and also what fixes a privileged output basis.

categorical_reading: AGZO is MeZO with its random line restricted to the slice \(\{XU_\ell^\top\}\), which contains the row space of every layer gradient \(Q_\ell H_\ell^\top\). The compression is still one directional derivative, but along a rank-\(r\) direction whose input side is a data frame. Per step it is LoRA-FA\((U_\ell^\top)\) along a single random line, re-based every step.

locus: all weight matrices (full-parameter zeroth-order fine-tuning) of OPT-1.3B/13B, LLaMA3-8B and Gemma2-2B (SuperGLUE, SQuAD) and ViT-B/16, ViT-L/16 (CIFAR-10/100)
structure: A multi-query forward-difference gradient estimate (RGE) is taken in a random rank-\(r\) left subspace \(\mathrm{col}(P)\), which is lazily resampled. The \(r\times d_{in}\) estimate is orthogonalized by the matrix sign function and lifted back by \(P\). With an exact matrix sign each update \(P\,\mathrm{msign}(\widehat G_Z)\) is a rank-\(\le r\) partial isometry whose nonzero singular values equal 1; the Newton–Schulz iteration used in practice makes them only approximately 1.
mergeable_reason: ZO-Muon edits the model's own weights in place; there is no adapter to merge.
identity_at_init: Trivial: there is no reparameterization, and training starts at \(W_0\).
key_idea: Estimate the ZO gradient of the projected variable \(Z\) (\(W\approx PZ\), with \(P\) random and column-orthonormal) by multi-query RGE. This cuts the dimension behind the estimator's variance from \(d_{out}d_{in}\) to \(rd_{in}\). Then orthogonalize the estimate Muon-style and lift it back with \(P\). Orthogonalizing full-space MeZO estimates (ZO-Muon-V0) does not help, but inside the subspace the matrix sign acts as a spectral noise filter, making ZO-Muon a zeroth-order approximation of low-rank Muon.
results_note: Versus MeZO, ZO-Muon needs 24.7% of the queries to reach 0.90 on SST-2 (OPT-1.3B, Fig. 2a) and reaches 72.4% versus 47.3% on CIFAR-100 with ViT-L (Table 1). The abstract attributes this +25.1-point gain to ViT-B, but Table 1 shows it is ViT-L.
categorical_reading: ZO-Muon is the zeroth-order version of a one-sided GaLore period with a random frame: per period it is FB\((P_k)\), the frozen-\(B\) sub-object of LoRA, trained by forward differences and orthogonalised steps. The subspace is what makes the matrix sign useful, since it then acts on an \(r\times d_{in}\) estimate whose variance scales with \(rd_{in}\) rather than \(d_{out}d_{in}\).

Each reallocation removes one triplet from each of } b(t) \text{ matrices and adds one to each of } b(t) \text{ others, so } \textstyle\sum_\ell r_\ell \text{ stays at the initial budget; the parameter count itself can drift when the adapted matrices differ in } d_{in}+d_{out}
locus: DeBERTaV3-base for GLUE (the paper's rank-allocation figure shows query, key, value, attention-output, intermediate and output dense matrices), the Q, K, V, Up and Down projections of LLaMA3-8B for commonsense reasoning, and ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-22K) for VTAB-1K, whose target modules the paper does not list
structure: An SVD-form additive update \(\Delta W_\ell=P_\ell\Lambda_\ell Q_\ell\) of rank \(r_\ell\). It uses the AdaLoRA parameterization, with a soft orthogonality penalty on \(P_\ell\) and \(Q_\ell\), and it moves rank between matrices during training. Allocation uses one score per matrix, the Shannon entropy of the normalized spectral energies \(s_i=\lambda_i^2/\sum_j\lambda_j^2\) divided by \(\log r_\ell\), which lies in \([0,1]\). Low entropy means the energy sits in a few directions, so the matrix can give up rank. High entropy means the energy is spread out, so the matrix should gain rank. Pruning removes the triplet with the smallest \(\lambda\) from each of the \(b(t)\) lowest-entropy matrices. Expansion appends a Gaussian pair \((p,q)\) with \(\lambda=0\) to each of the \(b(t)\) highest-entropy matrices, so insertion leaves the function unchanged. \(b(t)\) follows a cubic decay schedule between a warm-up and a final freeze phase. The released code differs from the paper in three details: its schedule is \(b_0(1-p^3)\) rather than \(b_0(1-p)^3\), with \(p\) the elapsed fraction of the allocation phase; pruning removes the triplet with the smallest signed \(\lambda\) rather than the smallest magnitude; and the orthogonality penalty uses the unsquared Frobenius norm, averaged over factors.
mergeable_reason: \(P_\ell\Lambda_\ell Q_\ell\) is a dense \(d_{out}\times d_{in}\) matrix that folds into \(W_0\). Ranks change only during training.
identity_at_init: Exact. \(\Lambda=0\) at initialization: in the released flexlora.py the singular-value vector is zero-initialized and \(P,Q\sim\mathcal{N}(0,0.02^2)\), so \(\Delta W=0\). Every expanded direction also starts at \(\lambda=0\) (the paper's zero-impact initialization), so growing a rank does not change the current output.
key_idea: FlexLoRA replaces per-direction sensitivity scores with a matrix-level score, the normalized entropy of each matrix's learned singular values \(\Lambda_\ell\). Under a fixed global budget it moves rank from low-entropy to high-entropy matrices, and new directions enter with \(\lambda=0\) so that expansion is function-preserving.
results_note: With DeBERTaV3-base FlexLoRA averages 89.1 on GLUE against 88.1 for AdaLoRA at the same 1.9M parameters; with LLaMA3-8B on eight commonsense tasks it scores 85.2 at rank 8 (AdaLoRA 85.1) and 85.5 at rank 32.
categorical_reading: FlexLoRA is AdaLoRA's object with a different budget dynamic. Rank leaves matrices whose learned spectrum \(\Lambda_\ell\) is concentrated and enters matrices whose spectrum is spread, moving between nested sub-cones (A2 truncations) and their \(\lambda=0\) extensions (A5 stages). Because the score reads \(\Lambda\) alone, it inherits the gauge dependence of \(P\Lambda Q\): \(\Lambda\) equals the singular values of \(\Delta W\) only when the orthogonality penalty is exactly satisfied.

structure: A token-routed mixture of \(Z\) dense spectral experts. Each expert update \(\Delta W_i\) is the inverse 2-D DFT of a sparse, Hermitian-symmetric spectrum supported on a fixed set \(\Omega_i\) of \(n\) frequencies. \(\Omega_i\) is drawn from a Gaussian band-pass around a per-expert centre frequency, so each expert is band-limited. \(\Delta W_i\) is therefore a real sum of 2-D sinusoids \(2|c|\cos(2\pi(uq/d_{out}+vy/d_{in})+\angle c)\), and each conjugate pair contributes rank at most 2. The router keeps the top \(k\) experts per token and mixes their spatial updates linearly, so the applied update \(\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}(x)}g_i(x)\Delta W_i\) depends on the input, with rank at most the number of non-zero spectral entries of the selected experts (App. H), which with conjugate partners counted is at most \(2kn\). Unlike FourierFT, the coefficients are complex, so the experts learn phase as well as amplitude. Catalogue observation, not from the paper: \(\mathrm{Re}\,\mathcal{F}^{-1}(F)=\mathcal{F}^{-1}\big(\tfrac12(F+\bar F^{\sharp})\big)\) with \(\bar F^{\sharp}(u,v)=\overline{F(\langle-u\rangle,\langle-v\rangle)}\) for every \(F\). Taking the real part of an unsymmetrized complex spectrum therefore reaches the same set of updates, and the substantive change from FourierFT is the learned phase rather than the symmetry constraint.
mergeable_reason: The gate values \(g_i(x)\) and the active set \(\mathcal{S}(x)\) change from token to token. Each \(\Delta W_i\) can be computed once per forward pass and cached, but no single static matrix reproduces the layer unless the routing is frozen.
identity_at_init: Not specified. The paper's algorithm only says that the complex coefficients are initialized and that the router starts random. \(\Delta W=0\) at the start would require zero coefficients (the FourierFT paper draws its coefficients from \(\mathcal{N}(0,1)\)), and no code is public.
key_idea: FourierMoE moves MoE-LoRA into the frequency domain. Each expert owns a band of 2-D Fourier frequencies with learnable complex coefficients (amplitude and phase), and a token-level top-\(k\) router decides which bands, and therefore how much rank, each token's weight update receives.
results_note: In the multi-task commonsense setting on LLaMA-2 7B FourierMoE averages 83.95 against 82.73 for GOAT, the strongest mixture-of-PEFT baseline, using 0.06% trainable parameters; on seven GLUE tasks with RoBERTa-large it averages 91.40 against 86.73 for FourierFT.
categorical_reading: FourierMoE is an \(X\)-point of a complex-coefficient FourierFT: the router chooses, per token, which frequency bands the update uses. Learning the phase as well as the amplitude takes each expert out of FourierFT's point-symmetric subspace \(\Delta W_{j,l}=\Delta W_{-j,-l}\) (the sine patterns are point-antisymmetric), so the experts share FourierFT's frame but are not FourierFT experts. Fibrewise the method still factors through LoRA-FA with a frozen trigonometric input frame.

categorical_reading: SMoA is MELoRA transported by HiRA's \(\theta_0\)-dependent Hadamard frame \(D_{W_0}\), after a spectral reordering of rows and columns; equivalently, HiRA\(_r\) with block-sparse factors. Its rank ceiling exceeds LoRA's, but at budget \(r\) its update set is a subset of HiRA\(_r\)'s, reached with \(1/K\) of the parameters. So its gain over HiRA is in parameter count, not expressivity.

The update is small because the prior scale is divided by the square root of the fan-in. The repository also has an InducingAdapter wrapper whose learnable output scale starts at 0, but the training script never uses it.

categorical_reading: Bayesian-LoRA is a family over a noise space whose samples are LoRA points with both factors random, generated from small inducing matrices through a bilinear GP conditional \(T_rUT_c\) that has LoRA's own shape. identity_at_init: Not exact. \(W^{1}=W_0+L(A^{1})^{\top}A^{1}R\), and \(A^{1}=0\) cannot be used because \(\nabla_AF=A(H+H^{\top})\) vanishes there. categorical_reading: FLoRG is SingLoRA's Gram form placed between two frozen frames. Its trained quantity is the \(O(r)\)-invariant core \(Q=A^\top A\), which is linear to average, so federated aggregation acts on a gauge-invariant statistic and is exact before re-factoring. The price is the image: a PSD cone, so \(L^\top\Delta WR^\top\) can only move in positive semidefinite directions.

structure: Each task adds two rank-\(r\) additive branches whose down-projections are frozen and designed from second moments of the layer inputs. The shared branch spans the top-\(r\) eigenspace of the accumulated old-plus-new statistics, for knowledge sharing. The isolated branch spans the top-\(r\) generalized eigenvectors of the pencil \((S^{t},S^{1:t-1})\), the directions with the largest ratio of new-task to old-task projection energy, instead of an approximate null space of old tasks. Training only \(B\) is gradient descent restricted to \(\mathrm{row}(A)\), with output change scaled by the projection energy \(\|Ax\|^2\) (Thm 3.1). The up-projections are trained with GAO, a two-subset look-ahead update that favors gradients agreeing across label-disjoint halves of a batch. Before merging, each rank-1 unit of the shared branch is shrunk by a closed-form ridge-type factor \(\gamma_j\in[0,1]\) that trades new-task fit against drift on old-task features. Both branches are then folded into the backbone.
mergeable_reason: After each task \(w_GB_G\Lambda_GA_G+B_IA_I\) is added to the backbone and the LoRA matrices are discarded, so inference uses a single weight matrix and needs no task identity.
identity_at_init: Exact for each task. \(B_G=B_I=0\) when a task starts, and on task 1 the isolated branch is disabled, so the layer equals \(W^{t-1}\). \(A_G\) and \(A_I\) are set beforehand from cached layer inputs.
key_idea: With a frozen down-projection, LoRA learns only along directions the inputs excite (projection energy \(\|Ax\|^2\)). LoDA therefore builds one subspace that old and new tasks both excite, for transfer, and one that the new task excites far more than old tasks, for isolation. Null-space designs instead use old-task null spaces, which the new task may barely use.
results_note: Without feature replay LoDA beats the strongest baseline, CoSO, by 0.80-1.70 points in final accuracy on its class-incremental benchmarks with a ViT-B/16, and the classifier-aligned LoDA+CA beats the replay-based MACIL by 0.15-5.11 points.
categorical_reading: LoDA is InfLoRA's scheme with a rank-\(2r\) frozen frame per task, split into a shared part (top eigenspace of the old-plus-new statistics) and an isolated part (top generalised eigenvectors of new against old statistics). Each stage is LoRA-FA\(([A_G;A_I])\). The ridge-type shrink \(\Lambda_G\) and the GAO updates choose a point of that linear stage and leave its image unchanged.

key_idea: Train every nested rank at once in a single forward pass: a fixed diagonal \(p_j=\sum_{r\in S,\,r\ge j}s_r\) between \(B\) and \(A\) turns the sum of all prefix adapters into one rank-\(R\) product. Its content is the choice of a frame that large-norm adapters cannot monopolise.

categorical_reading: SRR interpolates between the two orders of Prop V.2(b): \(k^\star=r\) is split-then-quantise (LQ-LoRA, QPiSSA) and \(k^\star=0\) is quantise-then-fit (one LoftQ step), with \(k^\star\) chosen per matrix from a closed-form proxy. categorical_reading: Activation prompting inserts a single translation box on the activation wire at layer \(l\), neutral at zero. Input-level additive VP is the case \(l=0\), and a position-uniform \(\delta\) is a bias edit, which is why Proposition 1 can match it with shift-only normalisation tuning at that layer. Its position resolution is what keeps it from being a weight-space method; its depth changes only how far the backward pass must reach.

The side network lives entirely on the cotangent side: it shapes the gradient that the selective block receives, which the deployed object cannot see.

The released code uses a centred depthwise kernel of size 5 confined to each chunk and, by default, the normalised MLP input rather than the token embedding as the target source. categorical_reading: In-Place TTT is a context-indexed section of 'fine-tune \(W_{down}\) only': a causal fast-weight memory written by one closed-form gradient step per chunk, i.e. a chunked linear-attention branch living inside an existing MLP box. Per (document, chunk) fibre it is a LoRA on \(W_{down}\) whose \(A\) factor is the activations of the earlier chunks and whose \(B\) factor is the generated targets, pointed at \(B=0\) by the zero convolution.

It therefore shrinks output directions that carry a large share of the stacked \(B\) energy. The strongest shrinkage, \(\alpha_j\to1/T\) as \(s_j\to1\), undoes the \(T\)-fold counting that a summed (Task Arithmetic) merge gives a direction used equally by all \(T\) tasks. A single scalar \(\gamma\) then restores the mean source Frobenius norm. \(A_t\) is untouched; in the ablation, calibrating \(A\) or the full \(BA\) instead lowers accuracy. Two consequences are derived here. (i) Task Arithmetic is linear, so \(\mathcal{M}(SB_tA_t)=S\,\mathcal{M}(B_tA_t)\) and Pico-TA equals the post-merge output-space reshaping \(\gamma S\Delta W_{\text{TA}}\); applying \(S\) before merging matters only for non-linear mergers such as TIES and TSV-M. (ii) \(s_j\) is a direction's share of the stacked spectrum, only a proxy for cross-task sharing, so a direction dominated by one task's energy is shrunk too. \(U\) is the left singular basis of the concatenated \(B\)'s. It is the same output basis Core Space builds (\(U_B\)). KnOTS instead takes the SVD of the stacked products \([B_1A_1,\dots,B_TA_T]\). Its left singular vectors span the same column space only when every \(A_t\) has full row rank, and they form a different basis.

key_idea: Across independently trained LoRAs, the output factors \(B_t\) reuse a few shared directions: pairwise overlap \(O_B\gg O_A\), and the effective rank of \(B\) is about 3 at LoRA rank 64. A linear merge counts these directions \(T\) times. Pico shrinks them before merging with the spectral weights \(\alpha_j=1/(1+(T-1)s_j)\) and then restores the update norm.
results_note: On Llama-3.1-8B with four rank-16 domain LoRAs, Pico raises the eight-benchmark average from 0.4093 to 0.4430 under Task Arithmetic, from 0.3859 to 0.4328 under TIES and from 0.3473 to 0.4305 under TSV-M. Pico+TA (0.4430) also beats a jointly trained multi-task LoRA (0.3688).
categorical_reading: Pico is a spectral reweighting of the shared output space before merging: under task arithmetic it is the post-merge map \(\Delta W\mapsto\gamma S\Delta W\), so its effect on nonlinear mergers comes only from applying \(S\) first. Because \(S\) is read off the \(B\) factors rather than the adapters, it depends on how each LoRA's scale is split between \(B\) and \(A\), which is what the design rule 'combine on products, or after a joint gauge fixing' (Prop V.4) warns about.

structure: A fixed two-sided frame expansion with a sparse block-diagonal core. \(\Delta W=\sum_iP_{out,i}C_iP_{in,i}^{\top}\) couples the \(i\)-th output subspace only with the \(i\)-th input subspace, and only \(n_c\) core entries are free. Rank is not capped by a small \(r\): \(\mathrm{rank}\,\Delta W\le\mathrm{rank}\,C\le n_c\). The general definition allows redundant frames (\(k\rho>d\)), but every reported experiment uses \(k\rho=d\) with Parseval normalisation. The main GLUE, instruction-tuning and ViT runs use \(\rho=2\), and the Appendix D ablation varies \(\rho\) from 2 to 256, still with \(k\rho=d\). Then \(\sum_iP_iP_i^{\top}=I\) with ranks summing to \(d\) forces the subspaces to be mutually orthogonal, so \(P_{out}\) and \(P_{in}\) are square orthogonal matrices and the frame is not redundant. Running the released construct_real_tff confirms this: the matrix is orthogonal to \(10^{-5}\) to \(10^{-4}\) (float32) for \(d=768\) to \(4096\), and its non-zero fraction is about \(2/\rho\) (99.6 to 99.9% at \(\rho=2\), about 50% at \(\rho=4\), about 25% at \(\rho=8\)). At \(\rho=2\) the Spectral Tetris unit-norm tight frame in \(\mathbb{C}^1\) is all ones, so the modulated frame is the realified \((d/2)\)-point DFT basis: each 2-D subspace is the realification of one conjugated DFT row. In this regime FrameFT is FourierFT-like: sparse coefficients in a fixed DFT-type basis on both sides. The block-sparse frames that the paper credits for throughput appear only at \(\rho\ge4\). The released code also decouples the coefficient blocks from \(\rho\). Llama-2-7B uses \(4\times4\) blocks, Llama-2-13B \(40\times40\), Gemma-2-2B one full block (no block-diagonal constraint, so a random sparse support over the whole two-sided realified-DFT basis), and Gemma-2-9B and Llama-3.1-8B 128 blocks. Four of the twelve released GLUE scripts use \(\rho=4\) (tff_l 4), although the paper states \(\rho=2\) for GLUE. Lemma 3.1: if \(f(W)\) is \(L\)-smooth, the reparameterised loss \(f(C)\) is \(LB_{out}B_{in}\)-smooth, unlike LoRA's factored \((A,B)\) landscape. Gradient descent with \(\eta\le1/\tilde L\) therefore gets the standard \(O(1/T)\) stationarity rate (Theorem 3.2).
mergeable_reason: \(\Delta W\) is a dense additive matrix computed from the frames and the sparse core. The released tuner's merge() adds it to \(W_0\), so inference cost is unchanged.
identity_at_init: Depends on the configuration. The released instruction-tuning scripts set init_std 0, so \(C=0\) and \(\Delta W=0\) at step 0. The GLUE scripts do not pass init_std, so the default 1.0 (GLUE/args.py and the FrameConfig default) applies: the \(n_c\) coefficients start as \(\mathcal{N}(0,1)\) samples and \(\Delta W\neq0\) at initialisation, as in FourierFT. The tuner's reset_frame_parameters, which would zero the coefficients, is defined but never called. The paper's Algorithm 1 only says 'Init'.
key_idea: Replace LoRA's learned factor subspaces with fixed, algorithmically generated Parseval fusion frames, shared by all layers of the same width, and learn only a sparse block-diagonal coefficient matrix between them. Storage drops to \(n_c\) scalars per matrix, and the coefficient-space loss inherits the smoothness of the weight-space loss.
results_note: Instruction-tuned on Alpaca with 320K trainable parameters, Llama-2-7B averages 63.62 on eight LM-eval-harness tasks, against 63.18 for LoRA (16.7M) and 63.22 for FourierFT (320K) (Table 3). LoRA stays 0.2 to 0.7 points ahead on Llama-2-13B, Gemma-2-9B and Llama-3.1-8B. On GLUE, FrameFT averages 86.1 (RoBERTa-base, 24K parameters) and 88.7 (RoBERTa-large, 48K) (Table 1).
categorical_reading: FrameFT is a SHiRA-type coordinate mask transported by a fixed two-sided frame \(X\mapsto P_{out}XP_{in}^\top\), which in all reported settings is a realified DFT on both sides; the transport is \(\theta_0\)-independent, unlike SVFT's. It is a FourierFT relative that couples each output frequency block only with the matching input block, through a dense \(\rho\times\rho\) core.

paper_title: PrefixMemory-Tuning: Modernizing Prefix-Tuning by Decoupling the Prefix from Attention

locus: Every attention head of every layer: a query-conditioned branch added to each head's output before \(W_O\) (LLaMA2-7B-Chat, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-7B)
structure: An additive, query-conditioned bias outside the softmax: \(o_i\mapsto o_i+M^{\top}\phi(q_i)\). Unlike a prefix, it is not renormalised against the input's attention mass. Prefix-tuning gives \(o^{pt}_i=(1-\alpha_i)o_i+\sum_{j\le\ell}\alpha_{ij}W_Vs_j\), where \(\alpha_i\) depends on the input and prefix lengths; this is the paper's tradeoff argument. In PMT the input path keeps weight 1 and the memory path is independent of length. A structural reading, derived here: through the frozen output projection, each layer gains the parallel branch \(\sum_hW_O^{(h)}M_h^{\top}\phi(W_Q^{(h)}x_i)\). That is a parallel adapter whose down-projection is the frozen query projection \(W_Q\) (width \(d_K\) per head and \(Hd_K=d\) in total for both LLaMA2-7B and Qwen2.5-3B, so it is not a bottleneck), whose nonlinearity is elu or gelu, and whose trained map is block-diagonal (one \(M_h^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_V\times d_K}\) per head), read out through the frozen \(W_O\). It is the linear-kernel counterpart of He et al.'s view of prefix-tuning as a gated parallel adapter. Memory capacity scales with \(d_\phi\times d_V\) rather than with prefix length. Remark 1 notes that a trainable \(\phi_W(x)=\mathrm{ReLU}(Wx+b)\) would turn the branch into a one-hidden-layer MLP; Table 2 reports such an 'MLP Kernel' variant, better than elu on some tasks and worse on others. The paper does not say whether \(q_i\) is taken before or after RoPE; after RoPE the branch would depend on position.
mergeable_reason: \(\phi(q_i)^{\top}M\) is a non-linear (elu/gelu) function of the query, so the branch cannot be folded into \(W_Q,W_K,W_V\) or \(W_O\) and stays at inference. It costs about one extra \(d_K\times d_V\) product per head per token and does not grow the KV cache.
identity_at_init: Not stated, and the linked code repository is empty. With \(M=0\) the branch vanishes and \(o^{PMT}_i=o_i\) exactly. Prefix-tuning has no such parameter value: any prefix with \(\ell\ge1\) takes softmax mass \(\alpha_i>0\) from the input.
key_idea: Prefix-tuning underperforms on deep LLMs because the prefix shares each head's softmax normaliser with the input, so prefix influence and input specificity trade off with sequence length. PMT moves the prefix out of the softmax, linearises it with a kernel feature map \(\phi\), and replaces the prefix key-value sum with a free memory matrix \(M\), giving \(o_i=\mathrm{Attn}_i+\phi(q_i)^{\top}M\).
results_note: With one training example per class, PMT reaches 71.2% on BigBench with LLaMA2-7B-Chat and 76.6% with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, above LoRA (\(r=64\)), prefix-tuning and full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: PMT turns prefix tuning's renormalised prompt contribution into an ungated kernel-feature memory: by Thm VI.5(b) a prefix rescales content attention by \(1-\lambda_q\), while PMT keeps the content path at weight 1 and adds \(M^\top\phi(q)\). That buys a neutral point (as LLaMA-Adapter's gate does) and makes the method a parallel branch around attention whose down-projection is the frozen \(W_Q\), whose activation is \(\phi\) (elu or gelu) and whose up-projection is \(W_O\) times a trained block-diagonal map. Because \(\phi\) is not ReLU, this is not the catalogued (ReLU) parallel adapter, so no arrow into it is recorded.

full_name: FourTune: fully 4-bit (W4A4G4) LoRA post-training with a frozen low-rank numerical stabilizer
paper_title: FourTune: Towards Fully 4-Bit Efficient Post-Training for Diffusion Models

structure: A QLoRA-type composite with three parallel branches on each linear layer. The first is a frozen 4-bit residual GEMM (W4A4). The second is a frozen high-precision low-rank stabilizer \(L_{\text{stab}}\) that absorbs the quantisation-sensitive outlier directions of \(W_0\); this is SVDQuant's decomposition, reused here during training. The third is a trainable rank-\(r\) LoRA \(BA\). The trainable update is the ordinary additive \(BA\); what changes is the arithmetic. QLoRA dequantises and computes in W4A16G16, while FourTune runs the forward and input-gradient GEMMs in 4-bit (W4A4G4). Its \(16\times16\) block-wise scales let the transposed weight be used in the backward pass without requantisation. The LoRA down-projection, the stabilizer and activation quantisation share one fused kernel, and the 4-bit GEMM is fused with the up-projections. The block granularity is \(16\times16\) instead of the usual \(1\times16\) groups (Table 5: LPIPS 0.227 vs 0.203 for reconstruction). An INT4 variant on an RTX 4090 is reported in Appendix B. Without the stabilizer, naive W4A4G4 training shows gradient explosion in the distillation runs (Fig. 8). The stabilizer and the LoRA have the same algebraic form (high-precision low-rank maps of \(x\)), so the trained LoRA can be concatenated into the stabilizer branch: \([L_1\ B][L_2;A]\).
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) can be concatenated into the high-precision low-rank branch, \(L_{\text{stab}}+BA=[L_1\ B]\,[L_2;A]\) (rank \(k+r\)), which keeps the trained function exactly in a W4A4 inference engine. Folding it into the 4-bit residual \(R\) requires requantisation. Folding it into a BF16 \(W_0\) gives \(W_0+BA\), which differs from the training-time function by the quantisation error of \(R\).
identity_at_init: Not stated. Under standard LoRA initialisation (\(BA=0\)) the model starts at the quantised base \(Q(R)Q(x)+L_{\text{stab}}x\approx W_0x\), not exactly at \(W_0x\).
key_idea: FourTune aims to make PEFT faster than BF16 LoRA, not only smaller, by running the whole frozen backbone in native 4-bit for weights, activations and gradients. A frozen high-precision low-rank stabilizer \(L_{\text{stab}}\) carries the outlier directions. \(16\times16\) block scales and fused LoRA and MLP kernels keep the 4-bit backward pass efficient.
results_note: In end-to-end FLUX.1-dev customization training, FourTune uses 14.51 GB against 29.35 GB for BF16 LoRA. A step takes 0.86 s on an RTX 5090, 2.27x faster than BF16 LoRA and 2.79x faster than NF4 QLoRA, at matched generation quality.
categorical_reading: FourTune is QLoRA over a different base change: the quantiser is SVDQuant's split into a high-precision low-rank part plus a 4-bit residual, kept frozen during training, and both passes run in 4-bit arithmetic. As an object it is LoRA at the translate \(Q(R)+L_{stab}\). The stabiliser and the adapter have the same algebraic form, which is why the trained LoRA can be absorbed exactly into the low-rank branch, but not into the 4-bit weight.

name: GradFix
full_name: GradFix: gradient-sign masking for task-vector transport across pre-trained models
paper_title: Gradient-Sign Masking for Task Vector Transport Across Pre-Trained Models
formula_latex: \tau_A=\theta_A^{ft}-\theta_A\ \ (\text{per matrix } \Delta W_A=W_A^{ft}-W_A);\ \ \hat s_i=\mathrm{sign}\Big(-\sum_{(x_n,y_n)\in\mathcal{D}_s}\mathrm{sign}\big(\nabla_\theta\ell(f_{\theta_B}(x_n),y_n)\big)_i\Big)\ \ (\text{majority vote over } N=|\mathcal{D}_s| \text{ labelled target examples});\ \ m_i=\mathbb{1}\{\mathrm{sign}(\tau_{A,i})=\hat s_i\},\ \ \theta_B^{\text{trans}}=\theta_B+\alpha\,(m\odot\tau_A);\ \ \text{full-data form: } g=\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L}(\theta_B),\ \ g^{\top}\big(\alpha\,m\odot\tau_A\big)=-\alpha\textstyle\sum_im_i|g_i||\tau_{A,i}|\le0;\ \ \text{frozen: } \theta_A,\ \theta_A^{ft},\ \theta_B;\ \text{nothing is trained; } \alpha \text{ is chosen on a validation set}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(training-free); each transport builds one binary mask } m\in\{0,1\}^{|\theta|} \text{ from } N \text{ per-sample target gradients, plus the scalar } \alpha
locus: All parameters covered by the source task vector: the CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 image encoders (text encoder frozen), and T5-base for language tasks (T5 v1.1 as source, FLAN-T5 as target).
structure: A coordinatewise Hadamard filter on a task vector, in parameter coordinates. The transported delta keeps \(\tau_A\) on the sign-agreement set \(\{i:\mathrm{sign}\,\tau_{A,i}=\mathrm{sign}(-g_i)\}\) unchanged and zeros it elsewhere. This makes it a base-change map: a displacement measured at base point \(\theta_A\) is projected onto the target's local descent orthant at \(\theta_B\), with no permutation alignment and no parameter updates. The first-order descent property \(g^{\top}\delta\le0\) holds by construction for the full-data gradient, so the update lowers the loss for sufficiently small \(\alpha\). With few samples the paper's lemma is per coordinate: under an independence assumption and \(p_i>1/2\), \(\Pr[\hat s_i=\mathrm{sign}(-g_i)]\ge1-e^{-2N(p_i-1/2)^2}\) (Hoeffding). A guarantee for the whole vector would need a union bound that the paper does not state. The filter acts on coordinates, not on functions, so it depends on the basis. One consequence, derived here: for a factored adapter, \(m\odot(BA)\) is in general full-rank, so a LoRA task vector would be transported as a masked dense matrix, not as low-rank factors. The paper's experiments use full fine-tuning task vectors. For multi-task merging, merge-then-mask with a consensus target-sign mask works best; for several sources fine-tuned on one task, mask-then-merge works best. Magnitude-weighted masks underperform, which the paper reads as directions transferring across pre-trainings while magnitudes do not.
mergeable_reason: The result is a single additive weight delta \(\alpha\,m\odot\tau_A\) on \(\theta_B\). It composes with Task Arithmetic and TIES (mask-then-merge or merge-then-mask) and adds no inference overhead.
identity_at_init: Nothing is trained. \(\alpha=0\), or an empty mask, returns the target base \(\theta_B\) exactly.
key_idea: A task vector trained on an old base \(\theta_A\) transfers to a new release \(\theta_B\) once its coordinates whose sign disagrees with the target's anti-gradient are removed. A few target gradients, combined by a majority vote of signs and with no update steps, rebase \(\tau_A\) onto \(\theta_B\) with a first-order descent guarantee \(g^{\top}\delta\le0\).
results_note: With one labelled example per class, transporting a DataComp-XL CLIP ViT-B/16 EuroSAT task vector to a LAION-2B ViT-B/16 gives 61.94%. Naive task-vector addition gives 49.58%, zero-shot 49.41%, and few-shot fine-tuning on the same samples 56.61%.
categorical_reading: GradFix is a base-change map for task vectors: a displacement measured at \(\theta_A\) is projected, coordinate by coordinate, onto the descent orthant \(\{\delta:\delta_ig_i\le0\}\) of the loss at \(\theta_B\), which is exactly its first-order guarantee. Being coordinatewise it is monomial-natural, not rotation-natural, and it would turn a LoRA task vector into a masked dense matrix.

Folding it into \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}\) needs dequantisation, and requantising would change the configuration, as with QLoRA. The mapper \(\theta\) has to be kept to serve other configurations.
identity_at_init: Not identity relative to the quantised base. In the code, the last MLP layer starts with \(\mathcal N(0,(10^{-3})^2)\) weights and zero bias, so \(I_r+U_\theta\approx I_r\). The LoRA factors start as the rank-\(r\) SVD of \(W_0-\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}\), so the initial model \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}+L_1L_2\) is the best rank-\(r\) correction of the quantisation error. It approximates \(W_0\), not \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}\).
key_idea: The quantisation configuration becomes a conditioning input. A hypernetwork of about 2M parameters turns each layer's bit-width and block-size choice into an \(r\times r\) adjustment \(I_r+U_\theta(Q_i)\) of that layer's LoRA, so one training run serves any per-layer configuration instead of one QLoRA or LQ-LoRA run per configuration. The configurations used for training are chosen by a Pareto search over accuracy and average bit-width.
results_note: On four GLUE tasks with RoBERTa-Large, one training run of about an hour covers 50 configurations from 2.5 to 6.25 bits, with accuracy comparable to or better than QLoRA and LQ-LoRA, which need 20-40 minutes of fine-tuning per configuration.
categorical_reading: CoA-LoRA is a section of LQ-LoRA over the space of per-layer quantisation configurations: one hypernetwork turns each configuration into an \(r\times r\) move inside a fixed pair of column and row spaces, as NaRA does over noise levels. Every fibre lives in a different translate of LoRA's cone, one per quantised base, and is pointed only up to that configuration's attained residual.

name: Low-Rank Ternary Adaptation
full_name: Ternary multiplicative adaptation: a Kronecker-factorised ternary keep/zero/flip mask applied elementwise to ternary weights
paper_title: Low-Rank Ternary Adaptation for Fine-Tuning Transformers
formula_latex: W_0=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,W_{\text{tern}},\ W_{\text{tern}}\in\{-1,0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}};\ \ h=\mathrm{diag}(s)\big(W_{\text{tern}}\odot\Delta_{\text{tern}}\big)x,\quad \Delta_{\text{tern}}=A\otimes B,\ \ A=\mathrm{Tern}(\bar A)\in\{-1,0,1\}^{p_1\times q_1},\ B=\mathrm{Tern}(\bar B)\in\{-1,0,1\}^{p_2\times q_2},\ \ p_1p_2=d_{out},\ q_1q_2=d_{in};\ \ \mathrm{Tern}:\ \text{entrywise threshold set from the mean absolute value of each factor, gradients passed to the real proxies } \bar A,\bar B \text{ by a straight-through estimator};\ \ W_{\text{merged}}=W_{\text{tern}}\odot(A\otimes B)\in\{-1,0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{frozen: } W_{\text{tern}}\ \text{and its scales } s;\ \text{trained: } \bar A\in\mathbb{R}^{p_1\times q_1},\ \bar B\in\mathbb{R}^{p_2\times q_2}
trainable_params: p_1q_1+p_2q_2\ \text{per adapted matrix}\ (p_1p_2=d_{out},\ q_1q_2=d_{in});\ 2d\ \text{for a square } d\times d \text{ layer only when } d \text{ is a perfect square } (p_i=q_i=\sqrt d);\ \text{Llama-3.2-1B's } 2048\times 2048 \text{ layers use } (32\times32,\ 64\times64)=5120=2.5d,\ 512\text{-wide k/v use } 2560,\ \text{MLP layers } 10240;\ \approx 7.4\times10^{5}\ \text{in total} \approx 0.06\%\ \text{of Llama-3.2-1B (Table 5)}
locus: All self-attention and feed-forward linear layers of ternary Transformers, output head excluded: SpinQuant-ternarised Llama-3.2-1B/3B, the pre-trained ternary BitNet b1.58 2B4T and Falcon-E-1B/3B-Instruct, and the ternary ViT-B/16 encoder of TernaryCLIP
structure: A Hadamard (entrywise) action of the multiplicative monoid \(\{-1,0,1\}\) on ternary weights. Each mask entry keeps (\(+1\)), zeroes (\(0\)) or flips (\(-1\)) the corresponding weight. \(\{-1,0,1\}\) is closed under multiplication and \(\odot\) commutes with the row scaling \(\mathrm{diag}(s)\), so adapted and merged weights stay ternary with unchanged scales. The mask is constrained to a Kronecker product \(A\otimes B\) of two small ternary factors, so \(\mathrm{rank}(A\otimes B)=\mathrm{rank}(A)\,\mathrm{rank}(B)\) is bounded by \(\min(p_1,q_1)\min(p_2,q_2)\) and reaches \(\min(d_{out},d_{in})\) for the balanced factor shapes of Table 5, with only \(p_1q_1+p_2q_2\) proxies. Despite the title, the update is neither low-rank nor additive. Written additively it is \(\Delta W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\big(W_{\text{tern}}\odot(A\otimes B-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top})\big)\). Because \(0\cdot\Delta_{ij}=0\), zero weights can never be reactivated (zero-locking). The weight-transition analysis confirms that no weight leaves 0 and that gains come from sign changes of nonzero weights. The 'balanced' and 'normalized' initialisations draw signed factors and pre-compensate the base, \(W_{\text{tern}}\leftarrow(\mathrm{sign}\bar A\otimes\mathrm{sign}\bar B)\odot W_{\text{tern}}\). A \(\pm1\) mask is an involution under \(\odot\), so the step-0 forward weights equal the pretrained ones.
mergeable_reason: The merged weight \(W_{\text{tern}}\odot(A\otimes B)\) lies again in \(\{-1,0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\) with the original scales. It replaces the base layer with no dequantisation, requantisation, extra parameters or latency, and the proxies \(\bar A,\bar B\) are discarded.
identity_at_init: Yes, by construction. All-ones factors give \(A\otimes B=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(W'_{\text{tern}}=W_{\text{tern}}\). The balanced and normalized schemes used in the main experiments have signed factors but pre-multiply the base by \(\mathrm{sign}\bar A\otimes\mathrm{sign}\bar B\), so the step-0 forward weights are again the pretrained ternary weights.
key_idea: Additive LoRA updates leave the ternary domain, so the update is made multiplicative: a ternary keep/zero/flip mask applied entrywise to ternary weights. The mask is parameterised as a Kronecker product \(A\otimes B\) of two small ternary matrices, trained through real-valued proxies with a straight-through estimator. The fine-tuned model merges into a strictly ternary model with no dequantisation.
results_note: On SpinQuant-ternarised Llama-3.2-3B fine-tuned on Alpaca, the merged ternary model raises the 9-task zero-shot average from 31.9 to 38.3 and cuts WikiText-2 perplexity from 45.6 to 22.3, ahead of QLoRA merged and requantised to ternary (37.5 and 22.9).
categorical_reading: Ternary adaptation replaces the additive update, which leaves the ternary grid, by a monoid action that preserves it. The merge is type-preserving by construction, so the quantised-type obstruction of Prop V.2(d) disappears, and so does any gain from merge-and-restart, since the masks form a submonoid. The Kronecker constraint is what makes a sign-flip mask cheap, and it is also an imposed structure.

name: AdaRank
full_name: AdaRank: Adaptive Rank Pruning (test-time learned binary masks on the singular components of task vectors)
paper_title: AdaRank: Adaptive Rank Pruning for Enhanced Model Merging
formula_latex: \tau_i^{l}=W_i^{l}-W_0^{l}=U_i^{l}\Sigma_i^{l}V_i^{l\top}\ (i=1,\dots,T);\quad W^{l}(B)=W_0^{l}+\lambda^{l}\sum_{i=1}^{T}U_i^{l}\,\mathrm{diag}(B_i^{l})\,\Sigma_i^{l}\,V_i^{l\top},\ \ B_i^{l}\in\{0,1\}^{\min(d_{out},d_{in})};\ \ B_{i,r}^{l}=\mathbf 1\{\sigma(\tilde b_{i,r}^{l}/T_{\text{temp}})\ge 0.5\}\ \ (\text{straight-through estimator},\ T_{\text{temp}}=10);\ \ \min_{\tilde b,\lambda}\ \sum_{i=1}^{T}\sum_{x\in\mathcal D_i^{\text{test}}}H\big(f(W(B),x)\big)\ \ (\text{output entropy on unlabeled test inputs});\ \ \text{frozen: } W_0 \text{ and all } (U_i,\Sigma_i,V_i);\ \text{optimised at test time: mask logits } \tilde b \text{ and layer coefficients } \lambda^{l}
trainable_params: T\cdot\min(d_{out},d_{in})\ \text{mask logits per weight matrix (one per singular component per task), plus one } \lambda^{l}\ \text{per layer; all discarded after merging}
locus: Every weight matrix of the task vectors of models fine-tuned from one backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 image encoders (8, 14 and 20 tasks), and RoBERTa and GPT-2 (7 NLP tasks)
structure: Merging in the SVD basis of each task matrix with a learned 0/1 selection of singular triplets: \(\Delta W^{l}=\lambda^{l}\sum_{i}\sum_{r}B^{l}_{i,r}\sigma^{l}_{i,r}u^{l}_{i,r}v^{l\top}_{i,r}\). Each layer's mask set \(\{0,1\}^{T\times\min(d_{out},d_{in})}\) contains top-\(k\) truncation (\(B_{i,r}=\mathbf 1[r\le k]\), as in SVD merging and TSV-M) and full-rank Task Arithmetic (\(B=\mathbf 1\)) as special points. The kept rank and the kept indices can vary by task and layer, and need not be the top ones. AdaRank plugs into a base merger. With Task Arithmetic \(\tau_i=W_i-W_0\); with CART \(\tau_i=W_i-\bar W\) around the average weight; with TSV-M the concatenated \(U\) and \(V\) are whitened before masking; Iso-CTS is a fourth base merger in the experiments. Masks start at the base method's best setting and are optimised AdaMerging-style, by straight-through estimation of an entropy objective on unlabeled test batches. The motivation is that adding a top singular component of one task often raises the total multi-task loss.
mergeable_reason: After test-time adaptation the masks are frozen and the output is one static weight set of the backbone's size. No masks, routers or per-task parameters are kept at inference, unlike router-based merging.
identity_at_init: Not applicable as an adapter. The masks start by reproducing the base merger: \(B=\mathbf 1\) with \(\lambda=0.3\) is Task Arithmetic, the top 16\% of components for CART, and top-\(k\) for TSV-M. Setting all \(B=0\) recovers \(W_0\) (or \(\bar W\) for CART).
key_idea: When merging, the top-\(k\) singular components of a task vector are not always the right ones to keep: large components of one task can raise the other tasks' losses, and the useful rank varies by task and layer. AdaRank instead learns a binary keep/prune mask on every singular component by test-time entropy minimisation, replacing the fixed top-\(k\) rule of SVD-based merging.
results_note: Added to Task Arithmetic on 8-, 14- and 20-task vision merging, AdaRank raises average accuracy by 18.6% (ViT-B/32) and 11.1% (ViT-L/14), outperforming all static merging baselines.
categorical_reading: AdaRank enlarges task arithmetic's coefficient line to a union of lines indexed by subsets of singular triplets: top-\(k\) truncation (SVD merging, TSV-M) and full task arithmetic are two of its points, and test-time entropy picks another. It is a spectral-coordinate analogue of DARE and TIES, with a learned mask instead of a random or magnitude-based one.

name: SLAO (Merge before Forget)
full_name: SLAO: Single LoRA continual learning with Orthogonal initialization via continual merging
paper_title: Merge before Forget: A Single LoRA Continual Learning via Continual Merging
formula_latex: h=\big(W_0+B^{t}_{\text{merge}}A^{t}_{\text{merge}}\big)x,\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{task }1:\ B^{1}_{\text{merge}}=B_{\text{ft},1},\ A^{1}_{\text{merge}}=A_{\text{ft},1}\ (\text{standard LoRA});\ \ \text{task } i\ge 2:\ Q_iR_i=\mathrm{QR}(A_{\text{ft},i-1}^{\top}),\ Q_i\leftarrow Q_i\,\mathrm{sign}(\mathrm{diag}R_i),\ \ A^{(0)}_{\text{ft},i}=Q_i^{\top}\ (A^{(0)}A^{(0)\top}=I_r),\ \ B^{(0)}_{\text{ft},i}=B_{\text{ft},i-1};\ \ (B_{\text{ft},i},A_{\text{ft},i})=\text{fine-tune on }\mathcal D_i;\ \ A^{i}_{\text{merge}}=A_{\text{ft},i},\ \ B^{i}_{\text{merge}}=B^{i-1}_{\text{merge}}+\lambda(i)\big(B_{\text{ft},i}-B^{i-1}_{\text{merge}}\big),\ \ \lambda(i)=1/\sqrt{i};\ \ \text{frozen: } W_0;\ \text{trained per task: one LoRA pair } (B_{\text{ft},i},A_{\text{ft},i})
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix, independent of the number of tasks } T\ (\text{storage: the merged LoRA plus the current fine-tuned LoRA, } 2r(d_{in}+d_{out}))
locus: LoRA on the query and value projections of every attention layer (Appendix B), fixed rank 8: Llama-2-7B/13B-chat, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B/7B; a rank ablation over 4, 8 and 16 on Llama-2-13B-chat finds 8 best on the standard CL benchmark and 4 best on the large-number-of-tasks benchmark
structure: A constant-memory recursion on one LoRA pair over a task stream, in three steps. (1) \(A\) is rebased: \(A^{(0)}_{\text{ft},i}=Q_i^{\top}=R_i^{-\top}A_{\text{ft},i-1}\) with \(\mathrm{diag}R_i>0\). This moves the previous task's \(A\) inside its own row space to the representative with orthonormal rows. (2) \(B\) is warm-started from the previous fine-tuned \(B\) without the compensating factor \(R_i^{\top}\). The starting product \(B_{\text{ft},i-1}R_i^{-\top}A_{\text{ft},i-1}\) therefore differs from the previous adapter unless \(R_i=I_r\). (3) After training, \(A\) is overwritten (\(A^{i}_{\text{merge}}=A_{\text{ft},i}\)) and only \(B\) is averaged, with weight \(1/\sqrt i\) taken from the OPCM continual-merging schedule. The deployed update is \(B^{t}_{\text{merge}}A_{\text{ft},t}=\sum_{i}c^{(t)}_{i}B_{\text{ft},i}A_{\text{ft},t}\) with \(c^{(t)}_{i}=\lambda(i)\prod_{j=i+1}^{t}(1-\lambda(j))\), so every past \(B\) is paired with the latest \(A\). This is only approximately coherent: each \(A^{(0)}_{\text{ft},i}\) spans the row space of \(A_{\text{ft},i-1}\), and training moves it by the small drift bounded below. The paper's Theorem 1, a Flora-style small-step analysis with \(A^{(0)}A^{(0)\top}=I_r\), writes \(A^s=A^{(0)}+\eta A^{(0)}f_A(s)\) with \(\|f_A(s)\|_2\le\eta L^2/(1-\eta^2L^2)\), so \(A\) drifts by at most \(\eta^2L^2/(1-\eta^2L^2)\), i.e. \(O(\eta^2L^2)\), while \(\Delta B_i\approx-\eta\big(\sum_s\nabla_W\mathcal L_i^{s}\big)A^{(0)\top}_i\) accumulates each task's gradient in the current \(A\) basis. An NTK-regime forgetting/intransigence bound in \(\|B_tA_t-B_iA_i\|_F\) motivates keeping \(\|A_t-A_i\|_F\) small and merging \(B\) rather than \(A\).
mergeable_reason: After any task, the deployed object is one LoRA \(B^{t}_{\text{merge}}A^{t}_{\text{merge}}\) that can be folded into \(W_0\), or kept as a side adapter while the stream continues. There are no per-task modules and no router.
identity_at_init: Only for the first task (standard \(B=0\), Gaussian \(A\)). Later tasks start training from \(B_{\text{ft},i-1}R_i^{-\top}A_{\text{ft},i-1}\ne 0\), and the merged LoRA is never zero after task 1.
key_idea: Continual learning becomes sequential merging inside one LoRA. Each new task starts from an orthonormal-row rebasing of the previous \(A\) together with the previous \(B\). After training, \(A\) is replaced and \(B\) is averaged with weight \(1/\sqrt i\), exploiting the asymmetry that \(B\) carries task-specific, near-orthogonal updates. Memory stays at one LoRA however many tasks arrive.
results_note: On the standard CL, large-number-of-tasks and SuperNI benchmarks with Llama-2-7B-chat, the paper reports that SLAO outperforms all data-free baselines, including O-LoRA, InfLoRA, CorDA, MagMax, KnOTS, LoRA-LEGO and OPCM; its own discussion notes that MagMax is comparable on the standard CL benchmark. SAPT-LoRA, which replays generated pseudo-samples, is not data-free and is excluded from that claim.
categorical_reading: SLAO is continual merging carried out inside one LoRA: the stream is a schedule of re-pointings within a fixed cone, each a non-gauge move (QR rebasing of \(A\), warm start of \(B\)) followed by a factor-level average of \(B\). It works to the extent that every \(A\) descends from one row space, which is the shared-factor condition under which factor-wise merging is exact (Prop V.4(b)). Memory stays constant because the rank never grows.

name: RAIN-Merging
full_name: RAIN-Merging: Reasoning-Aware Instruction-attention guided Null-space projection Merging
paper_title: RAIN-Merging: A Gradient-Free Method to Enhance Instruction Following in Large Reasoning Models with Preserved Thinking Format
formula_latex: \Delta_I^{k}=W_I^{k}-W_B^{k}\ (\text{instruction-model task vector of module } k\in\{Q,K,V,O,\text{FFN}\}\text{ in every layer});\ \ H_k=[h^{k}_t]_{t\in\Omega_{\text{think}}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times|\Omega|}\ (\text{inputs of module } k \text{ in the reasoning model at the thinking-marker positions, 150-sample reasoning calibration set});\ \ \Delta_I^{\perp,k}=\Delta_I^{k}\big(I-H_k(H_k^{\top}H_k)^{+}H_k^{\top}\big)\ \Rightarrow\ \Delta_I^{\perp,k}h^{k}_t=0\ \ \forall t\in\Omega_{\text{think}};\ \ g^{\tilde k}=\mathbb{E}_x\big[a^{\tilde k}-\rho\,u^{\tilde k}\big],\ \tilde H^{\tilde k}=1+\mathbb{E}_x[u^{\tilde k}],\ \alpha^{\tilde k}_\star=\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}\big(g^{\tilde k}/\tilde H^{\tilde k}\big)\ \ (a,u:\ \text{mean attention from instruction-constrained / unconstrained response tokens to instruction tokens, 365 IFEval-style samples});\ \ \theta_\star=\theta_R+\lambda\bigoplus_{k}\alpha^{k}_\star\,\Delta_I^{\perp,k};\ \ \text{frozen: } \theta_R,\theta_I,\theta_B;\ \text{nothing is gradient-trained}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{gradient-trained; computed in closed form: one coefficient } \alpha^{\tilde k} \text{ per attention head (FFN modules use the layer mean) and one global } \lambda\ (\text{grid search over } [0,1.5])
locus: Q, K, V, O and FFN weight matrices of an R1-style reasoning model: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B/14B/32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B. The instruction task vector \(\theta_I-\theta_B\) comes from Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B/14B/32B-Instruct or Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and their bases. For 1.5B and 7B the reasoning model was distilled from Qwen2.5-Math, so it does not share the instruction model's base.
structure: A two-stage, data-dependent but gradient-free transformation of a full task vector before it is added to a different model, the reasoning model \(\theta_R\), rather than to the base \(\theta_B\) it was computed from (for the 1.5B and 7B pairs \(\theta_R\) is not even fine-tuned from \(\theta_B\): it descends from Qwen2.5-Math). Stage 1 right-multiplies each module's task matrix by the orthogonal projector onto the complement of the span of that module's inputs at the thinking special tokens. This is the matrix form of the paper's vectorised Eq. (4), since \(\Phi=H^{\top}\otimes I\). The merged module then reproduces the reasoning model's outputs exactly on those inputs. Proposition 1 bounds the logit change at the marker tokens by \(C_1\|\Phi\,\mathrm{vec}(\Delta)\|_2+C_2\|\Delta\|_2^2\), so after projection only the second-order term remains; the paper states the resulting KL bound as \(O(\|\Delta\|_2^2)\), although its own inequalities give \(O(\|\Delta\|_2^4)\). Algorithm 1 uses the ridge version \(I-\Phi^{\top}(\Phi\Phi^{\top}+I)^{-1}\Phi\), which in matrix form is \(\Delta\mapsto\Delta(I+HH^{\top})^{-1}\). The released code (nullspace_merge_qkvo_ffn.py) uses a ridge of \(10^{-4}\) solved by conjugate gradient, on positions within 5 tokens after <think> and before </think>. It also relaxes the constraint set: Q and K are constrained through linearised attention logits between each marker and its neighbours, and V, O and the three FFN matrices through projections of the output change onto two random unit readout directions per position. The full \(\Delta h=0\) is not imposed. Stage 2 builds a diagonal quadratic model of an attention proxy (alignment minus \(\rho=10\) times leakage), with coefficients \(g\) and \(\tilde H\) measured at \(\alpha=\mathbf 1\). After dropping the \(\alpha_{(0)}\) offset, its maximiser is \(\mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}(g/\tilde H)\), not the Newton step \(\mathbf 1+g/\tilde H\). This gives per-head scalings. The result is a block-wise rescaling of a projected task vector: the same algebraic class as task arithmetic with per-module coefficients.
mergeable_reason: The output is one static weight set \(\theta_\star\) with the reasoning model's architecture. Projectors and calibration statistics are used only offline.
identity_at_init: Not an adapter. With \(\lambda=0\) (or all \(\alpha=0\)) the result is the reasoning model \(\theta_R\). Stage 2 expands around \(\alpha=\mathbf 1\), the plain projected merge.
key_idea: The goal is to add instruction following to a reasoning model by task arithmetic without breaking its <think>...</think> format. The instruction task vector is first projected onto the null space of the reasoning model's module inputs at the thinking-marker tokens, so those positions compute exactly as before. It is then rescaled per attention head by a closed-form score that rewards attention from instruction-constrained output tokens to the instruction span and penalises leakage.
results_note: Merging Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct into DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, RAIN-Merging outperforms all merging baselines (Task Arithmetic, SLERP, Karcher, TIES, DARE, ACM, LEWIS, AIM) and SFT on the same calibration data on instruction-following, mathematical-reasoning and general-capability benchmarks, while trailing the instruction model slightly on instruction following.
categorical_reading: RAIN-Merging is task arithmetic across bases with a null-space constraint: Stage 1 makes the added vector vanish on the thinking-marker activations, so the merged modules compute exactly as \(\theta_R\) there, and Stage 2 is a closed-form per-head reweighting. The family is still a line through \(\theta_R\) along one projected, block-rescaled vector, so the content is in the choice of vector, not in the family.

name: SmartFed (MoRE + EEQA)
full_name: SmartFed: Mixture of Rank-Wise Experts (MoRE) with Elastic Expert Quota Allocation (EEQA) for reusing existing LoRAs in federated fine-tuning
paper_title: Elastic Mixture of Rank-Wise Experts for Knowledge Reuse in Federated Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: \{(B_n,A_n)\}_{n=1}^{N}\ \text{retrieved pre-trained LoRAs (frozen)},\ \ E_m(x)=b_m a_m^{\top}x,\ \ b_m=(B_n)_{:,i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ a_m^{\top}=(A_n)_{i,:}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times d_{in}},\ \ m=1,\dots,M,\ M=\sum_n r_n;\ \ g=\mathrm{softmax}(W_{\text{router}}x),\ W_{\text{router}}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times d_{in}};\ \ \tilde g=g\odot\mathbf m,\ \mathbf m=\mathrm{TopK}_{q_j}(g)\in\{0,1\}^{M};\ \ h=W_0x+\sum_{m=1}^{M}\tilde g_m\,b_m a_m^{\top}x;\ \ s_{E_m}=1-\cos(x,E_m(x)),\ S^{\text{Sum}}_j=\sum_m\tilde g_m s_{E_m},\ \alpha_j=\mathrm{softmax}_j(S^{\text{Sum}}_j),\ q_j=\mathrm{EEQA}\big(\alpha;\ \textstyle\sum_j q_j=KJ,\ q_j\le M\big);\ \ \text{frozen: } W_0 \text{ and every LoRA expert};\ \text{trained (federated, FedAvg): the routers } W_{\text{router}}

locus: Query and value projections of every attention layer, where the reused LoRAs sit, in LLaMA2-7B/13B and Qwen2-7B; one router per adapted matrix
structure: A library of frozen LoRAs is split into a pool of rank-one experts \(\{b_ma_m^{\top}\}_{m=1}^{M}\) per matrix and recombined per token by a softmax router with top-\(q_j\) sparsification: \(\Delta W(x)=\sum_m\tilde g_m(x)\,b_ma_m^{\top}=\widehat B\,\mathrm{diag}(\tilde g(x))\,\widehat A\), with \(\widehat B=[B_1|\cdots|B_N]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times M}\) and \(\widehat A=[A_1;\cdots;A_N]\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times d_{in}}\). This is an input-dependent diagonal core in the concatenated LoRA basis. It avoids the cross terms \(B_1A_2,\ B_2A_1\) that factor averaging creates (the paper's Eq. 5), and it is finer than MoLE's one gate per LoRA. The kept gates are not renormalised after top-\(K\) masking. EEQA redistributes a fixed total budget \(KJ\) of active experts over the \(J\) adapted matrices, in proportion to softmax-normalised importance (gate-weighted cosine deviation between a matrix's input and its experts' outputs), capped at \(M\) per matrix and topped up greedily. Only router weights and importance scores travel between devices and server.
mergeable_reason: The gates \(\tilde g(x)\) depend on each token through a softmax and a top-\(K\) mask, so \(\Delta W(x)\) changes per token and cannot be folded into \(W_0\). The full expert pool must be kept. Fixing the gates to constants \(c\) would give a static merge \(\widehat B\,\mathrm{diag}(c)\,\widehat A\), but that is not what is trained.
identity_at_init: No. The experts are pre-trained nonzero LoRAs, so at initialisation the model already applies a gated mixture of their rank-one components; it is not the bare base model.
key_idea: Instead of training LoRA from scratch on each device, SmartFed reuses existing task LoRAs. Each LoRA is split into its rank-one components, and a federated-trained router sparsely mixes them per token. A budget allocator gives more active experts to the matrices whose experts change representations most.
results_note: Across three skill-composition tasks on LLaMA2-7B/13B and Qwen2-7B, SmartFed reports up to 10.21% higher average performance, 3.95x faster convergence, 31.47x lower communication cost and 3.61x lower energy use than existing federated and LoRA-reuse methods.
categorical_reading: MoRE is MoLE moved down from whole LoRAs to their rank-one atoms: per token it is a point of LoRA\(_M\) with frozen concatenated factors and a routed diagonal core, which avoids the cross terms of factor averaging. Splitting a LoRA into atoms is not a function of its product \(BA\), so the expert pool, and hence the method, depends on the representative in which each library LoRA was stored.

name: RotMoLE

paper_title: RotMoLE: Enhancing Mixture of Low-Rank Experts through Rotational Gating Mechanism

structure: Per-token mixture of \(n\) LoRA experts in which the router returns, for each selected expert, a scale \(g_i(x)\) and a rotation \(R_i(x)\in SO(r)\) that acts in that expert's rank space, between \(A_i\) and \(B_i\). For \(r>2\) the rotation is a single planar (Givens-type) rotation by \(\theta_i(x)\) in \(\mathrm{span}(A_ix,q_i)\). It turns the code \(A_ix\) towards or away from a learned per-expert centre \(q_i\) and preserves \(\|A_ix\|\). The printed \(R_i=[e_1\,e_2]\,\mathrm{Rot}(\theta_i)\,[e_1\,e_2]^{\top}\) is a rank-2 matrix. Because \(A_ix\) lies in that plane, it acts on \(A_ix\) exactly like the full rotation \(I_r+(\cos\theta_i-1)(e_1e_1^{\top}+e_2e_2^{\top})+\sin\theta_i(e_2e_1^{\top}-e_1e_2^{\top})\). Gauge reading (derived here): a constant \(R\) placed between \(B\) and \(A\) would be absorbed by the LoRA gauge, \((B,A)\mapsto(BR,A)\), and add nothing. RotMoLE's \(R_i\) depends on \(x\), both through \(\theta_i(x)\) and through the plane, which contains \(A_ix\). The expert map \(x\mapsto B_iR_i(x)A_ix\) is therefore a nonlinear, norm-preserving reshaping of each expert's code, and it enlarges the function class. The construction uses the Euclidean norm and Gram-Schmidt in rank space. Each expert is therefore invariant under \((B_i,A_i,q_i)\mapsto(cB_iO,\,c^{-1}O^{\top}A_i,\,O^{\top}q_i)\) for \(O\in O(r)\) and \(c>0\), with \(R_i\mapsto O^{\top}R_iO\) (the unit vector \(e_1\) does not see the scale \(c\)), but not under a general \(G\in GL(r)\): the residual gauge group of each expert shrinks from \(GL(r)\) to the similarity group \(\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times O(r)\). For \(r=2\) the fixed-basis rotation commutes with \(\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times SO(2)\); a reflection additionally needs \(W_\theta\mapsto-W_\theta\). Top-\(k\) selection uses only \(g\). The paper does not treat the degenerate case \(q_i\parallel A_ix\).
mergeable_reason: The scales \(g_i(x)\), the angles \(\theta_i(x)\) and the plane \(\mathrm{span}(A_ix,q_i)\) all depend on the token. \(\sum_i g_iB_iR_i(x)A_i\) is therefore not a fixed matrix and cannot be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Yes. \(B_i=0\) (the LoRA convention, stated in Appendix B) gives \(\Delta W x=0\). \(W_\theta=0\) gives \(\theta_i=0\), so \(R_iA_ix=A_ix\) and the model starts as a conventional MoE-LoRA. The centres \(q_i\) are Kaiming-uniform initialised.
key_idea: A scalar gate can only rescale an expert's output along a fixed direction. LoRA experts have an \(r\)-dimensional bottleneck, so an input-dependent rotation of the code \(A_ix\) costs only \(n\,d_{in}+n\,r\) extra parameters. Each selected expert can then also be turned, which lets a few shared experts serve several tasks differently.
results_note: On a jointly trained CSQA/OBQA/SIQA mixture with Qwen-2.5-3B (\(r=6\), \(n=4\), \(k=2\)), RotMoLE averages 45.82% accuracy, against 41.42 for AdaMoLE, 35.66 for MoLA and 34.57 for MoCLE; AdaMoLE is better on CSQA (49.39 vs 43.00). Against the plain MoE-LoRA baseline on the QA mixture, RotMoLE has the higher average in all 8 configurations and the higher accuracy on every task in 7 of them (the exception is OBQA with Llama-3.2-3B, \(r=3\), \(n=4\), \(k=2\)). On the SST-2/MRPC/QNLI mixture the gains are small (75.87 to 76.03 and 73.19 to 73.42 average).
categorical_reading: RotMoLE gives each routed LoRA expert an input-dependent rotation inside its rank space. A constant rotation there would be absorbed by LoRA's \(GL_r\) gauge and add nothing; a token-dependent one cannot be absorbed, and because it uses the Euclidean structure of the code space it cuts the residual gauge down to the similarity group.

structure: Rebasing inside a single LoRA run. Before each step the current product is re-split as \(W_t=\tilde W_0^{(t)}+\tilde B_t\tilde A_t\) with column- and row-scaled factors. The difference \(B_t\,\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf 1-\alpha_t\circ\beta_t)\,A_t\) is merged into the frozen weight. The summed increments therefore no longer telescope to \(B_TA_T\), and \(W_T-W_0\) can reach high rank: average rank 54 at \(r=4\) on RTE, and 1,347 to 3,703 singular values above 0.005 at \(r=8\) on LLaMA2-7B across the eight commonsense tasks (ScaLoRA-I falls to 20 on ARC-e and ARC-c). Gauge reading (derived here): where \(\alpha\circ\beta>0\), write \(\alpha=c\circ s\) and \(\beta=c^{-1}\circ s\) elementwise. The move is then a diagonal (maximal-torus) gauge transformation \((B,A)\mapsto(B\,\mathrm{diag}(c),\mathrm{diag}(c)^{-1}A)\), which leaves \(W\) fixed but changes the next step because LoRA's gradient descent is not gauge-invariant. It is followed by a per-direction rescaling \(\mathrm{diag}(s^{\circ2})\) of the adapter, whose complement is merged. Only diagonal scalings are used, because they are the transformations under which Adam's moment estimates transform in closed form (Lemmas 3.3 and 3.6); a full-matrix or row-wise transform is intractable. The unrestricted optimum of the same surrogate (Theorem 3.2) takes \(\tilde B\) and \(\tilde A^{\top}\) from \(2r\) top singular vectors of \(G_t\), split into two sets of \(r\), each up to an \(O(r)\) factor. LoRA-GA's initialisation is the \(t=0\), identity-rotation case. In the paper's printed Theorem 3.7, the second block matrix lists \(\mathbf B_t\) before \(\mathbf A_t^{\top}\nabla\ell\) and needs a transpose. The pairing given in formula_latex, \(S_{in}=[G^{\top}B,\ A^{\top}]\), is the one consistent with the stated \(\lambda\) and objective (re-derived here). The paper's 'fixed subspace' remark is the telescoping identity \(\sum_t\Delta W_t=B_TA_T\), i.e. a rank-\(r\) bound on vanilla LoRA's cumulative update.
mergeable_reason: The adapter is merged into the base at every re-split, and the final model is the dense \(W_T\). Because \(W_0^{(t)}\) itself changes, \(W_T-W_0\) is high-rank and cannot be shipped as a rank-\(r\) adapter. The paper states this as a limitation: ScaLoRA stores the entire merged matrix.
identity_at_init: Yes. Standard LoRA initialisation has one zero factor; the paper puts the Gaussian on the \(d_{out}\times r\) factor and zeros on the \(d_{in}\) side. This gives \(W_0^{(0)}+B_0A_0=W_0\), and every later re-split preserves \(W_t\) exactly.
key_idea: Vanilla LoRA's increments telescope, \(\sum_t\Delta W_t=B_TA_T\), so the cumulative update never exceeds rank \(r\). ScaLoRA merges and re-factors at every step and rescales Adam's moments to match, so it accumulates a high-rank update with no restarts. The column scaling of the current factors is chosen in closed form to minimise a smoothness upper bound on the next loss, which is the same as best matching the full fine-tuning step \(-G_t/L\).
results_note: With \(r=8\), ScaLoRA-I averages 74.75 on eight commonsense tasks with LLaMA2-7B and ScaLoRA averages 77.85 with LLaMA3-8B. Both are above LoRA (73.63/76.83), ReLoRA, LoRA-GA, MoRA and HiRA, and above rank-32 LoRA (74.52/77.54). On GLUE with DeBERTaV3-base (\(r=4\)) ScaLoRA averages 88.98 against 88.13 for LoRA. On LLaMA3-8B it needs about 0.01 GB more memory than LoRA (MoRA 1.08 GB, HiRA 7.83 GB), but ScaLoRA, like MoRA and HiRA, takes 50% or more extra fine-tuning time; ScaLoRA-I is close to LoRA.
categorical_reading: ScaLoRA is ReLoRA without restarts: every step is a merge-and-restart, but the restart lands at a rescaled copy of the current factors, a split smooth point, instead of the apex, and the optimizer state is transported instead of reset. Its one degree of freedom per re-split is a diagonal rescaling, the largest family under which Adam's moments transform in closed form, chosen to best match a full fine-tuning step.

locus: LoRA-adapted weights of transformer-based models. The poster reports Mix-of-Show image generation with LoRA ranks \(r=4,8,16\) and GPT-2 medium on E2E NLG (\(r=4\)); the poster does not name the base diffusion model.
structure: Optimizer for plain LoRA factors, built on the quotient \((\mathbb R_*^{d_{out}\times r}\times\mathbb R_*^{r\times d_{in}})/GL(r)\cong\mathcal M_r\). The base optimizer (Adam or RACS) preconditions the full-matrix gradient in matrix space. An \(r\times r\) Sylvester equation and a horizontal lift then map the resulting direction \(\dot X\) to factor updates. Derived here from the poster's formulas: \(\dot BA+B\dot A=P_B\dot X+\dot XP_A-P_B\dot XP_A\), with \(P_B=B(B^{\top}B)^{-1}B^{\top}\) and \(P_A=A^{\top}(AA^{\top})^{-1}A\). So the first-order change of \(W\) is the orthogonal projection of \(\dot X\) onto the tangent space \(T_{BA}\mathcal M_r\). The Sylvester matrix \(K\) is exactly what removes the double-counted term \(P_B\dot XP_A\), which the \(K=0\) lift contains; that lift is scaled GD, i.e. Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA. Setting \(K=\epsilon I\) instead turns the \(K\) terms into \(-\epsilon B\) and \(-\epsilon A\), i.e. decoupled weight decay on both factors. This is the paper's reading of weight decay as a crude approximation of \(K\), and the reason it removes the decay hyperparameter. The update is equivariant under \((B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A)\), with \(K\mapsto R^{\top}KR^{-\top}\), so the induced \(W\) update depends only on \(BA\). This is the poster's Theorem 1: transformation invariance plus the paper's 'efficient feature learning' condition. Each step costs \(\Omega(d_{out}d_{in}r)+O(r^{3}+(d_{out}+d_{in})r^{2})\).
mergeable_reason: Only the optimizer changes. The trained adapter is a standard \(BA\) that folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not specified in the material available. The lift needs \((AA^{\top})^{-1}\) and \((B^{\top}B)^{-1}\), i.e. full-rank factors in \(\mathbb R_*\), so LoRA's usual \(B=0\) start lies outside its domain. The paper presumably uses a nonzero or damped start, which the poster does not show.
key_idea: Precondition in matrix space, then lift. Any matrix-space optimizer becomes a gauge-invariant LoRA optimizer once its direction is lifted to the factors through the quotient geometry, with an \(r\times r\) Sylvester solve fixing the correction term. The \(\epsilon I\) weight-decay term of factor optimizers is reinterpreted as a crude approximation of that Sylvester matrix and dropped.
results_note: According to the official ICLR poster, with rank-4 LoRA on GPT-2 medium (E2E NLG) LRACS reaches BLEU 70.4, against 69.3 for LoRA-RITE and 68.6 for AdamW. On Mix-of-Show image customisation, AdamS at rank 16 reaches CLIP 32.64 / FID 46.32, against 31.90 / 55.68 for LoRA-RITE.
categorical_reading: LoRA-S is LoRA with a descending optimizer: any matrix-space preconditioner, followed by the orthogonal projection onto the fixed-rank tangent space and a horizontal lift. A zero Sylvester matrix gives scaled GD (Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA) and \(K=\epsilon I\) gives decoupled weight decay on both factors; as an object it is LoRA.

full_name: DiaBlo: fine-tuning only the diagonal blocks of weight matrices
paper_title: DiaBlo: Diagonal Blocks Are Sufficient For Finetuning

Table 4's 70M trainable parameters for Llama2-7B at \(N=64\) match q, k, v, up and down rather than all seven projections, so the paper is internally inconsistent about the quantized runs' modules
structure: A fixed block-diagonal sparsity pattern on \(\Delta W\): \(N\) independent dense blocks on the diagonal. Block \(i\) maps the \(i\)-th slice of \(d_{in}/N\) input coordinates to the \(i\)-th slice of \(d_{out}/N\) output coordinates, so \(\mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\) can reach \(\min(d_{in},d_{out})\) with \(d_{in}d_{out}/N\) parameters. The update set is a linear subspace, not a product manifold. There is therefore no \(GL(r)\) gauge, the loss restricted to it is the original loss (convex in \(D\) whenever it is convex in \(W\)), and Adam on \(D\) is Adam on the masked entries of \(W\). With decoupled weight decay (the quantized runs use decay 1.0) AdamW shrinks \(D\), i.e. pulls \(W_{ii}\) towards \(W_{0,ii}\) rather than towards 0. The block structure is tied to the coordinate basis of the hidden units: it is not invariant to permuting or rotating them. Relative to neighbouring shapes, factoring each block at rank \(r/N\) gives MELoRA, a full \(N\times N\) grid of low-rank blocks gives GraLoRA, and choosing the blocks by gradient magnitude gives SMT. Linear least squares (Theorem 1): if the inputs \(X\) are generic of rank \(r\) and \(N\le d_{in}/r\), every DiaBlo minimiser is a full fine-tuning minimiser. This uses \(d_{in}d_{out}/N\ge d_{out}r\) parameters, against LoRA's \((d_{in}+d_{out})r\). Nonlinear case (Theorem 2): if \(X\) and \(g_Y\) are generic of ranks \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) and \(N\ge\lceil r_1N/d_{in}\rceil\lceil r_2N/d_{out}\rceil\), DiaBlo's stationary points are stationary for full fine-tuning. Sizes that \(N\) does not divide use blocks of \(\lceil d/N\rceil\) with zero padding.
mergeable_reason: \(D\) is a \(d_{out}\times d_{in}\) block-diagonal matrix added to \(W_0\). It can be folded in, or stored compactly as an \(N\times\frac{d_{out}}{N}\times\frac{d_{in}}{N}\) tensor. On a quantized base (the GPTQ-DiaBlo and MagR-DiaBlo runs), merging needs re-quantization.
identity_at_init: Yes. \(D=0\), and since there is no product the gradient \(\nabla_{D_i}\mathcal L=(\nabla_W\mathcal L)_{ii}\) is nonzero from the first step. There is no LoRA-style zero-factor stall and no special initialisation.
key_idea: Update a structured subset of the weights directly instead of a low-rank product. Training only the diagonal blocks keeps LoRA-like memory and speed, since the forward pass is one batched matmul. It removes the bilinear factorisation's sensitivity to initialisation and optimizer. Under low-rank activations and gradients it provably reaches full fine-tuning minimisers in the linear case, and full fine-tuning stationary points in general.
results_note: On commonsense reasoning DiaBlo reaches an 87.3 average with Llama3-8B (\(N=64\)), against 85.2 for DoRA \(r=32\) and 80.8 for LoRA \(r=32\). The paper lists this run as 1.04% of parameters, but q, k, v, up and down blocks at \(N=64\) come to about 0.89% of Llama3-8B by our count. On MetaMathQA with Llama2-7B (\(N=32\), 2.09%) it averages 43.4 on GSM8K/MATH, against 43.2 for full fine-tuning. Training speed matches LoRA \(r=32\): 170 minutes per epoch on Commonsense-170k, against 480 for DoRA.
categorical_reading: DiaBlo is a fixed-mask selective method whose mask is block-diagonal: the linear shape between MELoRA (each block factored at rank \(r/N\)) and full fine-tuning. Linearity is the point: it has no gauge and no apex, so the zero-factor stall and initialisation sensitivity of bilinear adapters do not arise, at the price of an imposed coordinate partition.

structure: PEQA-type parametrisation trained with MeZO-style SPSA. The parametrisation is a group-wise multiplicative rescaling of frozen integer codes, \(\hat W=(S\otimes\mathbf 1_{1\times g})\odot\overline W\); per channel it is the left diagonal action \(\hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\overline W\). The gradient estimate is a rank-one random projection \(zz^{\top}\nabla_S\mathcal L\) of the scale gradient, computed from two forward passes of the quantized model. Weights are never de-quantized or re-quantized, and activations are not stored. Directional-derivative clipping caps the scalar \(d\) at \(C\) (100 in the paper), and the projection \(\max(\cdot,0)\) keeps the scales non-negative. Every code stays fixed, so the reachable set is \(\{(S\otimes\mathbf 1)\odot\overline W\}\), of dimension \(d_{out}d_{in}/g\). The paper's Theorem 1 states that the clipped estimate is unbiased. Its proof (Appendix A) passes from the clipped to the unclipped sum with only the remark that the two agree as \(\epsilon\to0\), which ignores that the clipping event depends on \(z\). In general a clipped SPSA estimate is biased. In the idealised case of a fixed batch, \(\epsilon\to0\) and Gaussian \(z\), \(\mathbb E[\mathrm{clip}(d)\,z]=c\,\nabla_S\mathcal L\) with \(c\in(0,1]\), a shrinkage along the true gradient (derived here). The second-moment bound \(\mathbb E\|d'z\|^{2}\le\mathbb E\|dz\|^{2}\) holds unconditionally. The paper's per-coordinate variance inequality is derived through Theorem 1 and is therefore not established in general.
mergeable_reason: The trained parameters are the quantization scales themselves. The result is an ordinary GPTQ or AQLM model with the same codes and inference kernels.
identity_at_init: No adapter is added. Training starts from the post-training-quantized model, whose GPTQ/AQLM scales approximate but do not equal \(W_0\).
key_idea: Zeroth-order training removes gradients and optimizer states, and quantization shrinks the weights. The two meet in the continuous quantization scales, which SPSA can perturb and update while the discrete codes stay fixed. Clipping the directional derivative keeps the noisy estimate stable.
results_note: On 4-bit GPTQ Llama-2-7B, QZO needs 5.0 GB, against 14.8 GB for 16-bit MeZO and 26.0 GB for 16-bit SGD fine-tuning, and beats MeZO on four of five tasks (for example SST-2 90.0 vs 83.5). On OPT-6.7B it trails MeZO on most tasks.
categorical_reading: QZO is PEQA's object, with EfficientQAT's group-wise scales, trained by MeZO's estimator: the continuous part of a quantised model is exactly the part a zeroth-order method can perturb without leaving the grid. The clipping belongs to the trained-method data; it biases the estimate towards a shrinkage along the gradient rather than leaving it unbiased.

The first block also uses randomly initialised static prompts. The paper describes no zero-output mechanism.
