What changes is how the rank-1 terms are trained. Component \(k\) is fitted to a deflation target that removes only its predecessors, \(k'<k\), using their latest estimates. All components are refined in parallel, and each worker's target is refreshed every round. Sequential (Hotelling-style) deflation, of which the paper counts ReLoRA as an instance, freezes earlier errors into every later residual. Here the mismatch \(\|Y_{k,\ell}-Y_k^{\star}\|_F\) vanishes as rounds proceed (self-correction, Proposition 2). Activation is staggered (worker \(k\) starts at round \(k\)), and before activation a component is trained privately against its current target (advance learning). key_idea: Treat a LoRA update as a sum of rank-1 deflation steps, but train all steps at once, each against a target rebuilt from its predecessors' current estimates. Errors in early components are then corrected over rounds instead of being frozen into later residuals. In the single-layer bilinear model, individual rank-1 directions converge nearly linearly (exponential decay with a linear prefactor). On top of this, ranks grow per module under a global budget, so the rank allocation is an output.

The bound reduces to the quadratic \(\mathrm{tr}(A\Omega A^{\top})\), whose Initialization Guidance Matrix \(\Omega\) has two parts. The variance part is the diagonal \(d_{in}\times d_{in}\) blocks of the inverse Fisher of \(\mathrm{vec}(W)\), summed over outputs, divided by \(N\). Under K-FAC this is \(\tfrac{1}{N}\mathrm{tr}(Y_F^{-1})Z_F^{-1}\). The update is therefore a full-matrix step in weight space followed by re-projection onto a rank-\(K_i\) manifold, close to training a low-rank model in factored form. It is not a frozen-\(W_0\) plus \(\Delta W\) method. In the released code the dense weight remains the optimised parameter and \(L,R\) are recomputed from it at each forward pass; the paper's Eq. Two further code-versus-paper details: the code starts from \(L=U_{K_i}\) (orthonormal) and \(R=\Sigma_{K_i}V_{K_i}^{\top}\), the reverse of Eq. categorical_reading: Hybrid-LoRA is a fixed \(\oplus\)-word, full fine-tuning on selected boxes plus LoRA on the others. key_idea: How much of each task survives merging depends on keeping the singular directions of its task vector, not the energy in its singular values. The cover basis contains every task's row and column spaces, so the round trip into it is exact; with task arithmetic inside and no mask the method is just the sum of the smoothed task vectors, and its effect lives in the mask and in rules applied in cover coordinates.

The gate is a causal, stateful function of the prefix: a selective state-space (Mamba/S6) recurrence of width \(r\) over the projected inputs \(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\), read out by a linear head and a softplus. It can therefore both suppress (\(\lambda<1\)) and amplify (\(\lambda>1\)) the update. The TopLoRA baseline instead inserts a stateless per-token diagonal \(\Lambda(x_t)=\mathrm{diag}(\exp(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Px_t)))\). MaLoRA trades the diagonal for a scalar (a stateful diagonal variant gave no consistent gain, Appendix C) and gives the gate memory across tokens. READ and SSMLoRA also use recurrence, but across layers; MaLoRA's runs across tokens. At the token level, GRU and LSTM gates perform about the same as the Mamba gate, so recurrence itself is what matters there. The paper notes that with KV caching the recurrence is restarted at each generated position, so only the prompt is modulated with its full history. MaRA is a separate adapter at the retrieval level, not a weight update. It combines an attention pool over frozen early-layer states, a two-layer Mamba that runs over paragraphs rather than tokens, and linear local and global scoring heads. It selects the top-\(k\) paragraphs (\(k=12\) on MuSiQue, \(k=4\) on 2WikiMultihopQA) over \(N_p=4\) chained passes and is trained on supporting-paragraph labels against the unadapted backbone, separately from MaLoRA.

The modulator must run at inference: one \(d_{in}\to r\) projection plus a width-\(r\), \(d_s=16\) Mamba step per token. Folding is possible only if \(\lambda\) is frozen to a constant \(c\), giving \(W_0+c\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\), and that changes the model.

The paper notes that its Eq. 3 reduces to LoRA when \(\lambda\equiv1\).

MaLoRA rescales that update per token with a gate \(\lambda(x_{1:t})\) produced by a Mamba recurrence over the prefix, so the adapter's strength depends on the whole trajectory up to token \(t\), not only on \(x_t\). The learned gate is mostly suppressive and separates token roles (markers and query versus content), but it does not separate supporting from distractor paragraphs. That limit motivates MaRA, which applies the same state-space idea one level up as a paragraph selector of about 3M parameters.

It is natural under all of \(\mathrm{Aff}(\Theta)\), and unlike task arithmetic it never refers to the base point. As an object it is the point \(\lambda=\mathbf 1_S/|S|\) of task arithmetic's coefficient family, and so it lives in the unpointed slice.

name: Fisher Merging
paper_title: Merging Models with Fisher-Weighted Averaging
formula_latex: W^{\star}_{[p]}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}\,W_{i,[p]}}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}}\ \ (\text{per coordinate }p),\quad F_i=\mathbb{E}_{x}\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x)}\big[(\nabla_{\theta}\log p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x))^{2}\big],\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_i\lambda_i=1;\ \text{models frozen}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one diagonal Fisher estimate per model, same size as the model)}
locus: all shared parameters of models fine-tuned from the same initialization (task heads excluded)
structure: Per-coordinate precision-weighted mean: the maximizer of \(\sum_i\lambda_i\log\mathcal{N}(\theta;\theta_i,F_i^{-1})\) under a diagonal Laplace approximation of each posterior; isotropic averaging is the case \(F_i=I\).
mergeable_reason: The output is one set of weights for the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: View merging as maximizing the joint likelihood of the models' posteriors; using each model's diagonal Fisher information as its posterior precision lets every coordinate be dominated by the model that is most certain about it.
results_note: Fisher merging beats isotropic averaging for robust fine-tuning and model ensembling and is competitive with intermediate-task transfer and domain-adaptive pre-training at much lower cost.
categorical_reading: Fisher merging is the barycentre of the \(\theta_i\) for the diagonal metrics \(F_i\), i.e. the maximiser of a product of diagonal Laplace posteriors. The diagonal approximation fixes a privileged basis, so this is a coordinate (Mon) operation. It sits between plain soups (\(F_i=I\), affine-natural) and full-Fisher merging (\(GL\)-natural).

name: RegMean
paper_title: Dataless Knowledge Fusion by Merging Weights of Language Models
formula_latex: W^{\star}=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}W_i\tilde G_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tilde G_i\Big)^{-1}=\arg\min_{W}\sum_i\|X_iW^{\top}-X_iW_i^{\top}\|_F^2\ (\text{with regularization}),\ G_i=X_i^{\top}X_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}},\ \tilde G_i=\alpha G_i+(1-\alpha)\operatorname{diag}(G_i);\ \text{non-linear-layer weights simply averaged}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(stores one }d_{in}\times d_{in}\text{ Gram matrix per linear layer per model)}
locus: every linear layer (embeddings and biases averaged)
structure: Layer-wise least-squares merge: the merged linear map is the Gram-weighted matrix mean of the individual maps; equals simple averaging when all \(G_i\) are equal, and the off-diagonal shrinkage \(\alpha\) (\(\approx0.9\)) acts as a pull toward the individual weights.
mergeable_reason: Produces one weight matrix per layer of the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free, closed form).
key_idea: Merge each linear layer so that on every model's own training inputs it reproduces that model's outputs as closely as possible; this regression has a closed form that needs only inner-product statistics of the inputs, not the data itself.
results_note: Across GLUE-style merging settings RegMean significantly outperforms Fisher-weighted averaging and model ensembling baselines and can preserve or improve individual-model performance without training data.
categorical_reading: RegMean is a barycentre of the linear maps \(W_i\), weighted by their input Gram matrices: the least-squares map that reproduces every model on its own inputs. It does not use \(\theta_0\), and at \(\alpha=1\) it is \(GL\times GL\)-natural. The off-diagonal shrinkage is what brings back a privileged input basis.

name: Task Arithmetic
paper_title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(weights, combination_type='svd' | 'cat' | 'linear'): 'svd' sums the weighted dense deltas exactly and then truncates them to svd_rank by SVD, 'cat' is exact at rank sum r_i, and 'linear' mixes the A and B factors (an approximation with cross terms); low-level operator peft.utils.merge_utils.task_arithmetic
formula_latex: \tau_i=\theta_i-\theta_0\ \ (\text{per matrix }\Delta W_i=W_i-W_0);\quad \theta_{\mathrm{new}}=\theta_0+\lambda\,\tau_{\mathrm{new}},\ \ \tau_{\mathrm{new}}\in\Big\{\textstyle\sum_i\tau_i\ (\text{addition}),\ -\tau\ (\text{negation}),\ \tau_C+(\tau_B-\tau_A)\ (\text{analogy})\Big\};\ \lambda\text{ tuned on held-out data; no training}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one scalar }\lambda\text{ chosen on validation data)}
locus: all parameters shared between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models
structure: Vector-space operations (sum, negation, analogy) on displacement vectors from the common base point \(\theta_0\); the edited model is \(\theta_0\) plus a linear combination of task vectors.
mergeable_reason: The edited model is a single weight vector of the original architecture; only element-wise operations on weights are used.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free); \(\lambda=0\) recovers the pre-trained model and \(\lambda=1\) with one task vector recovers that fine-tuned model.
key_idea: A fine-tuning run defines a direction in weight space; adding such task vectors builds multi-task models, negating one makes the model forget a task or behaviour, and analogies transfer skills to tasks with little data.
results_note: Adding task vectors from 8 CLIP image-classification tasks gives one model at 91.2% normalized accuracy (98.9% for pairs), and negating a toxicity task vector reduces toxic generations with little loss of fluency.
categorical_reading: Task arithmetic uses the vector-space structure of \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\) post hoc: its coefficient family is the linear method spanned by the task vectors, pointed at \(\lambda=0\). It is the \(GL(\Theta)\)-natural merge. For LoRA inputs it is the gauge-invariant rule, landing in \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{Nr}\) (Prop V.4(a)).

name: TIES-Merging
paper_title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='ties' | 'ties_svd', density=k, majority_sign_method='total' | 'frequency'); 'ties' trims and elects signs on the lora_A and lora_B factors separately, 'ties_svd' on the dense Delta W followed by SVD truncation; also IA3 vectors via merge_utils.ties
formula_latex: \hat\tau_i=\operatorname{TopK}_{k\%}(\tau_i)\ (\text{trim});\quad \gamma^{p}=\operatorname{sgn}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{i}\hat\tau_i^{p}\Big)\ (\text{elect});\quad \tau_m^{p}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}^{p}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}^{p}}\hat\tau_i^{p},\ \mathcal{A}^{p}=\{i:\operatorname{sgn}(\hat\tau_i^{p})=\gamma^{p}\}\ (\text{disjoint merge});\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\,\tau_m
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(hyper-parameters }k\approx20\%,\ \lambda\approx1)
locus: task vectors of full fine-tuning or of PEFT parameters (e.g. (IA)\(^3\) vectors, LoRA factors in HF PEFT)
structure: Coordinate-wise non-linear aggregation: magnitude sparsification, sign election by total mass, and a mean over agreeing non-zero entries only; not a linear combination of task vectors.
mergeable_reason: The merged task vector is added to the base weights once, giving a standard model.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: Merging interference comes from redundant small updates and sign conflicts; trimming small entries, electing one sign per parameter and averaging only agreeing values recovers much of the accuracy lost by plain averaging.
results_note: With validation-tuned hyper-parameters, TIES outperforms averaging, Fisher merging, RegMean and Task Arithmetic across T5, ViT and (IA)\(^3\)-PEFT merges, in-domain and out-of-domain. Without a validation set, the fixed recipe (\(k = 20\%\), \(\lambda = 1\)) is weaker than Task Arithmetic for the T5-base (IA)\(^3\) merge (69.7 vs 73.2).
categorical_reading: TIES applies a coordinatewise, magnitude- and sign-dependent operation to task vectors in \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\), followed by the line method \(\theta_0+\mathbb R\tau_m\). Its naturality group is \(\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_N\): it presupposes the coordinate basis and is not \(O(N)\)-natural. Applied to LoRA factors (HF's non-SVD `ties`), it is also gauge-dependent.

name: DARE
paper_title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
formula_latex: m_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\ \text{elementwise},\quad \hat\tau_i=\frac{(\mathbf{1}-m_i)\odot\tau_i}{1-p};\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\textstyle\sum_i\hat\tau_i\ (\text{DARE+TA})\ \text{or TIES on }\{\hat\tau_i\};\ \text{no training}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(drop rate }p\text{, up to }0.9\text{--}0.99)
locus: delta parameters (fine-tuned minus pre-trained) of homologous SFT models; LoRA factors in HF PEFT
structure: Random sparse coordinate mask with inverted-dropout rescaling \(1/(1-p)\), which preserves the expectation of each delta and of its action on inputs; a pre-processing operator applied before any merge rule.
mergeable_reason: Sparsified deltas are added back to the base weights, giving one ordinary model.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: SFT deltas of language models are extremely redundant: randomly dropping 90-99% of them and rescaling the rest barely changes behaviour, and sparsified deltas of several homologous models interfere less when merged.
results_note: DARE removes 90% or even 99% of delta parameters with little performance loss, and a DARE-merged 7B model ranked first among 7B models on the Open LLM Leaderboard at the time.
categorical_reading: DARE is a random coordinate mask with inverted-dropout rescaling: a pre-processing operator on \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\) that is exactly natural under the torus and natural under permutations in law. It preserves each task vector in expectation, so DARE+TA equals task arithmetic in law, not mask by mask.

name: AdaMerging
paper_title: AdaMerging: Adaptive Model Merging for Multi-Task Learning
formula_latex: \theta_m^{l}=\theta_0^{l}+\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i^{l}\,\tau_i^{l}\ \ (\text{layer-wise; task-wise uses one }\lambda_i\text{ per model});\quad \{\lambda\}=\arg\min_{\lambda}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{unlab}}_{\mathrm{test}}}H\big(f_{\theta_m(\lambda)}(x)\big),\ H=\text{prediction entropy};\ \text{task vectors frozen}
trainable_params: N\ \text{per layer (layer-wise) or }N\text{ in total (task-wise)}
locus: task vectors of all layers (CLIP ViT image encoders in the paper)
structure: Learned layer-wise linear combination of task vectors, fitted by test-time entropy minimization on unlabeled multi-task inputs.
mergeable_reason: After learning the coefficients the merged weights form one ordinary model.
identity_at_init: Coefficients initialized to the task-arithmetic default \(\lambda=0.3\) (not an identity initialization).
key_idea: Merging coefficients matter a lot; they can be learned per task and per layer without labels by minimizing the entropy of the merged model's predictions on unlabeled test inputs.
results_note: Merging eight ViT task models, AdaMerging improves average accuracy by about 11% over Task Arithmetic and generalizes better to unseen tasks and distribution shift.
categorical_reading: AdaMerging trains a \(\oplus\) of \(NL\) frozen line methods \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda\tau_i^l\) by test-time entropy minimisation. For LoRA task vectors this is exactly CAT's coefficient object. The two differ only in loss and starting point.

name: TSV-Merge
full_name: Task Singular Vectors Merge (TSV-M) and Compress (TSV-C)
paper_title: Task Singular Vectors: Reducing Task Interference in Model Merging
formula_latex: \Delta_i=U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}\ (\text{keep top }1/N\text{ components});\ U=[U_1|\cdots|U_N],\ \Sigma=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_N),\ V=[V_1|\cdots|V_N];\ U=P_UD_UQ_U^{\top}\Rightarrow U_\perp=P_UQ_U^{\top}\ (\text{same for }V);\ W=W_0+\alpha\,U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^{\top}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one scaling }\alpha\text{; the paper finds }\alpha=1\text{ best, so no tuning is needed)}
locus: per-layer task matrices of all weight matrices (ViT CLIP encoders in the paper)
structure: Per-layer low-rank truncation of each task matrix, then orthogonalization (whitening, equivalently orthogonal Procrustes) of the concatenated singular-vector bases to remove cross-task overlap measured by the Singular Task Interference \(\|(U^{\top}U-I)\Sigma(V^{\top}V-I)\|_1\).
mergeable_reason: The merged matrix is added once to the pre-trained weights.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: Layer task matrices are low-rank, so each can be kept as its top singular vectors; interference appears as overlap between different tasks' singular vectors and can be removed by orthogonalizing the stacked bases before summation.
results_note: TSV-C compresses task matrices to 10% of their size while retaining 99% of accuracy, and TSV-M significantly outperforms prior merging methods on 8/14/20-task ViT benchmarks.
categorical_reading: TSV-M works in the spectral frames of the task matrices. It truncates each matrix to its top singular triples and replaces the stacked bases by their polar factors, the nearest orthonormal frames. This is a \(CO\times CO\) (spectral) operation, and its output generally leaves the span of the task vectors.

name: KnOTS
paper_title: Model merging with SVD to tie the Knots
formula_latex: \big[\Delta W^{(1)}\ \cdots\ \Delta W^{(N)}\big]=U\Sigma\,\big[V^{(1)};\dots;V^{(N)}\big]^{\top}\ \ (\Delta W^{(i)}=B_iA_i);\quad V^{(m)}=\operatorname{Merge}\big(V^{(1)},\dots,V^{(N)}\big)\ (\text{TA, TIES, DARE},\dots);\quad W=W_0+U\Sigma\,V^{(m)\top}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(data-free, gradient-free)}
locus: LoRA-adapted attention projections (\(q\), \(k\), \(v\), \(o\)) of ViT-B/32, ViT-L/16 and Llama3-8B LoRA models in the paper (rank 16)
structure: Joint SVD of the column-concatenated LoRA updates: a shared orthonormal output basis \(U\Sigma\) (rank \(\le N r\)) and task-specific input-side factors \(V^{(i)}\); any existing merge rule is applied in this aligned coordinate system.
mergeable_reason: The merged update \(U\Sigma V^{(m)\top}\) is a dense matrix added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: LoRA updates of different tasks are much less aligned than full fine-tuning deltas; re-expressing them in a common SVD basis aligns them so that standard merging rules stop destroying each other's information.
results_note: KnOTS improves LoRA merging by up to 4.3% across vision and language benchmarks, including a new joint-task benchmark for general models.
categorical_reading: KnOTS is the joint gauge fixing of Prop V.4(b): a joint SVD of the concatenated updates produces a shared factor \(U\Sigma\), and coordinatewise merge rules then act on the task-specific factors. With task arithmetic as the inner rule it is exactly task arithmetic, since \(U\Sigma\sum_i\lambda_iV^{(i)\top}=\sum_i\lambda_i\Delta W^{(i)}\). Its content lies in the coordinatewise rules it makes well defined.

name: PEM Arithmetic
full_name: Composing parameter-efficient modules with arithmetic operations
paper_title: Composing Parameter-Efficient Modules with Arithmetic Operations
hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='linear'): PEFT scales each factor by sqrt(|w_i| * scaling_i) and puts the sign on lora_A only, so weights w_i = lambda_i^2 reproduce PEM addition and a negative weight reproduces PEM negation; IA3Model.add_weighted_adapter gives (IA)^3 addition, but the affine negation l -> 2 - l is not built in
formula_latex: \theta^{\mathrm{add}}=\lambda\theta^{(1)}\oplus(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}:=\lambda\theta^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}\ \ (\text{component-wise on }(A,B)\text{ or on }l);\quad \ominus\theta_{\mathrm{LoRA}}=\{A,-B\}\ \Rightarrow\ \Delta h=BAx\mapsto-\Delta h;\quad \ominus l_{(IA)^3}=\mathbf{2}-l;\ \text{e.g. domain transfer }\theta^{(1)}\ominus\theta^{(2)}\oplus\theta^{(3)};\ \text{no training}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(weight }\lambda\text{ tuned on validation)}
locus: LoRA factors or (IA)\(^3\) scaling vectors of modules trained from the same base model
structure: Addition is defined on module parameters (for LoRA \((A_1+A_2),(B_1+B_2)\), which creates cross terms \(B_1A_2+B_2A_1\)), whereas negation is defined through the induced hidden-state change \(\Delta h\): negate only \(B\) for LoRA, \(l\mapsto 2-l\) for (IA)\(^3\), because negating both factors leaves \(BA\) unchanged.
mergeable_reason: The composed module is again a LoRA/(IA)\(^3\) module, which can be folded into the base weights.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: PEFT modules trained from one base model can be composed by weight-space arithmetic; the subtle part is negation, which must flip the module's effect on hidden states rather than its raw parameters.
results_note: Arithmetic compositions of LoRA/(IA)\(^3\) modules (RoBERTa-base, T5-base) beat the individual modules for distribution generalization, multi-tasking, unlearning and domain transfer, and LoRA negation detoxifies Alpaca-LoRA.
categorical_reading: PEM arithmetic composes modules in factor space: barycentric addition of factors, plus a negation defined through the induced update. For (IA)\(^3\), whose \(\rho\) is linear and gauge-free, this is exactly task arithmetic on updates. For LoRA the addition is a factor-wise rule with cross terms \(B_1A_2+B_2A_1\), and it depends on the factor representatives.

name: AdapterSoup
full_name: AdapterSoup: weight averaging of domain adapters
paper_title: AdapterSoup: Weight Averaging to Improve Generalization of Pretrained Language Models
formula_latex: \theta_{\mathrm{soup}}=\tfrac{1}{l}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\theta_i,\ |\mathcal{S}|=l\le k;\quad y=f\big(x;\theta_m,\theta_{\mathrm{soup}}\big);\ \mathcal{S}\text{ chosen by sentence-BERT similarity or domain clustering on a little novel-domain text};\ \text{PLM }\theta_m\text{ and all adapters frozen}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{for the novel domain (}k\text{ domain adapters are trained beforehand, each a bottleneck adapter of }\approx2rd\text{ per layer)}
locus: Bapna and Firat (2019)-style bottleneck adapters (bottleneck size 64) in every Transformer layer of GPT-2
structure: Uniform average (a model soup) of a retrieved subset of adapter parameter vectors; one averaged adapter is executed at test time.
mergeable_reason: The soup collapses the selected adapters into one adapter, so inference costs a single adapter. That adapter is a nonlinear bottleneck module and cannot fold into \(W_0\). The same recipe applied to LoRAs (mentioned only as future work) would be foldable.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free combination of trained adapters).
key_idea: For an unseen domain, rather than picking one related-domain adapter, average the weights of several selected domain adapters to obtain ensemble-like gains at the cost of a single adapter.
results_note: On 10 held-out web domains with GPT-2, AdapterSoup with clustering-based selection gives the best average out-of-domain perplexity among single-adapter-cost methods.
categorical_reading: AdapterSoup is the model-soup barycentre applied in the parameter space \(\Theta'\) of an adapter extension, with the backbone fixed at \(\theta_0\). The adapter is non-linear, so averaging parameters is not averaging functions, and the result stays M∞. It reduces inference cost to one adapter but never returns to \(\Theta\).

name: LoraHub
paper_title: LoraHub: Efficient Cross-Task Generalization via Dynamic LoRA Composition
formula_latex: \Delta W=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iB_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iA_i\Big),\ \ w\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\ (\text{signed});\quad w^{\star}=\arg\min_{w}\ \mathcal{L}_{Q}(w)+\alpha\textstyle\sum_i|w_i|\ \text{by gradient-free CMA-ES (Nevergrad Shiwa)};\ W=W_0+\Delta W;\ \text{base model and all }(A_i,B_i)\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: N\ \text{scalars in total (e.g. }N=20\text{ randomly sampled LoRAs), shared by all layers}
locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices of the base model (Flan-T5 in the paper)
structure: Element-wise linear combination of the factor matrices (a product of sums, which introduces cross terms \(B_iA_j\)), with one global coefficient per module found by black-box optimization on a few examples.
mergeable_reason: The composed LoRA has fixed weights and can be merged into \(W_0\) like any LoRA.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (only composition weights are searched; modules are pre-trained).
key_idea: Given a hub of task LoRAs, an unseen task can be handled by searching, without gradients, for a weighted combination of existing LoRAs that minimizes loss on a handful of examples.
results_note: On Big-Bench Hard with Flan-T5-large and 20 candidate LoRAs, LoraHub approaches few-shot in-context learning while using far fewer tokens per example at inference.
categorical_reading: LoraHub's coefficient object is a quadratic cone over the frozen modules, pointed at its vertex \(w=0\). Its composition rule is a factor-wise product of sums that does not descend to a function of the adapters \(B_iA_i\) (Prop V.4). It behaves like update arithmetic only when the modules share an \(A\)-seed (Prop V.4, prediction).

name: LoRA Soups (CAT)
paper_title: LoRA Soups: Merging LoRAs for Practical Skill Composition Tasks
formula_latex: \Delta W^{l}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\alpha_i^{l}\,B_iA_i=\big[\alpha_1^{l}B_1\ \cdots\ \alpha_N^{l}B_N\big]\begin{bmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_N\end{bmatrix};\ \ \alpha_i^{l}\text{ trained per layer on a small data mixture};\ W_0\text{ and all }(A_i,B_i)\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: N\ \text{per layer}
locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices (Llama-family models in the paper)
structure: Rank-concatenation (direct sum along the rank axis) of LoRA factors with learned layer-wise scalars: a weighted sum of the LoRA updates without the cross terms of factor averaging; merged rank \(\sum_i r_i\). HF PEFT's add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='cat') builds the same concatenated adapter with fixed, user-given weights.
mergeable_reason: Coefficients are input-independent, so the concatenated LoRA is a fixed low-rank update that can be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not applicable; only the merging coefficients are trained after the skill LoRAs exist.
key_idea: For skill composition (e.g. hard math word problems solved by writing code), concatenating independently trained skill LoRAs and learning only per-layer mixing weights beats both data mixing and parameter-averaging merges.
results_note: On GSM-Hard, CAT beats existing model-merging and data-mixing baselines by 43% and 12% on average and shows super-linear gains over the individual skill LoRAs.
categorical_reading: CAT is a \(\oplus\)-word in the pointed slice: \(N\) frozen line methods per layer, whose sum is a linear sub-object of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{\sum r_i}\). It combines products rather than factors, so it is gauge-invariant. That is exactly what separates it from LoraHub.

name: LoRA-LEGO
full_name: LoRA-LEGO: rank-wise clustering of minimal semantic units
paper_title: Merging LoRAs like Playing LEGO: Pushing the Modularity of LoRA to Extremes Through Rank-Wise Clustering
formula_latex: s_{ij}=[a_{ij},b_{ij}]\ (a_{ij}\text{: row }j\text{ of }A_i,\ b_{ij}\text{: column }j\text{ of }B_i);\ \Phi=\textstyle\bigcup_i\{s_{i1},\dots,s_{ir_i}\};\ \{\mu_c\}_{c=1}^{k}=\operatorname{KMeans}_k(\Phi);\ \mu'_c=\frac{\overline{\|s\|}_{\mathbb{C}_c}}{\|\mu_c\|}\mu_c;\ A'=[a'_1;\dots;a'_k],\ B'=[b'_1\cdots b'_k];\ \Delta W=\tfrac{\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{k}}\,B'A'
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(merged rank }k,\ 1\le k\le\textstyle\sum_i r_i)
locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices
structure: Decomposes each LoRA into rank-1 'minimal semantic units' \(b_ja_j\) and uses two algebraic facts: permutation invariance \(BA=(BP^{\top})(PA)\) and concatenation-summation equivalence \([B_1\ B_2][A_1;A_2]=B_1A_1+B_2A_2\); units from all LoRAs are clustered and \(k\) centroids (norm- and variance-rescaled) form the merged LoRA.
mergeable_reason: The result is an ordinary rank-\(k\) LoRA.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
key_idea: A LoRA is an unordered bag of rank-1 units, so merging should regroup similar units across LoRAs instead of averaging factor matrices position by position, which mixes misaligned units.
results_note: Outperforms existing LoRA merging approaches on multi-task and mixed-task benchmarks.
categorical_reading: LoRA-LEGO regroups rank-one units across modules, using the permutation part of LoRA's \(GL_r\) gauge together with the concatenation isomorphism \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_s\cong\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+s}\). It fixes only the finite permutation gauge, not \(GL_r\), so it is a rule on factor representatives, not on adapters.

name: ZipLoRA
full_name: ZipLoRA: merging subject and style LoRAs
paper_title: ZipLoRA: Any Subject in Any Style by Effectively Merging LoRAs
formula_latex: \Delta W_m=\Delta W_c\operatorname{diag}(m_c)+\Delta W_s\operatorname{diag}(m_s)\ (\text{one coefficient per column});\ \min_{m_c,m_s}\ \|(D\oplus L_m)(x_c,p_c)-(D\oplus L_c)(x_c,p_c)\|_2+\|(D\oplus L_m)(x_s,p_s)-(D\oplus L_s)(x_s,p_s)\|_2+\lambda\sum_{l}|m_c^{(l)}\cdot m_s^{(l)}|;\ W_0,\Delta W_c,\Delta W_s\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: 2\times(\#\text{columns of }\Delta W)\ \text{per adapted matrix (two merger vectors), optimized for}\approx100\text{ steps}
locus: LoRA-adapted layers of the SDXL UNet
structure: Column-wise diagonal re-weighting of two frozen dense LoRA updates, with a penalty on the overlap \(|m_c\cdot m_s|\) so that columns from the two LoRAs are not superimposed; relies on the sparsity of LoRA updates.
mergeable_reason: The merged update is a fixed dense matrix added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Merger vectors initialized to all ones, i.e. training starts from the direct merge \(\Delta W_c+\Delta W_s\).
key_idea: Independently trained subject and style LoRAs interfere when their columns are aligned; learning per-column merger coefficients that keep the two LoRAs' columns apart while preserving each LoRA's own outputs yields a single subject-in-style LoRA.
results_note: On SDXL, ZipLoRA improves subject and style fidelity over direct LoRA merging and other baselines while needing only about 100 optimization steps.
categorical_reading: ZipLoRA is a \(\oplus\) of two input-scaling methods on frozen updates, i.e. a column-wise (IA)\(^3\) on each \(\Delta W\), pointed at the direct merge. Its image lies in the frozen-\(B\) LoRA \(\{[B_c\ B_s]Y\}\). Its overlap penalty is a loss, not part of \(\rho\).

name: Mix-of-Show
paper_title: Mix-of-Show: Decentralized Low-Rank Adaptation for Multi-Concept Customization of Diffusion Models
formula_latex: W=\arg\min_{W}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big\|(W_0+\Delta W_i)X_i-WX_i\big\|_F^2\ \ \Big(\text{closed form }W=\big(\textstyle\sum_i(W_0+\Delta W_i)X_iX_i^{\top}\big)\big(\textstyle\sum_iX_iX_i^{\top}\big)^{-1}\Big),\ X_i:\ \text{layer inputs collected by sampling concept }i\text{ with its own ED-LoRA (data-free)}

It is a basis-free merge that does not use \(\theta_0\). Its update \(\sum_i\Delta W_iG_i(\sum_jG_j)^{-1}\) is dense but still has rank \(\le\sum_ir_i\), and it leaves \(\mathrm{span}\{\Delta W_i\}\).

Independently trained concepts are therefore sub-objects \(\mathrm{FA}(A_i)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{FA}(A_S)\) of a single linear method with stacked frozen frame \(A_S\). Merging is addition inside that linear space, which is the shared-frozen-factor fix of Prop V.4(b), and the crosstalk is \(\Delta W_jA_i^\top A_i\approx0\).

LoRA Composite is an ensemble in score space: a post-hoc operation that lands in functions rather than in \(\Theta\). Neither ever forms a single weight, which is how both avoid weight-space interference.

name: Polytropon (Poly)
full_name: Polytropon: latent-skill routing over parameter-efficient modules
paper_title: Combining Parameter-efficient Modules for Task-level Generalisation

key_idea: Assume tasks share a small inventory of latent skills; jointly learn which skills each task uses and the skills themselves, so new tasks can be few-shot adapted by recombining skills. (arXiv title: 'Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning'.)
results_note: Improves sample efficiency on 8 BabyAI levels and few-shot generalization on CrossFit (160 NLP tasks) over fully shared, task-specific and hypernetwork-generated baselines.
categorical_reading: Poly is a \(T\)-point of LoRA over the base of tasks, with a shared skill inventory: \(\rho\circ a:T\to\Theta\). Its product-of-sums rule has the same form as LoraHub's, but it is trained jointly. With generic allocations fixed and fewer skills than tasks, the only symmetry on the inventory is the diagonal \(GL_r\) (checked numerically). Training the allocations adds a skill-mixing group and a normalisation scale. Either way, the cross terms are a design choice rather than an ill-definedness.

name: SMEAR
full_name: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing
paper_title: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing

categorical_reading: SMEAR is an \(X\)-point of an adapter extension. Parameter averaging is what makes the router differentiable, and it also ties all experts to one gauge representative.

key_idea: Memory layers are sparsely accessed by design; updating only the slots specifically activated by new knowledge (relative to their pretraining usage) learns new facts with much less interference than full fine-tuning or LoRA.
results_note: After learning new TriviaQA facts, NaturalQuestions F1 drops 89% with full fine-tuning and 71% with LoRA but only 11% with sparse memory finetuning, at the same level of new-knowledge acquisition.
categorical_reading: Sparse memory finetuning sits in the 'coordinate blocks, resampled every step' cell of the cotangent table (Exposé IV): by the degree-one collapse each step is a fixed-mask linear method re-based at \(\theta_t\), with the mask chosen by access counts relative to background usage. Its control of forgetting comes from the smallness and specificity of the moving support, not from a constraint on the image.

name: SEAL
paper_title: Self-Adapting Language Models
formula_latex: SE\sim \mathrm{LM}_\theta(\cdot\mid C),\ \ \theta'=\mathrm{SFT}_{\mathrm{LoRA}}(\theta,SE)\ \ (W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA;\ r=64,\alpha=128 \text{ for knowledge incorporation};\ r=128,\alpha=16 \text{ for ARC TTT});\ \ \text{outer loop: ReST}^{EM}\ \text{(SFT on self-edits with } r(SE)=1),\ r(SE)=\mathbb{1}\big[\text{adapting with } SE \text{ improves } \mathrm{LM}_\theta \text{ on } \tau\big]
trainable_params: \text{inner: } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted matrix per self-edit } (r=64 \text{ or } 128);\ \text{outer: the self-edit generation policy (LoRA } r=16 \text{ in the ARC RL-SFT)}
locus: inner LoRA on all attention and MLP projections (Qwen2.5-7B, knowledge incorporation) or on q/v/gate/up/down projections (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, ARC)
structure: Bi-level: the model writes its own fine-tuning data and hyperparameters ('self-edits'); a LoRA SFT step turns each self-edit into \(\Delta W = BA\); RL (filtered behavior cloning) reinforces self-edits whose induced update improves downstream performance.
mergeable_reason: Each realized update is an ordinary LoRA that can be merged into the weights.
identity_at_init: Each inner LoRA update starts from \(B = 0\).
key_idea: Let the LLM learn, through RL, to generate the training data and optimization directives that best update its own weights, turning LoRA fine-tuning into an action the model can take.
results_note: On SQuAD knowledge incorporation (no-context), accuracy rises from 32.7% to 47.0%, beating synthetic data written by GPT-4.1 (46.3%); ARC few-shot success 72.5% vs 20% without RL. The paper flags catastrophic forgetting under repeated self-edits.
categorical_reading: SEAL realises a context-to-weights family \(C\mapsto\mathrm{SFT}_{\rm LoRA}(\theta,\mathrm{SE}(C))\) by optimisation rather than by a forward pass: each fibre is an ordinary LoRA point, and RL shapes the data that selects it. SHINE and GenerativeAdapter amortise the same map into a hypernetwork.

name: SparseLoRA
paper_title: SparseLoRA: Accelerating LLM Fine-Tuning with Contextual Sparsity
formula_latex: h=W_0\big|_{\mathcal{S}(x)}\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx\ \ (\text{training only}),\ \ \mathcal{S}(x)=\mathrm{TopK}\ \text{channels of the cheap proxy } (U_k\Sigma_k^{1/2})(\Sigma_k^{1/2}V_k^{\top})x\ \ \big(U_k\Sigma_kV_k^{\top}=\text{offline rank-}k \text{ SVD of } W_0\big);\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ (same as LoRA)}
locus: frozen main branch of attention (QKVO) and MLP projections, with non-uniform layer sparsity (deeper layers sparser); output tokens and up to the first 10% of steps stay dense. The LoRA branch (QKVO, \(r=32\), \(\alpha=64\) in experiments) stays dense.
structure: Standard LoRA update; the forward/backward pass through the frozen \(W_0\) uses input-dependent channel sparsity, predicted by a training-free rank-\(k\) SVD sketch of \(W_0\) (activation norms for FFN/VO, query-key norm products for QK).
mergeable_reason: Sparsity is used only during training; the dense LoRA adapter merges into \(W_0\) and inference is unchanged.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) as in LoRA; the sparse frozen branch only approximates \(W_0 x\) during training.
key_idea: LoRA saves memory but not compute; predicting per input which channels of the frozen weights matter, with a cheap SVD proxy, lets fine-tuning skip most frozen-branch FLOPs without hurting accuracy.
results_note: Up to 2.2x compute reduction and 1.6x wall-clock speedup over LoRA at matched accuracy on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning, code generation and instruction following (LLaMA-2/3).
categorical_reading: SparseLoRA keeps LoRA's object and trains it on an input-dependent approximation of the network: an input-indexed base change of the forward pass, like QLoRA's \(\kappa\) but data-dependent and discarded at inference. The gradients are those of the sparsified model, so it changes the dynamics, not the image.

name: LoReFT
full_name: Low-rank Linear Subspace Representation Finetuning (ReFT family)
paper_title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
formula_latex: \Phi_{\text{LoReFT}}(h)=h+R^{\top}\big(Wh+b-Rh\big)=(I-R^{\top}R)\,h+R^{\top}(Wh+b),\quad R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\ (RR^{\top}=I_r),\ W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{r};\ \text{applied to the residual-stream vector } h^{(l)}_i \text{ at the first } p \text{ and last } s \text{ prompt positions of the chosen layers } l\in\mathcal{L};\ \text{LM frozen},\ \{R,W,b\}\ \text{trained};\ \text{DiReFT ablation: } \Phi(h)=h+W_2^{\top}(W_1h+b),\ W_1,W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}
trainable_params: (2rd+r)\ \text{per intervention } (R,W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{r});\ |\mathcal{L}|\,(2rd+r)\ \text{with prefix and suffix weights tied},\ 2|\mathcal{L}|\,(2rd+r)\ \text{untied (one intervention for the prefix and one for the suffix positions in each layer)}
locus: residual-stream hidden states (Transformer block outputs) at a fixed number of prefix and suffix prompt positions in selected layers; generated tokens are not intervened on
structure: Low-rank affine edit of hidden states confined to an \(r\)-dimensional subspace. With the orthogonal projector \(P = R^T R\), \(\Phi(h) = (I - P)h + R^T(Wh + b)\): the component of \(h\) in \(\mathrm{row}(R)\) is replaced by a learned affine function of \(h\), and the orthogonal complement is untouched. The edit is sparse in both positions (prompt prefix and suffix) and layers. DiReFT drops the orthonormality and the difference term, giving a LoRA-shaped map \(h \to h + W_2^T(W_1 h + b)\) on activations.
mergeable_reason: The edit acts on the residual stream, including the skip path, at specific token positions, so it cannot be folded into any weight matrix; its cost is a small constant per prompt rather than per generated token.
identity_at_init: Not identity-preserving. In pyreft \(R\) gets a random orthogonal initialization (torch orthogonal parametrization) and \(W\), \(b\) use the default nn.Linear initialization, so \(\Phi(h) \neq h\) at step 0; the identity is recovered only when \(W = R\) and \(b = 0\).
key_idea: Learn task-specific interventions on hidden representations instead of changing weights. LoReFT adapts the distributed interchange intervention from causal-abstraction interpretability (DAS): it rewrites the hidden state only inside a learned low-rank orthonormal subspace and only at a few prompt positions, using 15x-65x fewer parameters than LoRA.
results_note: With 0.031% trainable parameters on LLaMA-7B it averages 80.2 on eight commonsense-reasoning tasks, the best among the compared PEFTs. On Llama-2 7B instruction tuning it reaches an 85.60 AlpacaEval win rate with 0.0039% of parameters (LoRA: 81.48). It trails LoRA and adapters on arithmetic reasoning.
categorical_reading: Per hidden vector LoReFT is weight-space LoRA on an affine identity box that the architecture did not have, with \(B=R^\top\) on the Stiefel manifold, so it is simulated by, but not isomorphic to, LoRA\(_r\). Its neutral point \((B_0,A_0)=(R_0^\top,0)\) lies in LoRA's \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum, and position-selectivity is what blocks merging.

name: LongLoRA
full_name: LongLoRA (LoRA with trainable embeddings and norms, plus Shifted Sparse Attention)
paper_title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
formula_latex: W_{\{q,k,v,o\}}=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\ \ (B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}});\ \ E=E_0+\Delta E\ \text{(input embedding, dense)};\ \ \gamma_{\text{norm}}\ \text{(all RMSNorm gains) trained};\ \ \text{training-time attention } \mathrm{S^2\text{-}Attn}:\ \text{tokens split into groups of size } G,\ \text{half of the heads attend within groups, the other half within groups shifted by } G/2;\ \ \text{inference: standard full attention};\ \ \text{RoPE positions rescaled by Position Interpolation};\ \ \text{MLP weights frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted attention matrix } (4L \text{ matrices}) \;+\; |\mathcal{V}|\,d\ \text{(input embedding)} \;+\; (2L+1)\,d\ \text{(norm gains)}
locus: \(W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o\) of every attention layer (LoRA, \(r = 8\), \(\alpha = 16\) in the official code), plus the input token-embedding matrix and all normalization layers (trained densely); S\(^2\)-Attn changes only the training-time attention pattern
structure: Composite of three factors. (i) Rank-\(r\) additive updates \(\Delta W = BA\) on the attention projections. (ii) Dense, selective updates of the input-embedding table and the norm gains, which together are under 2% of Llama2-7B's parameters. (iii) A training-only sparsification of the attention graph into block-diagonal token groups, with a \(G/2\) shift on half of the heads so that information flows between neighbouring groups (Swin-style). The paper calls (i)+(ii) 'LoRA+', which is unrelated to LoRA+ by Hayou et al.
mergeable_reason: The LoRA factors merge into \(W_0\), the trained embedding and norm tensors replace the originals, and S\(^2\)-Attn is used only in training, so inference runs the original dense-attention architecture (with Position-Interpolation RoPE scaling) at the original cost.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA init (\(B = 0\)) and the pretrained embedding and norm values, so the weights are unchanged at step 0. The training-time function still differs from the base model, because attention is restricted to shifted local groups and positions are interpolated.
key_idea: Plain LoRA fails at context extension at any rank, but also training the cheap embedding and normalization layers closes almost all of the gap to full fine-tuning. Training can use shifted sparse local attention, which approximates full attention and takes two lines of code, while inference keeps dense attention.
results_note: Extends Llama2 7B, 13B and 70B to 100k, 64k and 32k tokens on a single 8xA100 machine. At 32k context on PG19, LoRA with trainable norms and embeddings reaches perplexity 8.12, versus 8.08 for full fine-tuning and 11.44 for plain rank-8 LoRA.
categorical_reading: LongLoRA is the \(\oplus\)-word LoRA\(_{qkvo}\oplus\) Embedding \(\oplus\) LN-tuning, trained on a different realisation from the one it is deployed on: S\(^2\)-Attn and Position Interpolation change \(f\), while \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\) depends only on \((\Theta,\theta_0)\). Its finding that LoRA alone fails at any rank is an O1 statement: the embedding and gain directions lie outside every LoRA\(_{qkvo}\) image, and LoRA and LN-tuning both map into it by A5.

name: O-LoRA
full_name: Orthogonal Low-Rank Adaptation (orthogonal subspace learning for continual learning)
paper_title: Orthogonal Subspace Learning for Language Model Continual Learning
formula_latex: W^{(t)}=W_0+\sum_{i<t}B_iA_i+B_tA_t,\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\quad \text{paper: }\min_{A_t,B_t}\ \mathcal{L}_{\text{task}}(\mathcal{D}_t)+\lambda_1\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}\big\|B_i^{\top}B_t\big\|_F^2\ \ (\mathcal{U}_t=\operatorname{col}(B_t)\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}};\ \text{the paper writes }\Delta W=AB\text{ with its }A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\text{ the output-side factor});\quad \text{official code: }\lambda_1\sum_{i<t}\big\|A_iA_t^{\top}\big\|_{1}\ (\text{entry-wise, on PEFT lora\_A})+\lambda_2\big(\|A_t\|_F+\|B_t\|_F\big);\quad W_0\ \text{and}\ \{A_i,B_i\}_{i<t}\ \text{frozen; after task } t:\ W_0\leftarrow W_0+\textstyle\sum_{i\le t}B_iA_i
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix per task (after } t \text{ tasks } t\,r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ are stored unless merged)}
locus: \(W_q\) and \(W_v\) of every attention layer (T5-large, LLaMA-7B)
structure: Sum of per-task rank-\(r\) updates. A soft penalty on an \(r\times r\) cross-Gram matrix, which vanishes exactly when two tasks' subspaces are orthogonal, pushes each new task's subspace away from all earlier ones. \(\Delta W\) is therefore close to a direct sum of mutually orthogonal rank-\(r\) pieces; orthogonality is a regularizer, not a hard constraint. The paper defines each task's subspace as the column span of the output-side factor (catalog \(B_t\), in \(\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\)) and squares the entries of \(B_i^\top B_t\). The official trainer instead penalizes the input-side rows (PEFT lora_A) with an entry-wise absolute value and adds an L2 term (\(\lambda_2\)).
mergeable_reason: Each task's \(BA\) is a static low-rank matrix that can be merged into \(W_0\) after training, and inference needs no task ID.
identity_at_init: Each new task's LoRA uses the standard init (\(B_t = 0\)), so the model function is unchanged at the start of every task.
key_idea: Use each finished task's LoRA subspace as a cheap stand-in for its gradient subspace, instead of storing gradients as OGD does, and learn the next task's LoRA in a subspace orthogonal to all earlier ones. This gives continual learning without rehearsal or task IDs and preserves instruction-following generalization.
results_note: On the standard 5-task continual-learning benchmark with T5-large, O-LoRA averages 75.8% over three task orders, against 72.7% for LFPT5 (the paper's previous state of the art) and 80.0% for multi-task training. On the 15-task benchmark it averages 69.6% against 69.2% for LFPT5. ProgPrompt, which needs task IDs at inference, scores 75.1% and 77.9%.
categorical_reading: O-LoRA is \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r^{\oplus T}\) unrolled over tasks, i.e. ReLoRA with one stage per task, plus a penalty that pushes each new stage away from the earlier ones. The paper penalises column spaces of the up-projections and the official code row spaces of the down-projections, so the two versions enforce orthogonality on opposite sides of the update.

name: InfLoRA
paper_title: InfLoRA: Interference-Free Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
formula_latex: W_t=W_{t-1}+B_tA_t,\quad A_t=(U_t)_{[1:r]}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen, from the SVD } \hat H_t^{\top}=V_t\Sigma_tU_t,\ \ \hat H_t=(I-M_tM_t^{\top})H_t\ \ \text{or}\ \ M_t^{\perp}M_t^{\perp\top}H_t;\quad B_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained, init } 0;\quad \Rightarrow\ \Delta_{B_t}W_t=(\Delta_{W}W_t)\,A_t^{\top}A_t,\ \ (B_tA_t)\,M_t=0
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}\ \text{per adapted matrix per task (}A_t\text{ is designed, not trained; one } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ branch is kept at a time, earlier branches are merged)}
locus: key and value projections of every ViT-B/16 attention block (variant InfLoRA-b5: bottom 5 blocks only)
structure: Rank-\(r\) additive update with a frozen, data-designed down-projection \(A_t\). Its orthonormal rows are the top principal directions of the current task's layer inputs \(H_t\) after projection onto the orthogonal complement of the old tasks' input subspace \(\mathrm{span}(M_t)\), which DualGPM maintains; they therefore lie in \(N_t\) intersected with \(M_t^{\perp}\). Training \(B_t\) alone equals full fine-tuning projected onto \(\mathrm{row}(A_t)\), \(\Delta W = G A_t^T A_t\), so \(\Delta W\) annihilates old-task inputs. Notation is swapped relative to the paper, which calls the up-projection \(A_t\) and the down-projection \(B_t\).
mergeable_reason: After each task the branch \(B_t A_t\) is merged into \(W_{t-1}\), and inference uses a single weight matrix without task identity.
identity_at_init: \(B_t = 0\) (zero-initialized up-projection), so the function is unchanged at the start of each task. \(A_t\) is set before training by an SVD of the projected current-task activations.
key_idea: Fine-tuning only the up-projection of a LoRA branch is exactly full fine-tuning restricted to the row space of the frozen down-projection. Choosing that row space inside the new task's input span but orthogonal to the old tasks' input space removes interference by construction.
results_note: With an ImageNet-21K ViT-B/16, InfLoRA reaches final accuracies of 75.65% on 10-task ImageNet-R (77.52% with 5 tasks, 71.01% with 20), 86.51% on 10-task CIFAR-100 and 74.53% on 5-task DomainNet. It leads L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-P, C-LoRA and LAE on ImageNet-R and DomainNet. On CIFAR-100, CODA-P has a slightly higher final accuracy (86.62%), while InfLoRA has the best averaged accuracy (91.70% vs 91.08%).
categorical_reading: InfLoRA is LoRA-FA with a data-designed frame, re-based once per task; in the cotangent table it shares GaLore's cell ('data frame, re-based periodically'), with the frame taken from projected activations rather than gradients. By the degree-one collapse a stage is full fine-tuning projected onto \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\), and \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\perp M_t\) gives \(\Delta W\,M_t=0\): old-task inputs are annihilated by construction.

name: Textual Inversion
paper_title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion
formula_latex: v_*=\arg\min_{v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}\ \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{E}(x),\,y,\,\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\,t}\Big[\big\|\epsilon-\epsilon_\theta\big(z_t,t,c_\theta(y)\big)\big\|_2^2\Big],\quad y=\text{neutral template (e.g. ``A photo of } S_*\text{'') whose token } S_* \text{ is embedded as } v;\quad c_\theta,\ \epsilon_\theta,\ \mathcal{E}\ \text{and all existing token embeddings frozen}
trainable_params: d\ \ \text{(one token embedding; } k\,d \text{ for a } k\text{-vector pseudo-word)}
locus: token-embedding table of the frozen text encoder (one new row for the pseudo-word \(S_*\)); the pseudo-word can appear anywhere in a prompt
structure: Extends the frozen vocabulary with one learned point \(v_*\) in input-embedding space. The update is a single new row of the embedding matrix, used compositionally inside arbitrary natural-language prompts rather than as a fixed task prefix.
mergeable_reason: The learned vector is just a new vocabulary entry: inference runs the unchanged text encoder and diffusion model at the same cost, with one token standing in for a word.
identity_at_init: The model itself is untouched. \(v\) is initialized to the embedding of a single-word coarse descriptor (e.g. 'cat', 'sculpture'), so prompts without \(S_*\) behave exactly as before and \(S_*\) starts out as that word.
key_idea: Personalize a frozen text-to-image model by inverting 3-5 images into a new word in its text-embedding space, trained with the ordinary denoising loss. One word embedding is enough to capture an object or style, which can then be composed into new prompts.
results_note: On LDM a single learned embedding reproduces object and style concepts from 3-5 images more faithfully than human-written captions or DALL-E 2 image prompts. CLIP-based and user-study evaluations place it at a favourable point on the reconstruction-editability trade-off, which the learning rate can shift.
categorical_reading: Textual inversion is a pointed extension of the input alphabet rather than of the network. It adjoins one symbol \(S_*\) whose embedding is a free point \(v\in\mathbb R^d\), neutral at \(v_0=E_w\) via the substitution \(S_*\mapsto w\). On the old inputs it is the initial object (Frozen). On prompts containing \(S_*\) it is Trainable Tokens on the extended table, the Lin row method of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta^+,\theta_0^+)\).

name: Custom Diffusion
full_name: Custom Diffusion (cross-attention K/V fine-tuning for multi-concept customization)
paper_title: Multi-Concept Customization of Text-to-Image Diffusion
formula_latex: K=W^{k}c,\ V=W^{v}c\ \text{in every U-Net cross-attention layer};\quad W^{k}=W^{k}_0+\Delta W^{k},\ W^{v}=W^{v}_0+\Delta W^{v}\ \text{(dense)},\ \text{plus a new modifier-token embedding } V^{*};\ \text{all other weights frozen; loss: denoising loss on the target images plus 200 retrieved real regularization images};\quad \text{merging } N \text{ concepts: } \hat W=\arg\min_W\|WC_{\text{reg}}^{\top}-W_0C_{\text{reg}}^{\top}\|_F\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ WC^{\top}=V_{\text{tgt}},\ \ \hat W=W_0+\mathbf{v}^{\top}\mathbf{d},\ \ \mathbf{d}=C(C_{\text{reg}}^{\top}C_{\text{reg}})^{-1},\ \ \mathbf{v}^{\top}=(V_{\text{tgt}}-W_0C^{\top})(\mathbf{d}C^{\top})^{-1}
trainable_params: 2\,d_{out}\,d_{text}\ \text{per cross-attention layer } (W^{k},W^{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{text}}) \;+\; d_{text}\ \text{per modifier token}
locus: key and value projections of the text features in all cross-attention layers of the diffusion U-Net (Stable Diffusion), plus the modifier-token embedding
structure: Block mask over the parameter tensors: only the two matrices that read the text condition (\(W^k, W^v\)) are updated, densely. Multi-concept merging is a closed-form, equality-constrained least-squares projection: it maps each concept's target-word features to the fine-tuned values while staying close to \(W_0\) on about 1000 regularization captions.
mergeable_reason: The fine-tuned \(W^k\) and \(W^v\) replace the originals and \(V^*\) is one extra vocabulary row, so inference runs the original architecture at the original cost; the closed-form merge folds several concepts into a single pair of matrices.
identity_at_init: Training starts from the pretrained \(W^k, W^v\) (\(\Delta W = 0\)), and \(V^*\) is initialized to a rarely occurring token's embedding, so the model is initially unchanged on ordinary prompts.
key_idea: Fine-tuning moves the cross-attention weights much more than any others, so update only the K/V projections that map text into latent features, together with a learned modifier token and retrieved real images as regularization. The method is fast, small and resists language drift, and concepts can be combined by joint training or a closed-form constrained merge.
results_note: On Stable Diffusion it beats Textual Inversion and matches or beats DreamBooth on text/image alignment and human preference, while training about 5x faster (~6 minutes) and storing 75MB instead of 3GB per concept. The closed-form multi-concept merge takes about 2 seconds.
categorical_reading: Custom Diffusion is Textual Inversion \(\oplus\) a selective block. The block is surgical fine-tuning of exactly the boxes that read the text wire (\(W^k,W^v\)), plus one adjoined vocabulary symbol. Its multi-concept merge is a P operation \(\Theta^N\to\Theta\). It solves a least-squares problem under hard equality constraints on the concepts' features, so it is a constrained RegMean rather than task arithmetic.

name: ESFT
paper_title: Let the Expert Stick to His Last: Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning for Sparse Architectural Large Language Models
formula_latex: g_i^{l}=\frac{1}{N_s}\sum_{j=1}^{N_s}\frac{1}{L_j}\sum_{k=1}^{L_j}g_{i,k}^{l}\ \ (\text{ESFT-Gate})\quad\text{or}\quad r_i^{l}=\frac{1}{N_s}\sum_{j=1}^{N_s}\frac{1}{L_j}\sum_{k=1}^{L_j}\frac{\mathbb{1}(g_{i,k}^{l}>0)}{K}\ \ (\text{ESFT-Token});\quad E_s^{l}=\text{top-scored experts with }\textstyle\sum_{i\in E_s^{l}}R_i^{l}\ge p;\quad \theta_e\ (e\in E_s^{l})\ \text{trained; all other routed experts, shared experts, attention, router and embeddings frozen}
trainable_params: \sum_{l=1}^{L}|E_s^{l}|\cdot 3\,d\,d_{ff}^{(e)}\ \ (\text{gate/up/down projections of each selected routed expert; on average 2-15 of 66 experts per layer})
locus: the routed (non-shared) FFN experts in each MoE layer that are most relevant to the task; attention, router, shared experts and embeddings stay frozen
structure: Data-dependent block mask over experts. In each layer the selected set is the smallest group of top-scored routed experts whose cumulative relevance (average gate score or token-selection ratio on sampled task data) reaches p. Selected experts are updated densely, everything else is frozen, and routing stays free during training and inference.
mergeable_reason: The updated experts simply replace the originals, so the architecture, routing and inference cost are unchanged.
identity_at_init: Training starts from the pretrained weights (\(\Delta W = 0\)); expert selection is computed from router statistics on a task sample.
key_idea: In fine-grained MoE LLMs, each task activates a concentrated and distinct set of experts, so fine-tune only the experts most relevant to the task. This nearly matches full fine-tuning on the target task, forgets less, and cuts storage by up to 90%.
results_note: On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, ESFT-Gate averages 50.2 on downstream tasks (FFT 51.0, LoRA 44.9) while keeping more general ability (ESFT-Token 61.5 vs FFT 58.8 and LoRA 59.1), with 2.57-3.20 GB of trained parameters versus 28.6 GB for FFT.
categorical_reading: ESFT is surgical fine-tuning indexed by experts instead of layers: the trainable set is a union of whole expert boxes, chosen from router statistics on task data. Like surgical FT and Spectrum, it is a Lin, regular, idempotent coordinate block. Only the selection rule (routing mass) is new.

name: Intruder-dimension reduction
full_name: Intruder Dimension Reduction (post-hoc spectral surgery on LoRA adapters)
paper_title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
hf_peft_config: from peft.tuners.lora.intruders import reduce_intruder_dimension; reduce_intruder_dimension(peft_model, old_adapter_name='default', new_adapter_name='intruder_reduced', top_k=10, threshold_epsilon=0.5, mitigation_lambda=0.75)  # adds and activates a new LoRA adapter
formula_latex: W_0+\Delta W=U\Sigma V^{\top},\ \ W_0=U^{0}\Sigma^{0}V^{0\top};\quad \mathcal{I}=\{\,j\le k:\ \max_i|\langle u_j,u^{0}_i\rangle|<\epsilon\,\};\quad W'=W_0+\Delta W+(\lambda-1)\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\sigma_j\,u_jv_j^{\top};\quad (B',A')=\text{rank-}r\ \text{truncated SVD of } (W'-W_0)/s,\ \ s=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\ (\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}\text{ with rsLoRA}),\ \ B'=U_r\Sigma_r^{1/2},\ A'=\Sigma_r^{1/2}V_r^{\top};\quad \text{no training: } W_0 \text{ frozen, the trained } (B,A) \text{ replaced by } (B',A')\ \ (\text{paper: only the top-ranked } j\in\mathcal{I}\text{ is scaled, no re-factorization})
trainable_params: 0\ \ (\text{training-free; the output is again a rank-}r\text{ adapter with } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ parameters per matrix})
locus: every LoRA-adapted linear (or embedding) layer of an already trained adapter
structure: Spectral endomorphism on the space of trained adapters. Among the top-\(k\) singular directions of the merged matrix, those nearly orthogonal to every pretrained left singular vector (the intruders) are shrunk by \(\lambda\), and the edited \(\Delta W\) is projected back to rank \(r\). The paper scales only the top intruder per matrix and does not re-project; HF PEFT scales every detected intruder and re-factorizes to rank \(r\).
