identity_at_init: Not applicable (post-hoc edit). \(\lambda = 1\) leaves the adapter unchanged up to rank-\(r\) truncation, \(\lambda = 0\) removes the intruder components, and \(\lambda > 1\) amplifies them.
key_idea: LoRA creates high-ranking intruder singular vectors that are nearly orthogonal to the pretrained spectrum; full fine-tuning does not. These directions drive most of the forgetting, so shrinking them after training recovers pretrained behaviour at little cost in task accuracy.
results_note: Scaling the top intruder dimension of each matrix with \(\lambda = 0.7\) (RoBERTa-base on QQP, LoRA \(r = 8\)) left test accuracy unchanged and cut fine-tuning-induced forgetting (pre-training loss) by 33.2%. For LLaMA2-7B on MetaMath (\(r = 256\)), \(\lambda = 0.3\) cost 0.1% accuracy and cut forgetting by 33.3%.
categorical_reading: A post-hoc spectral operation on the image of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\). A one-parameter torus acts on those singular values of the merged weight whose left singular vectors are nearly orthogonal to \(W_0\)'s. In other words it is SVDiff re-based at the trained point and restricted to the intruder directions. It reads only the product \(BA\), so it descends to adapters (Prop V.4(a)).

name: CODA-Prompt
paper_title: CODA-Prompt: COntinual Decomposed Attention-based Prompting for Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning
formula_latex: p(x)=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\alpha_m(x)\,P_m,\quad \alpha_m(x)=\gamma\big(q(x)\odot A_m,\;K_m\big),\quad q(x)=\theta(x)_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}\ \text{(frozen ViT pass)},\ \gamma=\cos;\quad p=[p_K;p_V],\ p_K,p_V\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{\ell}{2}\times d}:\ \mathrm{MSA}\big(h_Q,[p_K;h_K],[p_V;h_V]\big)\ \text{at each prompted layer};\quad \min_{P^{n},K^{n},A^{n},\phi_n}\ \mathcal{L}\big(f_\phi(f_{\theta,P,K,A}(x)),y\big)+\lambda\big(\|PP^{\top}-I\|_2+\|KK^{\top}-I\|_2+\|AA^{\top}-I\|_2\big);\ \ \theta\ \text{frozen},\ \text{components of earlier tasks frozen}
trainable_params: n_p\,M\,(\ell d+2d)+\text{head}\quad(n_p=\text{prompted layers, 5 in the paper};\ M/N\ \text{new components trained per task})
locus: keys/values (prefix form) of MSA layers 1-5 of a frozen ViT-B/16; the query comes from a separate frozen forward pass ([CLS] output)
structure: Input-conditioned linear combination of a growing dictionary of prefix components, \(p(x) = \sum_m \alpha_m(x) P_m\). The weights are unnormalized cosine similarities between a feature-gated query \(q(x) \odot A_m\) and a key \(K_m\). Each task adds \(M/N\) components, and the components, keys and attention vectors of earlier tasks are frozen, so the trainable space is an increasing chain of component sets with soft orthogonality penalties.
mergeable_reason: The prompt depends on the input through the query pass, and its prefix slots lengthen the key/value sequence, so nothing folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No identity: prefix slots change attention from the first step. \(P\), \(K\) and \(A\) are orthogonally initialized.
key_idea: L2P and DualPrompt select prompts from a pool by hard key-query matching. CODA-Prompt replaces that with an attention-weighted sum of prompt components, so the selection mechanism is trained end to end with the task loss. Capacity grows by adding components rather than lengthening prompts, and freezing past components plus orthogonality limits forgetting.
results_note: Rehearsal-free class-incremental ImageNet-R with ViT-B/16: 75.45% average final accuracy on 10 tasks vs 71.32% for DualPrompt (up to +4.5% across the 5/10/20-task splits). It is also ahead on CIFAR-100, DomainNet and a dual-shift ImageNet-R benchmark.
categorical_reading: CODA-Prompt is a continuous family over inputs, \(x\mapsto\sum_m\alpha_m(x)P_m\), of points of prefix tuning, with unnormalised cosine weights read from a frozen query pass. Each task adds components and freezes the earlier ones at their trained values. That freezing, not any property of the image, is how it limits forgetting.

name: Trans-LoRA
full_name: Trans-LoRA (nearly data-free transfer of PEFT modules across base models by distillation on filtered synthetic data)
paper_title: Trans-LoRA: towards data-free Transferable Parameter Efficient Finetuning
formula_latex: \phi^\ast=\arg\max_\phi\ \mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}}\log p_{\phi}(\text{yes}\mid t(x))+\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{M}_s}\log p_{\phi}(\text{no}\mid t(x));\quad \mathcal{D}_{syn}=\{x\sim\mathcal{M}_{gen}(\cdot\mid\bar{\mathcal{D}}):\ p_{\phi^\ast}(\text{yes}\mid t(x))>p_{\phi^\ast}(\text{no}\mid t(x))\},\ |\bar{\mathcal{D}}|=5,\ |\mathcal{D}_{syn}|=|\mathcal{D}|;\quad \theta_t=\arg\min_{\theta}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{D}_{syn}}H\big((\mathcal{M}_t+\theta)(x),\,(\mathcal{M}_s+\theta_s)(x)\big);\ \ \mathcal{M}_s,\mathcal{M}_t,\theta_s\ \text{frozen};\ \theta_t\ \text{trained (e.g. } W_t=W_{t,0}+B_tA_t)
trainable_params: r\,(d^{t}_{in}+d^{t}_{out})\ \text{per adapted target matrix (whatever the target PEFT needs)}\ +\ \text{a one-off LoRA discriminator on }\mathcal{M}_s
locus: the target model's adapter locations (default LoRA on \(W_q, W_v\)). The transfer acts on the model's input-output behavior, not on weights.
structure: Function-level transport of an adapter along a change of base model. The source pair (\(M_s, \theta_s\)) acts as a teacher, and the target adapter is fitted by knowledge distillation on synthetic inputs that a discriminator has filtered to imitate the distribution of the original training inputs. No weight correspondence between source and target is needed, so they may differ in family, size and even PEFT type (LoRA, DoRA, prompt tuning).
mergeable_reason: The output is an ordinary adapter of the chosen target type: a transferred LoRA or DoRA merges into the target weights, a transferred soft prompt does not.
identity_at_init: The target adapter starts from the standard initialization of its type (for LoRA, \(B = 0\), so \(M_t + \theta_t = M_t\) at the start). Algorithm 1 only says 'Initialize \(\theta_t\)'.
key_idea: When a base model is retired, its LoRAs can be retrained on the new base without the client's data. An LLM seeded with 5 examples synthesizes task inputs. A discriminator, trained once alongside the source LoRA, keeps only samples that look like the real training inputs. The target LoRA is then distilled from the source model plus LoRA on those samples.
results_note: Across 86 BBH, MMLU, MBPP and GSM8K tasks with Llama-2 and Gemma (within and across families), the transferred LoRA matches or beats both the source LoRA and the unadapted target. For example, BBH Gemma-2b to Gemma-7b: 43.61 vs 31.84 (source LoRA) and 37.75 (target base). It also transfers LoRA<->DoRA and prompt tuning, and survives two consecutive transfers.
categorical_reading: Trans-LoRA moves an adapter to a new base model that has no weight correspondence with the old one, so no base-change functor \(\phi_!\) exists. Instead it lifts the source realisation \(\Phi_{f_s}(\theta_s+\Delta_s)\) along the target realisation \(\Phi_{f_t}\circ\rho_{\rm LoRA}\), by distillation on synthetic inputs. The output is an object of the target slice, which is why the PEFT type may change in transit.

name: LoRA-X
paper_title: LoRA-X: Bridging Foundation Models with Training-Free Cross-Model Adaptation
formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^{\top}\ \text{(SVD, cached)},\quad W=W_0+\tilde U_r\,\Delta\Sigma\,\tilde V_r^{\top},\ \ \tilde U_r\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \tilde V_r\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{(top-}r\text{ singular vectors, frozen)},\ \ \Delta\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\delta\sigma_1,\dots,\delta\sigma_r)\ \text{(or a full } r\times r\text{ core) trained},\ \sigma_i+\delta\sigma_i\ge 0;\quad \text{transfer (no training): }\Delta W_{t\leftarrow s}=U_tU_t^{\top}\,\Delta W_s\,V_tV_t^{\top}=U_t\big(U_t^{\top}\tilde U_s\,\Delta\Sigma_s\,\tilde V_s^{\top}V_t\big)V_t^{\top}
trainable_params: r\ \ (\text{diagonal }\Delta\Sigma)\quad\text{or}\quad r^{2}\ \ (\text{full core})
locus: attention projections (to_q, to_k, to_v, to_out) of diffusion UNets: SDXL family (UNet only) and SD-v1.5 family (UNet and text-encoder attention); TinyLlama in an appendix. Transfer skips 'filter blocks' with low source-target subspace similarity and re-matches some blocks to a more similar source block.
structure: The update lives in \(\mathrm{span}(U_r) \otimes \mathrm{span}(V_r)\) of \(W_0\), i.e. a spectral core between frozen top-\(r\) SVD bases. Cross-model transfer is a two-sided orthogonal projection onto the target weight's column and row spaces (Eq. 3). Layers are matched by subspace similarity (Eq. 4); for mismatched sizes a least-squares map replaces the source bases (Sec. 4.2.2). Across architectures, an optimal-transport cost over the layer-similarity matrix (the Adapter Transferability Cost) scores how hard a transfer is; it is a metric, not the transfer map itself. Caveat (derived): the released pseudocode uses a thin SVD, so for square full-rank layers the projection is the identity and transfer copies \(\Delta W_s\) unchanged.
mergeable_reason: Both the trained and the transferred adapter are plain additive matrices that fold into the source or target \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not stated in the paper. The natural choice \(\Delta \Sigma = 0\) (inferred) gives \(\Delta W = 0\).
key_idea: An adapter becomes portable if it may not create new feature directions. LoRA-X trains only a rescaling or mixing of the base weight's top singular directions, then moves it to a new base model (an updated, distilled or fine-tuned version) by projecting onto that model's singular subspaces, with no data and no training.
results_note: Training-free transfer of LoRA-X style adapters, from SD-v1.5 to SD Eff-v1.0/RV-v3.0 and from SDXL to SSD-1B/RVXL-v3.0, gives HPSv2, LPIPS-diversity and DINOv2 scores close to adapters trained directly on the target, whereas projected plain LoRA degrades markedly. A TinyLlama 3T to 2.5T text experiment shows the same.
categorical_reading: Diagonal LoRA-X is the torus acting on the top-\(r\) singular values of \(W_0\), i.e. SVDiff truncated to rank \(r\); its full-core variant is LoRA-XS. The transfer \(\Delta W\mapsto U_tU_t^\top\Delta W\,V_tV_t^\top\) is a two-sided orthogonal projection between slices at different base points \(\theta_s\to\theta_t\), not an arrow. With a thin SVD it is the identity on full-rank square layers (catalog caveat).

name: LoFiT
paper_title: LoFiT: Localized Fine-tuning on LLM Representations
formula_latex: \text{Step 1 (localize): } z^{(l,i)}\leftarrow(1+A_l^{i})\odot z^{(l,i)},\ \ \min_{A}\ \mathcal{L}_{CE}+\lambda\textstyle\sum_{l,i}\|A_l^{i}\|_1,\ \ T=\operatorname{top\text{-}K}_{(l,i)}\|A_l^{i}\|;\quad \text{Step 2 (tune): } z^{(l,i)}\leftarrow z^{(l,i)}+v_l^{i}\ \ \text{for }(l,i)\in T,\ \ \mathrm{MultiHead}(h)=\operatorname{concat}\big(z^{(l,1)},\dots,z^{(l,H)}\big)W^{O};\ \ \text{all } W_0\ \text{frozen},\ v_l^{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{head}}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: K\,d_{head}\ \ (\text{final; }K=48,96,160\ \text{for Gemma-7B, Llama 2-7B, Llama 2-13B}\Rightarrow 48\cdot256=96\cdot128\approx12\text{K},\ 160\cdot128\approx20\text{K});\ \text{the discarded selection step trains }L\,H\,d_{head}\ \text{scalings }(=L\,d\ \text{when }H\,d_{head}=d,\ \text{e.g. Llama 2})
locus: outputs of a learned sparse set of attention heads (3-10% of all heads), before the output projection \(W^O\)
structure: Input-independent translation of selected head-output coordinates, \(z \mapsto z + v\), on a support \(T\) chosen by an L1-regularized multiplicative probe. Because \(z\) enters \(W^O\) linearly, the edit equals a bias \(\Delta b_O = \sum_{i\in T_l} W^O_{(i)} v_l^i\) on the attention output projection (derived here). It is therefore sparse, localized bias tuning in representation space, spanning at most \(K d_{head}\) directions.
mergeable_reason: The offset is constant and passes through the linear \(W^O\), so it folds into an output-projection bias. Llama and Gemma o_proj layers have no bias, so one bias vector per edited layer must be added (derived from the paper's equations).
identity_at_init: Approximate only: \(v \sim N(0, \sigma_v)\) and, in the selection step, \(A \sim N(0, \sigma_A)\), with \(\sigma_A = \sigma_v = 0.001\) in all experiments (App. D), so the model starts near the base model but not exactly at it.
key_idea: LoFiT borrows localization from interpretability. It first learns per-head scaling factors with an L1 penalty to find which attention heads matter for the task, then fine-tunes only additive offset vectors on those heads. Task-specific localization beats random head sets and head sets chosen for other tasks.
results_note: With 10% of heads (about 12K-20K parameters) on Gemma-7B and Llama 2-7B/13B, LoFiT beats ReFT on average and is comparable to LoRA (about 200x more parameters) and RED (about 20x more) on TruthfulQA, MQuAKE and CLUTRR. It is slightly below them on SIQA, ARC-c, BoolQ and SVAMP, and it outperforms ITI.
categorical_reading: LoFiT is BitFit on the attention-output bias, restricted to a learned sparse set of heads. It is a Lin method whose image \(\sum_{i\in T}W^O_{(i)}\mathbb R^{d_{head}}\) lies inside the bias space. Its localisation step is an (IA)\(^3\)-type scaling probe, used only to choose the support.

name: MoSLoRA
paper_title: Mixture-of-Subspaces in Low-Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: W=W_0+s\,B\,M\,A,\quad s=\alpha/r\ \text{(LoRA scaling, used in the official code; Eq. 7 omits it)},\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\quad \Delta W=s\textstyle\sum_{i,j=1}^{r}m_{ij}\,b_i\,a_j^{\top};\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen};\ A,M,B\ \text{trained}\quad\big(M=I_r:\ \text{LoRA};\ M=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}I&I\\ I&I\end{smallmatrix}\right]:\ \text{two-subspace mixing}\big)
locus: any linear layer; \(q\), \(k\), \(v\), up and down projections in the LLaMA-3 8B commonsense experiments (Table 7); \(q\), \(k\), \(v\), \(o\), up, down and gate for LLaVA visual instruction tuning (Table 8); also used for SDXL subject-driven generation
structure: Three-factor low-rank update \(B M A\), in which a learnable \(r \times r\) mixer weights all \(r^2\) rank-one 'subspaces' \(b_i a_j^T\). The reachable set is still \(\{\mathrm{rank} \le r\}\), the same as LoRA's, so the mixer changes the parametrization and the optimization, not the expressivity. The gauge symmetry grows from \(GL(r)\) to \(GL(r) \times GL(r)\): \((B, M, A) \sim (BG, G^{-1}MH, H^{-1}A)\) (derived here).
mergeable_reason: \(BMA\) is a single \(d_{out} \times d_{in}\) matrix that folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) (\(A\) Kaiming-uniform; mixer Kaiming-uniform or orthogonal), so \(\Delta W = 0\). A zero-initialized mixer gives all three factors zero gradient and training stalls (paper, Appendix C).
key_idea: Splitting LoRA into rank-one subspaces and mixing them improves results. MoSLoRA generalizes the fixed identity between \(A\) and \(B\) (LoRA), or the fixed butterfly (two-subspace mixing), to a learnable \(r \times r\) mixer, at negligible extra parameters and compute.
results_note: On LLaMA-3 8B commonsense reasoning (8 tasks) it averages 85.6, vs 82.8 for LoRA, 85.0 for DoRA and 84.2 for FLoRA, at about the same parameter count and LoRA-level training time. It also improves LLaVA visual instruction tuning and DreamBooth-style subject-driven generation.
categorical_reading: MoSLoRA is LoRA with a gauge-enlarging middle factor. \(\rho(B,M,A)=W_0+sBMA\) factors through LoRA by \(h=(BM,A)\), and LoRA factors back through it by freezing \(M\). The two simulate each other with the same image and the same \(S_1\), but they are not isomorphic (\(|Q|\) differs by \(r^2\)). Any gain is therefore in the cometric \(K=D\rho\,\Lambda\,D\rho^\top\), not in expressivity.

name: NOAH
paper_title: Neural Prompt Search
formula_latex: \text{block } l:\ \ x\leftarrow[\mathrm{CLS},P_l,E]\ (P_l\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_l\times d},\ l<D_V);\ \ Q=W_qx+s\,B^{l}_{q}A^{l}_{q}x,\ K=W_kx+s\,B^{l}_{k}A^{l}_{k}x\ \ (\text{rank } r^{L}_l,\ l<D_L);\ \ h\leftarrow h+W^{l}_{up}\,\phi\big(W^{l}_{down}h\big)\ \ (\text{width } r^{A}_l,\ l<D_A);\quad a=\big(D_V,D_L,D_A,\{\ell_l,r^{L}_l,r^{A}_l\}\big),\ \ \ell_l,r_l\in\{5,10,50,100\}\ \text{or}\ \{1,5,10\},\ D\in\{3,6,9,12\};\ \text{one-shot supernet (AutoFormer weight entanglement), then evolutionary search under a parameter cap};\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: \textstyle\sum_{l<D_V}\ell_l\,d+\sum_{l<D_L}4d\,r^{L}_l+\sum_{l<D_A}2d\,r^{A}_l\ (+\text{biases, head});\ \text{capped at }0.64\text{M on ViT-B/16 (found subnets average }0.43\text{M)}
locus: every ViT-B/16 block up to each module's searched depth: VPT-Deep tokens at the block input, LoRA on \(W_q\) and \(W_k\) as written in Eq. 3 (the official code instead attaches one rank-\(r\) LoRA to the fused qkv projection, \(d \to 3d\), with no scaling; it has the same \(4dr\) parameter count), and a bottleneck adapter applied residually to the MLP output
structure: Per-dataset architecture search over a product design space. Each point combines three PEFT modules, each truncated in depth and in width. With weight entanglement, every candidate is a coordinate restriction (a prefix slice) of one supernet's maximal-width modules. The found subnet is a sum of an additive part (LoRA), a serial insertion (adapter) and an input augmentation (VPT).
mergeable_reason: Only the LoRA part folds into \(W_q\) and \(W_k\); the adapter and prompt parts remain at inference unless the search gives them zero depth.
identity_at_init: No identity at init. LoRA starts at zero (LoRA_b = 0, LoRA_a Kaiming-uniform in the official code), but the adapter's down- and up-projections are both Xavier-uniform initialized (model/module/adapter_super.py), so its output is not near zero, and VPT tokens (also Xavier-uniform) change attention from the first step. The paper does not discuss this.
key_idea: NOAH treats Adapter, LoRA and VPT as interchangeable 'prompt modules' and lets neural architecture search decide, per downstream dataset, which modules to use, at what depth and with what width, instead of hand-designing a PEFT recipe.
results_note: On VTAB-1k with ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-22K) it averages 75.5% with 0.43M parameters, vs 74.5 for LoRA, 73.9 for Adapter, 72.0 for VPT and 68.9 for full fine-tuning. It is also stronger in few-shot learning and ImageNet domain generalization.
categorical_reading: NOAH searches the truncations of one supernet \(\mathrm{LoRA}\oplus\mathrm{Adapter}\oplus\mathrm{VPT}\). For LoRA and adapter widths, a prefix slice is an A2 sub-object (freeze the trailing coordinates at 0). For VPT it is not: dropping a token is not freezing it at a base value, because a zero token still draws attention mass. The candidates therefore form a lattice of sub-objects only along the LoRA and adapter axes, and the chosen object is an unpointed extension.

name: AutoPEFT
full_name: AutoPEFT (automatic, multi-objective configuration search for PEFT)
paper_title: AutoPEFT: Automatic Configuration Search for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: \text{layer } l\ (m_l=1):\ \ h\leftarrow F(x)+W^{up}_{SA}\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(W^{down}_{SA}F(x)\big)+W^{up}_{PA}\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(W^{down}_{PA}x\big),\ \ K'=[P_k;K],\ V'=[P_v;V],\ P_k,P_v\in\mathbb{R}^{L_{PT}\times d};\quad a=\big(m\in\{0,1\}^{L},\,D_{SA},\,D_{PA},\,L_{PT}\big)\in\mathcal{A};\quad \max_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\big(f(a,W^\ast(a)),\,-g(a)\big)\ \ \text{s.t.}\ W^\ast(a)=\arg\min_W\mathcal{L}_{train}(a,W)\ \ \text{(SAAS-GP surrogate, NEHVI acquisition, low-fidelity inner loop)};\ \text{PLM frozen}
trainable_params: \textstyle\sum_{l}m_l\,\big(2d\,D_{SA}+2d\,D_{PA}+2L_{PT}\,d\big)\ (+\text{biases})
locus: in each selected Transformer layer: a serial adapter after the FFN, a parallel adapter around the FFN, and prefixes on the attention keys/values
structure: Bi-level, bi-objective search (performance vs parameter count) over a discrete product space: a layer mask times three module sizes on a log scale, where 0 means the module is absent. The answer is a Pareto front of configurations, not a single PEFT. Each configuration is a sum of serial and parallel bottleneck insertions plus key/value prefixes.
mergeable_reason: ReLU bottleneck adapters and prefix slots cannot be folded into the frozen weights.
identity_at_init: Not addressed. Modules use AdapterHub defaults (near-zero adapter outputs), while prefixes change attention from the first step.
key_idea: Instead of hand-picking a PEFT recipe, AutoPEFT searches jointly over which layers get modules and how large the serial adapter, parallel adapter and prefix are. It uses multi-objective Bayesian optimization with cheap low-fidelity evaluations, and the discovered configurations transfer across tasks and models.
results_note: On GLUE with BERT-base, a configuration searched on RTE (0.76% parameters) averages 83.17 vs 83.15 for full fine-tuning, beating serial and parallel adapters, prefix-tuning, LoRA, UniPELT, MAM and AdaMix; per-task search reaches 83.49. Gains are similar on SuperGLUE, RoBERTa-large and T5, where it is compared with S3PET.
categorical_reading: AutoPEFT optimises over a finite grid of objects \(\mathrm{SA}_{D_{SA}}\oplus\mathrm{PA}_{D_{PA}}\oplus\mathrm{Prefix}_{L_{PT}}\) on a layer mask and returns a Pareto front in (performance, budget \(|M|\)). Size 0 removes a module, so the grid contains Pfeiffer-adapter, parallel-adapter and prefix-tuning objects as faces. The base-point type of a configuration jumps from neutral to unpointed as soon as \(L_{PT}>0\).

name: Laplace-LoRA
full_name: Laplace-LoRA (Bayesian low-rank adaptation via a post-hoc Laplace approximation over LoRA parameters)
paper_title: Bayesian Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
formula_latex: W=W_0+BA,\ \ \theta=\{A,B\}\ \text{fit by standard LoRA}\to\theta_{MAP};\quad p(\theta\mid\mathcal{D})\approx\mathcal{N}(\theta_{MAP},\Sigma),\ \ \Sigma^{-1}=\textstyle\sum_{n}\mathbb{E}\big[(a\,a^{\top})\otimes(g\,g^{\top})\big]+\lambda I\ \ \text{(K-FAC per factor, large Kronecker factor stored at rank } n_{kfac});\quad f(x_\ast)\sim\mathcal{N}\big(f_{\theta_{MAP}}(x_\ast),\,J_\ast\Sigma J_\ast^{\top}\big),\ \ J_\ast=\nabla_\theta f_\theta(x_\ast)\big|_{\theta_{MAP}};\ \ \lambda\ \text{maximizes the Laplace marginal likelihood};\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r\,(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(MAP, as LoRA)}\ +\ \text{post-hoc K-FAC statistics (not trained)}\approx n_{kfac}(d_{in}+d_{out})+2r^{2}\ \text{per matrix}\ +\ \text{one prior precision }\lambda
locus: LoRA factors on \(W_q\), \(W_v\) and the output (LM-head) layer in the paper; the LLLA variant uses only the output-layer LoRA
structure: A Gaussian (Laplace) posterior over the LoRA factors, treated as two separate linear layers with Kronecker-factored precision (the \(d\times d\) factor kept low-rank). Prediction integrates the linearized network over this posterior: a Bayesian model average over adapter parameters with the base weights fixed.
mergeable_reason: The posterior mean \(BA\) merges into \(W_0\), but the calibrated predictive needs the Jacobian with respect to the LoRA factors and the stored covariance at test time.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (\(B = 0\)) for the MAP fit. The Laplace step is post-hoc and leaves the mean unchanged.
key_idea: Fine-tuned LLMs are overconfident on small datasets. After ordinary LoRA training, Laplace-LoRA fits a Laplace approximation over the LoRA parameters only, with low-rank K-FAC so memory stays LoRA-sized, and predicts with the linearized model. This calibrates the model without a validation set.
results_note: On six commonsense reasoning tasks with LLaMA2-7B, full Laplace-LoRA keeps accuracy while greatly reducing ECE and NLL relative to MAP, MC dropout, checkpoint ensembles and LoRA ensembles. This holds under distribution shift too, at about 1-5% extra memory.
categorical_reading: Laplace-LoRA turns a trained point of LoRA into a Gaussian family over \(Q\), pushed forward by the linearised realisation. The Gaussian lives on \(Q\) rather than on \(\Theta\), and its isotropic prior is not gauge-invariant. As a result the predictive keeps only the isometric \(\mathfrak{so}(r)\) half of LoRA's gauge, and the \(\mathrm{Sym}_r\) half changes the calibrated uncertainty while fixing the mean.

name: BLoB
paper_title: BLoB: Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation by Backpropagation for Large Language Models
formula_latex: h = W_0x + B A x,\quad A\sim q(A\mid M,\Omega)=\prod_{ij}\mathcal{N}(A_{ij}\mid M_{ij},\Omega_{ij}^2),\ \Omega_{ij}=G_{ij}^2,\ B\ \text{deterministic};\quad \min_{M,G,B}\ -\mathbb{E}_{q(A)}\big[\log P(\mathcal{D}\mid A,B)\big]+\mathrm{KL}\big[q(A)\,\Vert\,\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_p^2 I)\big];\quad \text{equivalently } q(\mathrm{vec}\,W)=\mathcal{N}\big(\mathrm{vec}(W_0+BM),\,(I_{d_{in}}\otimes B)\,\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{vec}\,\Omega)^2\,(I_{d_{in}}\otimes B^{\top})\big);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}; M,G,B\ \text{trained}
locus: LoRA-targeted linear layers (paper: \(W_q\), \(W_v\) of every attention layer plus the output layer of Llama2-7B; RoBERTa for classification)
structure: Stochastic low-rank update \(\Delta W = BA\) in which only the down-projection \(A\) is a random matrix with a mean-field Gaussian posterior (mean \(M\), std \(\Omega = G^{\circ 2}\)); \(B\) is a point estimate. The induced full-weight posterior is a degenerate Gaussian centred at \(W_0 + BM\) whose covariance \((I\otimes B)\,\mathrm{diag}(\Omega)^2(I\otimes B^\top)\) has rank at most \(r\,d_{in}\). The prior is a matching low-rank Gaussian, so the full-weight KL reduces exactly to the KL on \(A\). Sampling uses Flipout restricted to \(A\).
mergeable_reason: The posterior mean \(W_0 + BM\) can be merged into \(W_0\) (BLoB with \(N=0\) samples), but the Bayesian predictive that gives the calibration gains averages \(N\) (default 10) sampled \(A\) matrices, and this cannot be folded into one weight.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\), as in LoRA. The mean \(M\) of \(A\) is uniform-Kaiming and \(G \sim \mathcal{U}(\epsilon/\sqrt2,\epsilon)\). The sampled update \(B A\) is therefore exactly zero at initialization. The authors fix the variance of \(B\) to 0 for this reason: a stochastic \(B\) would make the early forward passes noisy.
key_idea: BLoB does variational Bayes inside the LoRA subspace and trains the posterior mean and variance jointly during fine-tuning, instead of adding a Laplace approximation afterwards. Only \(A\) is made stochastic (asymmetric Bayesianization), and the prior is designed so that the full-weight ELBO equals a cheap ELBO on \(A\). The posterior std is parameterized as \(G\) squared for fast KL convergence, and LoRA-Flipout decorrelates the samples within a mini-batch.
results_note: On Llama2-7B over six commonsense tasks, BLoB (\(N=10\) samples) keeps accuracy close to MLE-LoRA while cutting ECE sharply (e.g. WG-S 29.8% to 9.4%, ARC-C 29.0% to 9.6%); it also improves NLL over MC-dropout, ensembles, BBB and Laplace-LoRA on most datasets, and the gains extend to OOD shifts.
categorical_reading: BLoB is a family over a Gaussian noise space whose samples all lie in one linear sub-object \(\mathrm{FB}(B)\) of LoRA. Making only \(A\) stochastic keeps \(\rho\) affine in the random variable, so the induced weight posterior is an honest, degenerate Gaussian. Because it is trained jointly, its symmetry is the monomial part of \(GL_r\). Laplace-LoRA is its post-hoc counterpart, as LoraHub is to Poly.

name: ModuLoRA
paper_title: ModuLoRA: Finetuning 2-Bit LLMs on Consumer GPUs by Integrating with Modular Quantizers
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: every linear layer of the quantized LLM (LLaMA, OPT, BLOOM up to 65B)
structure: Low-rank additive update \(\Delta W = BA\) on top of a frozen, quantizer-agnostic low-precision weight \(\hat W = \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{Q}(W_0))\). The quantizer is a black-box module that only has to expose dequantization (or a vector-by-quantized-matrix product). Memory is saved by recomputing \(\hat W\) row by row or layer by layer in both the forward and the backward pass, so only one dequantized matrix is ever resident.
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) can be added exactly to a high-precision copy of \(\hat W\). Keeping the 2-4-bit format would require re-running the quantizer on \(\hat W + BA\), which is lossy.
identity_at_init: \(A\) and \(B\) use the LoRA initialization of Hu et al. (\(B = 0\)), so at step 0 the model equals the quantized model \(\hat W\). That is the original \(W_0\) only up to quantization error, and ModuLoRA, unlike LoftQ, does not try to compensate for that error.
key_idea: The quantizer is decoupled from the adapter. The forward and backward passes need only dequantization, which is recomputed on the fly and never stored, so LoRA runs on top of any state-of-the-art PTQ method. This made LoRA fine-tuning of 2-bit (QuIP#) and 3-bit (OPTQ) 65B LLMs possible on a single 24-48 GB GPU.
results_note: A 4-bit LLaMA-65B fine-tuned with ModuLoRA set a then state-of-the-art ROUGE on SAMSum. 3-bit and 4-bit ModuLoRA models outperform 8-bit bitsandbytes LoRA and 4-bit QLoRA across the 7B-65B range, and 2-bit QuIP# models match them.
categorical_reading: ModuLoRA is the family \(\kappa\mapsto\mathrm{LoRA}_r(\kappa\theta_0)\) over all quantisers, not just NF4. Additive families commute with translation, so changing the quantiser only moves the base point and its defect \(e\). Its real contribution is on the lens side: the backward pass recomputes \(\hat W\) instead of caching it (Obs IV.4), which changes memory, not the object.

name: SLTrain
paper_title: SLTrain: a sparse plus low-rank approach for parameter and memory efficient pretraining
formula_latex: \text{pretraining: } W=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA+S;\quad \text{fine-tuning (SLTrain-FT): } W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA+S;\quad S=\mathrm{scatter}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mathcal{V}),\ \mathcal{I}\ \text{uniformly random and fixed},\ |\mathcal{I}|=\delta\,d_{out}d_{in};\quad h=\big(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\oplus_{\mathcal{I}}\mathcal{V}\big)x,\ \nabla_{\mathcal{V}}\mathcal{L}=(\nabla_h\mathcal{L}\,x^{\top})_{\mathcal{I}};\ B,A,\mathcal{V}\ \text{trained}, \mathcal{I}\ \text{and (FT) } W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+\delta\,d_{in}d_{out}
locus: all attention and MLP linear layers (LLaMA 60M-7B pretraining; RoBERTa-base GLUE for SLTrain-FT)
structure: Sum of a rank-\(r\) factorization and a sparse matrix whose support is a uniformly random index set fixed before training; only the values on that support are learned. Stored as \((B, A, \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{V})\); the dense \(BA \oplus_{\mathcal{I}} \mathcal{V}\) is formed transiently in each forward/backward and never saved. With \(\delta = \Omega(\log n/n)\), \(BA+S\) is full rank w.h.p. (Prop. 1), so the low-rank bottleneck is lifted at negligible cost.
mergeable_reason: In the fine-tuning form, both \(BA\) and \(S\) are dense additive terms that fold into \(W_0\). In pretraining the factors are kept on purpose to save memory, although they can also be densified into a single \(W\) for standard inference.
identity_at_init: The low-rank part uses the LoRA init (\(A\) Kaiming, \(B = 0\)), and the sparse values are drawn uniformly from \([-1/\sqrt{d_{in}}, 1/\sqrt{d_{in}}]\), which suits pretraining from scratch. For SLTrain-FT, Appendix G only says \(B\), \(A\) and \(S\) are learned 'as in Section 3.2', which implies the same non-zero uniform init for \(S\); the paper never states a zero init, so exact identity at init is not guaranteed. The public code supports pretraining only (SpLoRaLinear 'cannot be used for fine-tune').
key_idea: Low-rank and sparse are complementary parsimonies: low rank keeps the top subspace, and a random-support sparse matrix captures the small, evenly spread residual. A fixed random support needs no stored mask, so the memory cost is only \(O(\mathrm{nnz})\), and a low-rank model gains near-full-rank capacity for pretraining.
results_note: SLTrain pretrains LLaMA 60M-7B on C4 with perplexity close to full-rank training and far better than pure low-rank and ReLoRA at the same rank, while using fewer parameters; it is slightly behind GaLore at 130M-1B (e.g. 1B: 16.14 vs 15.64 PPL, full-rank 15.56) and slightly ahead at 60M (34.15 vs 34.88). With 8-bit optimizer states and per-layer updates it uses 51/58/73% less memory than full-rank Adam for 350M/1B/7B and 29/34/17% less than GaLore.
categorical_reading: SLTrain is the \(\oplus\)-word \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{Mask}_{\mathcal I}\) with a uniformly random frozen mask, i.e. RoSA with the support drawn instead of selected. The random sparse summand lifts \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\)'s rank obstruction (O2) at cost \(O(\mathrm{nnz})\), but its non-zero init moves the base point.

name: MEFT
paper_title: Make Pre-trained Model Reversible: From Parameter to Memory Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: h^1_n=\lambda h^1_{n-1}+\mathcal{F}_n(h^2_{n-1}),\quad h^2_n=\beta h^2_{n-1}+\mathcal{G}_n(h^1_n);\qquad h^2_{n-1}=\big(h^2_n-\mathcal{G}_n(h^1_n)\big)/\beta,\quad h^1_{n-1}=\big(h^1_n-\mathcal{F}_n(h^2_{n-1})\big)/\lambda;\ \ \text{MEFT}_1:\ \mathcal{F}_n=f_n\!+\!\text{adapter},\ \mathcal{G}_n=\text{adapter},\ \lambda\!\to\!0\ (\beta=1),\ \text{swap streams};\ \ \text{MEFT}_2:\ \mathcal{F}_n=\text{adapter},\ \mathcal{G}_n=f_n\!+\!\text{adapter},\ \lambda=1,\ \beta\!\to\!0,\ \text{swap};\ \ \text{MEFT}_3:\ \mathcal{F}_n=\text{Attn}_n\!+\!\text{adapter},\ \mathcal{G}_n=\text{MLP}_n\!+\!\text{adapter},\ \lambda=\beta\!\to\!0,\ \text{no swap};\ \ (\text{scaling sent to }0\text{ set to }0.1);\ h^1_0=h^2_0=h_0,\ \text{head on }(h^1_L+h^2_L)/2;\ \text{PLM frozen, only adapters } W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: \approx 4\,d\,r\ \text{per Transformer layer (two bottleneck adapters)},\ \text{i.e. }\approx 4\,d\,r\,L\ \text{per model plus the task head}
locus: every Transformer layer, which is recast as a two-stream reversible coupling block; adapters sit parallel to the FFN inside the pretrained sub-block and stand alone as the other coupling function
structure: Bottleneck adapters inserted so that each pretrained layer becomes the \(\mathcal{F}\) or \(\mathcal{G}\) of an additive RevNet coupling with scalings \(\lambda\), \(\beta\) (0.1 for the coupling scaled toward 0) and an optional stream swap. The layer map is then a bijection \((h^1,h^2)\mapsto({h^1}',{h^2}')\) with an explicit inverse, so activations are recomputed backwards from the outputs and activation memory is \(O(1)\) in depth instead of \(O(L)\).
mergeable_reason: Inference keeps the two-stream reversible topology, the \(\lambda/\beta\) scalings and the nonlinear bottleneck adapters, so the result cannot be folded back into the original single-stream PLM weights.
identity_at_init: Approximate only. Adapters are initialized with \(W_{down}\), \(W_{up} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.02^2)\) rather than zero, and the scaling of the coupling sent toward 0 is 0.1 rather than exactly 0, so one stream reproduces the PLM's hidden state \(h_n\) up to a small perturbation (the 'starting point hypothesis'). The stream swap keeps the input of each pretrained block continuous with the original network.
key_idea: MEFT turns a pretrained, non-reversible Transformer into a reversible one without re-pretraining. Each pretrained layer becomes one coupling function and an adapter becomes the other. The coupling scalars and the stream order are chosen so the network starts out computing what the PLM computed. Backpropagation then recomputes activations instead of caching them, which reduces activation memory as well as parameter count.
results_note: On GLUE with BERT-base, RoBERTa-large and BART-large, MEFT matches full fine-tuning while training about 0.2% of the parameters and saving up to 84% of activation memory. On OPT-1.3B question answering, MEFT1 is within 0.3 points of full fine-tuning at about half its activation memory (0.64% trainable parameters) and comparable to LoRA at 65% of LoRA's activation memory.
categorical_reading: MEFT embeds the PLM into a reversible two-stream architecture. The would-be neutral point of this extension (\(\lambda=0\)) is exactly where the coupling stops being invertible. MEFT therefore lives in the unpointed slice with a small fixed defect. Its payoff is on the lens side: reversibility lets the backward pass recompute activations instead of storing them (Obs IV.4).

name: Spectrum
paper_title: Spectrum: Targeted Training on Signal to Noise Ratio
formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^{\top},\ \ \hat\sigma=\mathrm{IQR}(\{\sigma_k\})/1.349,\ \ \varepsilon=\hat\sigma\big(1+\sqrt{\beta}\big),\ \beta=\tfrac{\min(d_{out},d_{in})}{\max(d_{out},d_{in})}\ \text{(Marchenko-Pastur edge)};\quad \mathrm{SNR}(W_0)=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\max}}\,\frac{\sum_{\sigma_k>\varepsilon}\sigma_k}{\sum_{\sigma_k\le\varepsilon}\sigma_k};\quad \mathcal{S}=\text{top-}p\%\ \text{matrices by SNR within each module type};\ \ W=W_0+\Delta W\cdot\mathbb{1}[W\in\mathcal{S}]\ \text{(selected matrices fully trained, the rest frozen)}
trainable_params: \sum_{W\in\mathcal{S}} d_{out}d_{in}\ +\ |\mathcal{V}|\,d_{model}\,(\text{embed\_tokens})\ +\ d_{model}|\mathcal{V}|\,(\text{lm\_head})\ \ (\mathcal{S}=\text{top-}p\%\ \text{of each module type; default } p=25\text{ in the paper, 50 in the script; the official script always unfreezes embeddings and lm\_head})
locus: whole weight matrices of a chosen subset of layers, ranked separately within each module type (q/k/v/o projections, MLP gate/up/down); the official script additionally always unfreezes model.embed_tokens and lm_head (not SNR-ranked)
structure: Coordinate projection onto a union of whole weight matrices chosen before training by a data-free spectral score: the Marchenko-Pastur bulk edge of each \(W_0\) splits its singular values into signal and noise, and matrices with the highest normalized signal/noise mass are unfrozen. Updates inside a selected matrix are dense and full-rank.
mergeable_reason: Selected weights are fine-tuned in place, so the result is an ordinary checkpoint with the original architecture and cost.
identity_at_init: Exact: no parameters are added, and training starts from the pretrained weights. The selection only decides which matrices may move.
key_idea: Spectrum chooses which layers to fine-tune from the pretrained weights alone. Random-matrix theory gives a noise threshold for each matrix's singular values, and only the matrices with the highest signal-to-noise ratio, about the top 25-50% per module type, are trained in full precision. This keeps much of full fine-tuning's quality at reduced memory and time, especially under ZeRO-3/FSDP sharding.
results_note: On Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B (airoboros-3.1), Spectrum-50/25 are competitive with full fine-tuning (sometimes better) and above QLoRA on most reported benchmarks. For Llama-3-8B under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 they use 17.72%/23.05% less per-GPU memory than full fine-tuning (QLoRA: 14.73%) and train 15.48%/36.78% faster; on a single GPU QLoRA uses less memory.
categorical_reading: Spectrum is a Lin coordinate block of whole matrices, chosen data-free by a Marchenko–Pastur signal-to-noise score of \(W_0\). Its image is of the same type as surgical fine-tuning's. What is new is the selection rule: it depends on \(W_0\) only through its spectrum, so it is natural only under orthogonal changes of basis.

name: LoRA-Dash
paper_title: Unleashing the Power of Task-Specific Directions in Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning
formula_latex: \text{pre-launch } (t=100\text{ LoRA steps}):\ W_0=\textstyle\sum_i\sigma_i u_i v_i^{\top},\ \ \delta_i=\Big|\frac{u_i^{\top}\Delta W\,v_i}{\sigma_i+\epsilon}\Big|,\ \Delta W=BA,\ \ \{\bar u_k\bar v_k^{\top}\}_{k=1}^{s}=\text{top-}s\ \text{by }\delta_i;\quad \text{dash: } W=W_0+BA+\textstyle\sum_{k=1}^{s}\Delta\sigma_k\,\bar u_k\bar v_k^{\top},\ \ \Delta\sigma_k\leftarrow 0;\ W_0,\bar u_k,\bar v_k\ \text{frozen}; A,B,\Delta\sigma\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+s\quad(s=8\ \text{by default})
locus: LoRA-targeted linear layers (\(W_q\), \(W_k\), \(W_v\), \(W_{up}\), \(W_{down}\) in the LLaMA commonsense setting; also DeBERTa and SDXL)
structure: LoRA update plus a diagonal update in \(W_0\)'s own singular basis restricted to \(s\) core directions \(u_k v_k^\top\). These are the task-specific directions (TSDs) whose coordinates change the most relative to their singular value, estimated from LoRA's \(\Delta W\) after a short warm-up. The second term is a learned \(s\)-dimensional diagonal perturbation of \(W_0\)'s spectrum along data-chosen singular pairs.
mergeable_reason: Both \(BA\) and \(\sum_k \Delta\sigma_k \bar u_k \bar v_k^\top\) are dense additive matrices that fold into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Exact. LoRA starts at \(B = 0\), and the dash coefficients \(\Delta\sigma_k\) are zero-initialized when the dash phase begins. The method needs a one-off SVD of each \(W_0\), and the directions are chosen from the LoRA update after about 100 steps. The companion LoRA-Init/LoRA-TSD variants instead initialize \(A\) and \(B\) from the top-\(r\) TSDs, which is a PiSSA-style split.
key_idea: LoRA's own paper says \(\Delta W\) amplifies directions of \(W_0\) that matter for the task. LoRA-Dash defines these as the core singular directions of \(W_0\) with the largest relative coordinate change, and shows that a briefly trained LoRA already identifies them with high precision. It then gives each identified direction its own scalar so its change can grow beyond what the low-rank product allows.
results_note: On commonsense reasoning, LoRA-Dash improves LoRA across LLaMA-7B, LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B (e.g. LLaMA3-8B \(r=32\): 80.8 to 85.4 average) with only \(s\) extra scalars per matrix; gains are also reported on GLUE (DeBERTaV3) and subject-driven SDXL generation.
categorical_reading: LoRA-Dash is \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\) a frozen-frame spectral line method: SVDiff on \(s\) singular pairs, selected from LoRA's own early trajectory. The dash summand moves along directions already present in \(W_0\)'s spectrum, so it supplies \(s\) dimensions of 'amplification' on which \(BA\) would otherwise spend rank.

name: LCM-LoRA
full_name: Latent Consistency Model LoRA (universal acceleration module)
paper_title: LCM-LoRA: A Universal Stable-Diffusion Acceleration Module
hf_peft_config: LoraConfig (plain LoRA weights; loaded in diffusers through the PEFT backend with load_lora_weights(..., adapter_name='lcm') and combined via set_adapters(['lcm','style'], adapter_weights=[1.0, 0.8]))
formula_latex: \text{train: } W=W_0+B_{\mathrm{LCM}}A_{\mathrm{LCM}}\ \text{on the U-Net, minimizing the latent consistency distillation loss } d\big(f_\theta(z_{t_{n+k}},\omega,c,t_{n+k}),\,f_{\theta^-}(\hat z^{\Psi,\omega}_{t_n},\omega,c,t_n)\big),\ W_0\ \text{frozen};\quad \text{use: } \theta'=\theta_{\mathrm{pre}}+\lambda_1\tau'+\lambda_2\tau_{\mathrm{LCM}},\ \text{i.e. } W=W_0+\lambda_1 B'A'+\lambda_2 B_{\mathrm{LCM}}A_{\mathrm{LCM}}\ \ (\lambda_1=0.8,\lambda_2=1.0),\ \text{no further training}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted linear},\ r(c_{in}k_hk_w+c_{out})\ \text{per adapted conv};\ r=64\ \text{(67.5M for SD-v1.5, 105M for SSD-1B, 197M for SDXL)}
locus: all LoRA-targeted modules of the Stable Diffusion U-Net (SD-v1.5, SSD-1B, SDXL): attention q/k/v/out, proj_in/proj_out and feed-forward linears, plus ResNet conv1/conv2/conv_shortcut, down/upsampler convolutions and time_emb_proj (diffusers LCM-LoRA training script; the released checkpoints contain conv LoRA tensors); applied to fine-tuned community checkpoints of the same base
structure: Two additive low-rank task vectors on a shared base: an 'acceleration vector' \(\tau_{LCM} = B_{LCM}A_{LCM}\), trained by consistency distillation of the probability-flow ODE, and a 'style vector' \(\tau' = B'A'\), trained by ordinary fine-tuning. They are combined linearly with fixed scalars in weight space, which is task arithmetic in the commutative monoid of additive low-rank updates. The result is a few-step (2-8) sampler for any style.
mergeable_reason: Both LoRAs and their weighted sum are additive low-rank terms that fuse into the U-Net weights, giving a standard model run with the LCM scheduler.
identity_at_init: LoRA init (\(B = 0\)) during distillation, so training starts from the teacher diffusion model. At composition time no training occurs, and the base is recovered with \(\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 = 0\).
key_idea: Few-step sampling can be distilled into a LoRA instead of a full model. That acceleration LoRA works as a portable 'neural PF-ODE solver': adding it to the base or to a fine-tuned checkpoint of the same base, or to any style LoRA, gives 4-step generation in that style with no extra training. It is a widely cited example of skill arithmetic between LoRA modules.
categorical_reading: LCM-LoRA is task arithmetic with two LoRA task vectors, one of which encodes a sampler (a distilled PF-ODE solver) rather than a skill. It ports to fine-tuned checkpoints of the same base because LoRA is additive (Def I.2, Prop V.2(a)). Since \(\delta_{\rm LCM}\) does not depend on \(\theta_0\), the same update is a method at every base \(\theta_{\rm pre}+\tau'\).

name: Concept Sliders
full_name: Concept Sliders (attribute-direction LoRA with a continuous inference-time strength)
paper_title: Concept Sliders: LoRA Adaptors for Precise Control in Diffusion Models
formula_latex: W(\alpha)=W_0+\alpha\,BA,\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}\ \text{(slider strength, set at inference)};\ \ \text{text sliders regress the slider model onto the frozen model's guided score: }\epsilon_{\theta^{*}}(X,c_t,t)\leftarrow\epsilon_{\theta}(X,c_t,t)+\eta\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\big(\epsilon_{\theta}(X,(c_{+},p),t)-\epsilon_{\theta}(X,(c_{-},p),t)\big);\ \ \text{image-pair sliders: }\min_{A,B}\|\epsilon_{\theta_{-}}(x^{A}_t,\varnothing,t)-\epsilon\|^2+\|\epsilon_{\theta_{+}}(x^{B}_t,\varnothing,t)-\epsilon\|^2\ (\theta_{\pm}:\ \alpha=\pm1);\ \ \text{composition: }W=W_0+\sum_k\alpha_kB_kA_k;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix per slider (default } r=4\text{)}
locus: LoRA on the diffusion U-Net (SD-XL, SD-1.4); the official text-slider config adapts all layers except cross-attention ('noxattn'), including \(3\times3\) conv layers ('c3lier'), with rank 4 and \(\alpha\) 1, so the code applies the fixed internal scale \(\alpha/r = 1/4\) times the slider multiplier; at inference the slider is switched on only after the first \(t\) denoising steps (SDEdit-style)
structure: Each slider is a rank-\(r\) ray \(\{W_0+\alpha BA:\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\}\) through \(W_0\), i.e. a one-parameter additive family in weight space; \(K\) sliders span the affine slice \(W_0+\mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{B_kA_k\}_{k=1}^{K}\), navigated by the coefficient vector (\(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_K\)). The training target is an output-space (score) contrast \(\epsilon(c_+)-\epsilon(c_-)\) distilled into this weight direction.
mergeable_reason: For any fixed strength vector the update \(\sum_k \alpha_k B_k A_k\) is a plain matrix that folds into \(W_0\); the SDEdit-style schedule only switches between \(W_0\) and the merged weights across denoising steps.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (\(B = 0\)); in addition, \(\alpha = 0\) recovers the base model exactly at any time after training, since every slider is a ray through \(W_0\).
key_idea: Train a LoRA whose direction encodes a single attribute, using the frozen model's own guidance-style score difference between opposing prompts (with preservation prompts to disentangle) or before/after image pairs as the target; scaling the LoRA multiplier then dials the attribute continuously up or down, and sliders add.
results_note: On SD-XL, a 'fix hands' slider cut the rater-judged rate of distorted hands from 62% to 22%, the disentanglement objective lowered attribute interference from 0.36 to 0.10, and up to 50 sliders were composed in one model.
categorical_reading: A concept slider is a ruling line of LoRA's cone through a trained point. \(\alpha\mapsto W_0+\alpha BA\) is the scalar action that every cone with vertex \(\theta_0\) carries, exposed as a user control. \(K\) sliders give the \(\oplus\) of \(K\) frozen line methods inside \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{Kr}\), i.e. task arithmetic with low-rank task vectors.

name: IC-LoRA
paper_title: In-Context LoRA for Diffusion Transformers
formula_latex: W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\ \text{in the FLUX.1-dev DiT},\ r=\alpha=16\ \text{(official config)};\ \ \text{training input: one composite image }X=[\,x_1\,|\,x_2\,|\cdots|\,x_n\,]\ \text{(n panels concatenated spatially) with one merged caption }c=[c_{\text{set}};c_1;\dots;c_n];\ \ \text{loss: the base model's own flow-matching objective on }(X,c);\ \ \text{image-conditioned use: mask some panels and inpaint them from the rest with SDEdit (training-free)};\ W_0\ \text{and text encoders frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained on 20--100 image sets per task}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix},\ r=16
locus: LoRA on the layers of a text-to-image diffusion transformer (FLUX.1-dev); the task itself is carried by the input format (panel-concatenated image + merged prompt), not by new modules
structure: Plain low-rank \(\Delta W=BA\); the cross-image conditioning is supplied by the DiT's existing full self-attention over the tokens of all panels in one canvas, so the adapter only re-weights an in-context capability the base model already has (no token-routing masks, no extra encoders).
mergeable_reason: The adapter is a standard LoRA on an unchanged DiT, so \(BA\) folds into \(W_0\); the multi-panel behaviour comes from the input canvas and prompt.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (\(B = 0\)) on an unmodified architecture, so the zero adapter is exactly FLUX.1-dev.
key_idea: Text-to-image DiTs can already draw coherent multi-panel images from one merged prompt; concatenating image sets into a single canvas with a joint caption and training a small task-specific LoRA on 20-100 examples activates this in-context ability, and SDEdit-style masking turns it into reference-conditioned generation.
results_note: Qualitative results only: storyboards, font design, portrait photography, home decoration, visual identity and visual effects, each trained for 5,000 steps (batch 4, rank 16) on one A100; no quantitative benchmark is reported.
categorical_reading: IC-LoRA changes nothing in the object: it is LoRA, and the in-context behaviour comes from the base DiT's full attention over a panel canvas. Categorically it is a choice of data distribution on an unchanged input space, which the slice does not see. OminiControl, by contrast, extends the input sequence and gates its LoRA by token.

name: Proxy-Tuning
full_name: Proxy-tuning (decoding-time tuning of a large model through a small tuned/untuned pair)
paper_title: Tuning Language Models by Proxy
formula_latex: p_{\tilde{\mathcal M}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})=\mathrm{softmax}\big[s_{\mathcal M}(X_t\mid x_{<t})+s_{\mathcal M^{+}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})-s_{\mathcal M^{-}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})\big];\ \ \mathcal M:\ \text{large base model (frozen; only its logits are used)},\ \mathcal M^{-}:\ \text{small base model (frozen)},\ \mathcal M^{+}:\ \mathcal M^{-}\ \text{after tuning};\ \text{models must share a vocabulary}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{in }\mathcal M;\ \text{only the small proxy }\mathcal M^{-}\to\mathcal M^{+}\ \text{is tuned (any method, done once)}
locus: next-token logits at decoding time; the large model's weights are never accessed
structure: Output-space (logit) arithmetic: the large model's logit vector is translated by the small model's tuning vector \(s_{\mathcal M^{+}}-s_{\mathcal M^{-}}\), i.e. task arithmetic in logit space, equivalently a product of experts \(\propto p_{\mathcal M}\,p_{\mathcal M^{+}}/p_{\mathcal M^{-}}\) with one expert and one anti-expert (DExperts).
mergeable_reason: Every decoding step needs forward passes of three models; nothing is folded into the large model's weights.
identity_at_init: If the proxy is untuned (\(\mathcal M^+ = \mathcal M^-\)), the offset vanishes and the large model's distribution is recovered exactly.
key_idea: Tune a small model, then add the difference between its tuned and untuned logits to a large (possibly black-box) model's logits at each decoding step, transferring the effect of tuning without touching the large model's weights.
results_note: Steering Llama2-13B and 70B base with Llama2-7B chat/base proxies closed 91.1% and 88.1% of the gap to the true chat models on average over five settings (AlpacaFarm, GSM, ToxiGen, TruthfulQA multiple-choice and open-ended); it was also applied to GPT-3.5 using only its top-5 log-probabilities (+2.3% on RealTimeQA).
categorical_reading: Proxy-tuning is task arithmetic transported from weight space to logit space. The tuning vector \(s_{\mathcal M^+}-s_{\mathcal M^-}\) of a small model is added to a large model's logits, a product of experts \(p_{\mathcal M}p_{\mathcal M^+}/p_{\mathcal M^-}\). Because it acts on realisations, it needs no weight correspondence between the two scales. Trans-LoRA works through \(\Phi_f\) for the same reason.

name: EFT
paper_title: An Emulator for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models using Small Language Models
formula_latex: \pi^{N}_{M}(y\mid x)\propto\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\,\frac{\pi^{M}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)}=\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\exp\big(r^{M}_{\pi}(x,y)\big),\ \ r^{M}_{\pi}=\log\tfrac{\pi^{M}}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}};\ \ \text{sampled per token: }\tilde\pi(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})=\tfrac{1}{Z(x,y_{<t})}\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})\tfrac{\pi^{M}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})};\ \ \text{up-scaling: }N>M\ \text{(large base, small fine-tuned and small base)};\ \text{all models frozen}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{(composes existing pre-trained and fine-tuned checkpoints)}
locus: next-token distributions at sampling time
structure: Reward transport across scales: fine-tuning is viewed as KL-regularized RL, so a fine-tuned model equals its base times \(\exp(\text{implicit reward})\); EFT moves the small-scale implicit reward \(\log(\pi^{M}/\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}})\) onto a large-scale base, a log-linear (logit-additive) composition of three models.
mergeable_reason: Sampling requires the large base and both small models at every step (speculative decoding reduces but does not remove this cost).
identity_at_init: Setting \(N = M\) returns the original fine-tuned policy; an untuned small model (\(\pi^M = \pi^M_{\mathrm{ref}}\)) returns the large base model.
key_idea: Fine-tuning's effect can be isolated as the log-ratio between a fine-tuned model and its base; adding a small model's log-ratio to a large base model emulates fine-tuning the large model, and decouples the scales of pre-training and fine-tuning.
results_note: Averaged over Llama-1, Llama-2 and Falcon on Anthropic-HH and ELI5, up-scaling recovered nearly 70% of the factuality gain of the truly fine-tuned large model (scores normalized so that the small fine-tuned model is 0 and the large fine-tuned model is 1); speculative EFT decoding sped up sampling by nearly 2.5x when up-scaling Llama-2-7B-chat with Llama-2-70B-base.
categorical_reading: EFT reads fine-tuning as a KL-regularised RL update, so a fine-tuned model is its base times \(\exp(r)\). It transports the implicit reward \(r\) from scale \(M\) to scale \(N\) in log-probability space. The per-token rule is Proxy-tuning's. EFT's derivation explains why the transport is meaningful: \(r\) is a base-independent, additive object in log space, as LoRA updates are in weight space.

name: WiSE-FT
paper_title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models
hf_peft_config: peft.helpers.rescale_adapter_scale(model, multiplier=alpha) with alpha in [0,1]: LoRA-adapter form only (scales Delta W toward W_0, which the PEFT docstring calls strictly equivalent to WiSE-FT); heads trained via modules_to_save are not interpolated
formula_latex: \theta_{\alpha}=(1-\alpha)\,\theta_0+\alpha\,\theta_1=\theta_0+\alpha(\theta_1-\theta_0),\ \ \alpha\in[0,1];\ \ \theta_0=[V_{\mathrm{enc}},W_{\text{zero-shot}}]\ \text{(zero-shot CLIP: pre-trained encoder + text-derived head)},\ \theta_1=\text{standard (end-to-end or head-only) fine-tuned weights};\ \ \text{per matrix: }W=W_0+\alpha\,\Delta W;\ \text{only }\alpha\ \text{is chosen post hoc (default }0.5\text{)}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{beyond the underlying fine-tuning (which updates all parameters); one scalar }\alpha
locus: all parameters of the image encoder and the classification head
structure: The segment \(\{\theta_0+\alpha(\theta_1-\theta_0)\}_{\alpha\in[0,1]}\) joining the pre-trained point and the fine-tuned point in weight space (a two-point convex combination); when only the linear head is fine-tuned it coincides with the output-space ensemble \((1-\alpha)f(x,\theta_0)+\alpha f(x,\theta_1)\).
mergeable_reason: The interpolated weights form a single model of the original architecture, so inference costs exactly one model.
identity_at_init: \(\alpha = 0\) returns the zero-shot model and \(\alpha = 1\) the fine-tuned one; for end-to-end fine-tuning the head is initialized with the (temperature-scaled) zero-shot classifier.
key_idea: Zero-shot CLIP is robust under distribution shift while fine-tuning is accurate in distribution; because the two endpoints are linearly connected in weight space, simply interpolating their weights keeps most of both at no extra inference cost.
results_note: On ImageNet and five derived distribution shifts with CLIP, WiSE-FT improved accuracy under shift by 4-6 pp over prior work while raising ImageNet accuracy by 1.6 pp.
categorical_reading: WiSE-FT is task arithmetic with one task vector and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\): the segment from the zero-shot point to the fine-tuned point. When only the head is tuned, the segment is also an output ensemble, because \(f\) is linear in the head. Otherwise its success rests on linear mode connectivity, a property of \(\Phi_f\) along the segment rather than of the object.

name: Linear probing
full_name: Linear probing (head-only tuning on frozen pre-trained features)
paper_title: DeCAF: A Deep Convolutional Activation Feature for Generic Visual Recognition
formula_latex: f(x)=V^{\top}g_{B_0}(x)\ (+\,b),\ \ B_0\ \text{(entire pre-trained backbone) frozen},\ \ V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times K}\ \text{new linear head, trained by }\min_{V}\sum_i\ell\big(V^{\top}g_{B_0}(x_i),y_i\big)+\lambda\|V\|^2\ \text{(convex: logistic regression or linear SVM)}
trainable_params: dK\ (+K)\ \text{for }d\text{-dim features and }K\text{ classes; nothing inside the backbone}
locus: a new final linear classifier on top of frozen penultimate (or intermediate) features
structure: The trivial selection: the trainable coordinate set is exactly the task head, so the backbone map \(g_{B_0}\) is held fixed (the identity on the backbone factor of parameter space); any PEFT method that also trains the head contains linear probing as its restriction to \(\Delta(\text{backbone})=0\).
mergeable_reason: Only the task head is learned and the backbone is untouched, so inference is the original network plus the head that any fine-tuning would need.
identity_at_init: The backbone function is preserved exactly throughout; the head is new (random or zero initialized), so there is no pre-trained output to preserve.
key_idea: Reuse a frozen pre-trained representation and fit only a linear classifier on it; the problem is convex and cheap and keeps the features intact (good out-of-distribution extrapolation), but it cannot adapt the features to the task.
results_note: In DeCAF, a linear SVM on frozen DeCAF6 features (trained with dropout) reached 86.9% mean per-class accuracy on Caltech-101 with 30 images per class, 2.6 points above the prior multi-kernel state of the art (84.3%); Kumar et al. (2022) later found linear probing about 7 points better out of distribution than full fine-tuning on 10 shift datasets (66.2% vs 59.3%).
categorical_reading: Linear probing is the smallest non-trivial selective object: the head block alone. It is a linear sub-object of every method that also trains the head (A2, by freezing everything else). It is convex in \(V\), and the backbone factor stays at its base value, so the features are an absolute invariant.

name: LP-FT
paper_title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
formula_latex: f_{v,B}(x)=v^{\top}g_B(x);\ \ \text{stage 1 (LP): }v_{\mathrm{lp}}=\arg\min_{v}\widehat L(v,B_0)\ \text{with }B=B_0\ \text{frozen};\ \ \text{stage 2 (FT): gradient descent on }\widehat L(v,B)\ \text{over all of }(v,B)\ \text{starting from }(v_{\mathrm{lp}},B_0)
trainable_params: \text{stage 1: }dK;\ \ \text{stage 2: all parameters (full fine-tuning)}
locus: first the linear head only, then every layer
structure: A two-stage training schedule: the head-only (selective) optimum initializes full fine-tuning, which shrinks the head-alignment error \(\varphi^2=|(v_0^{\top}v_\star)^2-(v_\star^{\top}v_\star)^2|\) that otherwise drives large, ID-only feature updates; in the two-layer linear theory, features in directions outside the training span are then not distorted.
mergeable_reason: The output is a single fine-tuned network of the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Stage 2 starts at the pre-trained backbone \(B_0\) with the linear-probing head \(v_{lp}\) instead of a random head, i.e. at the best frozen-feature predictor.
key_idea: With a random head, full fine-tuning distorts pretrained features: gradients from the badly aligned head change the features of in-distribution directions while out-of-distribution directions stay put. Fitting the head by linear probing first removes most of this coupling, so the method gets fine-tuning's in-distribution accuracy and linear probing's robustness.
results_note: Across 10 distribution-shift datasets, LP-FT was about 1% better in distribution and 10% better out of distribution than full fine-tuning, and changed features 10-100x less than fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: LP-FT does not change the object: its second stage is Full FT, the terminal object, with image \(\Theta\). What changes is the base point on the head factor, \((v_0,B_0)\to(v_{\rm lp},B_0)\). The theory's head-alignment error \(\varphi^2\) is a function of that base point, so the gain is a purely dynamical (Exposé III) effect that the image invariants cannot see.

name: FFA-LoRA
paper_title: Improving LoRA in Privacy-preserving Federated Learning
formula_latex: W=W_0+BA_0,\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained (init }0),\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random Gaussian, frozen and shared by all clients};\ \ \text{FedAvg: }B^{+}=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_k\Rightarrow W_0+B^{+}A_0=W_0+\sum_kp_kB_kA_0\ \text{(exact average of client updates, unlike }(\sum_kp_kB_k)(\sum_kp_kA_k));\ \ \text{DP-SGD noise enters only as }\xi_BA_0
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
locus: standard LoRA sites (attention and feed-forward linear layers in the RoBERTa experiments)
structure: \(\Delta W\) ranges over the linear subspace \(\{BA_0:B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\}\) with a fixed random row space, so \(\Delta W\) is linear in the trainable parameters and client aggregation commutes with the parametrization (no cross terms \(B_iA_j\), no quadratic noise term \(\xi_B\xi_A\)).
mergeable_reason: \(BA_0\) is an ordinary matrix that folds into \(W_0\) exactly as in LoRA.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\), so \(\Delta W = 0\); \(A_0\) is random Gaussian and never trained; the scaling factor \(\alpha\) becomes unnecessary (the paper shows LoRA's trajectory tends to FFA-LoRA's as \(\alpha\) goes to infinity).
key_idea: LoRA's bilinear \(BA\) breaks federated averaging (the average of products is not the product of averages) and amplifies differential-privacy noise; freezing the random \(A\) makes the update linear in \(B\), so FedAvg is exact, DP noise is not squared, and communication is halved.
results_note: In a 3-client heterogeneous federated setting with RoBERTa-Large, FFA-LoRA beat LoRA on GLUE tasks with and without DP (e.g. MNLI-m 78.8% vs 39.5% at \(\epsilon = 6\)), and reached 17.12% vs 15.68% on GSM-8K with LLaMA-7B.
categorical_reading: FFA-LoRA is the one-sided method \(\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\), i.e. LoRA-FA v1, chosen for its degree. \(\rho\) is linear in \(B\), so FedAvg commutes with \(\rho\), \((\sum p_kB_k)A_0=\sum p_kB_kA_0\), and DP noise enters linearly. This is Prop V.4(b): exactness needs a shared factor, not just a fixed gauge.

name: FLoRA (federated)
full_name: FLoRA: stacking-based federated fine-tuning with heterogeneous LoRA ranks
paper_title: FLoRA: Federated Fine-Tuning Large Language Models with Heterogeneous Low-Rank Adaptations
formula_latex: \text{client }k:\ W_0+B_kA_k,\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}}\ \text{(heterogeneous }r_k,\ \text{re-initialized every round)};\ \ \text{server: }A=p_1A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus p_KA_K\in\mathbb{R}^{(\sum_kr_k)\times d_{in}}\ \text{(row stacking)},\ B=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_K\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times\sum_kr_k}\ \text{(column stacking)};\ \ BA=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_kA_k,\ \ p_k=|D_k|/\sum_j|D_j|;\ \ \text{clients then update }W_0\leftarrow W_0+BA
trainable_params: r_k(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{on client }k;\ \text{the broadcast global module has }(\textstyle\sum_kr_k)(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{entries}
locus: LoRA on the self-attention layers only (following the original LoRA paper) of TinyLlama-1.1B, Llama-7B and Llama2-7B
structure: Direct sum of the clients' rank spaces \(\mathbb{R}^{r_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathbb{R}^{r_K}\): block concatenation of factors satisfies \([B_1\cdots B_K][A_1;\dots;A_K]=\sum_kB_kA_k\) exactly, so the aggregate factors through \(\sum_kr_k\) dimensions with no cross terms \(B_iA_j\) (which FedAvg of \(A\) and \(B\) separately introduces) and with no constraint that ranks agree.
mergeable_reason: After each round the aggregated \(BA\) is added into the base weights, so the final model is the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Clients re-initialize their local LoRA each round (the official code uses PEFT's LoraConfig, i.e. \(B = 0\)), so each round starts exactly at the current global model.
key_idea: Averaging LoRA's \(A\) and \(B\) separately does not average the products; stacking the client factors instead gives the exact weighted sum of updates and naturally supports clients with different ranks.
results_note: On MMLU and MT-bench with TinyLlama, Llama and Llama2 fine-tuned federatedly on Dolly, Alpaca, Wizard and ShareGPT, FLoRA outperformed FedIT in homogeneous settings and zero-padding in heterogeneous-rank settings (zero-padded FedIT dropped to 7.97% MMLU for Llama on Alpaca).
categorical_reading: FLoRA is a federated ReLoRA. Each round is the \(\oplus\) of the clients' LoRAs, \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_K}\cong\mathrm{LoRA}_{\sum r_k}\) by concatenation (Obs I.7), merged into the base before the next round. Stacking aggregates products, so it is exact and gauge-invariant, and heterogeneous ranks cost nothing. Its server step alone, with the client modules frozen, is the point \(\alpha=p\) of CAT's coefficient family; that is a point of LoRA soups, not an arrow from FLoRA's object, whose factors are trainable.

name: HetLoRA
paper_title: Heterogeneous LoRA for Federated Fine-tuning of On-Device Foundation Models
formula_latex: \text{distribute by truncation: }B_k^{(t,0)}=\overline B^{(t)}_{:,:r_k},\ A_k^{(t,0)}=\overline A^{(t)}_{:r_k,:};\ \ \text{local: }\min_{B_k,A_k}\ \ell(B_k,A_k\mid W_0)+\lambda\,\|B_{k,:,\gamma r_k:r_k}\|\,\|A_{k,\gamma r_k:r_k,:}\|\ (\gamma<1,\ \text{rank self-pruning});\ \ \text{server (zero-pad to }r_{\max}):\ \overline B^{(t+1)}=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_k,\ \overline A^{(t+1)}=\sum_kp_kA_k,\ \ p_k\propto\|B_kA_k\|_F;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r_k(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{on client }k\ (r_{\min}\le r_k\le r_{\max})
locus: LoRA on the self-attention layers only (following the original LoRA paper) of on-device PaLM 2 XXS and XS
structure: Nested rank truncations: client \(k\) sees the leading \(r_k\) columns of \(B\) and rows of \(A\) of a global rank-\(r_{\max}\) pair; aggregation zero-pads and averages factors separately with weights proportional to \(\|B_kA_k\|_F\) (so cross terms remain), and a tail-norm penalty lets clients shrink \(r_k\).
mergeable_reason: The final global pair \(BA\) is a plain low-rank matrix that folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper; clients receive truncations of the current global LoRA pair, so with LoRA's standard \(B = 0\) initialization the first round starts exactly at \(W_0\).
key_idea: Let resource-limited clients train smaller-rank slices of one global LoRA, prune unnecessary rank locally, and weight the server average toward clients whose updates carry more signal.
results_note: With PaLM 2 XXS/XS on multi-session chat (perplexity) and Reddit summarization (RougeL), HetLoRA beat homogeneous-rank LoRA and a reconstruct-then-SVD baseline, slightly below full federated fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: HetLoRA trains one \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_{\max}}\) through a filtration of truncations, as DyLoRA does, except that the truncation levels are the clients' ranks rather than sampled ones. Its aggregation \((\sum p_kB_k)(\sum p_kA_k)\) acts on factors, so it carries LoRA's bilinearity error even in a fixed gauge. FLoRA (stacking) and FFA-LoRA (frozen \(A\)) are the two exact repairs of Prop V.4(b).

name: TinyTL
full_name: Tiny Transfer Learning (bias tuning with lite residual modules)
paper_title: TinyTL: Reduce Memory, Not Parameters for Efficient On-Device Learning
formula_latex: a_{i+1}=\mathcal F_{W}(a_i)+b+\mathcal F_{w_r}\big(a_i'\big),\ \ a_i'=\mathrm{reduce}(a_i)\ \text{(}2\times2\ \text{average pooling)};\ \ W\ \text{frozen (8-bit)},\ \text{trained: biases }b,\ \text{lite residual weights }w_r\ \text{(group convolution, no }1\times1\ \text{expansion, output bilinearly upsampled), classifier head};\ \ \text{rationale: }\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial W}=a_i^{\top}\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial a_{i+1}}\ \text{needs the stored activation }a_i,\ \tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial b}=\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial a_{i+1}}\ \text{does not}
trainable_params: \textstyle\sum_{\text{layers}}d_{out}\ \text{(biases)}+\sum_{\text{blocks}}|w_r|\ \text{(lite residual group convs)}+\text{head}
locus: all bias vectors, one lite residual branch per mobile inverted-bottleneck block, and the classifier head (BatchNorm replaced by GroupNorm)
structure: Selective translation of every layer's output (bias shift) plus a parallel low-resolution, narrow residual branch (downsample, group conv, upsample) per block; chosen to minimize stored activations rather than parameter count.
mergeable_reason: Bias updates fold in trivially, but the lite residual branches are extra nonlinear modules that stay at inference (in the default protocol they are already part of the pre-trained architecture).
identity_at_init: By default the lite residual modules are present during pre-training and initialized from those weights, so transfer starts exactly at the pre-trained function; with randomly initialized lite residuals (TinyTL-RandomL+B) there is no such guarantee and accuracy drops.
key_idea: On-device training memory is dominated by the activations needed for weight gradients, not by the parameter count; bias gradients need no stored activations, so freeze weights, train biases, and recover capacity with tiny residual branches whose activations are small.
results_note: TinyTL saved up to 6.5x training memory relative to full fine-tuning with little accuracy loss, was up to 34.1% more accurate than last-layer tuning, and with feature-extractor adaptation saved 7.3-12.9x memory without accuracy loss.
categorical_reading: TinyTL picks its coordinate block by the backprop cone rather than by parameter count. Biases need no stored activation (Obs IV.4), and the lite residual branches see downsampled, narrow activations. As an object it is BitFit \(\oplus\) a selective block of small pretrained branches \(\oplus\) the head.

name: AutoPrompt
paper_title: AutoPrompt: Eliciting Knowledge from Language Models with Automatically Generated Prompts
formula_latex: x_{\text{prompt}}=\lambda(x_{\text{inp}},x_{\text{trig}}),\ \ x_{\text{trig}}=(x^{(1)}_{\text{trig}},\dots,x^{(\ell)}_{\text{trig}})\in\mathcal V^{\ell}\ \text{(discrete tokens shared across inputs, initialized to [MASK])};\ \ p(y\mid x_{\text{prompt}})=\textstyle\sum_{w\in\mathcal V_y}p([\mathrm{MASK}]=w\mid x_{\text{prompt}});\ \ \mathcal V_{\text{cand}}=\operatorname{top-}k_{w\in\mathcal V}\big[w_{\text{in}}^{\top}\nabla\log p(y\mid x_{\text{prompt}})\big]\ \text{(gradient w.r.t. the embedding of }x^{(j)}_{\text{trig}}),\ \text{keep the candidate with the highest }p(y\mid\cdot);\ \text{LM frozen}
trainable_params: 0\ \text{continuous parameters};\ \ell\ \text{discrete token choices (search space }|\mathcal V|^{\ell})\ \text{plus label-token sets }\mathcal V_y
locus: input token sequence (trigger tokens placed by a template around the input and the [MASK] slot)
structure: A discrete prompt: the prompt matrix is constrained to the vocabulary lattice \(\{E_w\}^{\ell}\subset\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\) and optimized by first-order (HotFlip-style) coordinate swaps; prompt tuning is the continuous relaxation of this set.
mergeable_reason: The trigger tokens lengthen every input, so inference is not at the original cost (though no new parameters exist).
identity_at_init: Triggers start as [MASK] tokens; there is no identity guarantee, since the template itself changes the input.
key_idea: Turn a task into masked-LM cloze form and search for a few shared discrete trigger tokens (and label words) with gradient-ranked candidate swaps, eliciting knowledge from a frozen MLM without any fine-tuning.
results_note: Without fine-tuning, AutoPrompt-prompted RoBERTa-large reached 91.4% on SST-2; on LAMA fact retrieval, AutoPrompt prompts for BERT reached 43.3% precision@1 (7 trigger tokens) vs 34.1% for the best prior single prompt (LPAQA Top1).
categorical_reading: AutoPrompt is prompt tuning restricted to the vocabulary lattice: a 0-dimensional object whose points map into prompt tuning's \(Q\) by \(w\mapsto E_w\). Its HotFlip search ranks swaps by the first-order term \(E_w^\top\nabla\). It uses the cotangent of the continuous relaxation to move on a discrete set.

name: LoRA
paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: h = W_0 x + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A x,\quad W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (PEFT also: Embedding, Conv1d/2d/3d, MultiheadAttention, raw nn.Parameter e.g. MoE experts via target_parameters); originally \(W_q\), \(W_v\), commonly 'all-linear'
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space: \(\Delta W = BA\), \(\operatorname{rank}\Delta W \le r\)
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) is a dense \(d_{out} \times d_{in}\) matrix that can be added to \(W_0\) after training (merge_and_unload), giving zero inference overhead.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) (\(A\) Kaiming-uniform in PEFT, Gaussian in the paper; init_lora_weights='gaussian' keeps \(B = 0\)); scaling \(\alpha/r\).
key_idea: Fine-tuning updates have low intrinsic rank, so freeze \(W_0\) and learn only a rank-\(r\) factorization of the update.
results_note: Paper reports on-par or better quality than full fine-tuning on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2 and GPT-3 175B, with 10,000x fewer trainable parameters and 3x less GPU memory for GPT-3.
categorical_reading: LoRA is the determinantal cone \(\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) pointed at its apex: the reference object of the slice, with gauge \(GL_r\) on the internal wire and merging as the canonical map \(\rho\) to the terminal object. Its \(\mathrm T_A\) pointings are classified by \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\in\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)\).

name: AdaLoRA
paper_title: AdaLoRA: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
hf_peft_config: AdaLoraConfig(init_r, target_r, tinit, tfinal, deltaT, beta1, beta2, orth_reg_weight, total_step)
formula_latex: W=W_0+P\Lambda Q,\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_i),\ Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\quad R(P,Q)=\lVert P^\top P-I\rVert_F^2+\lVert QQ^\top-I\rVert_F^2;\quad S_{k,i}=s(\lambda_{k,i})+\tfrac1{d_{out}}\textstyle\sum_js(P_{k,ji})+\tfrac1{d_{in}}\sum_js(Q_{k,ij}),\ s=\bar I\cdot\bar U,\ I(w)=|w\,\nabla_w\mathcal{L}|;\quad \lambda_{k,i}\leftarrow0\ \text{unless }S_{k,i}\in\text{top-}b^{(t)}
trainable_params: r_{init}(d_{in}+d_{out}+1)\ \text{per matrix during training},\ r_{init}=b^{(0)}/n\ (\text{masked triplets are kept and can be reactivated});\ \ \text{retained after pruning: }\textstyle\sum_k r_k(d_{in}+d_{out}+1),\ \sum_k r_k=b^{(T)}
locus: any linear layer; budget shared across all adapted matrices
structure: SVD-shaped update \(\Delta W=P\Lambda Q\) with soft-orthogonal \(P,Q\) and a diagonal of singular values that is masked (pruned) by a global importance ranking under a cubic budget schedule
mergeable_reason: \(P\Lambda Q\) is a dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: \(\Lambda=0\) (\(P,Q\) random Gaussian); importance scores are EMA-smoothed sensitivity times uncertainty.
key_idea: Parameterize each update in SVD form so that rank can be reduced by zeroing singular values without expensive SVDs, and move rank budget to the matrices whose triplets are most important for the loss.
results_note: Reported better or on-par GLUE results vs LoRA at all budgets with DeBERTaV3-base and a 1.2% F1 gain on SQuAD 2.0 with under 0.1% trainable parameters.
categorical_reading: AdaLoRA charts LoRA's cone by an SVD-shaped triple whose diagonal \(\Lambda\) is a zero gate, so it starts at an apex with only \(r\) first-order directions, and its budget mask moves between nested sub-cones (a union over rank allocations). It is simulated by LoRA via \(h=(P\Lambda,Q)\), but as pointed objects LoRA does not map into it.

name: AdaMSS
paper_title: AdaMSS: Adaptive Multi-Subspace Approach for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: \hat W_0=U_{[:,1:R]}S_{[1:R]}V_{[:,1:R]}^\top,\ \text{output units clustered into }K\text{ subspaces }\mathcal{S}_k;\quad \Delta W_{\mathcal{S}_k,:}=C_k\,B_k\,\tilde A_k,\ \tilde A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{R_k\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen orthonormal},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times R_k}\ \text{(QR-orthogonal init)},\ C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{S}_k|\times r_k},\ C_k=0;\ \text{ASA keeps the top-}K_t\text{ blocks by AdaLoRA-style importance}
trainable_params: \textstyle\sum_{k}r_k\,(R_k+|\mathcal{S}_k|)\ \text{over the active subspaces}
locus: linear layers
structure: block-structured low-rank update: the principal rank-\(R\) part of \(W_0\) is segmented (low-rank-representation clustering) into \(K\) subspaces, each receiving its own tiny low-rank update \(A_kB_kC_k\); whole subspaces are frozen by adaptive subspace allocation
mergeable_reason: The scattered block updates form a dense matrix of the original shape (HF PEFT implements merge).
identity_at_init: \(C_k=0\) (\(W_0\) untouched); frozen bases come from a data-free truncated SVD of \(W_0\) plus subspace clustering.
key_idea: The principal row space of a pretrained weight decomposes into several smaller subspaces; adapting each with its own small rank and pruning irrelevant subspaces gives a tighter generalization bound and far fewer parameters than a single-subspace adapter like PiSSA.
