results_note: Reported +4.7% average accuracy over LoRA on seven ViT-Large tasks with 15.4% of its parameters, and +7% over PiSSA on RoBERTa-Large with about 94% fewer trainable parameters.
categorical_reading: AdaMSS is a \(\oplus\)-word of \(K\) small LoRAs, each living on an output block \(\mathcal S_k\) and transported into a frozen principal-subspace frame of \(W_0\), with an AdaLoRA-style mask over whole summands. Although it starts from PiSSA's SVD, it keeps \(\theta_0\) as the residual and starts at an apex (Type I), so it is incomparable with PiSSA.

name: BEFT
paper_title: BEFT: Bias-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models in Low-Data Regimes
formula_latex: h = W_v x + b_v + \Delta b_v,\ \ \Delta b_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ trained, all weights frozen};\ \ a(V+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top)=aV+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top \text{ (rows of } a \text{ sum to 1)}
trainable_params: d_{out} \text{ per value projection } (\approx 0.01\% \text{ of parameters})
locus: bias of the value projection \(W_v\) in every attention block (bias added, zero-initialized, for bias-free LLMs)
structure: additive shift of the value-projection output; because attention rows sum to one, the shift passes straight to the attention output
mergeable_reason: \(\Delta b_v\) adds to an existing value-projection bias after training. PEFT raises an error when merging into a bias-free layer (for example LLaMA-style projections), so merging is only possible when the base layer has a bias.
identity_at_init: PEFT adds a separate zero-initialized \(\Delta b_v\) (init_weights=True), so the function is unchanged at init.
key_idea: Among q/k/v biases, fine-tuning only the value bias \(b_v\) gives the best accuracy per parameter in low-data regimes.
results_note: Paper reports \(b_v\) fine-tuning consistently beating \(b_q\) and \(b_k\) fine-tuning across encoder- and decoder-only LLMs up to 6.7B, with about 9x fewer parameters than tuning all biases.
categorical_reading: A one-bias coordinate subspace of BitFit, hence an A2 sub-object of it, translating the value projection; since attention rows sum to one it equals a constant shift of the attention output. It is Lin, regular and idempotent.

name: BOFT
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning via Butterfly Factorization
formula_latex: W = W_0 R(m,b)^{\top},\quad R(m,b)=\prod_{i=1}^{m}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)},\ \big(\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}\big)^{\top}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}=I,\ \text{each factor a permuted block-diagonal matrix of } b\times b \text{ Cayley-parameterized orthogonal blocks};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: \tfrac{1}{2}\,m\,(b-1)\,d_{in}\quad(\mathcal{O}(d_{in}\log d_{in})\ \text{for } b=2,\ m=\log_2 d_{in})
locus: any linear / conv layer (attention and MLP of ViTs, LLMs, SAM, Stable Diffusion); acts on the input side of \(W_0\)
structure: right action of a product of \(m\) sparse butterfly factors, each a permutation conjugate of the block-diagonal subgroup \(O(b)^{d/b}\); the product is a dense orthogonal matrix. The paper frames this as information transmission on a butterfly grid graph (a Cooley-Tukey style factorization of an \(O(d)\) element).
mergeable_reason: The product \(R(m,b)\) is a fixed orthogonal matrix after training, so \(W_0 R(m,b)^T\) can be precomputed.
identity_at_init: All skew-symmetric generators start at 0, so every butterfly factor is the identity and \(R = I\).
key_idea: Build a dense orthogonal matrix as a product of sparse butterfly-structured orthogonal factors. OFT then gets dense rotations from \(O(d \log d)\) parameters. Block-diagonal OFT is the \(m=1\) case.
results_note: Reports higher scores than LoRA and OFT on GLUE (DeBERTaV3), the best VTAB-1K average in its table (77.9% for BOFT \(m=2\), \(b=8\) with DINOv2-large), better Llama-2-7B MMLU and math (GSM8K/MATH) results, HQ-SAM-level segmentation with 3% of its parameters, and better controllable and subject-driven Stable Diffusion generation.
categorical_reading: BOFT (HF) is the torus saturation \(\mathrm{Diag}_m\cdot\mathrm{Im}(\text{butterfly OFT})\): an orthogonal action on the input side assembled from sparse block factors, plus a free output scale that weakens the Gram invariant to \(|\cos|\) between neurons (Cor II.6 remarks). Butterfly permutations connect the block hypergraph, and the rebasing closure is the group generated by its components.

name: C3A
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Delta W,\quad \Delta W = \big[\,\mathcal{C}(w_{ij})\,\big]_{i\le d_{out}/b,\ j\le d_{in}/b},\ \mathcal{C}(w)\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b}\ \text{circulant with first row } w\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\ (\text{trained});\ \mathcal{C}(w) = F\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\tfrac{1}{b}Fw\big)F^{-1}\ (\text{paper's convention}),\ \text{so } \Delta W x \text{ is computed blockwise with FFTs};\ \text{HF PEFT additionally divides } \Delta W \text{ by } d_{in}
trainable_params: \tfrac{d_{in}\,d_{out}}{b}
locus: any linear layer whose dimensions are divisible by the block size \(b\) (paper: RoBERTa, LLaMA-3-8B, ViT)
structure: block-circulant update: each \(b\times b\) block is a circulant matrix (simultaneously diagonalised by the DFT), so rank can reach \(\min(d_{in}, d_{out})\) independently of the parameter count
mergeable_reason: The block-circulant matrix can be materialised and added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: HF default initialises the kernels with xavier_uniform (non-zero, so not an exact identity); init_weights=True sets them to zero (no-op)
key_idea: Use circular convolution (a circulant matrix) as the update: rank is decoupled from parameter count, and FFTs make forward and backward passes fast and memory-light; block-circulant structure handles non-square weights and tunes the budget.
results_note: Consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants across fine-tuning tasks (e.g. on LLaMA-3-8B) while being efficient in compute and memory.
categorical_reading: C3A is a linear method: a coordinate subspace in the block-circulant frame (a DFT transport of a mask, Prop II.13), so its rank is decoupled from \(|M|=mn/b\) while its covariance is the imposed cyclic order \(\Pi_{\rm cyc}\). Its blocks include odd circulants, which FourierFT's point-symmetric image never reaches.

name: Cartridges
paper_title: Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long context representations via self-study
formula_latex: \forall l:\ K_l\leftarrow[Z_k^{(l)};K_l],\ V_l\leftarrow[Z_v^{(l)};V_l],\ Z_k^{(l)},Z_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times d};\ \ \min_Z\sum_{(x,\tilde c)}\sum_i D_{KL}\big(F(\cdot\mid\tilde c\oplus x_{:i})\,\|\,F_Z(\cdot\mid x_{:i})\big)
trainable_params: 2L\,(p-p_f)\,d_{kv} \ \ (p=\text{num\_virtual\_tokens},\ p_f=\text{num\_frozen\_tokens}=1 \text{ by default},\ d_{kv}=\text{per-layer key/value width})
locus: keys/values at every layer (a directly parameterized KV-cache prefix)
structure: learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, trained directly (no MLP reparameterization) by context distillation on synthetic self-study conversations about a corpus
mergeable_reason: The cartridge is extra KV state attended by the model, not a weight change.
identity_at_init: Not an identity. The paper recommends initializing \(Z\) from the prefill KV cache of the first \(p\) corpus tokens (PEFT: initialize_kv_prefix_from_text / initialize_kv_prefix_from_past_key_values). PEFT get_peft_model alone gives random \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) init. The first num_frozen_tokens (default 1) are frozen as an attention sink.
key_idea: Compress a long corpus offline into a small trainable KV cache via self-study distillation, so it can replace in-context documents at inference.
results_note: Paper reports matching ICL quality with 38.6x less memory and 26.4x higher throughput, and extending effective context to 484k tokens.
categorical_reading: Prefix tuning re-pointed: a deep key/value prefix \(Z\) on the sequence wire of every attention layer, an unpointed extension whose base point is the corpus prefill cache and whose attention-sink slot is frozen, which makes it an A2 sub-object of the direct prefix. Self-study distillation changes the loss, not the object \((Q,q_0,\rho)\).

name: CPT
paper_title: Context-aware Prompt Tuning: Advancing In-Context Learning with Adversarial Methods
formula_latex: X_{ctx}=[T_i(x_i),S_{intra},T_o(y_i),S_{inter}]_{i=1}^{N};\ E\leftarrow\Pi_{\|E-E_0\|_2\le\epsilon}\big(E-\eta\nabla_E\mathcal{L}\big);\ \mathcal{L}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\gamma^{N+1-k}\,\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(k)},t_O^{(k)})+\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(N+1)},t_O^{(N+1)})
trainable_params: \ell\,d \ \ (\ell=\text{number of context input/format tokens optimized; label tokens frozen})
locus: input embedding sequence (embeddings of the in-context demonstrations)
structure: soft prompt initialized from real few-shot demonstrations; per-token embedding changes projected onto an L2 ball (projected gradient descent) with a recency-decayed context loss
mergeable_reason: Optimized context tokens are extra inputs, not weights.
identity_at_init: Not a no-op relative to the bare query: at init it equals ordinary in-context learning with the given demonstrations.
key_idea: Treat the in-context demonstrations themselves as trainable soft prompts, but keep them within an \(\varepsilon\)-ball of the real tokens and down-weight early examples to counter recency bias.
results_note: Paper reports gains over LoRA, prompt tuning, IPT and ICL on SST-2, AG News, DBpedia and TREC in 2/4/6-shot settings with BLOOM-1.7B, GPT-J-6B and Llama-3-8B.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning restricted (A2) to the context tokens of real demonstrations, with label tokens frozen and every token confined to an \(\varepsilon\)-ball around its embedding; the base point is the in-context-learning state, not the frozen zero-shot function. The constraint is global: at \(q_0\) the germ is open in prompt space.

name: DEFT
paper_title: DEFT: Decompositional Efficient Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Image Models
formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0+QR,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(P),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{(PEFT default 'relu'): } W=(I-P\,\mathrm{relu}(P)^\top)W_0+PR
trainable_params: r(d_{out}+d_{in})
locus: Linear / Conv1D layers (mainly text-to-image diffusion transformers/UNets)
structure: rank-\(r\) update that removes an \(r\)-dimensional output subspace of \(W_0\) and injects new content into it: \(\Delta W = Q(R - Q^\top W_0)\)
mergeable_reason: The update equals a low-rank additive delta \(Q(R - Q^T W_0)\) that can be merged into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: PEFT (init_weights=True) draws \(P \sim N(0, 0.02^2)\) and sets \(R\) so that the injection exactly cancels the removal term, so \(W = W_0\) at init.
key_idea: Split adaptation into 'forget a subspace' (projection) and 'write new content there' (low-rank injection) to personalize while preserving the base model's instruction-following/editability.
results_note: Paper reports DreamBench Plus CLIP-T 0.361 on SDXL vs 0.341 for LoRA and 0.354 for PaRa.
categorical_reading: DEFT's 'forget a subspace, then write into it' is LoRA in disguise: the shear \((P,R)\mapsto(P,R-\mathrm{relu}(P)^\top W_0)\) identifies it, as germs at the HF initialisation, with \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) pointed at \((P_0,0)\) in the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum of Thm II.2. What separates it from default LoRA is the stratum of its pointing, not its image.

name: PaRa
paper_title: PaRa: Personalizing Text-to-Image Diffusion via Parameter Rank Reduction
formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(B),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ trained}
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
locus: attention/linear layers of text-to-image diffusion models
structure: left-multiplication of \(W_0\) by an orthogonal projector of corank \(r\), shrinking the output space of the layer (rank reduction)
mergeable_reason: \((I - QQ^\top) W_0\) is a single dense matrix.
identity_at_init: Not an identity: PEFT notes PaRa cannot be a no-op at initialization since only the projection is trained.
key_idea: Personalization works by reducing the rank of generation: projecting out a few output directions narrows the model's output space toward the target concept.
results_note: Paper reports about 2x fewer parameters than LoRA and 82-97% human preference over LoRA across tested concepts.
categorical_reading: PaRa is an unpointed object of action type: \(\rho(B)=(I-\Pi_{\mathrm{col}B})W_0\) is the orbit of \(W_0\) under the Grassmannian of corank-\(r\) projectors, a compact set at positive distance from \(\theta_0\). It is DEFT restricted to \(R=0\), but only as a weak morphism, since no parameter value reproduces the frozen model.

name: DeLoRA
paper_title: DeLoRA: Decoupling Angles and Strength in Low-rank Adaptation
formula_latex: W=W_0+\frac{\lambda\|W_0\|}{r}\,B\,\Xi\,A,\ \ \Xi=\mathrm{diag}\Big(\tfrac{1}{\|b_i\|\,\|a_i\|}\Big),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \lambda \text{ trainable}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+1
locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT)
structure: sum of \(r\) unit-Frobenius rank-1 terms with a learnable global strength, so \(\|\Delta W\|_F\le\lambda\|W_0\|\) (a Frobenius-ball boundary)
mergeable_reason: The normalized low-rank update is a fixed dense matrix after training.
identity_at_init: Paper: subtract a frozen copy of the initial update from \(W_0\); PEFT default: \(B = 0\) (\(A\) Kaiming) with \(\lambda\) initialized to delora_lambda.
key_idea: Normalize the low-rank directions and learn their strength separately, bounding how far the weights can drift and making training robust to learning rate and length.
results_note: Paper reports GLUE avg 85.6 vs 84.7 for LoRA, parity with LoRA/DoRA on subject-driven generation, and better robustness to learning rate and extended training.
categorical_reading: DeLoRA normalises each rank-one term and puts the strength in one scalar \(\lambda\). Its image is still LoRA's cone, and under HF's \(B=0\) initialisation it starts at the same apex, so LoRA simulates it through an explicit normalising \(h\). The normalisation changes the fibre (a non-linear gauge of dimension \(r^2+1\)) and hence the training geometry, not the expressivity.

name: FourierFT
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Discrete Fourier Transform
formula_latex: \Delta W=\alpha\,\mathrm{Re}\big(\mathcal{F}^{-1}_{2D}(F)\big),\ F\in\mathbb{C}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ zero except at } n \text{ fixed random frequency locations (shared across layers) holding trainable } c\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
trainable_params: n \ \ (n=\text{n\_frequency})
locus: any linear layer (typically \(W_q\), \(W_v\))
structure: \(\Delta W\) is the real part of the inverse 2D DFT of a sparse spectral matrix with \(n\) learnable coefficients
mergeable_reason: The spatial-domain \(\Delta W\) can be computed once and added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: PEFT default init_weights=False draws coefficients from \(N(0,1)\), so it is NOT an exact identity; init_weights=True zero-initializes for a no-op.
key_idea: Weight updates are compressible in the frequency domain, so learn only a handful of spectral coefficients.
results_note: Paper reports outperforming LoRA on LLaMA2-7B instruction tuning with 0.064M trainable parameters versus LoRA's 33.5M.
categorical_reading: FourierFT is a mask in the real Fourier frame: each frequency contributes a rank-two real pattern, so \(\Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha}{mn}B_F\,\mathrm{diag}(c,-c)A_F\) with frozen trigonometric frames and FourierFT factors through LoRA-FA\((A_F)\), as VeRA does through LoRA-FA\((A)\). Its image lies in the point-symmetric subspace \(\Delta W_{j,l}=\Delta W_{-j,-l}\), an absolute invariant that neuron permutations do not respect.

name: FRoD
full_name: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees
paper_title: FRoD: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees for Fast Convergence
formula_latex: W_i = U_i\big(\Sigma_i + S_i\big)V^{\top},\quad V\ \text{global orthonormal basis shared by all layers (hierarchical joint QR + eigendecomposition of the stacked weights)},\ U_i\ \text{per-layer factor (frozen)};\ \Sigma_i\ \text{diagonal strengths and } S_i\ \text{random-pattern sparse off-diagonal perturbation (density } s)\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: d_{in} + s\,d_{in}^{2}\ \text{per adapted matrix (diagonal plus sparse off-diagonal entries of an } d_{in}\times d_{in} \text{ core)}
locus: selected linear layers of ViT, LLaMA-style and encoder models (grouped by layer category for the joint decomposition)
structure: cross-layer shared latent basis with a per-layer diagonal-plus-sparse core: on-axis updates rescale generalised singular values, sparse off-diagonal entries inject small rotations; full-rank updates
mergeable_reason: \(U_i(\Sigma_i + S_i)V^T\) is a dense matrix that replaces \(W_i\) at no extra inference cost.
identity_at_init: \(S_i = 0\) and \(U_i \Sigma_i V^{\top}\) reconstructs \(W_i\) (maximum error below 1e-5), so the model is essentially unchanged at init; \(\Sigma_i\) (trained) starts at the decomposition's strengths; the joint decomposition is a costly one-off initialisation. HF PEFT: frod_lambda_l = diag strengths, frod_lambda_s_values = 0
key_idea: Extract a basis shared by all layers via a hierarchical joint decomposition, then fine-tune only per-layer scaling factors plus sparse off-diagonal rotations in that basis, giving full-rank updates and fast convergence.
results_note: On 20 vision, reasoning and language benchmarks FRoD matches full fine-tuning accuracy using 1.72% of trainable parameters under identical training budgets.
categorical_reading: FRoD is the linear method \((\Sigma_i,S_i)\mapsto U_i(\Sigma_i+S_i)V^\top\): a diagonal-plus-sparse mask in a cross-layer spectral frame \((U_i,V)\), pointed (up to reconstruction error) at the decomposition's strengths. Because \(V\) is shared across a layer group, its covariance holds only for transformations common to the whole group.

name: GLoRA
paper_title: One-for-All: Generalized LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
formula_latex: h=(W_0+W_0\odot A+B)\,x+b_0+b_0\odot D+E+W_0C;\ \ A,B\in\{\text{LoRA},\text{vector},\text{scalar},\text{none}\},\ C\in\{\text{LoRA},\text{vector},\text{none}\},\ D,E\in\{\text{vector},\text{scalar},\text{none}\}
trainable_params: \text{config-dependent; PEFT default (A,B=LoRA, C=LoRA, D,E=constant) on a layer with bias: } 2r(d_{in}+d_{out})+r(d_{in}+1)+2;\ \text{bias-free layers: } 2r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: nn.Linear layers (weights and biases)
structure: unified reparameterization: Hadamard rescaling of \(W_0\), additive (low-rank) weight shift, bias rescaling/shift, and a \(W_0\)-coupled bias (layer-wise prompt) path; per-layer path types chosen by evolutionary search in the paper
mergeable_reason: All paths are linear in the parameters and fold into \(W_{uni} = W_0 + W_0\odot A + B\) and \(b_{uni} = b_0 + b_0\odot D + E + W_0 C\).
identity_at_init: Zero-initialized down-projections make every path zero (no-op) by default.
key_idea: Subsume LoRA, scaling/shifting and prompt-like methods in one reparameterizable layer and search the best path configuration per layer.
results_note: Paper reports 78.0% average on VTAB-1K, up to 2.9% above prior methods, and strong few-shot and domain-generalization results.
categorical_reading: GLoRA is an \(\oplus\)-word on the slice: \(\mathrm{HiRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus(\text{bias paths})\), where HiRA \(=(D_{W_0})_*\mathrm{LoRA}\) supplies the coupling to \(\theta_0\). Its 'unification' is the statement that the torus ladder \(W_0\odot(J+Z)\) of Prop II.9 plus an additive term simulates (IA)\(^3\), SSF-type scalings, DoRA and LoRA.

name: GraLoRA
paper_title: GraLoRA: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\big[\,B_{ij}A_{ij}^{\top}\,\big]_{i,j=1}^{k},\quad A_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{in}}{k}\times\frac{r}{k}},\ B_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{k}\times\frac{r}{k}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_{ij},B_{ij}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer of LLMs
structure: \(k\times k\) grid of independent rank-\((r/k)\) blocks, equivalently \(B_G A_G^{\top}\) with sparse block-structured factors; rank up to \(k r\) at LoRA's parameter count; Hybrid GraLoRA adds a plain LoRA term.
mergeable_reason: The block matrix is an ordinary dense update.
identity_at_init: \(A\) Kaiming-uniform and \(B = 0\) (HF PEFT, all \(k\) blocks and the optional hybrid LoRA), so \(\Delta W = 0\). HF scales by \(\alpha/(r + \mathtt{hybrid\_r})\).
key_idea: Partition the weight into sub-blocks with their own small adapters so that input outlier channels only perturb local gradients and effective rank grows by k.
results_note: Up to +8.5% absolute Pass@1 on HumanEval+ over LoRA, with consistent gains on commonsense reasoning across model sizes and ranks.
categorical_reading: GraLoRA is the \(\oplus\)-word of \(k^2\) block-embedded \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r/k}\) (Obs I.7). It has the same budget and the same \(d\) as \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) and a larger cut (rank \(kr\)), but every block is capped at rank \(r/k\): it moves the cut rather than enlarging the image.

name: HiRA
paper_title: HiRA: Parameter-Efficient Hadamard High-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
formula_latex: W=W_0+W_0\odot(BA)=W_0\odot(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+BA),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B,A\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (LLM attention and MLP projections)
structure: entry-wise (Hadamard) multiplicative modulation of \(W_0\) by \(J + BA\). \(\Delta W = W_0 \odot BA\) has rank \(\le \mathrm{rank}(W_0)\cdot r\), so the update is high-rank at LoRA's parameter cost. LoRA is recovered by replacing \(W_0\) with the all-ones matrix.
mergeable_reason: \(W_0 + W_0 \odot BA\) is precomputed for deployment; the original weight can be recovered by element-wise division by \(1 + BA\).
identity_at_init: One factor is zero (the paper zero-initializes its \(d\times r\) factor and Kaiming-initializes the other), so \(\Delta W = 0\).
key_idea: Multiply the pretrained matrix element-wise by a low-rank matrix. The Hadamard product with \(W_0\) raises the possible rank of the update (up to \(\mathrm{rank}(W_0)\cdot r\)) without extra parameters and carries the pretrained structure into the update.
results_note: Reports gains over LoRA and other PEFT baselines on commonsense reasoning with Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B, plus further generation tasks, at LoRA's parameter count (ICLR 2025 oral).
categorical_reading: HiRA is LoRA transported by the \(\theta_0\)-dependent diagonal automorphism \(D_{W_0}:X\mapsto W_0\odot X\), i.e. LoRA in the Hadamard frame of \(W_0\). It has LoRA's \(d\), gauge and deficit, but a different cut (rank up to \(r\,\mathrm{rk}W_0\)) and only monomial covariance.

name: HRA
paper_title: Bridging The Gap between Low-rank and Orthogonal Adaptation via Householder Reflection Adaptation
formula_latex: W=W_0H,\ \ H=\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Big(I-2\frac{u_iu_i^\top}{\|u_i\|^2}\Big),\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}};\ \ \text{optional } \lambda\|I-U^\top U\|_F^2 \text{ (or Gram-Schmidt, apply\_GS)}
trainable_params: r\,d_{in}
locus: linear and Conv2d layers (rotation of the input space)
structure: product of \(r\) Householder reflections (orthogonal) acting on the input side of \(W_0\); equivalently \(W_0 + W_0U\Gamma U^\top\), an 'adaptive LoRA'
mergeable_reason: \(W_0 H\) is a single dense matrix.
identity_at_init: Reflection vectors initialized in identical pairs (\(u_{2i} = u_{2i-1}\)), so consecutive reflections cancel and \(H = I\); requires even \(r\) in PEFT.
key_idea: A chain of \(r\) Householder reflections is simultaneously an orthogonal transform and a rank-\(r\) additive update, bridging OFT and LoRA.
results_note: Paper reports better accuracy than LoRA/OFT-style baselines with fewer parameters on GLUE, LLaMA2-7B math reasoning, and subject-driven/controllable image generation.
categorical_reading: HRA is the image-level meet of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) with the full orthogonal orbit \(W_0\cdot SO(n)\), and HF's paired initialisation is an apex, the multiplicative twin of LoRA's dead \(A\)-direction. Rebasing commutes with the meet, so re-merged HRA walks \(W_0\cdot SO(n)\) as ReLoRA walks \(\Theta\).

name: (IA)³
full_name: Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations
paper_title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
formula_latex: k=l_k\odot(W_kx),\ v=l_v\odot(W_vx),\ h_{ff}=W_2\big(l_{ff}\odot\gamma(W_1x)\big);\ l_k,l_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},\ l_{ff}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{ff}} \text{ trained}
trainable_params: d_{out} \text{ per key/value projection},\ d_{ff} \text{ per FFN}
locus: outputs of key/value projections and inputs of the FFN down-projection (feedforward_modules)
structure: diagonal scaling: \(W=\mathrm{diag}(l)W_0\) (output rows) or \(W=W_0\mathrm{diag}(l)\) (FFN input columns)
mergeable_reason: Diagonal scalings fold into the rows/columns of \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Scaling vectors \(l\) initialized to 1.
key_idea: Learn only rescaling vectors that inhibit or amplify inner activations; with the T-Few recipe this beats in-context learning cheaply.
results_note: Paper reports T-Few (T0 + (IA)\(^3\)) outperforming GPT-3 in-context learning and reaching super-human performance on RAFT.
categorical_reading: (IA)\(^3\) is the left (or right) torus acting on \(W_0\); its orbit closure is linear, keeps the zeros of \(W_0\), and fixes row lines while scales are non-zero (Thm II.5(4)). It is the lowest rung \(W_0\odot(J+Z)\) of the torus ladder, a sub-object of HiRA\(_1\) at a non-default pointing, and it merges only into a neighbouring box by the calculus of Thm VI.3.

name: LN Tuning
paper_title: Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning
formula_latex: \mathrm{LN}(x)=\gamma\odot\frac{x-\mu(x)}{\sigma(x)}+\beta,\ \ \text{only } \gamma,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ of (attention-block) LayerNorms trained}
trainable_params: 2d \text{ per LayerNorm } (\gamma,\beta);\ d \text{ per RMSNorm (no } \beta)
locus: LayerNorm gains and biases
structure: per-channel affine rescaling/shift of normalized activations (diagonal), applied by training existing LayerNorm parameters
mergeable_reason: Only existing parameters change; the architecture is untouched.
identity_at_init: Trivially identity: starts from the pretrained \(\gamma\) and \(\beta\).
key_idea: Turning an LLM into a multimodal LLM is largely a domain-adaptation problem that LayerNorm parameters alone can absorb.
results_note: Paper reports, on 13B MLLMs, about 20% better average performance than LoRA across five multimodal benchmarks with 41.9% fewer trainable parameters and 17.6% less GPU memory.
categorical_reading: LN-tuning is a selective sub-object of full fine-tuning: it frees the coordinates \((\gamma,\beta)\) of the norm layers. By norm absorption (R6) a pre-norm gain is an input-side scaling of the consuming projections, tied across all of them: the transpose of (IA)\(^3\)'s output scaling.

name: LoHa
full_name: LoHa (Low-rank adaptation with Hadamard product; FedPara parameterization)
paper_title: FedPara: Low-Rank Hadamard Product for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2),\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ (k=1,2),\ \gamma=\alpha/r;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: 2r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear or convolutional layer; popular on Stable Diffusion UNet/text-encoder (LyCORIS)
structure: Hadamard (entrywise) product of two rank-\(r\) matrices; \(\mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le r^2\) (FedPara Prop. 1) at the parameter cost of a rank-\(2r\) LoRA. Equivalently \((B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}\): a rank-\(r^2\) factorization through row-wise Khatri-Rao products. Conv kernels can use a Tucker-style core variant (FedPara Prop. 3, use_effective_conv2d).
mergeable_reason: \(\Delta W\) is an explicit dense \(d_{out}\times d_{in}\) matrix that can be added to \(W_0\) after training.
identity_at_init: HF PEFT: three factors Kaiming-uniform and one (hada_w2_b) zero so \(\Delta W = 0\); the original LyCORIS code uses normal init with one factor zeroed.
key_idea: Entrywise-multiplying two low-rank matrices multiplies their ranks, so a LoRA-sized budget yields an update of rank up to \(r^2\). Proposed for communication-efficient federated learning (FedPara) and turned into a fine-tuning adapter by LyCORIS.
results_note: FedPara matches original-layer accuracy with 3-10x lower federated communication; as a PEFT adapter LoHa is benchmarked mainly for text-to-image customization in the LyCORIS study (ICLR 2024).
categorical_reading: LoHa is the Hadamard (copy-spider) composite of two LoRA cones; the face-splitting map exhibits it as factoring through \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_1r_2}\). It reaches high rank on a thin curved variety, because a whole two-sided torus is spent on gauge: rank is a cut, dimension a volume. Its Hadamard product involves no \(\theta_0\), so it is filed under R-additive (HiRA is the R-Hadamard row).

name: LoKr
paper_title: Navigating Text-To-Image Customization: From LyCORIS Fine-Tuning to Model Evaluation
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,C\otimes(BA),\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{u_p\times u_q},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{v_p\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times v_q},\ u_pv_p=d_{out},\ u_qv_q=d_{in};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ C,B,A\ \text{trained (C optionally factorized: decompose\_both)}
trainable_params: u_pu_q + r(v_p+v_q)\ \text{(right factor factorized, default when } r<\max(v_p,v_q)/2\text{)};\ r(u_p+u_q)+r(v_p+v_q)\ \text{(decompose\_both)};\ u_pu_q+v_pv_q\ \text{(neither factorized)}
locus: any linear or convolutional layer; widely used for diffusion-model customization
structure: Kronecker product of a small dense block \(C\) with a low-rank block \(BA\): \(\mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)=\mathrm{rank}(C)\,\mathrm{rank}(BA)\le \min(u_p,u_q)\,r\). Block sizes: paper Eq. 5 sets \(u_p\) = largest divisor of \(d_{out}\) not exceeding \(\min(f, \sqrt{d_{out}})\); HF's factorization() returns \((f, d/f)\) when \(f\) divides \(d\) and otherwise the divisor pair nearest \(\sqrt{d}\) subject to the smaller factor \(\le f\) (default \(f = -1\), i.e. near-square).
mergeable_reason: \(C \otimes (BA)\) is materialised as a dense matrix of \(W_0\)'s shape and added to it.
identity_at_init: HF PEFT zero-initializes the left Kronecker factor \(C\) (lokr_w1) and Kaiming-initializes the right factors, so \(\Delta W = 0\).
key_idea: Ranks multiply under the Kronecker product, so a tiny dense block times a low-rank block gives a high-rank, block-structured update with very few parameters.
results_note: Evaluated alongside LoRA and LoHa in the LyCORIS study of Stable Diffusion customization, which reports method-dependent trade-offs in fidelity, diversity and controllability rather than a single winner.
categorical_reading: LoKr is LoRA across a different cut of the same 4-leg tensor. The Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement \(\mathcal R\) transports it to a rank-one LoRA with a low-rank second factor, so 'ranks multiply' is a statement about the ordinary cut, and LoKr with small inner rank sits inside \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{\min(u_p,u_q)r'}\) (Thm II.11(e)).

name: MiSS (formerly Bone)
full_name: Matrix Shard Sharing (successor of Block-Affine Adaptation, Bone)
paper_title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
formula_latex: W=W_0+\Delta W,\ \ \Delta W=[\,D\ D\ \cdots\ D\,]=D\,(\mathbf{1}^\top_{d_{in}/r}\otimes I_r),\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\ \text{equivalently } \Delta W\,x=D\sum_{j=1}^{d_{in}/r}x^{(j)},\ x^{(j)}\in\mathbb{R}^{r} \text{ the } j\text{-th input shard}
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
locus: any linear layer
structure: shard sharing: one \(d_{out}\times r\) matrix replicated across the \(d_{in}/r\) input shards (rank \(\le r\)). Optional modes: 'bat' (Bone-style block-affine \(W_0\)-dependent update \(W_{blk} D + D\)) and 'mini' (\(D\) shared across output groups of size mini_r)
mergeable_reason: expand(D) is a fixed dense matrix after training.
key_idea: A single small matrix shared across input shards keeps LoRA-like expressivity with lower compute, memory and no expensive initialization.
results_note: Paper reports Llama2-7B GSM8K 48.16 vs 40.75 for LoRA and MATH 8.58 vs 5.22.
categorical_reading: MiSS (balance mode) is isomorphic to LoRA-FA with the frozen summing projection \(\mathbf 1^\top_{d_{\rm in}/r}\otimes I_r\): a linear sub-object of LoRA pointed at \((0,\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_r)\) whose covariance is the imposed shard structure \(\Pi\). Its BAT mode \((W_{\rm blk}+I)D\) is still linear in \(D\) but depends on \(W_0\), so it is not additive.

name: MPT
paper_title: Multitask Prompt Tuning Enables Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
formula_latex: P_k=P^*\odot(u_kv_k^\top),\ \ P^*\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d} \text{ shared (distilled from source tasks)},\ u_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell},v_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d};\ \text{input}=[P_k;E(x)]
trainable_params: \ell d+\ell+d \text{ per target task}
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: soft prompt = Hadamard product of a shared prompt matrix and a task-specific rank-one matrix
mergeable_reason: Prompt tokens extend the input sequence; they are not a weight change.
identity_at_init: Not an identity (adds tokens); target prompts initialized from the distilled shared source prompt.
key_idea: Distill many source-task prompts into one shared prompt and adapt it to each target task with a cheap multiplicative rank-one update.
results_note: Paper reports SuperGLUE average 74.1 vs 57.8 for vanilla prompt tuning while tuning 0.035% task-specific parameters.
categorical_reading: With the shared prompt also trained, \(\rho(P^*,u,v)=P^*\odot uv^\top\) is a Hadamard reparametrisation of prompt tuning: its image is all of \(\mathbb R^{\ell\times d}\) and its gauge is the torus \((\mathbb R^\times)^\ell\times(\mathbb R^\times)^d\). It is expressively equal to prompt tuning and differs only in the cometric and in the pointing at the distilled \(P^*\).

name: OFT
paper_title: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning
formula_latex: W=W_0R^\top,\ \ R=\mathrm{blockdiag}(R_1,\dots,R_n)\in O(d_{in}),\ R_i=(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i^\top=-Q_i\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b},\ n=d_{in}/b;\ \text{COFT: }\|Q\|\le\epsilon
trainable_params: n\,\tfrac{b(b-1)}{2}=\tfrac{d_{in}(b-1)}{2} \ \ (\text{or one shared block if block\_share})
locus: linear, Conv2d and Embedding layers in PEFT (rotation of the input space of \(W_0\))
structure: block-diagonal orthogonal \(R\in O(d_{in})\) (Cayley-parameterized) multiplying \(W_0\), preserving hyperspherical energy (pairwise angles between neurons)
mergeable_reason: \(W_0 R^T\) is a dense matrix that replaces \(W_0\).
key_idea: Fine-tune by rotating neurons rather than adding to them, which provably preserves the pairwise angular structure of pretrained weights.
results_note: Paper reports better generation quality and faster convergence than existing methods on subject-driven and controllable text-to-image generation.
categorical_reading: OFT is an action-type object \(\rho(Q)=W_0\,C(Q)^\top\) whose image is an orbit of the block-orthogonal group. It can never change \(K_{\rm out}\), the spectrum or the block partial Grams (Cor II.6), however often it is re-merged. Its expressivity is that of a group orbit, regular at \(\theta_0\), with the block normaliser as covariance.

name: OFTv2
full_name: Orthogonal Finetuning v2 (input-centric OFT with Cayley-Neumann parameterization; QOFT for quantized models)
paper_title: Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable
formula_latex: h = W_0\,(R^{\top}x),\quad R=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_r),\ R_i=(I+Q_i)\Big(I+\sum_{k=1}^{K}Q_i^{k}\Big)\approx(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i=-Q_i^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b};\ \text{QOFT: } h=\mathrm{Dequant}(W_q)\,(R^{\top}x);\ W_0 \text{ (or } W_q) \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: \tfrac{d_{in}(b-1)}{2},\ b=d_{in}/r
locus: any linear layer (input activations are rotated before the frozen matmul); works on top of quantized base weights
structure: the same block-diagonal (now only approximately) orthogonal action as OFT, evaluated as an action on the input vector \(x\) (two matrix-vector products, \(O(nd + d^2)\)) instead of on \(W_0\) (matrix-matrix, \(O(nd^2)\)). The truncated Neumann series makes the Cayley map only approximately orthogonal.
mergeable_reason: For a full-precision base, \(R\) can be folded into the weight (\(W_0 R^T\)); for QOFT, merging requires dequantizing and re-quantizing the merged weight.
identity_at_init: \(Q = 0\) gives \(R = I\).
key_idea: Rotate the input instead of the weight, which cuts OFT's cost from cubic to quadratic. Replace the matrix inverse in the Cayley transform with a truncated Neumann series. Because \(R\) acts on activations, the method runs on any quantized backbone (QOFT).
results_note: Reports up to 10x faster training and 3x lower GPU memory than the original OFT, and better results than QLoRA when fine-tuning quantized Qwen2.5 models (0.5B-72B) for math reasoning; also applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5.
categorical_reading: OFTv2 (HF's default OFTConfig) is OFT with the Cayley map replaced by its truncated Neumann series, \(R=C(Q)(I-Q^4)\). This is a quasi-orthogonal action whose image leaves the \(K_{\rm out}\) level set at order \(\|Q\|^4\) and whose rebasing closure is \(\prod GL^+(b)\) rather than \(\prod SO(b)\). With exact Cayley it is the same object as OFT.

name: OSF
full_name: Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning (adaptive-SVD constrained full fine-tuning)
paper_title: Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning
formula_latex:
W_0=U_{hi}\Sigma_{hi}V_{hi}^	op+U_{lo}\Sigma_{lo}V_{lo}^	op;\ U_{hi},\Sigma_{hi},V_{hi} 	ext{ frozen};\ U_{lo},\Sigma_{lo},V_{lo} 	ext{ trained with projected gradients } 
abla_{U_{lo}}\leftarrow(I-U_{hi}U_{hi}^	op)
abla_{U_{lo}},\ 
abla_{V_{lo}^	op}\leftarrow
abla_{V_{lo}^	op}(I-V_{hi}V_{hi}^	op)
trainable_params: k(d_{out}+d_{in}+1),\ \ k=\min(d_{in},d_{out})-\text{effective\_rank}
locus: any linear layer ('all-linear' supported)
structure: SVD split of \(W_0\): top singular subspace (important for prior tasks) frozen; minor singular components trained with gradients projected orthogonally to the frozen subspace
mergeable_reason: The frozen and trained SVD components recombine into one dense \(W\).
identity_at_init: Trainable components initialized from \(W_0\)'s own SVD, so \(W = W_0\) at init.
key_idea: For continual learning, update only directions orthogonal to the dominant singular subspaces of earlier tasks, giving full-rank-capacity updates with little forgetting.
results_note: Paper reports 71.3 vs 69.6 (O-LoRA) on the 15-task T5-Large benchmark and 48.4 vs 41.3 on TRACE with LLaMA-2 7B.
categorical_reading: OSF is a split (MiLoRA-type) pointing of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_k\) with \(k\) half the rank, plus a backward projection that confines the factors to the complements of the frozen top singular subspaces. Under that projection its reach is the linear minor block \(\theta_0+U_\perp(\cdot)V_\perp^\top\) of the SVD frame, the exact dual of PSOFT, which adapts only inside the principal block.

name: P-Tuning
full_name: P-Tuning (continuous prompts with a prompt encoder)
paper_title: GPT Understands, Too
formula_latex: T=\{[P_{0:i}],\,x,\,[P_{i+1:j}],\,y,\,[P_{j+1:k}]\}\ \longmapsto\ \{h_0,\dots,h_i,\,e(x),\,h_{i+1},\dots,h_j,\,e(y),\,h_{j+1},\dots,h_k\},\quad (h_0,\dots,h_k)=f_\psi(P_0,\dots,P_k)\ \ (f_\psi:\ \text{LSTM or MLP prompt encoder});\ \ P,\psi\ \text{trained, LM frozen (or tuned)}
trainable_params: \ell d+|\psi|\ \text{(encoder dropped after training, leaving } \ell d\text{)}
locus: input embedding sequence, at arbitrary template positions interleaved with discrete anchor tokens
structure: Virtual-token embeddings produced by a shared reparametrization network \(h=f_\psi(P)\) (bi-LSTM or MLP) that models dependencies between prompt tokens, inserted at template positions and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens.
mergeable_reason: The continuous prompt tokens lengthen the input; only the encoder can be discarded (its outputs cached as embeddings).
identity_at_init: No identity: the continuous prompt embeddings are freshly (randomly) initialized and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens, which the paper finds improves performance. The paper ablates LSTM, MLP and identity (EMB) prompt encoders and finds EMB unstable.
key_idea: Make prompts continuous and let a small encoder couple the prompt tokens, which stabilizes training against the large variance of discrete prompts and lets GPT-style models compete with BERT-style models on NLU.
results_note: With a frozen LM on LAMA knowledge probing P-Tuning beats manual prompts by 20+ points and searched prompts by 9 points; with tuned LMs it beats PET on SuperGLUE in both fully supervised and few-shot settings.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning precomposed with a 2-cell \(\sigma=f_\psi\) (LSTM or MLP encoder): the prompt image is unchanged and \(\sigma\) only replaces the flat metric on prompt space by the point-dependent \(D\sigma\,\Lambda\,D\sigma^\top\) (Obs III.2). The encoder is a training device; the stored object is a soft prompt.

name: PEANuT
full_name: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
paper_title: PEANuT: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
formula_latex: W=W_0+f(W_0;\theta),\ \ f(W_0;\theta)^\top=\sigma(W_0^\top\Theta_1)\,\Theta_2,\ \Theta_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Theta_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{out}} \ (\text{paper writes } \sigma(W_0\Theta_1)\Theta_2 \text{ with } W_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{out}};\ \text{optional depth: extra } r\times r \text{ encoder/decoder layers with residuals})
trainable_params: 2r\,d_{out}+2\,\text{depth}\,r^2
locus: nn.Linear layers
structure: nonlinear weight-conditioned update: a small MLP applied to the columns of \(W_0\) (one \(d_{out}\)-vector per input feature) produces \(\Delta W\) (rank \(\le r\))
mergeable_reason: \(f(W_0)\) is computed once after training and added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Output projection \(\Theta_2\) (\(B\)) zero-initialized.
key_idea: Generate the update as a nonlinear function of the frozen weight itself instead of a weight-agnostic linear factorization.
results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over strong PEFT baselines on four benchmarks spanning 20+ NLP and vision datasets at comparable or fewer parameters.
categorical_reading: PEANuT is a \(\theta_0\)-dependent object over LoRA: \(\rho=\theta_0+\Theta_2^\top\sigma(\Theta_1^\top\theta_0)\) factors through LoRA by \(h=(\Theta_2^\top,\sigma(\Theta_1^\top W_0))\), so it is LoRA's cone with a non-linear chart whose \(A\)-frame is computed from the base point (the whole cone when \(d_{out}\ge d_{in}\), a sub-cone when \(d_{out}+r\le d_{in}\)). Conversely, with \(W_0\) of full column rank, LoRA\(_r\) embeds in PEANuT\(_{2r}\) through \(\sigma(x)-\sigma(-x)=x\), which holds for ReLU, GELU and SiLU alike.

name: Prefix-Tuning
paper_title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
formula_latex: h_i=\begin{cases}P_\theta[i,:] & i\in P_{\mathrm{idx}}\\ \mathrm{LM}_\phi(z_i,h_{<i}) & \text{otherwise}\end{cases};\quad \text{equivalently, in each layer } l=1,\dots,L:\quad \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big),\quad P_k^{(l)},P_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d};\quad \text{training: } P_\theta[i,:]=\mathrm{MLP}_\theta(P'_\theta[i,:]),\quad P'_\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times k};\quad \phi\ (W_0)\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: 2L\ell d\ \text{(stored, one key and one value prefix per attention layer of a decoder-only LM; an encoder-decoder prefixes each attention stack)};\ \ \ell k+|\mathrm{MLP}_\theta|\ \text{during training (MLP discarded afterwards)}
locus: keys/values at every attention layer (decoder; encoder and decoder for enc-dec models in the paper)
structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, i.e. a learned initial KV-cache state of length \(\ell\). By He et al. (2022) this is equivalently a gated parallel attention-adapter: \(h \leftarrow (1-\lambda(x))\,h+\lambda(x)\,\mathrm{softmax}(xW_qP_k^\top)P_v\), with gate \(\lambda(x)\) = attention mass on the prefix.
mergeable_reason: The prefix adds \(\ell\) extra key/value slots to every attention layer (extra attention cost per token); it can be served as a cached prefix but not folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No exact identity: any prefix diverts attention mass \(\lambda(x)>0\) away from the content. HF PEFT's init_weights='zero' zeroes keys and values, which still rescales attention outputs by \(1-\lambda(x)\). Li & Liang initialize the prefix with activations of real (preferably task-relevant) words, which substantially helps in low-data settings; direct optimization of \(P\) is unstable, hence the MLP reparametrization.
key_idea: Optimize a short continuous 'context' that every token can attend to at every layer, steering a frozen LM like a prompt would but with far more expressive power than input embeddings alone (discrete prompt < embedding-only < prefix-tuning).
results_note: With 0.1% of parameters, GPT-2 prefix-tuning is comparable to fine-tuning on table-to-text (E2E, WebNLG, DART), outperforms it in low-data settings and extrapolates better to unseen categories, but trails full fine-tuning on XSUM summarization with BART.
categorical_reading: An unpointed extension on the key/value wire of every attention layer: by Thm VI.5(b) each layer becomes the gated parallel adapter \((1-\lambda_q)\mathrm{Attn}_q(C)+\lambda_q\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)\), so it has no neutral point and is not box-mergeable. Li–Liang's MLP is a training 2-cell that leaves the prefix image unchanged (Obs III.2).

name: Prompt Tuning
paper_title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
formula_latex: \text{input}=[P;\,E(x)],\ \ P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d} \text{ trained},\ \text{model frozen}
trainable_params: \ell\,d
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: learned soft-token embeddings prepended to the input
mergeable_reason: Soft tokens extend the input; nothing to fold into weights.
identity_at_init: Not an identity (adds tokens); initialized randomly, from text (vocab embeddings), or by random discrete vocab sampling (PEFT >= 0.18).
key_idea: With large enough models, a few learned input embeddings match full fine-tuning.
results_note: Paper reports prompt tuning closing the gap to model tuning as T5 scales past billions of parameters.
categorical_reading: The basic unpointed extension: soft tokens on the input sequence wire, \(\tilde f(\theta_0,P,x)=f(\theta_0,[P;x])\), with no \(P\) reproducing \(f(\theta_0,-)\). In causal decoders it maps into deep prompt tuning by \(p\mapsto(K_j(p),V_j(p))_j\), an arrow of the unpointed slice over the realisation, not of \(\mathsf{Meth}\) (Thm VI.5(e)).

name: PSOFT
paper_title: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
formula_latex: W=W_{res}+B\,\operatorname{diag}(\beta)\,R^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\,A,\quad W_0=U\Sigma V^{\top},\ A=V_{:,:r}^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{(row-orthonormal)},\ B=U_{:,:r}\Sigma_{:r,:r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ W_{res}=W_0-BA\ \text{(all frozen)};\ R\in SO(r)\ \text{(Cayley or Cayley-Neumann)},\ \alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{trained};\ \alpha=\beta=\mathbf{1}\Rightarrow W=W_0\big(I+A^{\top}(R^{\top}-I)A\big)
trainable_params: \tfrac{r(r-1)}{2}+2r
locus: any linear layer; acts on the principal input subspace of \(W_0\)
structure: OFT restricted to the \(r\)-dimensional principal input subspace. \(O(r)\) acts on \(W_0\) from the right through the embedding \(R \mapsto I + A^\top(R-I)A\) in \(O(d_{in})\), which is the identity on the orthogonal complement. Two diagonal scalings (\(\alpha\), \(\beta\)) gradually relax exact orthogonality.
mergeable_reason: The adapted weight \(W_{res} + B\,\mathrm{diag}(\beta)\,R\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)\,A\) is a fixed dense matrix after training.
identity_at_init: \(Q = 0\) (so \(R = I\)) and \(\alpha = \beta = 1\) give \(W = W_0\) exactly.
key_idea: Confine orthogonal fine-tuning to the principal subspace of \(W_0\) found by SVD. An \(r\times r\) rotation plus two tunable scaling vectors then preserves the subspace geometry the way OFT does, with LoRA-like memory and far fewer parameters.
results_note: Across 35 NLP/CV tasks and four backbones, avoids the out-of-memory failures of BOFT and GOFTv2/qGOFTv2, gives up to 18x higher parameter efficiency than BOFT, OFTv2 and LoRA variants on the smaller models, the best VTAB-1K average (73.4%), +2.28% over LoRA on LLaMA-3.2-3B GSM8K and +1.4% over LoRA on LLaMA-3.1-8B commonsense reasoning.
categorical_reading: PSOFT is OFT restricted to the principal singular block and saturated by two diagonal tori: \(\Delta W=U_r\Sigma_r(D_\beta C(Q)^\top D_\alpha-I)V_r^\top\). Its image lies in LoRA-XS's linear core (hence in PiSSA's cone), and its default pointing is an apex, because the two relaxation tori are first-order indistinguishable at \(R=I\).

name: PVeRA
paper_title: PVeRA: Probabilistic Vector-Based Random Matrix Adaptation
formula_latex: h = W_0x + \alpha\,\Lambda_b B\, z,\quad z = \mu + \epsilon\odot\sigma,\ \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\quad [\mu;\sigma] = \Lambda_d A x;\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{2r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{frozen random shared};\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{2r},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{trained};\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\sum \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(0,I));\ \text{deterministic inference: } W = W_0 + \alpha\Lambda_b B\,\Lambda_{d_\mu}A_\mu
trainable_params: d_{out} + 2r
locus: linear layers (paper: \(W_q\), \(W_v\) of ViT); shared random matrices as in VeRA
structure: VeRA with a stochastic (VAE-style reparameterised) rank-\(r\) bottleneck: the \(r\)-dim code is sampled from a Gaussian whose mean and std are VeRA-style scaled random projections of \(x\); KL prior on the code (HF PEFT reads the second half of \(\Lambda_d A x\) as a log-variance, \(\sigma = \exp(\tfrac12\log\sigma^2)\), and adds no explicit \(\alpha\))
mergeable_reason: With mean (deterministic) inference \(z = \mu\) the update is a fixed matrix that merges like VeRA; Monte-Carlo sampling mode at test time is input-dependent and cannot be merged.
identity_at_init: \(b = 0\) (HF: \(\lambda_b\) zeros), \(d = d_{initial}\) (0.1); so the adapter output is zero at init
key_idea: Make VeRA's shared-random-basis bottleneck probabilistic so the adapter learns a distribution over adaptations, enabling uncertainty estimates while keeping VeRA's tiny footprint and mergeability.
results_note: Outperforms VeRA and the other benchmarked adapters (seven adapters in total in the comparison) on average on VTAB-1k with ViT backbones; deterministic (mean) inference keeps it mergeable.
categorical_reading: PVeRA is VeRA times a variational coordinate: its merged map factors as \(\rho_{\rm VeRA}\circ\mathrm{pr}\), the \(\sigma\)-half of \(d\) never reaching \(\Theta\) and only shaping the stochastic training forward and the KL term. Under mean inference it is VeRA (toric cone, apex, scalar gauge); Monte-Carlo inference makes it a family over noise that cannot be merged.

name: RandLoRA
full_name: RandLoRA: full-rank PEFT via scaled random bases
paper_title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
formula_latex: \Delta W=\sum_{j=1}^{n}B_j\Lambda_jA\,\Gamma_j,\ \ B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ and shared } A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen random},\ \Lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ \Gamma_j \text{ trainable diagonal},\ n=\lceil\min(d_{in},d_{out})/r\rceil \ (\text{PEFT applies }\Gamma_j\text{ on the smaller dimension})
trainable_params: n\,\big(r+\min(d_{in},d_{out})\big)\ \approx\ \tfrac{d^2}{r}+d \text{ for } d_{in}=d_{out}=d
locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT)
structure: sum of \(n\) frozen random rank-\(r\) bases with trainable diagonal scalings on both sides, reaching full rank; parameter count grows as the basis rank shrinks
mergeable_reason: The scaled sum of bases is a fixed dense matrix.
identity_at_init: PEFT sets \(\Lambda_j = 0\) and \(\Gamma_j\) to the constant \(1/\max(n, \min(d_{in},d_{out}))\) (in practice \(1/\min(d_{in},d_{out})\)), so \(\Delta W = 0\).
key_idea: Separate parameter count from rank: combine many frozen random low-rank bases with learned diagonal scalings to get full-rank updates cheaply.
results_note: Paper reports RandLoRA overtaking LoRA as the parameter budget grows on vision (DinoV2, CLIP), vision-language and commonsense reasoning (e.g. LLaMA3-8B).
categorical_reading: RandLoRA is an \(\oplus\)-sum of \(n=\lceil\min(m,n)/r\rceil\) two-sided-diagonal random-frame terms \(B_j\Lambda_jA\Gamma_j\), with one scalar slide per term (a torus of dimension \(n\)) and \(\dim S_1=nr\) at \(\Lambda=0\); the sum reaches full rank and its rebasing span is \(\Theta\). It factors through LoRA\(_{nr}\) at a degenerate pointing whose stacked \(A_0\) repeats rows.

name: RoAd
paper_title: 3-in-1: 2D Rotary Adaptation for Efficient Finetuning, Efficient Batching and Composability
formula_latex: W=RW_0,\ \ R=\mathrm{blockdiag}_i\Big(\alpha_i\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta_i&-\sin\theta_i\\\sin\theta_i&\cos\theta_i\end{bmatrix}\Big) \text{ over output pairs};\ \ h=r_1\odot(W_0x)+r_2\odot\widehat{(W_0x)}
trainable_params: d_{out}\ (\text{RoAd}_1),\ 2d_{out}\ (\text{RoAd}_2),\ 4d_{out}\ (\text{RoAd}_4)
locus: linear layers (outputs); works with bitsandbytes-quantized bases
structure: block-diagonal 2x2 scaled rotations applied to pairs of output dimensions, implemented element-wise
mergeable_reason: \(R W_0\) is a dense matrix; unmerged it is cheap element-wise ops enabling mixed-adapter batches.
identity_at_init: \(\theta = 0\) and \(\alpha = 1\), so \(R = I\).
key_idea: Fine-tuning mostly rotates representations, so learn tiny 2D rotations that are element-wise (batchable across adapters) and composable.
results_note: Paper reports matching or beating full fine-tuning on GLUE with <0.1% trainable parameters and 2x LoRA's throughput in heterogeneous multi-adapter batches.
categorical_reading: RoAd\(_1\) is (IA)\(^3\) over \(\mathbb C\): the torus \((\mathbb C^\times)^{m/2}\) of scaled 2D rotations acting on pairs of output neurons, with a linear orbit closure of dimension \(m\). It multiplies each pair's input Gram by \(\alpha_i^2\); RoAd\(_{2,4}\) enlarge the torus to the non-abelian block monoid \(M_2(\mathbb R)^{m/2}\).

name: SHiRA
paper_title: Sparse High Rank Adapters
formula_latex: W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W,\quad \|M\|_0 \approx 1\text{--}2\%\ \text{of } d_{out}d_{in}\ \big(\text{HF PEFT: } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\big),\quad M\in\{\text{Struct (rows/cols + diagonal)},\ \text{Rand},\ \text{WM: top-}|W_0|,\ \text{Grad: top-}|g|,\ \text{SNIP: top-}|g\odot W_0|\}
trainable_params: \text{paper: } 1\text{--}2\%\ \text{of each adapted matrix};\ \text{HF PEFT: } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(budget matched to LoRA; the update itself is high-rank)}
locus: any nn.Linear (e.g. attention projections of LLMs, UNet layers of SDXL)
structure: fixed sparse, generally high-rank coordinate mask; SHiRA-Struct = diagonal (high-rank) plus a few full rows/columns (rank-1 part); non-overlapping SHiRA-Struct adapters are nearly orthogonal
mergeable_reason: The adapter overwrites only the masked entries of \(W_0\) (scatter), so it runs in fused mode at original cost while still allowing rapid switching.
identity_at_init: \(\Delta W\) initialized to 0 (HF PEFT init_weights=True).
key_idea: Directly fine-tune 1-2% of the base weights through a static sparse mask; the update is high-rank, can be switched by overwriting a few entries, and multiple sparse adapters interfere less when fused.
results_note: On LLaMA-7B and LLaMA2-7B commonsense reasoning SHiRA is up to 2.7% better than LoRA, and on SDXL style adapters it reduces concept loss in multi-adapter fusion; loading is 5x-16x faster than LoRA fusion on CPU.
categorical_reading: SHiRA is a coordinate sub-object of full fine-tuning, the linear method \(\Delta\mapsto W_0+M\odot\Delta\) (full FT with the complementary coordinates frozen at their base values). Its high rank is a cut property of the support, not of a factorisation.

name: Super-Tuning (Super / Supra)
full_name: Super-Tuning: sparse fine-tuning from activation-aware pruning saliency
paper_title: Super-Tuning: From Activation-Aware Pruning to Sparse Fine-Tuning
hf_peft_config: SupertuningConfig (r=None: Super; r>0: Supra hybrid; select_top=False: bottom-k)
formula_latex: W=W_0+M\odot U\ \big(+\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \text{ in Supra}\big),\ \ M=\mathrm{TopK}\ \text{or}\ \mathrm{BottomK}(S),\ S_{ij}=|W_{0,ij}|\,\|X_{:,j}\|_2 \text{ (paper: Wanda score from a calibration pass) or } S_{ij}=|W_{0,ij}| \text{ (magnitude; the only option in PEFT)}
trainable_params: (1-\text{sparsity})\,d_{in}d_{out}\ \big(+\,r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ for Supra}\big)
locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT)
structure: sparse coordinate mask chosen by Wanda saliency (paper) or data-free weight magnitude (PEFT); Supra = sparse-plus-low-rank
mergeable_reason: Sparse and low-rank deltas are fixed matrices that add into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Sparse values \(U = 0\) and LoRA \(B = 0\).
key_idea: Reuse pruning saliency to choose an unrestricted-rank sparse trainable support at a fixed budget, optionally adding a low-rank part.
results_note: Paper reports Supra beating LoRA on Math17K (Llama-3.2-1B 62.23 vs 61.07; Meta-Llama-3-8B 79.12 vs 73.17).
categorical_reading: A fixed coordinate mask \(W_0+M\odot U\) chosen once from saliency: a Lin method in the standard frame, the same object as SHiRA-WM for TopK magnitude and PaFi's mask for BottomK. Supra adds a LoRA summand (A5), which turns the germ into a cone at the apex.

name: TinyLoRA
paper_title: Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters
formula_latex: W=W_0+U_r\Sigma_r\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{u}v_iP_i\Big)V_r^\top,\ \ U_r,\Sigma_r,V_r \text{ from truncated SVD of } W_0 \text{ (frozen)},\ P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r} \text{ fixed random},\ v\in\mathbb{R}^{u} \text{ trained, optionally tied across modules} \ (\text{PEFT splits } \Sigma_r^{1/2} \text{ to both sides: } U_r\Sigma_r^{1/2}R\,\Sigma_r^{1/2}V_r^\top)
trainable_params: u \text{ per module, or } u \text{ for the whole model with full weight tying}
locus: Linear, Embedding and Conv1D layers
structure: LoRA-XS core \(R=\sum_i v_iP_i\) confined to a \(u\)-dimensional random subspace of \(r\times r\) matrices in the top-\(r\) singular frame of \(W_0\)
mergeable_reason: The update is a fixed rank-\(r\) matrix after training.
identity_at_init: PEFT default init_weights=True sets \(v = 0\), an exact no-op. init_weights='uniform' draws \(v \sim U(-0.02, 0.02)\).
key_idea: With RL, reasoning can be unlocked by a handful of parameters projected through fixed random tensors into the principal singular frame.
results_note: Paper reports Qwen2.5-8B reaching 91% on GSM8K with 13 trained parameters under RL, and RL vastly outperforming SFT at tiny budgets.
categorical_reading: TinyLoRA is a \(u\)-dimensional random linear subspace of LoRA-XS's \(r\times r\) core in the top-\(r\) SVD frame of \(W_0\): a linear method that maps into LoRA-XS and, composing with LoRA-XS\(\to\)PiSSA, into PiSSA. Full weight tying shares one \(v\) across modules, so the per-box covariance of Obs II.15 needs the same transformation on every tied box.

name: Trainable Tokens
formula_latex: E_{t,:}\leftarrow v_t\ (t\in\mathcal{T}),\ \ v_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ trained, initialized to } E_{0,t,:};\ \text{other rows frozen (equivalently } E=E_0+\textstyle\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}e_t(v_t-E_{0,t,:})^\top)
trainable_params: |\mathcal{T}|\,d
locus: rows of the input embedding (and tied LM head)
structure: sparse row mask on the embedding matrix
mergeable_reason: Updated rows are written back into the embedding matrix.
identity_at_init: New row values initialized to the existing token embeddings (no-op).
key_idea: Train only the embeddings of new or special tokens (e.g. reasoning tokens) without full-embedding fine-tuning or a LoRA on the embedding.
results_note: PEFT docs report about 4 GiB VRAM saved on gemma-2-2b versus fully fine-tuning the embedding matrix.
categorical_reading: LoRA-FB with frozen \(B=S_T\), the row selector of the chosen tokens: a Lin row mask on the embedding, regular and idempotent. It lies in the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum of LoRA, not in the default \(\mathrm T_A\) one.

name: Uni-LoRA
full_name: Uni-LoRA: one vector for all LoRA parameters via an isometric projection
paper_title: Uni-LoRA: One Vector is All You Need
formula_latex: \theta_D = P\,\theta_d,\quad \theta_D = \mathrm{Concat}_{\ell}\big(\mathrm{vec}(B^{\ell}),\mathrm{vec}(A^{\ell})\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{D},\ D=\sum_\ell r\,(d^{\ell}_{in}+d^{\ell}_{out}),\quad W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + B^{\ell}A^{\ell};\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times d}\ \text{frozen: each row one-hot at a uniformly random column, column } j \text{ scaled to } 1/\sqrt{n_j};\ \theta_d\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained (a single vector for the whole model)}
trainable_params: d\ \text{for the whole model (independent of } L,\ d_{in},\ d_{out},\ r)
locus: all LoRA-adapted modules of the model jointly (global, cross-layer)
structure: global random isometric projection from one vector to all LoRA factors: a random partition of the \(D\) LoRA entries into \(d\) groups, each group sharing one (\(1/\sqrt{n_j}\)-scaled) value; the projection framework \(\theta_D = P\theta_d\) also expresses LoRA (\(P=I\)), Tied-LoRA, VeRA, LoRA-XS and VB-LoRA
mergeable_reason: \(\theta_d\) determines fixed \(B\), \(A\) for every layer, and each \(BA\) merges into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not exact: \(\theta_d \sim U(-0.02, 0.02)\) (HF default; zeros avoided to prevent vanishing gradients), so \(B\), \(A\) are small and \(\Delta W = BA\) is near zero but non-zero
key_idea: All parameter-efficient LoRA variants are projections of a low-dimensional vector into LoRA's parameter space and differ only in the projection matrix; a global, uniform, isometric random-grouping projection gives maximal cross-layer sharing at negligible cost (matching Fastfood).
results_note: Matches or outperforms state-of-the-art LoRA variants on GLUE, mathematical reasoning (GSM8K/MATH) and instruction tuning while training a single vector for the whole LLM; the random-grouping projection matches Fastfood at much lower cost.
categorical_reading: Uni-LoRA is LoRA precomposed with a frozen random isometric linear map \(P:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^D\): \(\rho=\rho_{\rm LoRA}\circ P\), a quadratic cone in \(\theta_d\) with \(S_1=0\) at \(\theta_d=0\), which is why it must start off the base point. Its 'projection framework' parametrises a family of objects by \(P\); different fixed \(P\) give incomparable images, so it supplies arrows into LoRA, not arrows from the methods it 'generalises'.

name: VB-LoRA
paper_title: VB-LoRA: Extreme Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning with Vector Banks
formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad \text{every length-}b\text{ sub-vector } u \text{ of every column of } B \text{ and row of } A:\ u = \sum_{s=1}^{h} w_s(\sigma)\,\alpha_s,\ \ w(\sigma) = \mathrm{Softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(\sigma,k)\big);\ \text{bank } \{\alpha_s\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\}_{s=1}^{h}\ \text{shared by all modules and layers (trained)},\ \sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{h}\ \text{logits per sub-vector (trained)}
trainable_params: \text{training: } \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\,h\ \text{logits per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared};\ \ \text{stored } (k=2,\ \text{uint8 indices}): \tfrac{3}{2}\,\tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{b}\ \text{per matrix} + hb\ \text{shared}
locus: any linear layer, sharing across modules and layers (paper: query/value or all linear layers of RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama2, Mistral, Gemma)
structure: divide-and-share: LoRA's rank-one component vectors are split into sub-vectors, each a sparse top-\(k\) convex combination (simplex-constrained) of a globally shared vector bank -- a hierarchical, constrained CP/tensor factorisation spanning the whole model
mergeable_reason: After training the logits are discarded, the selected mixtures define fixed \(B\), \(A\), and \(BA\) merges into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not exact: bank \(\sim U(-0.02, 0.02)\) and logits \(\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.1^2)\) (HF defaults), so \(\Delta W\) is small but non-zero; an all-zero bank is avoided because it would give zero gradients
key_idea: Treat all LoRA parameters of a model as sub-vectors drawn from one small learned vector bank via differentiable sparse top-\(k\) admixture, so storage stops scaling with model width, depth and number of modules.
results_note: On Llama2-13B instruction tuning VB-LoRA uses only 0.4% of LoRA's stored parameters yet scores higher on MT-Bench; competitive with or better than VeRA, Tied-LoRA and LoRA on GLUE, E2E (about 20% fewer stored parameters than VeRA) and GSM8K/MATH (Mistral-7B, Gemma-7B).
categorical_reading: VB-LoRA assembles every length-\(b\) chunk of LoRA's factors as a top-\(k\) softmax mixture of one shared trainable bank: on each top-\(k\) chamber \(\rho=\rho_{\rm LoRA}\circ h\) with \(h\) of degree two, so the image is a cone with \(S_1=0\) at a zero bank and the method starts at a small defect. Its geometry is the imposed chunk partition \(\Pi\) (a reshape \(\mathbb R^m=\mathbb R^{m/b}\otimes\mathbb R^b\) tied across all boxes), not a random frame, since the bank is trained.

name: VeRA
paper_title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
formula_latex: h=W_0x+\Lambda_bB\Lambda_dAx,\ \ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ frozen random, shared across layers},\ \Lambda_d=\mathrm{diag}(d),\Lambda_b=\mathrm{diag}(b) \text{ trained}
trainable_params: r+d_{out}
locus: linear layers (shared \(A\)/\(B\) sliced to each layer's shape)
structure: frozen shared random low-rank bases with trainable diagonal scalings on both sides
mergeable_reason: \(\Lambda_b B \Lambda_d A\) is a fixed low-rank matrix.
identity_at_init: \(b = 0\) (\(d = 0.1\)), so the update is zero.
key_idea: Random projections are good enough as LoRA bases; only learn per-layer scaling vectors.
results_note: Paper reports matching LoRA with 10x fewer trainable parameters on GLUE, E2E and instruction tuning.
categorical_reading: VeRA is the toric cone \(\{\Lambda_bB\Lambda_dA\}\) of dimension \(m+r-1\): an A3 sub-object of LoRA-FA\((A)\) via \(h(b,d)=\Lambda_bB\Lambda_d\), with apex at \(b=0\), a one-scalar gauge and rebasing closure exactly LoRA-FA\((A)\) (Thm V.3, Cor 3). It is the NOLA construction with coordinate-structured bases \(E_{ii}B\), \(E_{jj}A\).

name: WaveFT
paper_title: Exploring Sparsity for Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning Using Wavelets for Vision
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \lambda\,\mathrm{IDWT}_{2D}(C),\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{sparse: exactly } p \text{ entries chosen uniformly at random are trainable, the rest fixed at } 0
trainable_params: p\ \ (\text{any integer, e.g. far below LoRA's rank-1 count } d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (paper: SDXL attention layers for personalisation, ViT-Base, RoBERTa on GLUE)
structure: sparse coefficients in a 2-D discrete wavelet basis (semi-local receptive fields); SHiRA is the special case IDWT = identity; the linear, rank-preserving IDWT keeps the high-rank property of sparse updates
mergeable_reason: The inverse wavelet transform of the trained sparse coefficients is a dense matrix added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(C = 0\), so \(W = W_0\) at the start of training (Gaussian init explored as an ablation)
key_idea: Learn highly sparse updates in the wavelet domain: wavelets aggregate spatially coherent gradients (better coverage than raw weight sparsity) without the global interference of Fourier bases, giving fine-grained parameter control below LoRA's minimum.
results_note: On DreamBooth with SDXL WaveFT reaches 0.495 DINO similarity versus LoRA's 0.463 at equal parameter counts with higher diversity; on ViT-Base it reaches 78.29% average accuracy with 72K parameters versus LoRA's 77.58% at 581K; slightly below FourierFT on GLUE.
categorical_reading: WaveFT is a mask in the 2-D wavelet frame, \(\Delta W=\lambda\,\mathrm{IDWT}_{2D}(C_\Omega)\), i.e. SHiRA transported by the invertible IDWT: a transport is an automorphism of the slice and not an arrow, so WaveFT and SHiRA are the same kind of object in different frames, with different images. With a separable DWT every atom is a rank-one outer product, so WaveFT factors through LoRA-FA with frozen wavelet frames.

name: DoRA
paper_title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: W_{i,:}=m_i\,\frac{(W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)_{i,:}}{\|(W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)_{i,:}\|_2},\ \ m\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ trained (init } m_i=\|(W_0)_{i,:}\|_2),\ B,A \text{ as LoRA}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+d_{out}
locus: linear, embedding and Conv1d/2d/3d layers (PEFT DoRA variants)
structure: magnitude-direction decomposition: learned per-output norm times the normalized (\(W_0\) + low-rank) direction (the paper's 'column-wise' norm in its transposed convention)
mergeable_reason: After training \(m\) and the normalized direction combine into one dense weight (merging recommended to remove the overhead).
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) and \(m =\) row norms of \(W_0\), so \(W = W_0\).
key_idea: Full fine-tuning changes magnitude and direction differently; let LoRA handle direction and a separate vector handle magnitude.
results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over LoRA on commonsense reasoning (LLaMA family), visual instruction tuning and image/video-text understanding.
categorical_reading: DoRA's image is \(\mathrm{Diag}_m\cdot(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})\), exactly LoRA followed by a trainable output scale (Prop II.8): a torus saturation of LoRA's cone that inherits LoRA's apex and \(GL_r\) gauge. What it adds beyond that image is training geometry (the row-normalised metric, or HF's detached, non-gradient backward).

name: rsLoRA
paper_title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
formula_latex: W=W_0+\gamma_r BA,\quad \gamma_r=\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}\ \ (\text{instead of }\tfrac{\alpha}{r}),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: same \(\Delta W=BA\) as LoRA; only the scalar multiplier changes so that activations and gradients stay \(\Theta(1)\) as \(r\) grows
mergeable_reason: Identical to LoRA up to a scalar.
identity_at_init: \(B=0\) as in LoRA.
key_idea: Shows that the standard \(\alpha/r\) scaling makes higher-rank adapters learn too slowly (gradient collapse), and that \(\alpha/\sqrt{r}\) is the rank-stable choice that lets larger ranks actually help.
results_note: Fine-tuning Llama 2 on 20k OpenOrca examples with \(r \in \{4,\dots,2048\}\): with \(\alpha/r\) larger ranks learn no better (gradient collapse), while with \(\alpha/\sqrt{r}\) perplexity keeps improving as \(r\) grows and gradient norms stay rank-stable.
categorical_reading: rsLoRA is LoRA itself: the scale change is the isomorphism \(h=(\sqrt r\,B,A)\) of the slice, or equivalently a point of the hyperparameter torus (Thm III.10). Its content is a choice of trajectory \(r\mapsto(\alpha,\eta)\) across ranks, not a new object.

name: PiSSA
full_name: Principal Singular values and Singular vectors Adaptation
paper_title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: W_0=U S V^\top,\quad B=U_{[:,:r]}S_{[:r,:r]}^{1/2},\quad A=S_{[:r,:r]}^{1/2}V_{[:,:r]}^\top,\quad W^{res}=U_{[:,r:]}S_{[r:,r:]}V_{[:,r:]}^\top=W_0-BA,\qquad h=(W^{res}+BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections)
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space (\(\Delta W = BA - B_0A_0\)); the base point is moved from \(W_0\) to the rank-\((\min(d_{in},d_{out})-r)\) residual \(W^{res}\) and the adapter starts on the principal rank-\(r\) SVD component of \(W_0\)
mergeable_reason: \(W^{res}+BA\) is a dense matrix of the original shape; to ship as a plain LoRA on the untouched \(W_0\) the paper converts it to \(\Delta W=[B'\ B][A';-A]\) at rank \(2r\).
identity_at_init: Exact: \(W^{res}+B_0A_0=W_0\) by construction (data-free truncated SVD of \(W_0\); fast randomized SVD makes it seconds).
key_idea: Instead of zero-initializing the adapter, put the top-\(r\) singular triplets of \(W_0\) into the trainable factors and freeze the residual, so training updates the directions that matter most and converges faster; the residual also quantizes better (QPiSSA).
results_note: Reported consistent gains over LoRA on 11 models (184M-70B), e.g. GSM8K 53.22 vs 42.85 on LLaMA-2-7B and 77.78 vs 74.53 on Gemma-7B; QPiSSA on LLaMA-3-70B reaches 86.05 vs 81.73 for QLoRA.
categorical_reading: PiSSA is the Type II point \(P=[W_0]_r\) of the stratum \(\mathcal M_r\): the vertex moves to \(W_0-[W_0]_r\), \(\theta_0\) becomes a smooth point with full first-order reach, and the pointing is balanced at equal rates (Prop III.8). Measured from \(\theta_0\), its updates \(Y-P\) reach rank \(2r\), which is the PiSSA \(\to\) LoRA\(_{2r}\) conversion.

name: OLoRA
paper_title: OLoRA: Orthonormal Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: W_0=QR,\quad B_0=Q_{[:,1:r]},\quad A_0=R_{[1:r,:]},\quad W^{res}=W_0-s\,B_0A_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+s\,BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}\ \ (s=\alpha/r,\text{ or }\alpha/\sqrt r\text{ with rsLoRA, in HF PEFT})
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space; \(B\) starts with orthonormal columns (first \(r\) columns of the QR factor \(Q\) of \(W_0\)) and \(A\) with the first \(r\) rows of the upper-triangular factor \(R\)
mergeable_reason: \(W^{res}+s\,BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: Exact as implemented in HF PEFT (olora_init subtracts \(s B_0A_0\) and the forward adds \(s BA\)); data-free QR of \(W_0\). Note the paper's Alg. 1 subtracts \(s B_0A_0\) but writes the forward as \(W+B A\), which is exact only for \(s=1\).
key_idea: Use a cheap QR decomposition of \(W_0\) to give the adapter an orthonormal starting basis, which the author argues improves conditioning, stability and convergence speed.
results_note: Reported higher final accuracy than LoRA in 53 of 60 model/task/rank settings on six commonsense benchmarks for Mistral-7B, LLaMA-2-7B, TinyLlama-1.1B, Gemma-2B and OPT-1.3B.
categorical_reading: OLoRA is another point of the Type II stratum, \(P=Q_rR_r\), chosen by a QR flag rather than a spectral frame. The flag privileges the first \(r\) input coordinates, so unlike PiSSA its pointing is not permutation-natural, and its charge \(\Phi_0=I/\eta_B-R_rR_r^\top/\eta_A\) is generally unbalanced.

name: LoftQ
paper_title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(init_lora_weights="loftq", loftq_config=LoftQConfig(loftq_bits=4, loftq_iter=1))  (on the full-precision model; or replace_lora_weights_loftq(peft_model) on a bnb-quantized model)
formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert_F:\quad Q_t=q_N(W_0-B_{t-1}A_{t-1}),\ \ W_0-Q_t=\textstyle\sum_i\sigma_{t,i}u_{t,i}v_{t,i}^\top,\ \ B_t=[\sqrt{\sigma_{t,i}}u_{t,i}]_{i\le r},\ A_t=[\sqrt{\sigma_{t,i}}v_{t,i}^\top]_{i\le r};\qquad h=(Q_T+BA)x;\ Q_T\text{ frozen (N-bit)},\ A,B\text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer of a quantized model
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space; the base point is an \(N\)-bit quantized matrix \(Q\) and the adapter is initialized to the rank-\(r\) SVD of the quantization residual, alternating \(T\) times
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) can be added to the dequantized \(Q\), but the merged matrix is no longer \(N\)-bit unless re-quantized, which reintroduces error.
identity_at_init: Approximate: \(Q_T+B_TA_T\approx W_0\) (built to be closer than QLoRA's \(Q+0\); HF's initialiser ignores the LoRA scale \(s=\alpha/r\), so with one iteration it is closer only for \(0<s<2\)); data-free alternating quantization/SVD.
key_idea: When the base will be quantized, choose the quantized base and the low-rank adapter jointly so that their sum best approximates \(W_0\), instead of zero-initializing the adapter on top of an inaccurate quantized weight.
results_note: Reported large gains over QLoRA at low bit widths, e.g. about 8% on MNLI and over 10% on SQuAD v1.1 at 2-bit, and convergence where QLoRA fails.
categorical_reading: LoftQ is base change along the quantiser followed by an approximate section: it chooses \((Q,q_0)\) with \(\rho(q_0)\) close to \(\theta_0\), landing at a smooth point of the cone over \(Q_T\). With one iteration it is QLoRA's own map \(\kappa\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), re-pointed from the apex to \(s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(\theta_0-\kappa\theta_0)=-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\), with \(s=\alpha/r\) the LoRA scale that HF's initialiser ignores (Prop V.2(b)).

name: EVA
paper_title: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning via Explained Variance Adaptation
formula_latex: X^{\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times d_{in}}\ \text{(input activations)}=U\Sigma V^\top\ \text{(incremental SVD)},\quad A^{\ell}=V_{[:,:r_\ell]}^\top,\quad B^{\ell}=0,\quad \xi_j=\frac{\sigma_j^2}{(M-1)\lVert\sigma\rVert_1},\quad \{r_\ell\}=\text{top-}Nr\text{ of }\{\xi_j^\ell\}_{j\le \rho r},\qquad h=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha_\ell}{r_\ell}B^{\ell}A^{\ell}x,\ \alpha_\ell=\alpha\,r_\ell/r\ (\text{effective scale }\alpha/r\text{ in every layer});\ W_0\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: r_\ell(d_{in}+d_{out}),\ \ \textstyle\sum_\ell r_\ell=N r,\ r_\ell\le\rho r
locus: any linear layer; ranks redistributed across all adapted layers
structure: \(\Delta W=BA\) with \(A\) spanning the top right-singular (principal input-activation) directions of the downstream data; per-layer rank \(r_\ell\) chosen by globally ranking explained-variance ratios
mergeable_reason: Plain LoRA update on an untouched \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B=0\) (\(W_0\) untouched); \(A\) is data-driven: top right-singular vectors of minibatch input activations, computed by incremental SVD until cosine similarity of successive estimates exceeds a threshold \(\tau\).
key_idea: Initialize the down-projection on the directions of maximal input-activation variance for the downstream task and redistribute a fixed rank budget to the layers whose activations have the most explainable variance.
results_note: Reported the highest average score among LoRA initializations across 51 tasks spanning language generation/understanding, image classification and RL, with initialization costing about 0.7% of training time.
categorical_reading: EVA is LoRA in the stratum \(\mathrm T_A\) at the data-chosen point \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0=\) top-\(r_\ell\) input principal subspace of \(\mathrm{Gr}(r_\ell,n)\): same cone \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r_\ell}\) and apex as LoRA, but a different isomorphism class of pointed object, detected by \(S_1=\{XV_{r_\ell}^\top\}\) (Thm II.2(a)). Its image is \(GL\times GL\)-covariant; only the pointing and the rank allocation are \(CO(n)\)-covariant (Prop II.16).

name: CorDA
paper_title: CorDA: Context-Oriented Decomposition Adaptation of Large Language Models for Task-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
