formula_latex: C=XX^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}},\quad \mathrm{SVD}(W_0C)=U\Sigma V^\top,\quad W_0=U\Sigma(V^\top C^{-1});\ \ \text{IPM: }B=U_{[:,:r]}\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2},\ A=\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2}(V^\top C^{-1})_{[:r,:]};\ \ \text{KPM: same with the last }r\text{ components};\quad W'=W_0-BA,\ \ h=(W'+BA)x;\ W'\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space; the base point is split along the singular directions of \(W_0C\) (covariance-whitened weight), i.e. a generalized SVD of \(W_0\) w.r.t. the input-activation metric \(C\)
mergeable_reason: \(W'+BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(W'+B_0A_0=W_0\) because the \(C^{-1}\) factor undoes the covariance orientation; data-driven (covariance from a few hundred task or QA samples).
key_idea: Orient the weight decomposition by the covariance of activations from either the downstream task (instruction-previewed mode: train the dominant components) or world-knowledge data (knowledge-preserved mode: train the least-used components to limit forgetting).
results_note: Reported IPM GSM8K 53.90 / MATH 8.52 vs PiSSA 51.48 / 7.60 on LLaMA-2-7B, KPM preserving more NQ-open knowledge than LoRA, and best GLUE average (83.38) with RoBERTa-base.
categorical_reading: CorDA is a Type II pointing of LoRA (stratum \(\mathrm S\)): the cone is translated to the vertex \(W_0-P\), \(P=[W_0C]_rC^{-1}\) (IPM) or its covariance-oriented tail (KPM), so \(\theta_0\) is a smooth point with full first-order reach \(S_1=T_P\mathcal M_r\). The split is \(CO(m)\times CO(n)\)-covariant undamped (Prop II.16(b)); damping \(C+\lambda I\) cuts the input side to \(O(n)\).

name: Astra
paper_title: Astra: Activation-Space Tail-Eigenvector Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: \mathrm{Cov}(y)=\mathbb{E}[yy^\top]-\mathbb{E}[y]\mathbb{E}[y]^\top=Q\Lambda Q^\top,\ y=W_0x,\quad B_0=Q_{tail}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_0=Q_{tail}^\top W_0,\quad W^{res}=W_0-B_0A_0=(I-Q_{tail}Q_{tail}^\top)W_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+BA)x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space whose output side starts on the \(r\) tail eigenvectors (smallest eigenvalues) of the output-activation covariance; the base is \(W_0\) projected off that subspace
mergeable_reason: \(W^{res}+BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(B_0A_0=Q_{tail}Q_{tail}^\top W_0\) is subtracted from the base; data-driven from a small calibration set (e.g. 64 samples).
key_idea: Characterize each layer by the output activations it produces on the downstream task and place the trainable update in the under-used tail eigenspace of those activations, which preserves dominant behaviour while giving room for task adaptation.
results_note: Reported outperforming LoRA/PiSSA/CorDA-style baselines on 16 NLU and NLG benchmarks at equal or lower rank, sometimes surpassing full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: Astra is a Type II split with vertex \(W_0-\Pi_{\rm tail}W_0\), \(\Pi_{\rm tail}\) the tail eigenprojector of the output covariance \(W_0\,\mathrm{Cov}(x)\,W_0^\top\); because the split sees the data only through that output covariance it is \(CO(m)\times GL(n)\)-covariant (Prop II.16(a), with \(C\) the centred input covariance). On layers with \(d_{\rm out}-\operatorname{rank}W_0\ge r\) the tail lies in \(\mathrm{coker}\,W_0\), \(A_0=0\), and the pointing collapses into the apex stratum \(\mathrm T_B\).

name: MiCA
paper_title: MiCA Learns More Knowledge Than LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^\top;\ B=U_{[:,-r:]} \text{ (frozen)},\ A=0 \text{ (trained)};\ W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA
trainable_params: r\,d_{in}
locus: linear and embedding layers
structure: update confined to the column space of the \(r\) minor left-singular vectors of \(W_0\) (\(B\) fixed, only \(A\) learned)
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) is a fixed low-rank update.
identity_at_init: \(A = 0\) (exact no-op without modifying the base weight).
key_idea: Write new knowledge into the least-used singular directions of the pretrained weight to absorb more and interfere less.
results_note: Paper reports up to 5.9x better knowledge acquisition than LoRA, e.g. 61.33% vs 58.28% on BLOGS-MC with Llama-2-7B.
categorical_reading: MiCA is the one-sided method \(\mathrm{FB}(U_{-r})\) in the minor left-singular frame: an A2 sub-object of LoRA pointed in stratum \(\mathrm T_B\), and also of MiLoRA, whose image \(W_p+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) contains \(W_0+\{U_{-r}Y\}\). Its image is a fixed affine subspace, so merge-and-restart with the frame frozen is idempotent.

name: LoRA-GA
paper_title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
formula_latex: G=\nabla_{W}\mathcal{L}(W_0)=USV^\top,\quad A_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\quad B_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}U_{[:,r+1:2r]},\quad W^{res}=W_0-\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}B_0A_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space; \(A\) and \(B\) are initialized from disjoint blocks of the top-\(2r\) singular vectors of a sampled full gradient so that the first LoRA step \(\eta^2(G A_0^\top A_0+B_0B_0^\top G)\) best approximates \(\zeta G\)
mergeable_reason: \(W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape (but the base differs from \(W_0\), so the adapter alone is not a LoRA on \(W_0\)).
identity_at_init: Exact: the offset \(W_0-\eta B_0A_0\) cancels the nonzero adapter; initialization is gradient-driven (one sampled batch, layer-by-layer backward for \(O(1)\) memory) with the stable scale factor \(\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}/\sqrt{\gamma}\) (paired with \(\eta=\alpha/\sqrt r\)) chosen so that forward and backward magnitudes stay rank- and width-stable.
key_idea: Choose \(A\) and \(B\) from the SVD of the full-fine-tuning gradient so that the very first LoRA update is the best low-rank approximation of the full-fine-tuning update, with a rank- and width-stable scale.
results_note: Reported +5.69% over LoRA on a GLUE subset with T5-Base and +0.34 / +11.52 / +5.05 points on MT-Bench / GSM8K / HumanEval with LLaMA-2-7B, converging 2-4x faster than LoRA.
categorical_reading: LoRA-GA is a Type II object: it picks the point \(P\propto U_{G,[r+1:2r]}V_{G,[1:r]}^\top\) of the stratum \(\mathcal M_r\) and moves the cone's vertex to \(\theta_0-P\), combining smoothness, gradient alignment of \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\) and a stable scale (Prop II.3). It is incomparable with zero-init LoRA.

name: KaSA
paper_title: KaSA: Knowledge-Aware Singular-Value Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: W_0=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\quad W_{world}=\sum_{i=1}^{k-r}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\qquad W=W_{world}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A,\qquad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\textstyle\sum_j\Delta\sigma_j^2+\gamma\big(\lVert B^\top B-I_r\rVert_F+\lVert AA^\top-I_r\rVert_F\big);\ W_{world}\text{ frozen},\ B,\Delta\sigma,A\text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+r
locus: linear layers (attention and MLP projections)
structure: SVD-shaped update \(\Delta W=B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A\) with soft orthogonality on \(B,A\) and a learnable singular-value vector, added on top of a base whose \(r\) smallest singular components were removed
mergeable_reason: \(B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A\) is a dense \(d_{out}\times d_{in}\) matrix that folds into the (truncated) base, though the truncation itself is irreversible.
identity_at_init: Not exact: \(B=0\) (official repo and HF KasaLinearVariant; \(\Delta\sigma\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)\), \(A\) Kaiming-uniform) makes the adapter zero, but the base is permanently truncated by its \(r\) smallest singular components (a small, data-free perturbation of \(W_0\)).
key_idea: Treat the smallest singular components of \(W_0\) as task-irrelevant noise, discard them, and relearn that subspace with an explicitly SVD-shaped adapter whose singular values are learned and regularized.
results_note: Reported outperforming 14 PEFT baselines on GLUE (86.3 average with RoBERTa-base at about 0.24% trainable parameters), instruction following and commonsense benchmarks.
categorical_reading: KaSA is base change along the truncation \(\kappa:W_0\mapsto W_0-[W_0]_{\rm tail\,r}\) followed by a diagonal-core LoRA at \(\kappa\theta_0\): like QLoRA it carries the defect \(e=-[W_0]_{\rm tail\,r}\). Its image is exactly MiLoRA's, \(W_p+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), but it starts at the vertex \(W_p\) instead of the smooth point \(\theta_0\), so the two are related only by a weak morphism.

name: aLoRA
paper_title: Activated LoRA: Fine-tuned LLMs for Intrinsics
formula_latex: h_t=\begin{cases}W_0x_t,& t<t_{inv}\\(W_0+BA)\,x_t,& t\ge t_{inv}\end{cases}\quad\text{for } W\in\{W_q,W_k,W_v\}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: attention projections of causal LMs, applied only to tokens at/after the invocation sequence
structure: token-position-gated low-rank update: identity before the invocation token, LoRA after it, so prefix KV caches equal the base model's
mergeable_reason: The adapter is applied selectively by token position, so it cannot be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) as in LoRA.
key_idea: Activate the adapter only after an invocation string, so the base model's KV cache can be reused and adapters can be switched in mid-conversation for free.
results_note: Paper reports 2-7x faster adapter generation even for 250-token prompts and over 20x on long prompts, with no consistent accuracy difference from LoRA.
categorical_reading: Activated LoRA is LoRA pulled back along a position gate: a family \(T\to Q\) that sits at \(q_0\) before the invocation token, so its realisation \(\Phi\circ\rho\circ a\) is not \(\Phi_f(\theta)\) for any single \(\theta\). Being pointed before \(t_{inv}\) is what makes the base KV cache reusable, and it is also what blocks merging.

name: QA-LoRA
paper_title: QA-LoRA: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
formula_latex: \tilde W=\alpha\odot(\hat W-\beta),\ \hat W=\lfloor W_0/\alpha\rceil+\beta \text{ (group-wise INT-}k\text{, group size } g);\ h=\tilde Wx+s\,BA\,\mathrm{pool}_g(x),\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}/g} \ (\mathrm{pool}_g=\text{sum over each group});\ \text{merge: } \beta'=\beta-s\,\mathrm{expand}_g(BA)\oslash\alpha
trainable_params: r\big(\tfrac{d_{in}}{g}+d_{out}\big)
locus: linear layers of a group-wise quantized (GPTQ) model
structure: LoRA on group-average-pooled inputs, so the update is constant within each quantization group
mergeable_reason: The group-constant update is absorbed into the quantization zero-points, keeping the merged model in INT4.
key_idea: Balance quantization and adaptation degrees of freedom with group-wise pooling so the fine-tuned model stays quantized after merging.
results_note: Paper reports LLaMA-7B 5-shot MMLU 39.4 vs 36.0 for QLoRA+GPTQ at INT4, with faster inference.
categorical_reading: QA-LoRA is QLoRA precomposed with group pooling: LoRA on the quotient of the input space by the quantisation groups, so its image is the determinantal cone inside the group-constant subspace. That subspace is exactly the zero-point direction of the quantiser, which is why this is the one adapter whose exact merge stays in the quantised type.

name: MonteCLoRA
paper_title: Robust and Efficient Fine-tuning of LLMs with Bayesian Reparameterization of Low-Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: A=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\pi_k\theta_k,\ \theta_k\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma),\ \Sigma\sim\mathcal{W}_r(V,n),\ \pi\sim\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha),\ \mu=A_{LoRA};\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\eta\,(\mathrm{KL}_{\mathcal{D}}+\mathrm{KL}_{\mathcal{W}}+\mathrm{KL}_{\mathcal{N}})+\textstyle\sum_k\pi_k^2
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+O(r+N)
locus: same as LoRA (training-time variational sampler on lora_A)
structure: LoRA whose \(A\) factor is treated as a Gaussian mixture (Wishart covariance, Dirichlet weights) estimated by Monte Carlo during training; plain LoRA at inference
mergeable_reason: At inference the sampler is disabled and the adapter is a standard LoRA.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) as in LoRA.
key_idea: Treat low-rank parameters as a distribution and average Monte Carlo samples to make LoRA robust to hyperparameters.
results_note: Paper reports up to 62% lower accuracy spread than LoRA across hyperparameters on LLaMA-3.2-3B (and 53% on LLaMA-1-7B commonsense).
categorical_reading: MonteCLoRA is LoRA times an inert factor: LoRA \(\to\) MonteCLoRA \(\to\) LoRA (freeze the variational coordinates, then project them out), so the two simulate each other without being isomorphic. Everything it adds is trained-method data: a stochastic cotangent signal for \(A\) plus KL penalties.

name: VeLoRA
full_name: Memory-efficient training with rank-1 sub-token projections
paper_title: VeLoRA: Memory Efficient Training using Rank-1 Sub-Token Projections
formula_latex: \text{fwd: } z=\mathrm{group}_M(x),\ z_p=z\,v \text{ (stored)};\ \text{bwd: } \hat x=\mathrm{ungroup}(z_pv^\top),\ \nabla_A\mathcal{L}=\delta^\top\hat x;\ v\in\mathbb{R}^{M} \text{ fixed (first-batch average)}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \ (\text{unchanged; saves activation memory})
locus: input activations of the LoRA \(A\) projection
structure: activation compression for the backward pass: sub-tokens projected onto a fixed rank-1 direction and coarsely reconstructed when computing weight gradients
mergeable_reason: Only the backward pass changes; the adapter is a standard LoRA.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) as in LoRA.
key_idea: Weight gradients tolerate coarse activations, so store each sub-token as a single scalar along a fixed vector instead of the full activation.
results_note: Paper reports beating QLoRA by 0.5pp on LLaMA-7B with 15.4% less memory, and 45% less memory than GaLore on RoBERTa.
categorical_reading: VeLoRA keeps LoRA's object and replaces its backward lens by an approximate one: the \(A\)-block is fed \(\hat G\) while \(B\) is fed the true \(G\). By Thm III.5 this block-dependent cotangent breaks LoRA's Noether charge, which is the dynamical cost of the activation-memory saving.

name: BD-LoRA
paper_title: Block-Diagonal LoRA for Eliminating Communication Overhead in Tensor Parallel LoRA Serving
formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,BA,\ \ B=\mathrm{diag}(B_1,\dots,B_N),\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{N}\times\frac{r}{N}}\ (\text{column-sharded: } W_q,W_k,W_v,\text{up},\text{gate})\ \text{or}\ A=\mathrm{diag}(A_1,\dots,A_N),\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{N}\times\frac{d_{in}}{N}}\ (\text{row-sharded: } W_o,\text{down}),\ N=\text{tensor-parallel degree};\ s=\alpha/\sqrt{r/N}\ \text{in the paper (rsLoRA-style, since it trains independent rank-}r/N\text{ adapters per shard); HF uses the LoraConfig scaling}
trainable_params: r\,d_{in}+\tfrac{r}{N}d_{out}\ \ (B\ \text{block-diagonal})\quad\text{or}\quad \tfrac{r}{N}d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \ (A\ \text{block-diagonal})
locus: attention and MLP projections, with the block-diagonal factor chosen to match the layer's tensor-parallel sharding
structure: LoRA with one factor constrained to a block-diagonal matrix aligned with the tensor-parallel shards, so the adapter factors through a direct sum of \(N\) per-device maps and needs no extra all-gather/all-reduce.
mergeable_reason: It is a constrained LoRA, so \(BA\) can be merged; the design target is unmerged multi-adapter serving.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (\(B = 0\), or \(B_i = 0\) per block), so \(\Delta W = 0\).
key_idea: Choose the shape of the adapter to fit the hardware sharding: block-diagonal factors make multi-LoRA serving communication-free with almost no loss in quality per parameter.
results_note: Matches LoRA's downstream quality at similar parameter counts and gives up to 1.79x end-to-end serving speed-up over S-LoRA tensor parallelism for Llama-3.1-8B on eight A100 GPUs.
categorical_reading: BD-LoRA is the \(\oplus\) of \(N\) row-block-embedded \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r/N}\), i.e. GraLoRA with the grid on one side only. It is a constrained sub-object of LoRA, chosen so that the adapter factors through the direct sum of the tensor-parallel shards (a hardware-imposed \(\Pi\)).

name: GenKnowSub
paper_title: GenKnowSub: Improving Modularity and Reusability of LLMs through General Knowledge Subtraction
formula_latex: A_i\leftarrow A_i-\tfrac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}A^{gen}_g,\ \ B_i\leftarrow B_i-\tfrac{1}{G}\sum_{g=1}^{G}B^{gen}_g \text{ (PEFT implementation)};\ \text{then Arrow routing over the residual experts}
trainable_params: 0 \ (\text{post-hoc arithmetic on trained adapters})
locus: LoRA library used by Arrow
structure: adapter arithmetic: subtract the mean general-domain LoRA from each task LoRA to obtain residual task modules, then route
mergeable_reason: Inference uses token-level Arrow routing.
identity_at_init: Not applicable (operates on trained adapters).
key_idea: Task LoRAs carry generic language knowledge; subtracting a general-knowledge LoRA purifies them and improves zero-shot recombination.
results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over Arrow on Phi-3 in monolingual and cross-lingual settings, also confirmed on Phi-2.
categorical_reading: GenKnowSub is a post-hoc map on factor tuples composed with Arrow's \(F_X\) router. It subtracts factors rather than products, and \((B_i-\bar B)(A_i-\bar A)=B_iA_i-B_i\bar A-\bar BA_i+\bar B\bar A\) depends on the gauge representatives. By Prop V.4 it is well defined only after a joint gauge fixing, such as a shared frozen \(A\).

name: LoRA+
full_name: LoRA+ (decoupled learning rates for A and B)
paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA;\qquad A \leftarrow A - \eta_A\, g_A,\quad B \leftarrow B - \eta_B\, g_B,\quad \eta_B = \lambda\,\eta_A,\ \ \lambda\gg 1\ (\text{e.g. } \lambda=2^4)
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: same as LoRA
structure: Unchanged rank-\(r\) factorization; the optimizer applies a block-diagonal learning-rate operator \(\mathrm{diag}(\eta_A I,\ \lambda\eta_A I)\) to \((A,B)\). Infinite-width analysis: efficient feature learning requires \(\eta_A=\Theta(n^{-1}),\ \eta_B=\Theta(1)\), i.e. \(\eta_B/\eta_A=\Theta(n)\) (\(n\) = model width); this explicitly breaks the \(GL(r)\) gauge symmetry in favour of \(B\).
mergeable_reason: Only the training procedure changes; the trained adapter is a standard LoRA product that merges into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(\Delta W = 0\) at init under either zero-product scheme analysed in the paper: Init[1] (\(B = 0\), \(A\) random with variance \(\Theta(1/n)\); the standard LoRA/PEFT default) or Init[2] (\(A = 0\), \(B\) random with variance \(\Theta(1)\)). Most of the paper's experiments (and the recommended ratio \(\lambda \sim 2^4\) for RoBERTa) use Init[2]; with Init[1] the optimal ratio is smaller (\(\sim 2^2\)-\(2^3\)).
key_idea: With one shared learning rate, \(A\) and \(B\) cannot both learn features efficiently as width grows; setting the \(B\) learning rate a fixed large multiple of the \(A\) learning rate fixes this while keeping a 1-D LR search.
results_note: Reports 1-2% accuracy improvements and up to ~2x faster fine-tuning at the same compute as LoRA (RoBERTa/GPT-2 on GLUE, Llama-7b on MNLI and flan-v2/MMLU); the best ratio is model/task/init dependent: \(\sim 2^4\) for RoBERTa with Init[2], \(\sim 2^2\)-\(2^3\) with Init[1], \(\sim 2^1\)-\(2^2\) for Llama.
categorical_reading: LoRA+ is not a new object but a point of LoRA's hyperparameter torus: under Adam, from zero-initialised \(B\), its ratio \(\lambda\) is absorbed into \(\alpha\), so any gain must come from torus-breaking ingredients (global clipping, a shared \(\varepsilon\) or decay). Under gradient flow it moves the crossover scale \(\sigma^*\) by \(\sqrt\lambda\), and LoRA-FA is the endpoint \(\lambda\to\infty\).

name: LoRA-FA
paper_title: LoRA-FA: Memory-efficient Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models Fine-tuning
hf_peft_config: peft.optimizers.create_lorafa_optimizer(model, r, lora_alpha, lr) on a LoraConfig model
formula_latex: W=W_0+s\,BA_0,\ \ s=\tfrac{\alpha}{r},\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random and frozen},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained with}\ \ \tilde g_B=\tfrac{1}{s^{2}}\,\nabla_B\mathcal L\,(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}\ \Rightarrow\ s\,\tilde g_BA_0=G\,A_0^{\top}(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}A_0=\arg\min_{\hat g\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}A_0}\lVert\hat g-G\rVert_F,\ \ G=\nabla_W\mathcal L
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
locus: any linear layer targeted by LoRA
structure: \(\Delta W=sBA_0\) with \(A_0\) a frozen random row space: the update lives in the fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace \(\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}(A_0)\); the corrected \(B\)-gradient is the orthogonal projection of the full gradient onto that subspace
mergeable_reason: \(sBA_0\) is an ordinary rank-\(r\) matrix that folds into \(W_0\) exactly, as in LoRA.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) with \(A_0\) random (Gaussian or uniform; the paper ablates the choice), so the initial model equals the pretrained one.
key_idea: Freezing \(A\) has two effects. Memory: LoRA no longer stores the full \(d_{in}\)-dimensional input activation, only the \(r\)-dimensional \(A_0x\). Optimization: with SGD, \(\Delta W=-\eta s^{2}GA_0^{\top}A_0\) is a fixed random projection of the gradient, and the \((A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}\) correction turns it into the exact least-squares projection of the full gradient.
results_note: Matches existing PEFT methods and full fine-tuning on GLUE (RoBERTa), GSM8K, MT-Bench and HumanEval (Llama-2/3 and MoE models) while substantially reducing activation memory and compute.
categorical_reading: LoRA-FA is the sub-object \(\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LoRA}_{(0,A_0)}\) obtained by freezing \(A\) (A2): a linear method with the same first-order image as zero-init LoRA. Its corrected gradient gives the frame-only cometric \(K(G)=\eta\,GP_V\), which depends only on \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\) under SGD, but on \(A_0\) modulo \(B_r\) under the published AdamW.

name: Riemannian LoRA
paper_title: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
formula_latex: A\leftarrow A-\eta\,(B^\top B+\delta I_r)^{-1}\nabla_A\mathcal{L},\ \ B\leftarrow B-\eta\,\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(AA^\top+\delta I_r)^{-1}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: LoRA layers (optimizer-level)
structure: \(r\times r\) preconditioners turning Euclidean gradients into scaled (Riemannian) gradients on the manifold of rank-\(r\) matrices
mergeable_reason: The trained adapter is a standard LoRA.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) as in LoRA (\(\delta\) regularizes the singular preconditioner).
key_idea: LoRA's factorization is ill-conditioned; precondition each factor by the Gram matrix of the other to follow the geometry of the low-rank manifold.
results_note: Paper reports faster convergence and more robustness to learning rate with SGD and AdamW on GPT-2, Mistral-7B and diffusion models, with negligible overhead.
categorical_reading: Riemannian preconditioning keeps LoRA's object and chooses a cometric that is a function of \(W\) on the full-rank locus, i.e. a metric descended to the quotient \(\mathcal M_r=Q^{\rm full}/GL_r\). The damping and the Adam wrapper used in practice shrink the respected gauge from \(GL_r\) to \(O(r)\) and then to \(B_r\).

name: QLoRA
paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(target_modules='all-linear', ...) on a model loaded with BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16), after peft.prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model)
formula_latex: h=\mathrm{doubleDequant}\big(c_1^{\mathrm{FP32}},c_2^{\mathrm{FP8}},W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}\big)\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\quad W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}=q_{\mathrm{NF4}}(W_0)\ \text{frozen (blockwise, constants double-quantized)},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained in BF16 (paged optimizer)}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: every linear layer of the transformer (attention and MLP); base weights stored as 4-bit NormalFloat
structure: rank-\(r\) additive update \(BA\) on top of a frozen 4-bit NF4 (quantile-quantized, blockwise, double-quantized constants) base weight; storage dtype NF4, compute dtype BF16, so \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space while \(W_0\) lives on a 16-level grid
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) merges exactly only into a dequantized 16-bit copy of \(W_0\); merging and re-quantizing to NF4 adds fresh rounding error, so exact inference at the original 4-bit cost is not preserved.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) (LoRA default, \(A\) random), so the initial function is the quantized model \(\mathrm{dequant}(q_{NF4}(W_0))\), not \(W_0\): the quantization gap is left uncompensated at init (the gap LoftQ / LQ-LoRA / ApiQ are built to shrink).
key_idea: Backpropagate through a frozen 4-bit base model into LoRA adapters. Three memory tricks make this work: NF4 (a quantile data type that is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights), double quantization of the scale constants, and paged optimizers. Together they let a 65B model be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU.
results_note: Fine-tunes a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU while matching 16-bit fine-tuning; Guanaco-65B reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's score on the Vicuna benchmark after 24 hours on one GPU.
categorical_reading: QLoRA needs no new structure: it is the LoRA cone translated to the quantised base \(\kappa\theta_0\), an object with pointing defect \(e\). Since \(-e\) is generically full rank, \(\theta_0\notin\mathrm{Im}\,\)QLoRA, and its exact merge leaves the NF4 grid (Mq).

name: LoRA layer replication (DUS)
full_name: Memory-efficient depth up-scaling with per-replica LoRA
paper_title: SOLAR 10.7B: Scaling Large Language Models with Simple yet Effective Depth Up-Scaling
formula_latex: f=\ell_{\pi(L')}\circ\cdots\circ\ell_{\pi(1)},\ \ \pi:[L']\to[L] \text{ (stacked layer ranges, base weights shared)};\ W^{(j)}=W_{0,\pi(j)}+B^{(j)}A^{(j)} \text{ (distinct LoRA per replica)}
trainable_params: \sum_{j=1}^{L'} r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted module type}
locus: whole transformer stack (layer duplication) plus LoRA on every replica
structure: depth up-scaling by repeating layer ranges (mergekit passthrough convention) with weight sharing, differentiated by per-replica low-rank updates
mergeable_reason: Merging requires materializing separate weights for each replica, yielding a larger (deeper) model rather than the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Not an identity of the original model: replication changes depth; each replica's LoRA starts at \(B = 0\).
key_idea: Grow a model's depth by reusing its own layers, then specialize the copies cheaply with LoRA instead of storing duplicated weights.
categorical_reading: Layer replication is an unpointed extension: the depth-upscaled network lives over a larger \(\Theta\times\Theta'\) with tied weights, and no parameter value recovers \(f(\theta_0,-)\), so it is not an object of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\). The per-replica LoRAs are ordinary pointed objects over the replicated base point.

name: KappaTune
paper_title: The Condition Number as a Scale-Invariant Proxy for Information Encoding in Neural Units
formula_latex: \kappa(W)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(W)}{\sigma_{\min}(W)};\ \ \mathcal{S}=\text{lowest-}\kappa \text{ top-}p \text{ fraction of tensors};\ \text{train (or attach LoRA to) } W\in\mathcal{S},\ \text{freeze the rest}
trainable_params: \sum_{W\in\mathcal{S}}|W| \ (\text{KappaTune}) \text{ or } \sum_{W\in\mathcal{S}}r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \ (\text{KappaTune-LoRA})
locus: module selection over all linear layers and fused MoE expert parameters
structure: data-free target selection by spectral condition number (most isotropic tensors are adapted)
mergeable_reason: Selected parameters or LoRAs are ordinary weight changes.
identity_at_init: Inherits from the chosen tuner (LoRA: \(B = 0\)).
key_idea: Well-conditioned (low-\(\kappa\), high-entropy) tensors encode less specialized information and can absorb new tasks with less forgetting.
results_note: Paper reports about 6x lower forgetting than LoRA on OLMoE and 2.8x lower with KappaTune-LoRA on DeepSeek-V2-Lite.
categorical_reading: KappaTune is the coordinate sub-object of full fine-tuning spanned by a spectrally chosen block of tensors, i.e. full FT with the complement frozen. Its only dependence on \(\theta_0\) is through the \(CO\times CO\)-invariant \(\kappa\): a spectral selection at the granularity of whole tensors.

name: MiLoRA
paper_title: MiLoRA: Harnessing Minor Singular Components for Parameter-Efficient LLM Finetuning
formula_latex: W_0=\sum_{i}\sigma_i u_i v_i^\top=W_p+W_m,\quad W_m=\sum_{i>k-r}\sigma_i u_i v_i^\top=\underbrace{U_m\Sigma_m^{1/2}}_{B}\,\underbrace{\Sigma_m^{1/2}V_m^\top}_{A},\qquad h=(W_p+BA)\,x;\ W_p\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections)
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space; base point \(W_p\) is the rank-\((k-r)\) principal truncation of \(W_0\) (\(k=\min(d_{in},d_{out})\)) and the adapter is initialized on the \(r\) smallest singular triplets
mergeable_reason: \(W_p+BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(W_p+B_0A_0=W_0\) by construction (data-free SVD of \(W_0\)); no extra scaling hyperparameter is needed.
key_idea: Keep the principal subspace (assumed to store pretrained knowledge) frozen and adapt only within the minor singular subspace, which is less likely to interfere with pretrained abilities.
results_note: Reported gains over LoRA on LLaMA-2-7B / LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning (+1.6 / +1.1), math reasoning (+2.0), instruction following and LLaVA-1.5 visual instruction tuning.
categorical_reading: MiLoRA is the Type II pointing with \(P=\) bottom-\(r\) SVD part of \(W_0\): image \((W_0-P)+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), \(\theta_0\) smooth, \(S_1=T_P\mathcal M_r\). It is the \(C=I\) member of CorDA-KPM, but for \(C\not\propto I\) the vertices differ and no arrow connects the two.

name: LoRA-One
paper_title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space and is initialized to the (normalized, scaled) best rank-\(r\) approximation of one full-batch negative gradient, i.e. a truncated gradient step; the LoRA-One-P variant adds \((B^\top B+\lambda I)^{-1},(AA^\top+\lambda I)^{-1}\) preconditioners
mergeable_reason: Plain additive low-rank update on \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No: \(W_0\) is not offset, so the initial model equals one best rank-\(r\) full-batch gradient-descent step from \(W_0\) (gradient-driven spectral initialization from a large sampled batch).
key_idea: Theory shows LoRA iterates align with the top singular subspace of the one-step full fine-tuning gradient, so initializing there (and preconditioning against ill-conditioning) achieves the alignment immediately; it also corrects LoRA-GA's choice of singular vectors.
results_note: Reported 88.73 vs 82.72 GLUE average over LoRA (T5-base) and 28.66 vs 25.85 HumanEval, with negligible time/memory overhead.
categorical_reading: LoRA-One enters LoRA's own cone at a smooth point instead of the apex: a base change \(\theta_0\mapsto\theta_0+[-\eta G]_r\) (one truncated full-FT step), followed by a split pointing whose residual is the original \(\theta_0\). In \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\) it is only an unpointed object, related to LoRA by \(h=\mathrm{id}\) without preservation of base points.

name: GoRA
paper_title: GoRA: Gradient-driven Adaptive Low Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: \bar G=\tfrac1N\textstyle\sum_i\partial\mathcal{L}_i/\partial W_0,\quad I(W)=\mathrm{avg}(|W_0\odot\bar G|),\quad a_\ell=\tfrac{I(W_\ell)}{\sum_j I(W_j)},\quad r_\ell=\mathrm{clip}\big(\mathrm{round}(b\,a_\ell/\sqrt{d_{in}+d_{out}}),\,r_{min},\,r_{max}\big);\quad A_0\sim\mathcal{U}_{\text{Kaiming}},\ B_0=-\xi\,\bar G A_0^\top(A_0A_0^\top)^{-1},\ \xi=\gamma\sqrt{d_{in}}/\alpha,\qquad W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_\ell}}BA
trainable_params: r_\ell(d_{in}+d_{out}),\ \ \text{budget }b=\textstyle\sum_\ell\sqrt{d_{in}+d_{out}}\;r_{ref}
locus: any linear layer; ranks allocated across all adapted layers
structure: \(\Delta W=BA\) with per-layer rank \(r_\ell\) set by gradient sensitivity; \(B_0\) is the least-squares solution making \(B_0A_0\) the best approximation of \(-\bar G\) in the row space of the random \(A_0\)
mergeable_reason: Plain additive low-rank update on \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No: \(W_0\) is not offset; the initial adapter \(\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}B_0A_0\approx-\gamma\bar G\) restricted to the row space of the random \(A_0\), i.e. a compressed gradient-descent step with tunable step size \(\gamma\) (\(\xi=\gamma\sqrt{d_{in}}/\alpha\)), computed from gradients accumulated over \(N\) mini-batches.
key_idea: A single accumulated-gradient pass before training is used twice: to allocate ranks across layers by gradient sensitivity and to initialize \(B\) so that the adapter starts as a compressed gradient step, without touching \(W_0\).
results_note: Reported Llama-3.1-8B-Base GSM8K 75.74 vs full fine-tuning 73.69 and HumanEval 52.03 vs 51.63 at reference rank 128.
categorical_reading: GoRA is LoRA with the frozen residual \(W_0\) untouched but started off the base point, at \(\theta_0+e\) with \(e\approx-\gamma\bar G P_{\mathrm{row}A_0}\) a compressed gradient step: an object of the unpointed slice with a designed defect, which over its own start is a Type II split with \(P=e\). Its rank allocation by \(|W_0\odot\bar G|\) is a coordinatewise statistic.

name: LoRA-SB
paper_title: Initialization using Update Approximation is a Silver Bullet for Extremely Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: \Delta W_{avg}=-\eta\,\mathrm{sign}\Big(\textstyle\sum_i\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0,x_i)\Big)=USV^\top,\quad B=U_{[:,1:r]},\ A=V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\ R_0=\tfrac1s S_{[1:r,1:r]},\qquad W=W_0+s\,BRA;\ B,A\text{ frozen},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\text{ trained}
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W=BRA\) with frozen orthonormal outer factors \(B,A\) (from the SVD of an approximate first full-FT update) and a trainable \(r\times r\) core \(R\)
mergeable_reason: \(BRA\) is a dense matrix of the original shape and folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No: \(W_0\) is not offset, so the model starts at \(W_0\) plus the optimal rank-\(r\) approximation of the simulated first AdamW step (sign of summed gradients over ~0.1% of the training data).
key_idea: With the LoRA-XS architecture (frozen \(B,A\), trainable \(r\times r\) \(R\)), initializing \(B,A\) from the SVD of an approximate full-FT update makes the learning dynamics hyperparameter-free in the scale \(s\) and gives the optimal low-rank approximation of full-FT gradients.
results_note: Reported beating LoRA with 27-90x fewer trainable parameters and comprehensively outperforming LoRA-XS on GSM8K/MATH, commonsense reasoning and GLUE with RoBERTa-large, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B.
categorical_reading: LoRA-SB is the categorical product \(\mathrm{FA}(V_r^\top)\times\mathrm{FB}(U_r)\) of Prop I.8(a) taken in the frame of the simulated first Adam update rather than of \(W_0\), re-pointed at \(R_0=S_r/s\): a linear \(r^2\)-dimensional image with a designed defect. Because that frame is the SVD of \(\mathrm{sign}(\sum\nabla)\), its covariance is only signed permutations and homotheties on each side, not \(CO\times CO\).

name: LoRA-Null
full_name: LoRA initialized in the Null space of activations
paper_title: Put the Space of LoRA Initialization to the Extreme to Preserve Pre-trained Knowledge
formula_latex: X_{pre}=U\Sigma V^\top,\ U_{null}=U_{[:,-r:]}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\quad W_0U_{null}U_{null}^\top=U'\Sigma'V'^\top,\quad B=U'_{[:,:r]}\Sigma'^{1/2}_{[:r]},\ A=\Sigma'^{1/2}_{[:r]}V'^\top_{[:r,:]},\quad W_0'=W_0-BA,\qquad h=(W_0'+BA)x
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W\) factors through an \(r\)-dimensional space initialized as the projection of \(W_0\) onto the (approximate) null space of pre-training-knowledge input activations
mergeable_reason: \(W_0'+BA\) is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
identity_at_init: Exact: \(W_0'+B_0A_0=W_0\); data-driven from activations of knowledge-probing (pre-training-like) data.
key_idea: Argues that the space in which LoRA is initialized, not the residual weight, governs forgetting, and initializes the adapter in the null space of pre-trained-knowledge activations so that updates minimally disturb what the model already knows.
results_note: Reported better knowledge preservation than CorDA (e.g. 93.18% vs 89.00% on LLaMA-3.2-3B math setting) with competitive downstream accuracy.
categorical_reading: LoRA-Null is a Type II split with \(P=W_0P_{\rm null}\), the projection of \(W_0\) onto the minor input-activation directions of pretraining data; \(\theta_0\) is a smooth point of \((W_0-P)+\mathcal M_{\le r}\). Since \(P\) depends on the output side only through \(W_0\), the split is \(GL(m)\times CO(n)\)-covariant.

name: DyLoRA
paper_title: DyLoRA: Parameter Efficient Tuning of Pre-trained Models using Dynamic Search-Free Low-Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: b\sim p_B\ \text{on}\ \{r_{min},\dots,r_{max}\},\quad h=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{b}\,B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]}\,x,\quad \mathcal{L}^{DY}_{\downarrow b}=\textstyle\sum_i\ell\big(f(x_i;A_{[1:b,:]},B_{[:,1:b]}),y_i\big)
trainable_params: r_{max}(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (typically \(W_q\), \(W_v\))
structure: nested family of truncations \(\Delta W_{\downarrow b}=B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]}\) trained jointly (nested-dropout-like ordering of rank-1 components), so every prefix rank is a usable adapter
mergeable_reason: After choosing any rank \(b\) at deployment, \(B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]}\) folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (up-projection \(B=0\)).
key_idea: Train a single adapter for a whole range of ranks by sampling a truncation rank at every step, so the rank can be chosen after training without a search.
results_note: Reported training 4-7x faster than searching LoRA ranks, with GLUE average 86.66 vs 86.49 for LoRA on RoBERTa-base.
categorical_reading: DyLoRA's object at full rank is LoRA\(_{r_{\max}}\), but its nested-dropout loss is a sum over the filtration \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le b}\), and only the torus \(T_r\) preserves every truncation, so the training gauge is \(T_r\) rather than \(GL_r\). The truncations are A2 sub-objects DyLoRA\(_b\hookrightarrow\)DyLoRA\(_{r_{\max}}\).

name: SoRA
paper_title: Sparse Low-rank Adaptation of Pre-trained Language Models
formula_latex: h=W_0x+B\big(g\odot(Ax)\big),\ g\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{max}};\quad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_0+\lambda\textstyle\sum_k\lVert g^{(k)}\rVert_1;\quad g_{t+1}=\mathcal{T}_{\eta_t\lambda}\big(g_t-\eta_t\nabla_g\mathcal{L}_0\big),\ \mathcal{T}_\xi(x)=\mathrm{sign}(x)\max(|x|-\xi,0)
trainable_params: r_{max}(d_{in}+d_{out}+1)\ \text{during training};\ r'(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{after pruning zero gates}
locus: any linear layer
structure: \(\Delta W=B\,\mathrm{diag}(g)\,A\) with a sparse gate vector driven to exact zeros by proximal (soft-thresholding) updates; zeroed rank-1 components are removed
mergeable_reason: After pruning, \(B\,\mathrm{diag}(g)\,A\) is a plain low-rank matrix that folds into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B=0\) as in LoRA (\(A\) Kaiming-uniform, gate \(g \sim N(0,1)\) in the official code).
key_idea: Start with a generous rank and let an L1-regularized gate, optimized by proximal gradient, decide how many rank-1 components each matrix keeps.

Its test-time ensemble is a family over mask space realised at function level, hence not mergeable.

name: AsyLoRA
full_name: Asymmetric LoRA (random frozen A, train only B)
paper_title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,B\,Q,\quad Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random with orthonormal rows (Haar/Stiefel), frozen};\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained from } B=0
trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
locus: same as LoRA (RoBERTa, BART, LLaMA-2, ViT experiments)
structure: Linear (not bilinear) parametrization: \(\Delta W\) ranges over \(\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}(Q)\) for a fixed random \(r\)-dim input subspace; freezing \(A\) gives least-squares/logistic regression on randomly projected features \(Qx\), whereas freezing \(B\) only fits outputs projected onto a random subspace.
mergeable_reason: \(B Q\) is an ordinary additive low-rank update that merges into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) with \(Q\) random orthogonal and never updated.
key_idea: \(A\) and \(B\) play asymmetric roles: \(A\) extracts input features (and a random \(A\) works about as well as a learned one) while \(B\) maps them to the task; training only \(B\) halves parameters, tightens information-theoretic generalization bounds, and lets one double \(r\) at fixed budget.
results_note: Across RoBERTa, BART-Large, LLaMA-2 and ViT, \(B\)-only tuning with a random orthogonal \(A\) matches or beats standard LoRA at matched parameter count and improves out-of-domain accuracy on DomainBed.
categorical_reading: AsyLoRA is the one-sided object \(\mathrm{FA}(Q)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LoRA}_{(0,Q)}\) with a Haar-random orthonormal frame: the same object as LoRA-FA up to the law of \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\). Orthonormality makes its plain-SGD cometric \(s^2\eta\,GQ^\top Q=s^2\eta\,GP_V\), which is already LoRA-FA's corrected (least-squares) cometric.

name: LoRA Without Regret
full_name: LoRA Without Regret (Thinking Machines Lab recipe and analysis)
paper_title: LoRA Without Regret
hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(lora_alpha=32, target_modules='all-linear')  # same-LR AdamW, LR ~10x the FullFT LR
formula_latex: W = W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\ \ \alpha=32,\ \ A_{ij}\sim\mathcal{U}\big(\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{d_{in}}}\big),\ B=0,\ \ \eta_A=\eta_B=\eta_{\text{LoRA}}\approx 10\,\eta_{\text{FullFT}};\ \ \text{apply to all linear layers incl. MLP/MoE}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: all weight matrices, especially MLP and MoE layers (attention-only LoRA underperforms MLP-only LoRA)
structure: Standard LoRA parametrization; of the four hyperparameters (\(\alpha\), \(\eta_A\), \(\eta_B\), init scale of \(A\)) only two affect the dynamics, and with the \(1/r\) multiplier and \(B=0\) the expected first update \(\tfrac{1}{r}\sum_i b_ia_i^{\top}\) is rank-independent, making the optimal LR approximately independent of \(r\).
mergeable_reason: It is plain LoRA, so the adapter merges into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\) with \(A\) uniform of scale \(1/\sqrt{d_{in}}\) (the PEFT default parametrization).
key_idea: LoRA matches full fine-tuning in the regime that matters for post-training when applied to all layers (especially MLPs) with ~10x the FullFT learning rate and when the dataset does not exceed adapter capacity; RL needs very little capacity, so even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT for policy-gradient training.
results_note: On Llama 3 / Qwen3 models with Tulu3 and OpenThoughts3 SFT, LoRA matches FullFT until capacity is exceeded; on MATH/GSM8K/DeepMath RL even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT; LoRA is less tolerant of large batch sizes; LoRA costs slightly more than 2/3 of FullFT FLOPs per pass.
categorical_reading: LoRA Without Regret studies LoRA's trained-method data rather than a new object: its hyperparameter redundancy is the 2-torus action of Thm III.10, and its capacity claims are statements about when the cone \(\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) contains the needed update.

name: Flat-LoRA
full_name: Flat-LoRA (low-rank adaptation over a flat full-space loss landscape)
paper_title: Flat-LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation over a Flat Loss Landscape
formula_latex: \min_{A,B}\ \mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon_W}\,\mathcal{L}\big(W'+\varepsilon_W\big),\quad W'=W_0+sBA,\quad (\varepsilon_W)_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\tfrac{\sigma^2}{d_{in}}\|W'_{i,:}\|_2^2\big)\ \ (\text{fresh noise each step, regenerated from a seed})
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: same as LoRA (LLMs and text-to-image diffusion models)
structure: Random-weight-perturbation (Bayesian expected loss) regularizer applied in the full \(d_{out}\times d_{in}\) weight space rather than in the \((A,B)\) space, with filter(row)-norm-scaled Gaussian noise; a cheap relaxation of SAM's min-max over full-space perturbations.
mergeable_reason: Noise is used only during training; the learned \(BA\) merges like LoRA.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (\(B = 0\)); the perturbation is zero-mean training noise only.
key_idea: A minimum that is flat in LoRA's \((A,B)\) coordinates can still be sharp in the full weight space; averaging the loss over full-space random weight perturbations steers LoRA toward full-space flat minima without SAM's extra gradient step or weight copy.
results_note: Improves in-domain and out-of-domain generalization over LoRA on mathematical reasoning, coding, dialogue, instruction following and text-to-image generation in the paper's experiments.
categorical_reading: Flat-LoRA moves the sharpness regulariser from the chart \(Q\) to weight space. A loss that factors through \(\rho\) is constant on gauge fibres, so its flatness is a property of the point of \(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}\), not of the representative \((B,A)\). The object stays LoRA.

name: AltLoRA
paper_title: AltLoRA: Towards Better Gradient Approximation in Low-Rank Adaptation with Alternating Projections
formula_latex: \text{even } t:\ A\leftarrow A-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}(B^{\top}B)^{-1}\nabla_A\mathcal{L}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta P_BG);\qquad \text{odd } t:\ B\leftarrow B-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(AA^{\top})^{-1}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta\, G P_A);\quad \tilde M^B = M^BA_tA_{t+1}^{\top}(A_{t+1}A_{t+1}^{\top})^{-1}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: same as LoRA
structure: Alternating one-sided projections of the full gradient onto \(\mathrm{col}(B)\) and \(\mathrm{row}(A)\) (each the exact least-squares solution for the factor being updated), with momentum transported into the new low-rank subspace by an \(r\times r\) change-of-basis; avoids LoRA-Pro's non-unique \(X\) and full-size optimizer state.
mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the result is a standard LoRA adapter.
identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization; Gram inverses are damped as \((B^T B + \lambda I)^{-1}\) to stay invertible when a factor is rank-deficient.
key_idea: Instead of jointly matching the full gradient (LoRA-Pro), alternately update \(A\) and \(B\) so each step is an exact projection of the full gradient, and keep momentum aligned with the changing subspace without extra memory; this gives stable feature learning and transformation invariance.
results_note: Outperforms LoRA and its variants (including LoRA-Pro) across SFT and NLU tasks while keeping LoRA-level memory, narrowing the gap to full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: AltLoRA alternates between the linear sub-objects \(\mathrm{FB}(B_t)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LoRA}\) and \(\mathrm{FA}(A_t)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LoRA}\), taking an exact least-squares step in each. By the degree-one collapse each half-step is a backward lens with anchor \(P_B\) or \(P_A\), so AltLoRA is a period-1 rebasing schedule of one-sided linear methods, with momentum transported between frames.

name: LoFT
full_name: Low-rank adaptation that mimics Full fine-Tuning
paper_title: LoFT: Low-Rank Adaptation That Behaves Like Full Fine-Tuning
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: same as LoRA
structure: Six building blocks (alternating updates, scaled gradients, momentum recalibration across changing subspaces via \(C_k=(A_{k-1}A_k^{\top})(A_kA_k^{\top})^{-1}\) [the paper's \((V_{k-1}^{\top}V_k)(V_k^{\top}V_k)^{-1}\) with \(V=A^{\top}\)], second-moment alignment with cross terms, reconstruction of the full AdamW update followed by projection, gradient clipping) that make the low-rank step the tightest approximation to the AdamW full-fine-tuning step; \(\alpha\) is fixed to 1, and LoFT reduces exactly to AdamW when \(r=\max(d_{in},d_{out})\) with full-rank factors.
mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the adapter is a standard mergeable low-rank product.
identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA's zero-product initialization; Gram inverses fall back to pseudo-inverses when a factor is rank-deficient.
key_idea: Not only gradients but also Adam's first and second moments are misaligned between LoRA and full fine-tuning; projecting and recalibrating them in the evolving low-rank subspace makes LoRA behave like full fine-tuning and removes the need to tune \(\alpha\).
results_note: Substantially narrows the gap to full fine-tuning and consistently outperforms standard LoRA-style methods without increasing inference cost; memory overhead \(O((d_{in}+d_{out}) r^2)\) for second-moment calibration.
categorical_reading: LoFT keeps LoRA's object and lifts the full-space AdamW update into the moving tangent frames of the cone, transporting optimizer state along the gauge (unlike GaLore, which carries state over without transport). The cone is already \(\Theta\) at \(r=\min(m,n)\), but the update reduces exactly to AdamW on full FT (the terminal object) only at \(r=\max(m,n)\), where both projections \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) (with pseudo-inverses) are the identity.

name: PoLAR
paper_title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
formula_latex: W=W_0+X\,\Theta\,Y^{\top},\quad X\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r),\ Y\in\mathrm{St}(d_{in},r),\ \Theta\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r};\ \text{retraction-free landing field } \Gamma(X)=\psi(X)X+\lambda\nabla\mathcal{N}(X);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+r^2
locus: any linear layer
structure: rank-\(r\) additive update in polar form: two direction factors on Stiefel manifolds (orthonormal \(r\)-frames, i.e. points of \(O(d)/O(d-r)\)) and an unconstrained \(r\times r\) scale/core matrix, optimized by Riemannian 'landing' without retractions
mergeable_reason: \(X \Theta Y^\top\) is a fixed rank-\(r\) matrix that can be added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \(\Theta_0 = 0\), with \(X_0\) and \(Y_0\) drawn uniformly at random from the Stiefel manifolds.
key_idea: LoRA updates collapse to a very low stable rank. Writing the update as two orthonormal direction frames times a free core, and training with GPU-friendly Riemannian landing, keeps the directions diverse and provably speeds up convergence on a canonical low-rank problem.
results_note: Reports gains over LoRA on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3-base 88.94 vs 88.18), commonsense reasoning (Llama-2-7B, 73.71 vs 72.18) and math (Gemma-3-27B) across models from 350M to 27B parameters.
categorical_reading: PoLAR reparametrises LoRA's cone through \(\mathrm{St}(m,r)\times\mathbb R^{r\times r}\times\mathrm{St}(n,r)\), a partial gauge fixing that cuts \(GL_r\) down to \(O(r)\times O(r)\) and so removes the non-compact directions that carry the charges \(\Phi\). It factors through LoRA by \(h=(X\Theta,Y^\top)\), but starts at a deeper apex whose first-order image is the LoRA-XS-type tangent \(\{X_0RY_0^\top\}\).

name: GOFT
paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
formula_latex: W = W_0 R^{\top},\quad R=\prod_{\ell=1}^{\log_2 d_{in}}P_\ell,\ P_\ell=\prod_{k=0}^{d_{in}/2^{\ell}-1}G\big(2^{\ell}k,\ 2^{\ell-1}(2k+1);\ \theta_k^{\ell}\big),\ G(i,j;\theta) \text{ a Givens rotation in the } (i,j) \text{ plane};\ W_0 \text{ frozen, angles } \theta \text{ trained}
locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of \(W_0\)
structure: right action of \(SO(d_{in})\), with the group element written as a product of \(d-1\) Givens rotations (one-parameter subgroups \(SO(2)\) embedded in coordinate planes) arranged in \(\log_2(d)\) parallel layers of non-overlapping rotations, a butterfly-like layout
mergeable_reason: The product of Givens rotations is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: All angles start at 0 (each rotation initialized to the identity).
key_idea: \(d-1\) Givens rotations can map any vector to any other vector on the same sphere, so OFT-level expressiveness only needs \(O(d)\) angles instead of \(O(d^2)\) parameters. A parallel arrangement keeps the depth at \(O(\log d)\) sequential layers.
results_note: On GLUE with DeBERTaV3-base, GOFT with 0.08M parameters matches OFT (\(b=8\), 0.66M parameters) at an 88.78 average; also evaluated on LLaMA-2-7B instruction tuning and VTAB-1K.
categorical_reading: GOFT writes an element of \(SO(d)\) as a log-depth circuit of \(d-1\) Givens rotations: an action-type object, regular at \(\theta_0\), whose image is a thin \((d-1)\)-dimensional slice of the orbit \(W_0\cdot SO(d)\). A single run stays far from the orbit; rebasing walks all of it because the plane graph is connected.

name: qGOFT
paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
formula_latex: W = W_0\tilde{R}^{\top},\quad \tilde{R}=\prod_{\ell}\tilde{P}_\ell,\ \text{each Givens block replaced by a free } \tilde{G}_i=[\alpha_i\ \beta_i]\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2};\ \min\ \mathcal{L}+\lambda\sum_i\langle\alpha_i,\beta_i\rangle^2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of \(W_0\)
structure: right action of a product of embedded free \(2\times2\) blocks (singular ones included) laid out like GOFT. Leaving \(SO(d)\) lets the update change neuron norms and angles, and a soft column-orthogonality penalty keeps it near the orthogonal group.
mergeable_reason: The product of \(2\times2\) blocks is a fixed matrix that can be multiplied into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Every quasi-Givens block is initialized to the \(2\times2\) identity.
key_idea: Relax each Givens rotation to an arbitrary \(2\times2\) linear map, so fine-tuning can also rescale neurons and shift their angles. A soft regularizer keeps the map close to orthogonal.
results_note: Reports an 89.35 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base with 0.33M parameters (above OFT \(b=8\) with 0.66M) and a 79.4% VTAB-1K average.
categorical_reading: qGOFT relaxes each Givens rotation to an arbitrary \(2\times2\) block, so it is the action of a monoid circuit rather than a group. It leaves the \(K_{\rm out}\) level set at first order, carries a torus gauge on internal index wires, and rebasing walks \(W_0\,\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), the closure of \(W_0\cdot GL(n)\), instead of \(W_0\cdot SO(n)\).

name: ETHER
paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
formula_latex: W = W_0 H^{B},\quad H^{B}=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\dots,H_n),\quad H_j=I-2u_ju_j^{\top},\ \|u_j\|=1,\ u_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}/n};\quad \|H_j-I\|_F=2;\quad W_0 \text{ frozen, } u_j \text{ trained}
trainable_params: d_{in}
locus: any linear layer (diffusion attention, LLM projections); acts on the input side of \(W_0\)
structure: right action of a block-diagonal product of \(n\) hyperplane reflections, an element of \(O(d_{in})\) that lies at fixed distance \(\|H_j - I\|_F = 2\) from the identity in every block
mergeable_reason: \(H^B\) is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No. A Householder reflection is never the identity (\(\|H - I\|_F = 2\) per block), and the official code initializes \(u\) with Kaiming-uniform random values, so the model is moved by a bounded reflection at step 0. Training only re-orients the reflection hyperplanes.
key_idea: Restricting the multiplicative update to hyperplane reflections bounds how far the fine-tuned weights can move from the pretrained ones, whatever the learning rate. The result needs very few parameters and is robust to hyperparameters.
results_note: Reports performance matching or beating LoRA and OFT with about 10-100x fewer parameters on subject-driven and controllable Stable Diffusion generation, GLUE and LLaMA instruction tuning.
categorical_reading: ETHER is an unpointed action-type object: its image is a compact set of block reflections \(W_0H^B\subset W_0\cdot O(n)\) at fixed distance from \(\theta_0\). It preserves \(K_{\rm out}\) and the spectrum (Cor II.6) but has no base point over \(\theta_0\); its 'bounded deviation' is literally \(\|H_j-I\|_F=2\).

name: ETHER+
full_name: ETHER+ (relaxed two-hyperplane transformation applied on both sides)
paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
formula_latex: W=\tilde{H}^{+}\,W_0\,H^{+},\quad H^{+}=I-uu^{\top}+vv^{\top}\ (u,v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}\ \text{unit, block-diagonal}),\ \tilde{H}^{+}=I-\tilde u\tilde u^{\top}+\tilde v\tilde v^{\top}\ (\tilde u,\tilde v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}});\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: 2(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer; acts on both the input and the output side of \(W_0\)
structure: two-sided action (left on \(\mathbb R^{d_{out}}\), right on \(\mathbb R^{d_{in}}\)) by rank\(\le 2\) perturbations of the identity. These are not orthogonal in general, so they leave the group \(O(d)\), but their distance to \(I\) is bounded by ETHER's.
mergeable_reason: Both transforms are fixed matrices after training, so \(\tilde H^+ W_0 H^+\) can be precomputed.
identity_at_init: Yes. The official code initializes the second vector as the negative copy of the first (\(v = -u\)), so \(vv^\top = uu^\top\) and \(H^+ = I\) on both sides; the paper notes that \(H^+\) returns the identity when the two hyperplanes coincide.
key_idea: Relax the Householder reflection to \(I - uu^\top + vv^\top\) so that two hyperplanes can interact or cancel. Applied on both sides of \(W_0\), this gives finer, still norm-bounded updates.
results_note: Reports e.g. 0.666 DINO for subject-driven generation with 0.4M parameters vs OFT's 0.652 with 11.6M, and 27.3 mIoU vs 24.5 for controllable generation.
categorical_reading: ETHER+ is a two-sided action by rank-2 symmetric perturbations of the identity. Its default pointing (\(v=-u\)) is the vertex of the cone of such perturbations, so unlike ETHER it is pointed, but it sits at an apex, like zero-init LoRA. Its update has rank \(\le2\) per block and side, so LoRA of that rank simulates it.

name: Spectral Adapter^R
paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
formula_latex: W=[U_1R_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1R_V,\ V_2]^{\top}=\tilde{U}\,W_0\,\tilde{V}^{\top},\quad \tilde{U}=I+U_1(R_U-I)U_1^{\top},\ \tilde{V}=I+V_1(R_V-I)V_1^{\top};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ R_U,R_V\in O(r)\ \text{(Cayley) trained}
trainable_params: 2r^2\ \ (r(r-1)\ \text{with skew-symmetric Cayley generators})
locus: any linear layer (top-\(r\) spectral space of each pretrained weight)
structure: two-sided orthogonal action of \(O(r)\times O(r)\), embedded in \(O(d_{out})\times O(d_{in})\) as rotations of the top-\(r\) left and right singular subspaces of \(W_0\) (identity on their complements). Singular values are unchanged and only the principal singular frames are rotated.
mergeable_reason: The rotated singular factors recombine into one dense matrix of the original shape.
key_idea: Run the SVD of each pretrained weight and fine-tune only by rotating its top singular vectors. The adapter is very compact, and keeping the adapted subspaces orthogonal helps when several adapters are fused.
categorical_reading: Spectral Adapter\(^R\) is a two-sided orthogonal orbit confined to the principal singular block: it rotates the top singular frames and keeps every singular value, so the spectrum and the principal subspaces are absolute invariants. Through the SVD frame it factors through LoRA-XS's linear core.

name: Spectral Adapter^A
paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
formula_latex: W=[U_1+A_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1+A_V,\ V_2]^{\top},\quad A_U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{trained};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: any linear layer (top-\(r\) singular vectors)
structure: additive perturbation of the top-\(r\) singular-vector factors: \(\Delta W = A_U S_1 V_1^T + U_1 S_1 A_V^T + A_U S_1 A_V^T\). This has rank \(\le 2r\) for LoRA's parameter budget (the paper's 'twice the rank capacity' lemma).
mergeable_reason: The perturbed factors recombine into a single dense matrix.
key_idea: Fine-tune the top singular vectors of the pretrained weight additively. For the same number of trainable parameters this doubles LoRA's rank capacity and uses the pretrained spectrum.
results_note: Reports 49.73 on GSM8K with Mistral-7B vs 44.81 for LoRA and 43.82 for DoRA (\(r=8\)), and an 88.03 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base, above LoRA, DoRA, OFT and AdaLoRA.
categorical_reading: Spectral Adapter\(^A\) is PiSSA in affine coordinates: \((A_U,A_V)\mapsto((U_1+A_U)S_1^{1/2},S_1^{1/2}(V_1+A_V)^\top)\) is a pointed isomorphism, so its 'twice the rank capacity' is Thm II.1(c) for split pointings. The coordinate change alters only the induced cometric (rates weighted by \(S_1\)), not the object.

name: SVDiff
paper_title: SVDiff: Compact Parameter Space for Diffusion Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: W=U\,\operatorname{diag}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(\sigma+\delta)\big)\,V^{\top},\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{(SVD, frozen)},\ \delta\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: \min(d_{in},d_{out})
locus: 2-D linear weights and reshaped 4-D conv kernels of the diffusion UNet (1-D weights such as biases and norms are not decomposed and are tuned directly); optimizing the cross-attention layers gives the best subject preservation in the paper's layer ablation
structure: the singular values are adjusted by a diagonal (torus) map while the singular vectors stay fixed. For \(\sigma > 0\) this equals \(W = U\,\mathrm{diag}(s/\sigma)\,U^\top W_0\) with \(s = \mathrm{ReLU}(\sigma+\delta) \ge 0\), a positive-semidefinite rescaling that commutes with \(W_0 W_0^\top\).
mergeable_reason: \(U\,\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{ReLU}(\sigma+\delta))\,V^\top\) is a fixed dense matrix.
key_idea: Fine-tune only the singular values of every weight matrix (spectral shifts). The tiny parameter space resists overfitting in personalization and supports multi-subject training (Cut-Mix-Unmix) and single-image editing (CoSINE).
results_note: About 1.7MB of parameters for Stable Diffusion vs 3.66GB for full DreamBooth (roughly 2,200x smaller) and 1/2-1/3 of a LoRA checkpoint.
categorical_reading: SVDiff is the positive torus acting on the singular values of \(W_0\) in its frozen SVD frame; its image is the orbit closure \(\{U\mathrm{diag}(s)V^\top:s\ge0\}\), linear at \(\theta_0\). It is the spectral analogue of (IA)\(^3\): frames are absolute invariants, singular values move.

name: SVF (Transformer²)
paper_title: Transformer-Squared: Self-adaptive LLMs
formula_latex: W=U\big(\Sigma\otimes\operatorname{diag}(z)\big)V^{\top}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma\odot z)V^{\top}\ \Big(\times\tfrac{\sum_i\sigma_i}{\sum_i\sigma_iz_i}\ \text{in the official code}\Big),\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ z\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained (REINFORCE + KL)};\ \text{test time: } z'=\sum_k\alpha_kz_k
trainable_params: \min(d_{in},d_{out})
locus: weight matrices of the LLM (the official code adapts the MLP matrices)
structure: multiplicative diagonal (torus) action on the singular values with fixed singular vectors. Trained expert vectors \(z_k\) can be linearly mixed at inference.
mergeable_reason: Once \(z\) (or the mixture \(z'\)) is chosen, \(W\) is a fixed dense matrix; self-adaptation is a two-pass procedure that sets \(z\) before the second pass.
identity_at_init: \(z\) starts near a constant value (the paper's hyperparameter table lists an initial mean of 0.1). The official code passes \(z\) through a sigmoid and renormalizes by \(\mathrm{sum}(\sigma)/\mathrm{sum}(\sigma * z)\), so a uniform \(z\) leaves \(W_0\) unchanged up to this normalization (approximately the identity).
key_idea: Train one scaling vector over each weight's singular values with RL to get compact, composable 'expert' vectors. At test time a dispatcher identifies the task and mixes the experts, so the LLM adapts itself.
results_note: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, SVF beats LoRA on GSM8K (79.15 vs 77.18) and ARC-Easy while training less than 10% of LoRA's parameters.
categorical_reading: SVF trains a torus element acting on the spectrum of \(W_0\) in its frozen SVD frame; for \(\sigma>0\) it is isomorphic to diagonal SVFT and, near \(\theta_0\), to SVDiff. Transformer\(^2\)'s self-adaptation is a \(T\)-point of this linear method over the simplex of expert mixtures, where mixing parameters is legitimate because the map is of degree one.

name: SVFT
paper_title: SVFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Singular Vectors
formula_latex: W=U(\Sigma+M)V^{\top}=W_0+UMV^{\top},\quad U,\Sigma,V\ \text{from the SVD of frozen } W_0,\ M\ \text{sparse with fixed pattern } \Omega\ \text{(plain/diagonal, banded, random, top-}k\text{)};\ \text{only } M_{\Omega} \text{ trained}
trainable_params: |\Omega|\ (+1\ \text{gate scalar per layer in the official code});\ \ \min(d_{in},d_{out})\ \text{for SVFT}^{P}
locus: any linear layer
structure: sparse additive update in the singular-vector basis of \(W_0\): \(\Delta W = \sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega} m_{ij} u_i v_j^T\), a fixed dictionary that depends on the weight rather than a free low-rank factorization. A diagonal \(\Omega\) reduces it to a spectral shift.
mergeable_reason: \(U M V^T\) is a fixed dense matrix after training.
identity_at_init: Not exactly in the official code: the coefficients of \(M\) are Kaiming-normal initialized and multiplied by a learnable gate \(\mathrm{sigmoid}(g)\) with \(g = 0\), so \(\Delta W = U (0.5 M_{\mathrm{init}}) V^T\) is non-zero at step 0. The paper does not state an initialization.
key_idea: Use the outer products of \(W_0\)'s own singular vectors as a fixed dictionary and learn sparse coefficients for it, including off-diagonal ones. This trades parameters against expressivity smoothly.
results_note: Recovers up to 96% of full fine-tuning performance while training 0.006-0.25% of parameters (e.g. Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B on GSM8K/MATH); baselines reach at most 85% with 0.03-0.8%.

LoRA-XS is its dense top-left \(r\times r\) block, and the diagonal mask SVFT\(^P\) shifts the spectrum at full rank.

name: BiDoRA
paper_title: BiDoRA: Bi-level Optimization-Based Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
formula_latex: W=\operatorname{diag}(m)\,\frac{W_0+BA}{\|W_0+BA\|_{row}};\quad \min_{m}\ \mathcal{L}_{val}\big(\mathcal{V}^{*}(m),m\big)\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ \mathcal{V}^{*}(m)=\arg\min_{\mathcal{V}=\{B,A\}}\ \mathcal{L}_{tr}(\mathcal{V},m)+\gamma\sum_k\big\|(V_k+\Delta V_k)^{\top}(V_k+\Delta V_k)-I\big\|_F^2

identity_at_init: As DoRA: \(B = 0\) and \(m = \|W_0\|\) per neuron.
key_idea: Train DoRA's magnitude and direction asynchronously: the direction on the training split and the magnitude on a validation split via hypergradients, then refit the direction. This decouples the two further and reduces overfitting.
results_note: Reports an 85.2 GLUE average on RoBERTa-base vs 84.6 for DoRA, a smaller train-test gap, and consistent gains over DoRA on NLU, NLG, token classification and extremely small biomedical datasets (Wilcoxon p = 2.4e-4 on GLUE).

Image germ, fibre and merge type are unchanged; only the cotangent signal (hypergradient-driven, non-gradient) differs.

name: SSF
paper_title: Scaling & Shifting Your Features: A New Baseline for Efficient Model Tuning
formula_latex: y=\gamma\odot x+\beta\ \text{after each operation (MSA, MLP, LayerNorm)};\ \text{after a linear op: } W=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma)\,W_0,\ b=\gamma\odot b_0+\beta;\ W_0,b_0\ \text{frozen},\ \gamma,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: 2d\ \text{per SSF-wrapped operation}
locus: after every operation of a ViT block (attention, MLP, LayerNorm)
structure: a per-channel affine map (diagonal scaling plus shift), i.e. an action of the diagonal affine group \((\mathbb R^\times)^d\ltimes\mathbb R^d\) on output channels, re-parameterizable into the preceding linear layer
mergeable_reason: The paper re-parameterizes \((\gamma, \beta)\) into the preceding linear/conv weight and bias, so inference runs the original architecture.
identity_at_init: \(\gamma \sim N(1, 0.02)\) and \(\beta \sim N(0, 0.02)\) in the official code (init_ssf_scale_shift): close to, but not exactly, the identity.
key_idea: Fine-tuning a pretrained vision backbone can be reduced to learning a per-channel scale and shift of its features. These fold back into the weights, so there is no inference overhead.
results_note: With ViT-B/16, reports 90.72% on FGVC and 73.10% on VTAB-1k (about 0.3M trainable parameters), above full fine-tuning (88.54% and 65.57%).
categorical_reading: SSF is the diagonal affine group \((\mathbb R^\times)^d\ltimes\mathbb R^d\) acting on output channels after every operation. Its orbit closure is linear: the output-side torus of (IA)\(^3\) plus a BitFit-type shift. It fuses into the preceding box only under the side conditions of Thm VI.3.

name: RED
paper_title: Advancing Parameter Efficiency in Fine-tuning via Representation Editing
formula_latex: h_2=l_{scaling}\odot h_1+l_{bias},\ h_1=\text{output of each FFN sub-layer};\ \text{equivalently } W_{down}=\operatorname{diag}(l_{scaling})\,W_{down}^{0},\ b=l_{scaling}\odot b^{0}+l_{bias};\ \text{model frozen},\ l_{scaling},l_{bias}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: 2dL
locus: outputs of the FFN sub-layer in every Transformer layer (ablations also edit Q, K, V)
structure: per-channel affine edit (diagonal scaling plus shift) of each FFN's contribution to the residual stream; the same algebraic form as SSF, applied to LLM FFN outputs
mergeable_reason: The scaling always folds into the FFN down-projection; the shift folds into its bias only if that layer has one (LLaMA-style down-projections have no bias, so a bias term must be added).
identity_at_init: \(l_{scaling} = 1\) and \(l_{bias} = 0\).
key_idea: Instead of adding modules, edit hidden representations directly with one scaling vector and one bias vector per layer. This uses about 25,700x fewer parameters than full fine-tuning and about 32x fewer than LoRA, with no rank to tune.
results_note: Comparable to or better than full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods on GLUE (RoBERTa, T5), E2E NLG (GPT-2) and LLaMA-2 instruction tuning (AlpacaEval) with far fewer parameters.
categorical_reading: RED is SSF's scale-and-shift restricted to the FFN outputs of an LLM: an output-side diagonal affine action on \(W_{\rm down}\) and its bias, linear and regular at \(\theta_0\). The scale always fuses into \(W_{\rm down}\); the shift needs a bias slot.

name: DiffFit
full_name: DiffFit (bias tuning plus learnable residual scaling for diffusion transformers)
paper_title: DiffFit: Unlocking Transferability of Large Diffusion Models via Simple Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: x\leftarrow x+\gamma_1\odot\mathrm{Attn}(x),\quad x\leftarrow x+\gamma_2\odot\mathrm{FFN}(x),\ \gamma_1,\gamma_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ (\text{init } \mathbf{1});\ \text{trained: } \gamma,\ \text{biases, normalization parameters, class embedding; all other weights frozen}
trainable_params: \approx 0.12\%\ \text{of DiT-XL/2 (0.83M of 673.8M)}
locus: learnable scales \(\gamma\) on the residual branches of the first 14 DiT-XL/2 blocks, plus QKV-linear and final layers; all biases, normalization parameters and the class embedding are also tuned
structure: diagonal scaling of each residual branch's output (foldable into the branch's output projection) combined with BitFit-style selective tuning of biases and normalization parameters
mergeable_reason: \(\gamma\) folds into the output projection weight and bias of the attention/FFN branch; the tuned biases and norms replace the old ones.
identity_at_init: \(\gamma = 1\), and biases and norms start from their pretrained values.
key_idea: For diffusion transformers, tuning the biases plus a learnable per-channel scale on each residual branch is enough to transfer quickly to new domains and resolutions.
results_note: About 2x faster training than full fine-tuning, storing about 0.12% of the parameters; FID 3.02 on ImageNet 512x512 after 25 epochs from a 256x256 checkpoint.
categorical_reading: DiffFit is BitFit plus an output-side torus on each residual branch: \(\gamma\odot\mathrm{Attn}(x)\) becomes \(\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)W_o\) after a spider slide through the adaLN gate, so the whole method is linear, regular and idempotent. It sits in the selective row because most of its coordinates are existing biases and norms.

name: LieRA
full_name: Lie-group Rank Adaptation (Lie-group-based generalized tensor PEFT)
paper_title: Generalized Tensor-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Lie Group Transformations
formula_latex: W=W_0\odot\exp_{\odot}(\Delta W)\approx W_0+W_0\odot\Delta W\ \ (\text{first-order form used in all experiments}),\quad \Delta W=BA\ (\text{LoRA-factorized; conv kernels are treated as tensors}),\ \exp_{\odot}\ \text{entry-wise};\ W_0\ \text{frozen (non-zero entries)},\ B,A\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: linear layers and higher-order (convolutional) kernels
structure: action of the abelian Lie group of entry-wise non-zero tensors under the Hadamard product (identity = all-ones tensor) on \(W_0\). The update lives in its Lie algebra (all real tensors) and is mapped back through the entry-wise exponential; truncating at first order gives \(W_0 + W_0 \odot \Delta W\).
mergeable_reason: The trained first-order update \(W_0 + W_0 \odot BA\) (or \(W_0 \odot \exp(BA)\)) is a fixed tensor of the original shape.
key_idea: Treat parameters as elements of a Lie group under element-wise multiplication. Matrix PEFT updates (LoRA-style) then lift to high-dimensional (conv) tensors without flattening, via the exponential map from the Lie algebra.
results_note: Reports gains over LoRA, e.g. a 75.5 vs 74.1 VTAB-1K average with ConvNeXt-V2-B (\(r=16\)), plus improvements on COCO detection, LLaMA commonsense reasoning and GLUE.
categorical_reading: As evaluated, LieRA is HiRA, \((D_{W_0})_*\mathrm{LoRA}\) inside the slice at \(\theta_0\). Its defining form \(W_0\odot\exp_\odot(BA)\) is the further non-linear transport \(\Psi_*\) of that object: an action of the positive Hadamard torus \((\mathbb R_{>0})^{m\times n}\), with Lie algebra \(\Theta\), restricted to \(\exp_\odot\) of a determinantal cone. That action preserves both the sign and the zero pattern of \(W_0\), however often it is merged.

name: FLoRA
full_name: Fast LoRA (batched, example-specific multiplicative low-rank adaptation)
paper_title: Batched Low-Rank Adaptation of Foundation Models
formula_latex: W_i=W_0\odot(B_iA_i),\quad h_i=\operatorname{reduce}_{j=1..r}\Big[b^{(i)}_j\odot\big(W_0\,(a^{(i)}_j\odot x_i)\big)\Big]\ (\text{the paper uses a reduction such as torch.mean over the } r \text{ terms}),\ B_i=[b^{(i)}_1,\dots,b^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i^{\top}=[a^{(i)}_1,\dots,a^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{per example/adapter } i;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapter}
locus: linear layers, with per-request adapters in multi-tenant serving
structure: entry-wise (Hadamard) modulation of \(W_0\) by a rank-\(r\) matrix. The rank-1 case is a two-sided diagonal scaling \(\mathrm{diag}(b)\, W_0\, \mathrm{diag}(a)\), an action of the torus \((\mathbb R^\times)^{d_{out}}\times(\mathbb R^\times)^{d_{in}}\); rank \(r\) is a sum of \(r\) such scalings, so a batch with different adapters needs only element-wise operations around one shared matmul.
mergeable_reason: For a fixed adapter, \(W_0 \odot BA\) can be precomputed; the point of the method is to keep it unmerged so different examples in a batch can use different adapters.
identity_at_init: Not specified in the method section read. The parameterization reproduces \(W_0\) only when \(B_iA_i\) is the all-ones matrix (e.g. rank-1 all-ones vectors), not with LoRA's \(B = 0\).

results_note: Reports about 2x throughput over LoRA on StarCoder-15B when each request needs a different low-rank adapter, while keeping LoRA-level accuracy on MultiPL-E multilingual code generation and on multilingual speech recognition (Whisper).
categorical_reading: FLoRA is the Hadamard action \(\rho(B,A)=W_0\odot BA\) of the multiplicative monoid \((\Theta,\odot)\) on \(W_0\), pointed at a factorisation of \(J\). Rank one is the two-sided torus orbit, rank \(r\) is the transported determinantal cone with vertex at \(0\), and it and HiRA simulate each other with a one-step rank shift (\(\mathrm{FLoRA}_r\to\mathrm{HiRA}_{r+1}\to\mathrm{FLoRA}_{r+2}\)). Its batching advantage is a property of the realisation (one shared matmul), not of the object.

name: Quantum-PEFT
paper_title: Quantum-PEFT: Ultra parameter-efficient fine-tuning
formula_latex: W = W_0 + U\Lambda V^{\top},\quad U=Q_P(\theta_U)\,I_{d_{out}\times K},\ V=Q_P(\theta_V)\,I_{d_{in}\times K},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K},\ Q_P=\prod_{l=1}^{L}\Big(\big(I\otimes\mathrm{CZ}^{\otimes\frac{q-1}{2}}\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=2}^{q}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,2l+1})\big)\big(\mathrm{CZ}^{\otimes\frac{q-1}{2}}\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=1}^{q-1}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,2l})\otimes I\big)\Big)\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=1}^{q}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,1}),\ q=\log_2 d;\ \theta_U,\theta_V,\lambda\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: (2L+1)(\log_2 d_{in}+\log_2 d_{out})-4L+K\ \ \text{(Pauli parameterization: } (2L+1)\log_2 N-2L \text{ per unitary, plus } K \text{ diagonal entries)}
