structure: SVD-form update whose orthogonal factors are quantum-circuit (Pauli) parameterizations: Kronecker products of \(2\times 2\) RY rotations interleaved with diagonal \(\pm1\) CZ entanglers, so parameters grow logarithmically in \(d\).
mergeable_reason: \(U \Lambda V^\top\) is a dense matrix that can be added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the sections consulted (AdaLoRA-style SVD form; a zero diagonal \(\Lambda\) would give \(\Delta W = 0\)).
key_idea: Parameterize the singular-vector frames by a small quantum circuit, so trainable parameters scale like \(\log d\) instead of \(d\).
results_note: Reports orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters than the lowest-rank LoRA with competitive accuracy on language and vision transfer benchmarks.
categorical_reading: Quantum-PEFT is AdaLoRA's SVD-shaped object \(P\Lambda Q\) precomposed with a low-dimensional map into Stiefel frames generated by a qubit circuit. This is an A3 arrow into AdaLoRA and LoRA; the parameter count is logarithmic because the frames are confined to the image of a short Lie-group word, which imposes \(\Pi_\otimes\).

name: P-Tuning v2
full_name: P-Tuning v2 (deep prompt tuning for NLU)
paper_title: P-Tuning v2: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Universally Across Scales and Tasks
formula_latex: \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big)\ \ \forall l\le L,\quad \hat y=\mathrm{softmax}(W_{\mathrm{cls}}\,h_{\mathrm{tok}});\ \ P^{(l)}\ (\text{optionally } \mathrm{MLP}\text{-reparametrized}),\ W_{\mathrm{cls}}\ \text{trained};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: 2L\ell d+d\,|\mathcal{Y}|\ \ (\approx 0.1\%\text{--}3\%\ \text{of the model})
locus: keys/values at every layer (deep prompts) plus a randomly initialized linear head on token representations
structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer (identical parameter shape to prefix-tuning), with a linear classification head instead of a verbalizer, task-dependent prompt length (short for classification, ~100 for sequence labeling) and optional reparametrization / multitask initialization.
mergeable_reason: Same as prefix-tuning: \(\ell\) extra key/value slots per layer that cannot be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No identity; random initialization, optionally a multitask-pretrained prompt as initialization.
key_idea: Inserting prompts at every layer (not just the input) gives more capacity and more direct influence on predictions, making prompt tuning match fine-tuning even for 300M-scale models and for hard sequence-labeling tasks.
results_note: Matches fine-tuning across model scales from 300M to 10B parameters and on hard sequence tagging (NER, extractive QA, SRL) while tuning 0.1%-3% of parameters.
categorical_reading: Deep prompt tuning: the unpointed key/value extension of prefix tuning in the direct parameterisation, summed with a new linear head. Prompt tuning maps into it in causal decoders (Thm VI.5(e)); whether that inclusion is strict is open.

name: WARP
paper_title: WARP: Word-level Adversarial ReProgramming
formula_latex: P_\Theta(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{y}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)}{\sum_{i\in C}\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{i}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)},\quad \Theta^P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{(prompt embeddings inserted by template } T\text{ around a [MASK])},\ \Theta^V\in\mathbb{R}^{|C|\times d}\ \text{(verbalizer embeddings)}\ \text{trained; MLM body frozen}
locus: input embedding sequence (template positions around a [MASK] token) and the output verbalizer vectors of the MLM head
structure: Adversarial reprogramming in word-embedding space: learned input embeddings at template positions plus learned class vectors that replace output-embedding rows of the masked-LM head (an input-side and an output-side reprogramming map around a frozen body).
mergeable_reason: Prompt embeddings lengthen the input; only the verbalizer vectors act like a (new) linear head.
identity_at_init: No identity; prompt tokens initialized with the [MASK] embedding or embeddings similar to the vocabulary; verbalizers from the MLM head.
key_idea: Treat task adaptation as adversarial reprogramming: search continuous prompt and verbalizer embeddings by SGD so a frozen masked LM's [MASK] prediction solves the task.
results_note: With up to 25K trainable parameters per task on RoBERTa-large it reaches 81.6 on the GLUE test leaderboard, beating submissions with up to three orders of magnitude more trainable parameters; strong few-shot SuperGLUE results with ALBERT.

name: PPT
paper_title: PPT: Pre-trained Prompt Tuning for Few-shot Learning
formula_latex: P^\star=\arg\min_{P}\ \sum_{(X,Y)\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{self-sup}}}-\log\Pr_\theta\big(Y\mid[P;X]\big)\ \text{(unified pre-training tasks built from unlabeled text)};\ \ \text{then prompt tuning on the target task initialized at } P^\star;\ \theta\ \text{frozen throughout}
trainable_params: \ell d
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: Vanilla soft prompt whose initialization is obtained by pre-training the prompt alone on self-supervised tasks cast in the same formats as downstream tasks (sentence-pair, multiple-choice, single-sentence classification, or a unified multiple-choice format).
mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt that lengthens the input.
identity_at_init: No identity; the contribution is the initialization itself (a prompt pre-trained on the PLM's own pre-training-style objective).
key_idea: Prompt tuning fails in few-shot regimes mainly because of poor initialization, so pre-train the soft prompt on large unlabeled corpora using task formats that mirror downstream classification.
results_note: With T5-XXL and CPM-2 (~11B), tuning pre-trained prompts reaches or exceeds full-model fine-tuning in both full-data and few-shot settings, far above vanilla prompt tuning in few-shot.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning re-pointed: \((Q,\rho)\) is that of prompt tuning and only the base point \(q_0=P^\star\) changes, obtained by pre-training the prompt on self-supervised tasks in downstream formats. In the framework a change of pointing is a genuine change of object (cf. Type I versus Type II LoRA).

name: SPoT
paper_title: SPoT: Better Frozen Model Adaptation through Soft Prompt Transfer
formula_latex: P_{s}=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{s}\big([P;X]\big),\quad P_{t}^{(0)}\leftarrow P_{s^\star},\quad P_t^\star=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{t}\big([P;X]\big);\ \ s^\star=\arg\max_s\cos\Big(\tfrac1\ell\textstyle\sum_i e^{s}_i,\ \tfrac1\ell\sum_j e^{t}_j\Big)\ \text{(early-checkpoint prompts as task embeddings; a per-token average cosine is the alternative metric)};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: \ell d
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: Vanilla soft prompt initialized from a prompt trained on a source task (or multi-task mixture); early-checkpoint prompts double as task embeddings whose cosine similarity predicts transferability for source retrieval.
mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt.
identity_at_init: No identity; initialization from a source-task prompt is the method.
key_idea: Soft prompts are transferable task representations: train them on source tasks, use them to initialize target prompts, and use prompt similarity as a cheap task-similarity metric to choose sources.
results_note: Across all T5 sizes, SPoT matches or outperforms full model tuning on SuperGLUE while using up to 27,000x fewer task-specific parameters; a 26-task, 160-pair transfer study shows widespread positive transfer.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning re-pointed at a source-task prompt \(P_{s^\star}\). The retrieval step compares candidate base points by a cosine, a \(CO(d)\)-invariant comparison of points of one unpointed slice.

name: ATTEMPT
paper_title: ATTEMPT: Parameter-Efficient Multi-task Tuning via Attentional Mixtures of Soft Prompts
formula_latex: P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X)=P_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\sum_{j=1}^{t+1}a_j(X)\,P_j,\quad a_j=\frac{\exp(\hat P_j^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)}{\sum_{k=1}^{t+1}\exp(\hat P_k^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)},\quad H_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathrm{LN}\big(W_{up}^{\top}\,\mathrm{SiLU}(W_{down}^{\top}\hat X)\big),\ P_{t+1}=P_{\mathrm{tgt}};\ \ \text{input }[P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X);X];\ \text{train } P_{\mathrm{tgt}},W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d};\ \text{source prompts } P_{1..t}\ \text{and LM frozen}
trainable_params: d\big(\ell+2(r+1)/N\big)\ \text{per task (attention module shared across } N \text{ target tasks)}
locus: input embedding sequence (instance-specific prompt)
structure: Instance-wise softmax mixture (a point of the simplex) over a library of frozen source prompts plus the trainable target prompt, added to the target prompt; mixture weights come from a bottleneck network on the max-pooled input (\(\hat X\), \(\hat P_j\) are max-pooled).
mergeable_reason: The prompt depends on the input instance and lengthens the sequence; it can never be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: No identity; source prompts pre-trained by prompt tuning on large source tasks, target prompt newly initialized.
key_idea: Treat pre-trained soft prompts as modular knowledge units and learn, per input, an attention-weighted interpolation of them with a new target prompt, sharing the router across tasks.
results_note: On 21 datasets with T5-base, significantly outperforms prompt tuning and matches or beats full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods that use over 10x more parameters, while updating ~2,300x fewer parameters than fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: A family over inputs \(F_X\): the router gives a point \(a(X)\) of a simplex and the prompt \(P_{\rm tgt}+\sum_ja_j(X)P_j\) is a convex mixture of a frozen prompt library plus a trainable offset, fed to prompt tuning. Input dependence takes it outside every fixed-prompt image, and max-pooling makes the router coordinatewise.

name: DePT
paper_title: DePT: Decomposed Prompt Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
formula_latex: \text{input } \big[P_s;\ E_X+AB\big],\quad P_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell'\times d},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ E_X\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times d}\ \text{frozen word embeddings of the input padded to the maximum length } s;\ \ \ell' d+(s+d)r=\ell d;\ \ A\sim\mathcal{N},\ B=0;\ \text{learning rates } \alpha_1(P_s)\gg\alpha_2(A,B);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}

locus: input embedding sequence: a shorter soft prompt plus a position-wise offset to the input token embeddings
structure: Short soft prompt (concatenation) plus a rank-\(r\) additive, position-indexed offset \(AB\) to the frozen \(s\times d\) input-embedding matrix, i.e. a LoRA-style low-rank update applied to the input activation matrix rather than to a weight (the paper writes the product as \(BA\); dimensionally it is the \(s\times d\) matrix \(A B\)).

key_idea: Trade prompt length for a low-rank update of the input embeddings: same parameter budget, shorter sequences, so lower time/memory, trained with two learning rates.
results_note: Across 23 NLP and vision-language tasks, outperforms vanilla prompt tuning and other PEFT methods (sometimes full fine-tuning) while saving over 20% training/inference time and memory relative to prompt tuning with T5-Base.

The prompt summand makes the sum unpointed, so no pointed arrow relates DePT to LoRA.

name: Residual Prompt Tuning
paper_title: Residual Prompt Tuning: Improving Prompt Tuning with Residual Reparameterization
formula_latex: P'_i=\Phi(P_i)=\mathrm{LN}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(P_iW_{down})\,W_{up}\big)+P_i,\ \ i=1,\dots,\ell\ \ (P_i\ \text{a row vector});\ \ \text{input }[P';X];\ \ \text{train } P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\ W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d},\ \mathrm{LN};\ \text{after training store only } P'=\Phi(P);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}

locus: input embedding sequence
structure: Soft prompt reparametrized through a shared bottleneck MLP with LayerNorm and a residual skip, applied token-wise; the reparametrization is discarded after training (an over-parameterization that only changes the optimization geometry).
mergeable_reason: At inference only the projected prompt \(P'\) remains, which still lengthens the input.
identity_at_init: No model-level identity; the residual skip lets each virtual token choose between its free embedding and the shared projection, improving robustness to learning rate and initialization.
key_idea: Prompt tuning is unstable because prompt tokens are optimized independently; a shared residual MLP couples them and speeds and stabilizes training at no inference cost.
results_note: Significantly outperforms prompt tuning on SuperGLUE with T5-Large, T5-Base and BERT-Base (e.g., +7 points with T5-Base), allows 10x shorter prompts without loss, and helps in few-shot settings.

name: LPT
paper_title: Late Prompt Tuning: A Late Prompt Could Be Better Than Many Prompts
formula_latex: h^{(l^\ast)}\leftarrow\big[p(x);\,h^{(l^\ast)}\big],\quad p(x)=W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(\mathrm{Pool}_{n\to\ell}(W_1h^{(l^\ast)}+b_1)\big)+b_2\ \ (\text{pooling generator}),\ \ \text{or}\ \ p(x)=\mathrm{Reshape}\big(W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}(W_1h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}+b_1)+b_2\big)\ (\text{naive});\ \ W_1\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d};\ \text{single insertion layer } l^\ast\ (\text{e.g. 13 of 24});\ \text{backbone frozen}
trainable_params: \approx 2dm+m+d\ \ \text{(pooling generator)};\ \ \approx dm+\ell dm\ \ \text{(naive generator)}
locus: hidden-state sequence at a single intermediate layer
structure: Instance-dependent prompt generated by a bottleneck MLP (with optional pooling from input length \(n\) to prompt length \(\ell\)) from the hidden states just below the insertion layer, inserted once at an intermediate layer.
mergeable_reason: The prompt is input-dependent and adds tokens to the upper half of the network.
identity_at_init: No identity.
key_idea: There is a trade-off between how far the label signal must propagate back to the prompt and how much the prompt can influence outputs; a single 'late' prompt in a middle layer, generated from the instance's own hidden states, balances both and skips backprop through the lower layers.
results_note: Competitive with full model tuning and other PEFT methods in full-data and few-shot settings (RoBERTa-large among backbones), with faster training and lower memory than prompt tuning.
categorical_reading: A family over inputs: a bottleneck hypernetwork reads the layer-\(l^\ast\) hidden states and outputs a point of single-layer prompt space, inserted at \(l^\ast\). It is unpointed and input-dependent, so it is neither mergeable nor in the image of a static prompt.

name: IDPG
paper_title: IDPG: An Instance-Dependent Prompt Generation Method
formula_latex: W_p(T,x)=G\big(M(x),T\big)=W_2\,\sigma\big(W_1M(x)+b_1\big)+b_2\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\quad \hat y=\mathrm{softmax}(W h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}),\ h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}=M\big(\mathrm{concat}[x,W_p(T,x)]\big);\ \ W_{1,2}\ \text{PHM-factorised as } \textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes B_i;\ M\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: m(d+1)+\ell d(m+1)\ \text{(dense generator)}+\text{classification head};\ \ \text{generator reduced by }\approx n\times\text{ with PHM layers (e.g. 1.5M}\to\text{105K)}
locus: input embedding sequence (optionally multiple layers, M-IDPG)
structure: Two-layer bottleneck hypernetwork mapping a frozen sentence embedding \(M(x)\) to an \(\ell\)-token prompt; its second-layer bias is exactly a task-level soft prompt, so the generated prompt = task prompt + instance-dependent part; weights parameterized as sums of Kronecker products (PHM).
mergeable_reason: The prompt is input-dependent and requires an extra forward pass to compute \(M(x)\).
identity_at_init: No identity.
key_idea: Condition the soft prompt on each input sentence through a lightweight generator, recovering vanilla prompt tuning as the bias term.
results_note: On ten NLU tasks with RoBERTa-large, consistently outperforms prompt-tuning baselines and is on par with Compacter while tuning far fewer parameters.
categorical_reading: A \(T\)-point of prompt tuning over inputs, \(x\mapsto b_2+W_2\sigma(W_1M(x)+b_1)\), with PHM (Kronecker-sum) weights; its \(W_1=0\) slice is prompt tuning. PHM imposes \(\Pi_\otimes\) and a \(GL_n\) gauge on the PHM index, as for Compacter.

name: XPrompt
full_name: XPrompt (extremely small prompts via hierarchical structured pruning)
paper_title: XPrompt: Exploring the Extreme of Prompt Tuning
formula_latex: \hat P=\gamma\cdot P,\ \gamma\in\{0,1\}^{\ell}\ \text{(token mask)};\quad \hat q=\zeta\cdot q,\ \zeta\in\{0,1\}^{k}\ \text{(piece mask; each } p_i \text{ split into } k \text{ pieces)};\quad I_{p_i}=\mathbb{E}_{x}\Big|\tfrac{\partial\mathcal{L}(x)}{\partial\gamma_i}\Big|,\ I_{q_i}=\mathbb{E}_{x}\Big|\tfrac{\partial\mathcal{L}(x)}{\partial\zeta_i}\Big|;\ \text{prune low-importance units, rewind survivors to post-PT values, retrain};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: \rho\,\ell d,\ \ \rho<1\ \text{(fraction of tokens/pieces kept)}
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: Structured sparse mask on a soft prompt at two granularities (whole tokens, then equal-size pieces of each token embedding), found by gradient-sensitivity importance scores and lottery-ticket weight rewinding.
mergeable_reason: The pruned prompt is still a prompt that lengthens the input.
identity_at_init: No identity; starts from a fully trained vanilla prompt (stage 1), then prunes and rewinds.
key_idea: Some trained prompt tokens hurt the task; finding a 'winning ticket' sub-prompt by hierarchical structured pruning gives a smaller and better prompt.
results_note: On SuperGLUE with T5, largely closes the gap between prompt tuning and fine-tuning at moderate model scales (below 11B) while using fewer prompt parameters.
categorical_reading: A structured mask on prompt space: the winning sub-prompt is an A2 sub-object of prompt tuning, with pruned tokens and pieces frozen at \(0\), pointed at the rewound trained prompt. Piece masks impose a block partition of the embedding coordinates.

name: BBT
paper_title: Black-Box Tuning for Language-Model-as-a-Service
formula_latex: p=Az+p_0,\quad z^\star=\arg\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{k}}\ \mathcal{L}\big(f(Az+p_0;\tilde X),\tilde Y\big),\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell d\times k}\ \text{fixed random},\ p_0\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell d}\ \text{(random vocab embeddings or an MNLI-pretrained prompt)};\ z\ \text{searched by CMA-ES with forward (API) queries only; model frozen, no gradients}
locus: input embedding sequence
structure: Soft prompt restricted to a random \(k\)-dimensional affine subspace \(p_0+\mathrm{col}(A)\) (intrinsic-dimension reparametrization), optimized by derivative-free CMA-ES.
mergeable_reason: The result is a soft prompt that lengthens the input.
identity_at_init: No identity; \(z=0\) gives the initial prompt \(p_0\).
key_idea: Because large PLMs have low intrinsic dimension, a soft prompt can be optimized in a small random subspace by gradient-free evolution strategies, using only inference API access (Language-Model-as-a-Service).
results_note: With RoBERTa-large on few-shot classification, black-box tuning significantly outperforms manual prompts and GPT-3 in-context learning and surpasses gradient-based prompt tuning and full model tuning.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning restricted to a random affine subspace \(p_0+\mathrm{col}\,A\), the prompt-space analogue of intrinsic-dimension and frozen-frame methods; covariance holds only in law. CMA-ES is a derivative-free update on \(Q=\mathbb R^k\) and does not change the object.

name: VPT
paper_title: Visual Prompt Tuning
formula_latex: \text{Shallow: } [x_1,Z_1,E_1]=L_1([x_0,P,E_0]),\ [x_i,Z_i,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},Z_{i-1},E_{i-1}]);\quad \text{Deep: } [x_i,\_\,,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},P_{i-1},E_{i-1}]),\ i=1,\dots,L;\quad y=\mathrm{Head}(x_L);\ \ P,P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{and Head trained; ViT frozen}
trainable_params: \ell d\ \text{(shallow)};\ \ L\ell d\ \text{(deep)};\ \ +\ \text{head}
locus: token sequence after the patch embedding (shallow) / input of every Transformer layer (deep)
structure: Learned tokens inserted into the residual stream of a ViT. In VPT-Deep the prompt outputs are discarded after each layer, so their only effect on image tokens is as extra keys/values \(\mathrm{LN}(P_{i-1})W_k,\ \mathrm{LN}(P_{i-1})W_v\): a prefix tied through the frozen projections (derived from the equations here).
mergeable_reason: Prompts add tokens at every layer (deep) or at the input (shallow).
identity_at_init: No identity; prompts initialized with Xavier-uniform (class-prototype initialization was not better).
key_idea: Transfer NLP prompt tuning to vision Transformers: a handful of learnable tokens per layer plus a head adapts a frozen ViT, often better than full fine-tuning.
results_note: With ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21k), VPT-Deep outperforms full fine-tuning on 20 of 24 tasks (FGVC + VTAB-1k) and all other PEFT protocols, while storing 0.04%/0.53% extra parameters per task (shallow/deep).
categorical_reading: VPT-Shallow is prompt tuning on a ViT; VPT-Deep is a deep prefix tied through the frozen maps \(P\mapsto(\mathrm{LN}(P)W_k,\mathrm{LN}(P)W_v)\), plus a new linear head. The LN tie adds a per-token scaling gauge, and Thm VI.5(e) (shallow into deep) does not apply because ViTs are bidirectional.

name: Visual Prompting
paper_title: Exploring Visual Prompts for Adapting Large-Scale Models
formula_latex: \max_{\phi}\ \log P_{\theta;\phi}\big(y\mid x+v_\phi\big),\quad v_\phi\ \text{a single pixel-space perturbation shared by all images (padding frame of width } p\text{, or a patch)};\ \ \theta\ \text{frozen; labels via CLIP text prompts}
trainable_params: 2Cp(H+W-2p)\ \text{(padding)};\ \ Cp^{2}\ \text{(patch)}
locus: input pixels
structure: An additive translation of input space, \(x\mapsto x+v_\phi\), supported on a border frame (or a patch).
mergeable_reason: For a ViT with a fixed-location prompt (padding or fixed patch) the patch embedding \(E\) is linear, so \(E(x+v)=Ex+Ev\) and the per-patch constant \(Ev\) folds exactly into the positional embeddings (derived here, not claimed in the paper); the random-location patch variant cannot be merged, and CNN backbones would need a per-position bias map after the first convolution, which is not a standard parameter.
identity_at_init: No identity at initialization: the official code initializes \(v_\phi\) with a standard normal (torch.randn); \(v_\phi=0\) would recover the frozen model exactly.
key_idea: Adapt a frozen vision model by learning a single input perturbation (adversarial reprogramming as prompting), with the output mapped to labels through text prompts for CLIP.
results_note: Particularly effective for CLIP, where a padding prompt (\(p=30\) best) is competitive with linear probing and robust to distribution shift.
categorical_reading: A pointed extension by a translation box \(x\mapsto x+v\) on the pixel wire, neutral at \(v=0\) but initialised randomly, hence a pointing defect. On a ViT with a fixed prompt location the linear patch embedding slides it onto the positional-embedding table (R1), so there it is a Lin method.

name: CoOp
paper_title: Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models
formula_latex: t_i=[V]_1[V]_2\cdots[V]_{\ell}[\mathrm{CLASS}_i],\qquad p(y=i\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\cos(g(t_i),f(x))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp\big(\cos(g(t_j),f(x))/\tau\big)};\ \ [V]_m\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained (unified or class-specific)};\ \text{CLIP encoders } f,g\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: \ell d\ \text{(unified context)};\ \ K\ell d\ \text{(class-specific context)}
locus: input embedding sequence of the CLIP text encoder
structure: Soft prompt (shared or per-class context vectors) prepended to each class-name token sequence; the classifier weights are the frozen text encoder's images \(g(t_i)\) of the prompted class names.
mergeable_reason: In closed-set classification the \(K\) prompted class embeddings \(g(t_i)\) are computed once after training and cached as a linear classifier, so inference costs exactly as much as zero-shot CLIP; the learned context itself cannot be folded into the text encoder's weights, and any new class name requires re-running the text encoder with the prompt.
identity_at_init: Can be initialized from the embedding of a hand-crafted context such as 'a photo of a' (starting at the zero-shot classifier) or randomly.
key_idea: Replace hand-engineered CLIP prompts by learnable context vectors optimized end-to-end through the frozen text encoder.
results_note: On 11 image-recognition datasets, one or two shots suffice to beat hand-crafted prompts, and with 16 shots the average gain is around 15%.
categorical_reading: Prompt tuning on CLIP's text tower with a context shared across class sequences. In closed-set use the realisation factors through the \(K\times d\) head \(W(V)=[g([V;c_i])]_i\), so CoOp is a non-linear reparametrisation of the zero-shot head that fuses into it, pointed at zero-shot CLIP under 'a photo of a' initialisation.

name: CoCoOp
paper_title: Conditional Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
formula_latex: v_m(x)=v_m+h_\theta\big(f(x)\big),\ \ t_i(x)=\{v_1(x),\dots,v_\ell(x),c_i\},\qquad p(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_y(x)))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{i=1}^{K}\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_i(x)))/\tau\big)};\ \ h_\theta=\text{Linear-ReLU-Linear (16}\times\text{ bottleneck)};\ \text{train } v_{1..\ell},\theta;\ \text{CLIP frozen}
trainable_params: \ell d+\tfrac{d_v}{16}\,(d_v+d)\ \ (\text{plus biases; } d_v=\text{image-feature width})
locus: input embedding sequence of the CLIP text encoder, conditioned on the image feature
structure: Context vectors shifted by one image-conditioned token \(\pi=h_\theta(f(x))\) produced by a lightweight meta-network (an input-dependent translation of the shared prompt).
mergeable_reason: Class embeddings depend on the image, so the text encoder must be re-run for all \(K\) classes per image (much higher inference cost than CoOp).
identity_at_init: No identity; reduces to CoOp when \(h_\theta\) outputs zero.
key_idea: Static learned prompts overfit to base classes; making the prompt conditional on each image improves generalization to unseen classes and domains.
results_note: Generalizes much better than CoOp to unseen classes within a dataset, and improves cross-dataset transfer and domain generalization across 11 datasets.
categorical_reading: A family over images: \(x\mapsto V+h_\theta(f(x))\mathbf 1^\top\) is a \(T\)-point of CoOp with \(T\) the image features. The classifier rows then depend on \(x\), so no fixed head, hence no CoOp point, realises it.

name: MaPLe
paper_title: MaPLe: Multi-modal Prompt Learning
formula_latex: [\_\,,W_i]=L_i([P_{i-1},W_{i-1}]),\quad [c_i,E_i,\_\,]=V_i\big([c_{i-1},E_{i-1},F_{i-1}(P_{i-1})]\big),\ \ i=1,\dots,J;\quad \tilde P_k=F_k(P_k),\ F_k:\mathbb{R}^{d_l}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_v}\ \text{linear};\ \ \text{train } \{P_i\},\{F_i\};\ \text{CLIP frozen}
trainable_params: J\ell d_l+J\,(d_ld_v+d_v)
locus: token sequences of both the text and image encoders up to depth \(J\) (deep prompts)
structure: Deep prompts in the language branch, with vision-branch prompts obtained as linear images \(F_k(P_k)\) of the language prompts (one shared parameter pushed forward into both modalities, coupling their gradients).
mergeable_reason: Vision-branch prompts add tokens to every image forward pass (the text side alone could be cached).
identity_at_init: No identity.
key_idea: Prompt both towers of CLIP and couple vision prompts to language prompts so the two representation spaces adapt jointly instead of independently.
results_note: Over CoCoOp, gains of +3.45% on novel classes and +2.72% harmonic mean averaged over 11 datasets in base-to-novel generalization, also improving cross-dataset and domain-shift results.
categorical_reading: A coupled pair of deep prompt extensions on both CLIP towers, the vision prompts being the push-forward \(F_k(P_k)\) of the language prompts along trainable linear maps, so one parameter moves both towers. Deep replacement makes each layer's prompts act only through LayerNorm, and the coupling is read only at the \(\ell\) prompt rows, so the gauge fibre is large and non-linear.

name: L2P
full_name: Learning to Prompt (prompt pool for continual learning)
paper_title: Learning to Prompt for Continual Learning
formula_latex: K_x=\arg\min_{\{s_i\}_{i=1}^{N}\subseteq[1,M]}\ \sum_{i=1}^{N}\gamma\big(q(x),k_{s_i}\big),\ \ q(x)=f(x)[0]\ \text{(frozen ViT [CLS])};\ \ x_p=[P_{s_1};\dots;P_{s_N};x_e];\ \ \min_{P,K,\phi}\ \mathcal{L}\Big(g_\phi\big(\mathrm{AvgPool}(f_r(x_p)[0{:}N\ell])\big),y\Big)+\lambda\sum_{s_i\in K_x}\gamma\big(q(x),k_{s_i}\big)
trainable_params: M(\ell d+d_k)+\text{head}
locus: input token sequence of a frozen ViT (prompts selected from a pool)
structure: Key-value prompt memory \(\{(k_j,P_j)\}_{j=1}^M\): input-conditioned hard top-\(N\) retrieval by cosine matching between a frozen-model query and learnable keys; the selected prompts are concatenated.
mergeable_reason: Prompts are selected per input and lengthen the token sequence; the query also costs an extra frozen forward pass.
identity_at_init: No identity.
key_idea: For rehearsal-free continual learning, keep the backbone frozen and store knowledge in a pool of prompts that are retrieved per instance, so tasks share or separate prompts automatically without task identity at test time.
results_note: Consistently outperforms prior state of the art in class-incremental, domain-incremental and task-agnostic continual learning (e.g., Split CIFAR-100, 5-datasets) and is competitive with rehearsal-based methods without any buffer.
categorical_reading: A family over inputs by hard retrieval: a key–query cosine match picks \(N\) of \(M\) prompts, so the prompt is a piecewise-constant function of \(x\). Its realisations jump at selection boundaries, which no continuous family (static prompts, softmax routers) can reproduce.

name: DualPrompt
paper_title: DualPrompt: Complementary Prompting for Rehearsal-free Continual Learning
formula_latex: h_g^{(i)}=f_{\mathrm{prompt}}\big(g,h^{(i)}\big),\ \ h_e^{(j)}=f_{\mathrm{prompt}}\big(e_t,h^{(j)}\big),\ \ f^{\mathrm{Pre\text{-}T}}_{\mathrm{prompt}}(p,h)=\mathrm{MSA}\big(h_Q,[p_k;h_K],[p_v;h_V]\big);\ \ t^\star=\arg\min_t\gamma\big(q(x),k_t\big);\ \ \min_{g,e_t,k_t,\phi}\ \mathcal{L}\big(f_\phi(f_{g,e_t}(x)),y\big)+\lambda\,\gamma\big(q(x),k_t\big)
trainable_params: n_g\ell_g d+T\,(n_e\ell_e d+d)+\text{head}\ \ (n_g,n_e=\text{number of layers carrying G/E prompts};\ \ell_g,\ell_e\ \text{total prompt lengths, split into } \ell/2 \text{ key and } \ell/2 \text{ value vectors in prefix form})
locus: keys/values (prefix form) of a few shallow (G-prompt) and middle (E-prompt) ViT layers
structure: A task-invariant prefix \(g\) shared by all tasks at shallow layers plus a pool of task-specific prefixes \(e_t\) at deeper layers, the latter retrieved by key matching against a frozen-model query.
mergeable_reason: Extra prefix key/value slots and input-dependent selection at inference.
identity_at_init: No identity.
key_idea: Split continual-learning knowledge into a general prompt and expert prompts attached at different depths, using prefix-style (key/value) attachment, which works better than prompt-token insertion for this purpose.
results_note: Sets state of the art for rehearsal-free class-incremental learning and even outperforms methods with sizable rehearsal buffers; introduces the Split ImageNet-R benchmark.
categorical_reading: A static shallow prefix (G-prompt) summed with a hard-retrieved task prefix (E-prompt) at middle layers: an \(F_X\) family with piecewise-constant selection on the key/value wire. Like L2P it realises discontinuous functions of the input.

name: Initial State Tuning
full_name: Initial State Tuning (for state space models)
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
formula_latex: h_t=\bar A_t h_{t-1}+\bar B_t x_t,\ \ y_t=C_th_t\ \ \text{run from } h_0=h'\ \text{instead of } 0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\Big(\prod_{i=1}^{t}\bar A_i\Big)h',\quad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel trained; all SSM weights frozen}
trainable_params: DH\ \text{per SSM layer}
locus: initial hidden state of each SSM (e.g. Mamba S6) layer
structure: Learned initial state of a linear recurrence. On S4, any prefix of virtual tokens acts only through \(h_{\mathrm{prefix}}=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\bar A^{i}\bar Bx_{-i}\), so prefix-tuning is exactly an initial-state update (Prop. 1); conversely every initial state is realizable by a prefix iff \(\ell\ge H\) (under a genericity condition).
mergeable_reason: No weight changes and per-token cost is unchanged, since SSM scan kernels accept an initial state natively, but the state is injected per sequence (in S6 its effect \(C_t(\prod_i\bar A_i)h'\) is input-dependent) and cannot be folded into \(W_0\), exactly like a cached prefix.
identity_at_init: \(h'=0\) recovers the base model exactly.
key_idea: For SSMs, the whole effect of prompt/prefix tuning is captured by the initial hidden state, so tune that state directly: an upper bound on prefix-tuning's expressivity at the same cost.
results_note: On Mamba with <0.5% trainable parameters, initial state tuning outperforms prefix-tuning and prompt tuning on five of seven tasks, but LoRA consistently outperforms it.
categorical_reading: A pointed extension: the SSM's initial state, fixed at \(0\) in \(f\), becomes a parameter \(h'\) with neutral point \(0\), and the output moves affinely, \(\hat y_t=y_t+C_t(\prod_{i\le t}\bar A_i)h'\). On S4 every prefix acts through this slot (Galim et al., Prop 1), and the zero prefix is neutral there: prefix tuning's unpointedness is a softmax phenomenon.

name: State-offset Tuning
paper_title: State-offset Tuning: State-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for State Space Models
formula_latex: \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\,h'\ \ \text{(State-offset (h))},\qquad \hat y_t=y_t+y'\ \ \text{(State-offset (y))},\qquad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel},\ y'\in\mathbb{R}^{D};\ \text{SSM weights frozen}
trainable_params: DH\ \text{(h variant)};\ \ D\ \text{(y variant) per SSM layer}
locus: state readout at every timestep of each SSM (Mamba S6) layer
structure: A constant learned offset added to the hidden state before readout at every step (Initial State Tuning with the time-varying factor \(\prod_i\bar A_i\) removed). In S6, \(C_th'=(W_Cx_t)^\top h'\), so the \(h\)-variant is a rank-\(\le H\) linear term in \(x_t\); the \(y\)-variant is a bias on the SSM output.
mergeable_reason: The offset enters before Mamba's multiplicative output gate (and as a linear term in \(x_t\) for the \(h\)-variant), so it cannot be absorbed into the existing diagonal skip or biases, although its cost is negligible.
identity_at_init: \(h'=0\) (or \(y'=0\)) recovers the frozen model exactly; the official code supports zero or Kaiming-uniform initialization of the offset parameters.
key_idea: State-based PEFT for SSMs: instead of injecting external virtual tokens, add a learnable constant to the internal state at every timestep, giving a uniform rather than decaying effect.
results_note: On Mamba-family models, State-offset Tuning (\(h\)) outperforms prompt-, prefix- and initial-state tuning and BitFit, and surpasses LoRA on most datasets; the (\(y\)) variant beats initial state tuning with 0.01% vs 0.23% of parameters.
categorical_reading: A pointed extension adding a constant state offset at every step. The \(h\)-variant is a LoRA-FA-type path \(x_t\mapsto H'W_Cx_t\) with frozen frame \(W_C\) on a new parallel box, and the \(y\)-variant is a new bias; both are neutral at \(0\), but they sit before Mamba's multiplicative gate, so no existing box absorbs them.

name: LQ-LoRA
paper_title: LQ-LoRA: Low-rank Plus Quantized Matrix Decomposition for Efficient Language Model Finetuning
formula_latex: \min_{Q\in\mathbb{Q}_{c},\,B,A}\big\lVert\sqrt{F}\odot\big(W_0-(Q+BA)\big)\big\rVert_F\ \ (F\equiv\mathbf 1\ \text{or diagonal empirical Fisher}):\ \ B^{(t)}A^{(t)}=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q^{(t-1)}),\ \ Q^{(t)}=\mathrm{Quantize}_c(W_0-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}),\ Q^{(0)}=0;\ \ c=(\text{bits, block sizes})\ \text{per matrix from an ILP under a global bit budget};\quad h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
locus: all linear layers of the transformer, each with its own NF quantization configuration
structure: robust-PCA-style low-rank-plus-quantized decomposition \(W_0 \approx Q + BA\); \(Q\) uses a per-matrix mixed-precision configuration chosen by integer linear programming; data-aware variant uses a row/column-scaled (Fisher-weighted) SVD
mergeable_reason: The low-rank component is high-precision and can be folded only into a dequantized copy of \(Q\); folding into the quantized \(Q\) needs re-quantization.
identity_at_init: Approximate: \(Q+BA\) is the alternating approximation of \(W_0\) (stopped when the error rises). Since \(Q^{(0)}=0\), the first low-rank component is the top-\(r\) SVD of \(W_0\) itself, so the adapter starts on \(W_0\)'s principal subspace rather than at zero.
key_idea: Split each pretrained matrix into a fixed, easily quantized part and a trainable high-variance low-rank part. Integer linear programming then allocates bits across matrices to meet any target memory budget.
results_note: Beats QLoRA and GPTQ-LoRA at matched bit budgets on LLaMA-2 (C4, OpenAssistant) and RoBERTa-large (GLUE). For example, 3.5-bit Fisher LQ-LoRA roughly equals 4.127-bit NF4 QLoRA, and a 2.75-bit LLaMA-2-70B (27GB) stays competitive with 16-bit.
categorical_reading: LQ-LoRA is LoftQ's object with the other starting order: split first (\(Q^{(0)}=0\) gives PiSSA's top-\(r\) factor) and quantise the residual, iterated. It is a Type II translated cone over a quantised apex, pointed up to an attained residual, and with the identity quantiser and one iteration it is exactly PiSSA.

name: IR-QLoRA
paper_title: Accurate LoRA-Finetuning Quantization of LLMs via Information Retention

trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2
locus: all linear layers of LLaMA/LLaMA2; NF2-NF4 or integer-quantized base
structure: LoRA with parameter-free 'elastic' shortcuts: \(\Delta W=\alpha(B+\beta_2E)(A+\beta_1P)\), where \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\) averages \(r\) contiguous input groups and \(E\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times r}\) repeats each of the \(r\) entries \(d_{out}/r\) times; still rank \(\le r\). Base is an entropy-calibrated NF-k quantizer with a per-block shift \(\tau\)
mergeable_reason: The IEC shortcuts are linear and fold into the LoRA factors (and then into a 16-bit copy of the weight), but folding into the NF-k base requires re-quantization.
identity_at_init: Exact relative to the quantized base: \(B = 0\) and, in the official code, \(\beta_1=\beta_2=0\) (the paper itself does not state their initialization), so the adapter is zero at step 0. The starting model is the ICQ-quantized one, not \(W_0\).
key_idea: View quantize-then-LoRA through information retention. Calibration Quantization (ICQ) maximizes the entropy of the quantized weights so they keep more information. The Elastic Connection (IEC) adds parameter-free pooling and tiling paths so LoRA can directly reuse the original features.
results_note: Improves LLaMA/LLaMA2 at 2-4 bits over QLoRA and QA-LoRA, e.g. +1.4% MMLU for 4-bit LLaMA-7B over the prior state of the art, at only 0.31% extra training time.
categorical_reading: IR-QLoRA is QLoRA over an entropy-calibrated base: ICQ moves the base point to \(\kappa_{\tau^*}\theta_0\), and IEC is a pure reparametrisation \((B+\beta_2E,\,A+\beta_1P)\) of LoRA's factors that leaves the image unchanged. What IEC changes is the cometric \(K=D\rho\,\Lambda\,D\rho^\top\), i.e. the dynamics, not the expressivity.

name: L4Q
full_name: Low-rank adaptive Learning quantization for LLMs
paper_title: L4Q: Parameter Efficient Quantization-Aware Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
formula_latex: W_{comb}=W_0+\alpha BA,\quad \tilde w=\mathrm{round}\Big(\mathrm{clamp}\big(\tfrac{W_{comb}-b}{s},Q_N,Q_P\big)\Big),\ \ W_q=\tilde w\,s+b,\quad h=W_qx;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B,s,b)\ \text{trained with STE};\ \ \tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial B}=\alpha\big(\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial W_q}\odot\mathbb 1_{[Q_N,Q_P]}\big)A^{\top}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2\,d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \ \text{(LoRA factors + one scale and bias per quantization group of size } g)
locus: all linear layers (LLaMA 7B-33B, OpenLLaMA-3B, Mistral-7B)
structure: learned-step-size quantizer composed after a rank-\(r\) additive update: \(W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA)\); custom backward reuses \(\partial\mathcal L/\partial W_q\) so no weight-gradient buffer is stored
mergeable_reason: The deployed model is exactly the fully quantized \(W_q=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA)\); no adapter or 16-bit branch remains at inference.
identity_at_init: \(B = 0\), so training starts from the 'L4Q init' symmetric quantization of \(W_0\) (scale \(s=\max(|\min W/Q_N|,|\max W/Q_P|)\), chosen to avoid clipping outliers), not from \(W_0\) itself.
key_idea: Put the LoRA update inside the quantizer rather than beside it, and train LoRA jointly with the quantization scale and bias. The result is a fully quantized model without QA-LoRA's constraints on the factors, at roughly LoRA's training memory.
results_note: On LLaMA and Mistral models with instruction data, 4-bit and 3-bit L4Q is more accurate than decoupled quantize-then-fine-tune schemes and QA-LoRA, at inference speed comparable to other fully quantized models.
categorical_reading: L4Q postcomposes LoRA with a trainable quantiser, \(\rho=\kappa_{s,b}\circ\mathrm{LoRA}\). For the exact map the LoRA factors are fibre directions, because codes are locally constant, and the smooth germ is only the quantiser's scale-and-shift action on frozen codes; LoRA acts through discrete code flips and the STE surrogate. This is the fine-tune-then-quantise order, which is why its merge stays exactly in the quantised type.

name: PEQA
paper_title: Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compressed Large Language Models via sub-4-bit Integer Quantization
formula_latex: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s_0+\Delta s)\,\overline W_0,\quad \overline W_0=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor W_0/s_0\rceil+z_0,\,0,\,2^b-1\big)-z_0\ \ \text{(frozen integer codes)},\ \ s_0,z_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}};\ \ \text{only } s_0+\Delta s \text{ trained}
trainable_params: d_{out}\ \text{(per-channel; } d_{out}\,d_{in}/g \text{ for group size } g)
locus: every linear layer of a weight-only (3-4 bit) quantized LLM
structure: diagonal rescaling of the output rows of a frozen integer matrix: \(\hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\overline W_0\) (group-wise: one scale per output row and input group); the integer codes never change
mergeable_reason: The trained parameters are the quantization scales themselves, so the result is a standard quantized model with the same integer codes and kernels.
identity_at_init: \(\Delta s = 0\): the model starts as the RTN/OPTQ-quantized model whose scales \(s_0\) minimize \(\lVert W_0-\hat W_0\rVert_F\), so the starting point is close to but not exactly \(W_0\).
key_idea: Treat the quantization step sizes as the PEFT parameters. Freeze the integer codes and fine-tune only per-channel scales, so each task adapter is a tiny scale vector and the deployed model stays quantized.
results_note: Scales to LLaMA-65B. After instruction tuning, sub-4-bit PEQA models recover or exceed their full-precision language-modeling, few-shot in-context and comprehension performance.
categorical_reading: PEQA is (IA)\(^3\)'s output-side torus acting on the quantised base \(\kappa\theta_0\) instead of \(\theta_0\): a linear object, regular relative to \(\kappa\theta_0\), whose parameters are the quantiser's own scales, so merging never leaves the quantised type. It is the multiplicative twin of QA-LoRA, which moves the zero-points instead.

name: ApiQ
paper_title: ApiQ: Finetuning of 2-Bit Quantized Large Language Model
formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\ \big\lVert W_0X-(Q+BA)X^{q}\big\rVert_F\ \ \text{(layer-wise; block-wise: } \lVert\mathcal F(W_s,X)-\mathcal F(Q_s,A_s,B_s,X^{q})\rVert),\ \ Q=q_b(W_0;\gamma,\beta)\ \text{with learnable clipping }(\gamma,\beta)\ \text{via STE},\ X^{q}=\text{inputs from the already-quantized preceding layers};\ \text{then fine-tune } h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{during fine-tuning}
locus: all linear layers (or whole transformer blocks for ApiQ-bw); DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa, Llama-2, Mistral
structure: the same \(Q+BA\) shape as LoftQ, but fitted in activation space with calibration data, sequentially layer-by-layer or block-by-block so that quantization error does not accumulate with depth
mergeable_reason: \(BA\) can be merged only into a high-precision copy; merging into the \(b\)-bit \(Q\) requires re-quantization.
identity_at_init: Approximate: \(Q\), \(A\), \(B\) are calibrated so that the quantized layer or block reproduces the full-precision activations given the already-quantized inputs \(X^{q}\); the model function is close to, not equal to, the original.
key_idea: Initialize LoRA and quantize jointly by matching activations, not weights. Each quantized layer is fitted given its quantized inputs, so the adapter stops error propagation from shallow to deep layers, which is crucial at 2 bits.
results_note: Attains the lowest activation error and the best fine-tuning results against QLoRA, LoftQ and LQ-LoRA across 2-4 bits on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) and on Llama-2/Mistral language modeling, arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, with the largest gains at 2 bits.
categorical_reading: ApiQ builds the same Type II object as LoftQ, a rank-\(r\) translated cone over a quantised apex, but chooses the section by matching activations sequentially. Its defect is therefore measured through the realisation \(\Phi_f\) on calibration data rather than in \(\Theta\).

name: EfficientQAT
paper_title: EfficientQAT: Efficient Quantization-Aware Training for Large Language Models
formula_latex: \text{Block-AP: }\min_{W,s,z}\lVert\mathcal F_{blk}(W_0,X)-\mathcal F_{blk}(Q_{s,z}(W),X)\rVert\ \text{block by block};\quad \text{E2E-QP: } \hat W=s\odot(\overline W-z),\ \overline W\ \text{frozen integers},\ \text{only step sizes } s \text{ trained end-to-end on the task loss}
trainable_params: d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \text{step sizes in E2E-QP (group size } g)
locus: all linear layers of the LLM; 2-4 bit group-wise uniform quantization
structure: two stages: block-wise reconstruction training of all weights plus quantization parameters, then end-to-end training of group-wise multiplicative step sizes only (diagonal-per-group scaling of a frozen integer matrix)
mergeable_reason: Block-AP trains the latent weights together with step sizes and zero points and then rounds them to integer codes; E2E-QP trains only step sizes on those frozen codes. The output is a standard group-wise uniformly quantized model, with no adapter.
identity_at_init: E2E-QP starts from the Block-AP-calibrated quantized model (step sizes from Block-AP); there is no exact identity with \(W_0\), by design of quantization.
key_idea: Make quantization-aware training feasible for 70B models in two stages. First, train all parameters block by block against a reconstruction loss. Then, end to end, train only the quantization step sizes, which is a PEQA-style parameter-efficient stage on a frozen integer model.
results_note: Produces a 2-bit Llama-2-70B on a single A100-80GB in 41 hours with less than 3 points of accuracy loss (69.48 vs 72.41), and outperforms prior quantization methods from 7B to 70B, including instruction-tuned and multimodal LLMs.
categorical_reading: EfficientQAT is a base change followed by PEQA: Block-AP constructs a calibrated quantised base \(\kappa_{\rm BAP}\theta_0\) by block-wise full training, and E2E-QP is the group-wise scale torus acting on its frozen codes. Only the second stage is an object of the slice; the first chooses where it is pointed.

name: LoQT
paper_title: LoQT: Low-Rank Adapters for Quantized Pretraining
formula_latex: h=\big(W_Q+s\,P_QB\big)x,\ \ W_Q=q_{NF4}(W),\ \ P=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{from}\ \mathrm{SVD}(\nabla_W\mathcal L)\ \text{(frozen, } P_Q=q_{NF4}(P)\text{; projector on the smaller side, shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}),\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained},\ B_{init}=P^{+}(W-Q)\ \text{refined for up to 5 steps with } Q=q_{NF4}(W-PB);\quad \text{at } t\in\{T_i\}:\ W\leftarrow W_Q+sP_QB,\ \text{recompute }P,\ \text{re-quantize, re-init }B;\ \ T_{i}=\tau+\psi^{i}

mergeable_reason: \(PB\) is periodically merged into the (quantized) full-rank weight, with a final merge at the end, so inference uses a plain dense or quantized matrix.
identity_at_init: Approximate: \(B\) is initialized to compensate the quantization error (\(B \approx P^{+}(W-q_{NF4}(W))\)) instead of 0; without quantization (LoQT-nq), \(B=0\) gives exact identity.
key_idea: Realize GaLore's projected step as a trainable adapter. Freeze a gradient-SVD projector \(P\) and train only \(B\) in \(W+PB\); since \(\partial\mathcal L/\partial B=P^{\top}\nabla_W\mathcal L\), Adam on \(B\) equals GaLore within a window. Periodically fold \(PB\) into an NF4 weight, so neither \(W\) nor \(P\) ever needs 16-bit storage or gradients.
results_note: Trains models up to 7B on a single 24GB GPU (13B with per-layer gradient updates). Perplexity is close to unquantized low-rank baselines in LLaMA pre-training on C4, with competitive DeBERTaV3 GLUE and GSM8K fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: LoQT realises GaLore's projected step as a forward one-sided adapter (Prop IV.2) and re-bases it ReLoRA-style into a quantised weight. Unlike GaLore it resets \(B\) at each re-basing, so it shares GaLore's per-stage image but not its trajectory.

name: GaLore
paper_title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
formula_latex: G_t=\nabla_W\mathcal L(W_t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}},\ \ P_t=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{of}\ \mathrm{SVD}(G_{t_0})\ \text{(refreshed every }T\text{ steps)};\ \ R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ (M_t,V_t)=\mathrm{Adam}(R_t),\ N_t=M_t/(\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_tN_t\ \ \text{(all of }W\text{ trained; no adapter; shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}\text{, else project on the right)}
trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \text{vs. } 2d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{for Adam (for } d_{out}\le d_{in})
locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP blocks (embeddings / LM head usually kept on standard Adam)
structure: each step's update lies in an \(r\)-dimensional left subspace: \(\Delta W_t=-\eta\alpha P_tN_t\) with \(P_t\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r)\) the gradient's top singular vectors; the subspace switches every \(T\) steps, so the accumulated \(\sum_t\Delta W_t\) is high-rank
mergeable_reason: There is no auxiliary module: updates are written straight into \(W\), so the result is an ordinary dense checkpoint with the original architecture.
identity_at_init: Trivial: training starts at \(W_0\) with no reparameterization; the projector is initialized from the SVD of the first gradient.
key_idea: Put the low-rank structure on the gradient rather than the weights. Project each gradient onto a periodically refreshed top-\(r\) singular subspace, run Adam there, and project back. This gives full-parameter learning with LoRA-like optimizer memory.
results_note: Cuts optimizer-state memory by up to 65.5% (82.5% with 8-bit GaLore) while matching full-rank LLaMA 1B/7B pre-training on C4 (up to 19.7B tokens) and RoBERTa GLUE fine-tuning. It was the first to pre-train a 7B model on a single 24GB RTX 4090 without model parallelism, checkpointing or offloading.
categorical_reading: GaLore is a backward lens with compression \(P_t^\top\) and anchor \(P_t\); by the degree-one collapse it is one-sided LoRA \(W_k+P_kC\) re-based every period, with \(C\)'s optimizer state carried over untransported. As a set over its possible sequences of projectors, its reach is \(\Theta\), because the linear shape moves, not because any single period is high rank.

name: GaLore 2
paper_title: GaLore 2: Large-Scale LLM Pre-Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection

locus: all 2-D weight matrices; designed for large-scale pre-training under FSDP
structure: same projected-gradient structure as GaLore (\(\Delta W_t\in\mathrm{span}(P_t)\otimes\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}\)), with randomized-SVD projectors and sharded per-layer updates

identity_at_init: Trivial: starts at the initial (or pretrained) \(W\) with no reparameterization.
key_idea: An engineering consolidation of GaLore. name: Q-GaLore
paper_title: Q-GaLore: Quantized GaLore with INT4 Projection and Layer-Adaptive Low-Rank Gradients
formula_latex: W^{\mathrm{INT8}}_{t+1}=\mathrm{SR}_{8}\Big(W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}}\,\rho_t\big(P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}\top}G_t\big)\Big),\ \ \mathrm{SR}=\text{stochastic rounding (unbiased)};\ \ P_t^{\mathrm{INT4}}\ \text{block-wise INT4};\ \text{SVD interval of layer } l \text{ doubled when } \cos(P^{(l)}_{k\text{ intervals}})\ge\text{threshold (lazy layer-adaptive refresh)};\ \text{fused per-layer backward update}

locus: all 2-D weight matrices; pre-training and fine-tuning
structure: GaLore projected update with quantized operands: INT8 weights updated through stochastic rounding, INT4 projector, per-layer adaptive subspace-refresh schedule
mergeable_reason: Training directly updates the (INT8) weights; no adapter remains.
identity_at_init: Trivial: starts from the (INT8-quantized) initial weights with no reparameterization.
key_idea: Gradient subspaces settle early in many layers and projectors tolerate 4-bit quantization. Q-GaLore therefore refreshes subspaces lazily per layer, stores projectors in INT4 and weights in INT8, and uses stochastic rounding so small updates are not lost.
results_note: Pre-trains LLaMA-7B from scratch on a single 16GB RTX 4060 Ti. In fine-tuning it uses up to 50% less memory than LoRA and GaLore and beats QLoRA by up to 5.19 MMLU points at the same memory cost.
categorical_reading: Q-GaLore is GaLore after base change to a quantised type: the moving linear shape is unchanged in expectation, but unbiased stochastic rounding pushes the iterates onto the INT8 lattice. Its lazy refresh changes the schedule, not the object.

name: Flora
paper_title: Flora: Low-Rank Adapters Are Secretly Gradient Compressors
formula_latex: \text{LoRA dynamics} \approx W_0-\eta\textstyle\sum_t G_tA_0^{\top}A_0\ \ (\text{random } A_0,\ \text{only } B \text{ moving});\ \ \text{Flora: } C_t=G_tA_t^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\tfrac1r)^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{regenerated from a seed, resampled every }\kappa\text{ steps};\ \ M_t=\beta M_{t-1}T_t+(1-\beta)C_t,\ \ T_t=A_{t-1}A_t^{\top}\ \text{at resampling steps (momentum transfer), else } T_t=I_r;\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\mathcal U(M_tA_t)\ \ (\mathcal U=\text{base optimizer, Adafactor in the paper})
trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); compressed state } r\,d_{out}\ \text{per EMA / accumulator (+ a random seed for } A_t)
locus: attention and feed-forward weight matrices (embeddings and vector parameters handled uncompressed); T5, GPT-2 (ViT in the appendix)
structure: random-projection (Johnson-Lindenstrauss) compression of the gradient along its input dimension, \(C=GA^{\top}\), decompressed by \(CA\); resampling \(A_t\) makes the accumulated update high-rank; sublinear \(O(r\,d_{out})\) state
mergeable_reason: Flora is an optimizer that writes directly into \(W\); no adapter is created.
identity_at_init: Trivial: \(W\) starts at \(W_0\); only optimizer states are compressed.
key_idea: Under SGD with a small learning rate, LoRA's update is dominated by \(B\) moving under a nearly fixed random \(A_0\), i.e. \(-\eta GA_0^{\top}A_0\), which is random-projection compression of the gradient. Resampling the projection breaks LoRA's low-rank ceiling while keeping its sublinear memory for momentum and gradient accumulation.
results_note: With Adafactor as base optimizer, Flora-compressed gradient accumulation matches full-matrix accumulation on T5 (XSum) and GPT-2 (IWSLT17 De-En) at reasonably large \(r\), using only about 30% of its memory overhead for T5-3B / GPT-2-XL at \(r=256\). Compressed momentum recovers or surpasses naive momentum when training from scratch, where LoRA lags badly.
categorical_reading: Flora is the random-projection row of the cotangent table: per period LoRA-FA\((A_t)\) with a fresh Gaussian \(A_t\), re-based, reaching \(\Theta\). Its momentum transfer \(A_{t-1}A_t^\top\) is an approximate transport of optimizer state between frames, the ingredient GaLore lacks.

name: Fira
full_name: Fira (full-rank training under a low-rank constraint)
paper_title: Fira: Can We Achieve Full-rank Training of LLMs Under Low-rank Constraint?
formula_latex: R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t,\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,P_t\psi_t(R_t)-\eta\,\big(G_t-P_tR_t\big)\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\phi_t(R_t)\big),\ \ \phi_t(R_t)_i=\frac{\lVert\psi_t(R_{t,:,i})\rVert}{\lVert R_{t,:,i}\rVert}\ \text{(column-wise)};\ \ \text{limiter: if } \lVert S_t\rVert/\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert>\gamma,\ S_t\leftarrow\gamma\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert\,S_t/\lVert S_t\rVert,\ \ S_t=(G_t-P_tR_t)\,\mathrm{diag}(\phi_t(R_t))

In the framework it is Full FT with a different cometric, and \(\phi\equiv0\) collapses it to GaLore's rank-\(r\) periods.

name: APOLLO
full_name: Approximated Gradient Scaling for Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization

name: Online Subspace Descent

mergeable_reason: The final delta is scatter-added into the pretrained weights, producing a standard dense model.
identity_at_init: \(\phi = 0\) and \(\eta\) a random index subset (all of it is replaced at the first update).
key_idea: Make sparse fine-tuning memory-efficient for LLMs by storing only indices and deltas and letting the support evolve during training through drop-and-grow, instead of computing a dense mask up front.
results_note: Instruction-tuning LLaMA 2 7B/13B on Flan v2, GPT4-Alpaca and Tulu v2, SpIEL is often better than LoRA and (IA)\(^3\) at comparable run time and is compatible with 4-bit quantization and SM3.
categorical_reading: SpIEL is a learned-support object like Diff pruning, but it searches the strata of the union of \(k\)-planes by drop-and-grow instead of a relaxed L0 gate. It is not a rebasing scheme, because dropped deltas are discarded rather than merged.

name: GPS
paper_title: Gradient-based Parameter Selection for Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: M_{ij} = \mathbb{1}\Big[j\in\text{top-}K_{j'}\ \big|\partial\mathcal{L}_{SCL}/\partial W_{0,ij'}\big|\Big]\ \text{for every output neuron (row) } i,\qquad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W,\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \epsilon\,\nabla_W\mathcal{L}\odot M

locus: every weight matrix of the backbone (ViT, Swin, ConvNeXt), all layers; gradients computed with a supervised contrastive loss
structure: row-balanced sparse mask: exactly \(K\) nonzeros in every row of \(\Delta W\), so each neuron's activation can be adjusted through its \(K\) most gradient-relevant input connections
mergeable_reason: Only selected entries of existing weights change; inference uses the unchanged architecture.
identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights (\(\Delta W = 0\)); selection uses a supervised contrastive loss so that no randomly initialized head biases the gradients.
key_idea: Pick, for every neuron, the few incoming weights with the largest task gradient, which spreads the budget over all layers instead of concentrating it at the top, and train only those.
results_note: On FGVC and VTAB-1k with ViT-B/16, GPS improves over full fine-tuning by 3.33% and 9.61% mean accuracy while tuning 0.36% of parameters on average.
categorical_reading: GPS is a fixed mask with a row-regular support of \(K\) incoming connections per neuron. Row regularity constrains which stratum of the \(k\)-sparse union is chosen, not the shape of the object.

name: S²FT
paper_title: S²FT: Efficient, Scalable and Generalizable LLM Fine-tuning by Structured Sparsity
formula_latex: \Delta W = U_S V^{\top},\ \ U_S = [e_{a_1},\dots,e_{a_s}]\ \text{a frozen one-hot channel selector},\ V \text{ trainable};\ \text{in practice: the slices of } W_O \text{ belonging to selected heads } S_{MHA} \text{ and of } W_{down} \text{ belonging to selected FFN channels } S_{FFN}, \text{ co-permuted to be contiguous}
trainable_params: s\cdot d\ \text{per adapted matrix (s selected channels, i.e. selected heads}\times d_h\text{ or FFN channels)}
locus: output projection \(W_O\) (rows of the selected attention heads) and FFN down projection (selected channels) in every block; for LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B only the down projection is tuned because of grouped-query attention
structure: structured (row/column-block) sparsity: \(\Delta W = U_S V^\top\) with \(U_S\) a fixed coordinate projection, i.e. a LoRA whose one factor is a frozen selection matrix; permutation invariance of coupled head/channel structures makes the trainable slice a dense block

identity_at_init: Selected slices start at their pretrained values (\(\Delta W = 0\)); selection is random by default (S²FT-R) or by weight, activation, weight×activation or gradient magnitude.
key_idea: Select sparsely but compute densely: choose a few attention heads and FFN channels, permute coupled weight matrices so they are contiguous, and back-propagate only through that dense slice.
results_note: On LLaMA and Mistral models S²FT improves over other PEFT methods by 1.2-4.1% on commonsense and 0.6-1.9% on arithmetic reasoning, while saving up to 3x training memory and running 1.5-2.7x faster than full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: S\(^2\)FT is LoRA-FA whose frozen factor is a coordinate selector, \(\Delta W=VU_S^\top\): the structured-sparse and the low-rank readings are one linear object. Its dense-compute trick is a base change by a hidden-unit permutation, a symmetry of \(f\), so it costs nothing in expressivity.

name: SIFT
paper_title: Sparse is Enough in Fine-tuning Pre-trained Large Language Models
formula_latex: \mathcal{S} = \text{top-}x\%\ \text{coordinates of } |g_1|\ (\text{gradient of the first batch(es)}),\quad W = W_0 + \Delta W,\ \ \mathrm{supp}(\Delta W)\subseteq\mathcal{S},\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \eta\,P_{\mathcal{S}}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_t)
trainable_params: x\%\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{per adapted matrix (stored as values + indices)}
locus: attention \(W_q\), \(W_k\), \(W_v\), \(W_o\) by default
structure: coordinate-subspace update: the gradient is projected onto the span of the top-\(|g|\) standard basis directions, and the increment is stored as a sparse (value, index) tensor filled via backward hooks
mergeable_reason: The sparse increment is added into the existing weights.
identity_at_init: \(\Delta W = 0\); support fixed after the first batch.
key_idea: Pre-training shifts the PAC-Bayes prior so that fine-tuning gradients become quasi-sparse (a few components carry most of the norm); hence updating only the top-gradient components is enough, implemented memory-efficiently with gradient hooks.
results_note: With RoBERTa-large on GLUE (0.8% sparsity on Q/K/V/O) SIFT is competitive with LoRA and adapters, and when instruction-tuning LLaMA on Alpaca it is competitive with full fine-tuning and LoRA on MMLU and HumanEval.
categorical_reading: SIFT is a fixed coordinate mask chosen by the magnitudes of the first gradient, implemented as a backward projection with a frozen coordinate compression. By the degree-one collapse it is the same object as training \(W_0+P_S(\Delta W)\) directly.

name: HiFT
paper_title: HiFT: A Hierarchical Full Parameter Fine-Tuning Strategy
formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{G_1},\dots,\theta_{G_k})\ \text{(k groups of m layers)};\ \text{at step } t \text{ update only } \theta_{G_{\pi(t \bmod k)}} \text{ with any optimizer (others frozen, their optimizer states offloaded)};\ \text{learning rate advanced once per full cycle}
trainable_params: \approx|\theta|/k\ \text{per step};\ \text{all parameters over one cycle}
locus: groups of consecutive layers (embedding = bottom, head = top), iterated bottom2up, top2down or in a fixed random order
structure: cyclic block-coordinate update over layer groups with delayed learning-rate schedule; accumulated \(\Delta W\) is dense

identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters.
key_idea: Achieve full-parameter fine-tuning with PEFT-like memory by updating one group of layers per step in a fixed cyclic order, keeping only that group's gradients and optimizer states on the GPU.
results_note: HiFT matches PEFT and standard full fine-tuning across six models, reduces per-step trainable parameters by about 89% on average and fits full fine-tuning of 7B models in 24GB.
categorical_reading: HiFT is block-coordinate descent over layer groups: a backward lens whose anchor is a coordinate projection rotated every step, the resampled-every-step coordinate-block cell of Exposé IV. Since each group keeps its own optimizer state, the schedule is full fine-tuning in a cyclic order and reaches \(\Theta\) after one cycle.

name: Surgical FT
paper_title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{B_1},\dots,\theta_{B_n});\ \text{fine-tune only } \theta_{B_j} \text{ (one contiguous block), others frozen};\ \text{Auto-RGN: per-tensor learning rate } \propto \mathrm{RGN} = \|g\|_2/\|\theta\|_2 \text{ normalized to } [0,1]
trainable_params: |\theta_{B_j}|\ \text{(one block of layers)}
locus: one contiguous block of layers: first block for input-level shift, middle blocks for feature-level shift, last layer for output-level shift
structure: layer-block coordinate mask: \(\Delta W\) nonzero only on the weights of one contiguous block (soft version: per-tensor learning rates from relative gradient norms)
mergeable_reason: Only existing layers are fine-tuned; architecture unchanged.
identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained (source) model; no new parameters.
key_idea: Which layers to fine-tune should depend on where the distribution shift lives: tuning only early layers fixes input-level shifts, middle layers feature-level shifts, and the head output-level shifts, often beating full fine-tuning.
results_note: Across seven real distribution shifts (e.g. CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, Living-17, Entity-30, Waterbirds, CelebA) tuning a single block outperforms full fine-tuning, and Auto-RGN beats full fine-tuning without per-block search.
categorical_reading: Surgical FT is a fixed coordinate block of whole layers: Full FT on the chosen block and frozen elsewhere, the shift type deciding which block. Auto-RGN keeps Full FT's image and changes only the metric \(\Lambda\) through per-tensor learning rates (Exposé III).

name: Masking
full_name: Learning binary weight masks instead of fine-tuning
paper_title: Masking as an Efficient Alternative to Finetuning for Pretrained Language Models
formula_latex: W = W_0\odot M_{bin},\quad (M_{bin})_{ij} = \mathbb{1}[m_{ij}\ge\tau],\quad m\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ trained with the straight-through estimator};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{real-valued scores during training};\ d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{bits stored}
locus: linear layers of selected Transformer blocks (top-down masking works best); biases and the classifier handled separately
structure: Hadamard product with a learned binary mask, i.e. selection of a sub-network of pretrained connections; equivalently the additive update \(\Delta W = -(\mathbf{1}-M_{bin})\odot W_0\) is constrained to zeroing coordinates
mergeable_reason: The masked weight \(W_0 \odot M_{bin}\) is an ordinary dense (or sparse) matrix with the original shape.
identity_at_init: No: scores are drawn from a uniform distribution tuned so that a target fraction of weights starts masked (5% for BERT/RoBERTa/DistilBERT; 3-10% works well), so the initial function differs from the pretrained one.
key_idea: Instead of changing pretrained weights, learn which ones to switch off for each task; a 1-bit mask per weight suffices to reach fine-tuning-level accuracy.
results_note: Masking BERT, RoBERTa and DistilBERT on eleven NLP tasks performs comparably to fine-tuning, and masked and fine-tuned solutions are linearly connected with nearly constant accuracy.
categorical_reading: Masking is a monoid-orbit method: the Boolean monoid acts on \(\theta_0\) by Hadamard product, so the image is the finite vertex set of the box between \(0\) and \(W_0\), which keeps \(W_0\)'s zeros and can only create new ones. Its real-valued scores are pure torus gauge of the exact \(\rho\), and the 5% masked start makes it an object with a pointing defect.

name: Piggyback
full_name: Piggyback (learning to mask weights of a fixed backbone)
paper_title: Piggyback: Adapting a Single Network to Multiple Tasks by Learning to Mask Weights
formula_latex: y = (W_0\odot m)\,x,\quad m_{ji} = \mathbb{1}[m^{r}_{ji}\ge\tau],\quad \partial E/\partial m = (\delta y\,x^{\top})\odot W_0 \text{ used as straight-through gradient for } m^{r};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{real-valued mask weights during training};\ 1\ \text{bit per weight stored}
locus: all convolutional and fully-connected layers of a fixed ImageNet backbone (VGG-16, ResNet, DenseNet)
structure: Hadamard product with a learned binary mask (task-specific sub-network of a fixed backbone)
mergeable_reason: The masked weights form an ordinary network of the original architecture.
identity_at_init: \(m^r\) initialized to \(10^{-2}\) with threshold \(\tau = 5\times 10^{-3}\), so the mask starts as all ones and the network equals the backbone.
key_idea: Add new tasks to one frozen network by learning only a binary mask over its weights, at 1 bit per parameter per task.
results_note: With ImageNet-pretrained VGG-16/ResNet-50 backbones, Piggyback approaches individually fine-tuned networks on fine-grained and large-shift classification tasks (e.g. within 0.36% top-1 error on Places365).
categorical_reading: Piggyback is the orbit of \(\theta_0\) under the Boolean Hadamard monoid, pointed at its identity \(\mathbf 1\): the earliest selective method is an action method, not an additive one. Its update \(-(\mathbf 1-M)\odot W_0\) is a sparse diff forced to equal \(-W_0\) on its support, which is the precise sense in which it is dual to Diff pruning.

structure: fixed diagonal 0/1 mask matrix \(M\) on parameter space, chosen as the analytic optimum of a second-order (upper-bounded) surrogate, which reduces to top squared-gradient selection
