Its claim that every PEFT method is \(\theta_0+M\Delta\theta\) holds for linear methods up to a transport \(T\) (Prop II.13), but not for cones such as LoRA, whose image is a union of planes rather than one plane.

name: LIFT
paper_title: LIFT the Veil for the Truth: Principal Weights Emerge after Rank Reduction for Reasoning-Focused Supervised Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: W_t' = \mathrm{SVD}_r(W_t)\ \text{(best rank-}r\text{ approximation of the current weight; } W_0 \text{ at the start)},\quad M_t = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|W'_t| \in \text{top-}k\big],\quad W_{t+1} = W_t - \eta\,(M_t\odot \hat g_t);\ M_t \text{ recomputed every } \texttt{update\_mask\_interval} \text{ steps}
trainable_params: k\ \text{per matrix active at any time (top } 5\%\text{ Principal Weights)};\ \text{the accumulated } \Delta W \text{ is supported on the union of successive masks}
locus: LLM linear layers (attention and MLP)
structure: sparse coordinate mask given by the largest-magnitude entries of the rank-\(r\) truncation of \(W_0\) ('Principal Weights'), refreshed at fixed intervals; the resulting update is high-rank
mergeable_reason: Only existing entries are updated in place.
identity_at_init: \(\Delta W = 0\); the mask is data-free (SVD of the pretrained weight).
key_idea: Plain magnitude selection works poorly for LLM sparse fine-tuning, but after discarding small singular directions the largest remaining entries identify the weights that carry reasoning-relevant knowledge, so tuning only those beats full fine-tuning.
results_note: Updating the top 5% Principal Weights, LIFT outperforms full fine-tuning on reasoning tasks (arithmetic and commonsense) with LoRA-level memory, and retains up to 20% more source-domain knowledge than full fine-tuning and LoRA.
categorical_reading: LIFT is a LISA-type rebasing scheme in the coordinate frame: each interval trains a fixed mask, and the next mask is read from the principal part of the merged weight, so its anchor depends on \(\theta\) across intervals. The spectral filter changes which coordinates are chosen, not the coordinate geometry of the image.

name: RoSA
paper_title: RoSA: Accurate Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Robust Adaptation
formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA + S,\quad \mathrm{supp}(S)\subseteq M,\ \ M = \mathrm{TopK}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{D}_M}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_s)^{\alpha}\big|_{W_0+\tilde B\tilde A},\ d\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\Big),\ \alpha\in\{1,2\},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0 \text{ frozen};\ \tilde B\tilde A = \text{LoRA after a 64-batch warm-up}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) + d\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\ \ (d = \text{mask density})
locus: all fully connected layers of the LLM
structure: robust-PCA-style decomposition of the update: low-rank \(BA\) plus a sparse \(S\) on a fixed gradient-statistics mask (accumulated squared gradients, i.e. a diagonal-Fisher mask for \(\alpha=2\))
mergeable_reason: Both the low-rank and the sparse components are additive and can be folded into \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: LoRA is first trained alone for 64 batches to compute the mask, then training restarts with both adapters at \(BA = 0\) (\(B = 0\)) and \(S = 0\); the mask is fixed from then on.
key_idea: Full fine-tuning updates are not low-rank but are well approximated by low-rank plus sparse, so train both components jointly with system support for sparse adapters.
results_note: Fine-tuning LLaMA2-7B on GSM8K, ViGGO and SQL generation, RoSA outperforms LoRA and pure sparse adaptation at equal budget and can match full fine-tuning.
categorical_reading: RoSA is the monoidal sum \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{Mask}_M\) of Obs I.7: robust PCA as a Minkowski sum of a determinantal cone and a coordinate subspace. Both summands map into it by A5, and its image is strictly larger than either.

name: ABBA
full_name: ABBA-Adapters (learnable Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices)
paper_title: ABBA-Adapters: Efficient and Expressive Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2) = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top},\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2\ \text{trained}
locus: any linear layer of an LLM
structure: Hadamard product of two independently learnable rank-\(r_1\) and rank-\(r_2\) matrices (rank \(\le r_1r_2\)), executed without materialising \(\Delta W\) via the row-wise Khatri-Rao identity \((B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2)=(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}\); rank-stabilised scale \(\alpha/\sqrt{r_1r_2}\).
mergeable_reason: The product is an ordinary dense matrix that can be added to \(W_0\).
identity_at_init: \((B_1,A_1)\) initialised from the top-\(r_1\) truncated SVD of \(W_0\); \(B_2 = 0\) and \(A_2\) Kaiming-uniform, so \(\Delta W = 0\) at init.
key_idea: Make both Hadamard factors learnable (HiRA fixes one to \(W_0\)), anchor one to the principal subspace of \(W_0\), and use a rank-stabilising scale; the Khatri-Rao trick keeps memory at LoRA level.
results_note: Reports state-of-the-art results on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks across multiple LLMs, outperforming LoRA, HiRA and other PEFT baselines.
categorical_reading: ABBA is a re-pointed LoHa. As unpointed objects \(\mathrm{ABBA}_{r_1,r_2}\cong\mathrm{LoHa}_{r_1,r_2}\) (up to rescaling one factor); what is new is the base point, where the first Hadamard factor starts at the principal part \([W_0]_{r_1}\), an SVD-anchored point of LoHa's apex stratum.

name: KronA
paper_title: KronA: Parameter Efficient Tuning with Kronecker Adapter
formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,(A_k\otimes B_k),\quad A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{a_1\times a_2},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{b_1\times b_2},\ a_1b_1=d_{out},\ a_2b_2=d_{in};\quad \Delta W x = s\,\mathrm{vec}(B_k X A_k^{\top}),\ X=\mathrm{mat}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{b_2\times a_2};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_k,B_k\ \text{trained}
locus: parallel to attention/FFN weight matrices (KronA); KronA\(^B\) and KronA\(^B_{res}\) sit parallel to the whole FFN block
structure: Single Kronecker product of two dense small factors; \(\mathrm{rank}(A_k\otimes B_k)=\mathrm{rank}(A_k)\,\mathrm{rank}(B_k)\), reaching full rank with \(O(\sqrt{d_{in}d_{out}})\) parameters; forward pass by the vec-trick without materialising \(\Delta W\).
mergeable_reason: The weight-parallel KronA merges into \(W_0\) like LoRA (zero added latency in the paper's Table 2); KronA\(^B\) / KronA\(^B_{res}\) are linear branches placed in parallel to the whole (nonlinear) FFN block, \(Y = \mathrm{FFN}(X) + sX[A_k \otimes B_k]\) (\(+ s_{res} X\)), so there is no single existing weight to fold them into (127%/136% latency).
identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized and the other Kaiming-uniform (\(a = \sqrt{5}\)); the paper reports zero-init of one factor markedly improves results.
key_idea: Replace LoRA's low-rank product by a Kronecker product, which is full-rank-capable for the same tiny budget and cheap to apply via reshaping.
results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, KronA variants outperform LoRA, adapters and Compacter at comparable budgets, with KronA\(^B_{res}\) the strongest (at extra inference latency).
categorical_reading: KronA generates the Kronecker family: it is \(\mathcal R^{-1}_*\mathrm{LoRA}_1\), rank-one LoRA across the \(\{U_1V_1\}|\{U_2V_2\}\) cut. For equal square splits it is incomparable with every \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\), \(r<d\) (Thm II.11(d)), and it is LoKr with an unfactorised right factor.

name: PHM-Adapter
paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{D}\otimes B_i^{D},\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{U}\otimes B_i^{U},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\ B_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d}{n}},\ B_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters trained}
trainable_params: 2\left(\tfrac{dr}{n}+n^{3}\right)\ \text{per adapter}
locus: bottleneck adapters after the attention and feed-forward sublayers (Houlsby placement)
structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with residual connection whose down/up projections are PHM layers: sums of \(n\) Kronecker products (Kronecker rank \(\le n\), i.e. rank \(\le n\) after Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement), reducing parameters by about \(1/n\).
mergeable_reason: The adapter contains a GeLU nonlinearity in a new serial branch, so it cannot be folded into existing weights.
identity_at_init: No exact zero-init guarantee is stated in the method section; like Houlsby adapters it relies on the residual connection with small-initialized adapter weights.
key_idea: Learn the 'multiplication rule' of an \(n\)-dimensional hypercomplex algebra: a dense projection becomes a sum of \(n\) Kronecker products, cutting adapter parameters by ~\(n\).
results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, PHM-Adapter (\(n = 12\)) trains 0.179% of parameters and is competitive with full fine-tuning and standard adapters.
categorical_reading: The PHM adapter is the Houlsby adapter precomposed with the Kronecker-sum map \((A_i,B_i)\mapsto\sum_iA_i\otimes B_i\) on each projection, an A3 arrow into Houlsby. Compacter maps into it by tying the slow weights and restricting the fast weights to rank \(\rho\).

name: KAdaptation
paper_title: Parameter-efficient Model Adaptation for Vision Transformers
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(u_iv_i^{\top}),\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{(shared across layers)},\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{n}\times r},\ v_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{in}}{n}\times r};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_i,u_i,v_i\ \text{trained}
trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per matrix} + n^{3}\ \text{shared}
locus: ViT attention weight matrices (submodules selected by lowest local intrinsic dimension)
structure: Low-rank PHM (sum of \(n\) Kronecker products of shared slow weights with low-rank fast weights) applied directly to the weight update \(\Delta W\) rather than to an inserted adapter.
mergeable_reason: \(\Delta W\) is a dense matrix added to frozen attention weights; the paper notes no added inference latency.
identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the method section consulted; presumably one fast factor starts at zero so \(\Delta W = 0\) (unverified).
key_idea: Choose where to adapt via the local intrinsic dimension of each ViT submodule, then express the update as a Compacter-style Kronecker sum so it merges like LoRA.
results_note: Best accuracy/parameter trade-off among compared methods on 20 image-classification datasets few-shot and 7 datasets full-shot with CLIP ViTs.
categorical_reading: KAdaptation is the weight-space shadow of Compacter: the same LPHM parametrisation moved from an inserted non-linear box to an additive update of \(W_0\), which makes it an object of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\) (M1). It is a \(\oplus\) of \(n\) LoKr terms with tied slow weights and maps into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{n^2r}\) by A3.

name: KRAdapter
paper_title: Towards Higher Effective Rank in Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning using Khatri--Rao Product
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\big[U\odot_{KR}V\big]_{1:d_{out},\,:},\quad (U\odot_{KR}V)_{:,j}=U_{:,j}\otimes V_{:,j},\ U\in\mathbb{R}^{k_1\times d_{in}},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{k_2\times d_{in}},\ k_1k_2\ge d_{out};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ U,V\ \text{trained}

locus: linear layers of vision-language models and LLMs

categorical_reading: KRAdapter is the column-wise (Khatri-Rao) cousin of KronA and a sub-object of LoHa: freezing LoHa's left factors at 0/1 row selectors gives exactly \([U\odot_{KR}V]_{1:d_{out}}\). Its high effective rank is LoHa's Hadamard rank multiplication, with a torus of per-column gauges.

name: LoTR
paper_title: LoTR: Low Tensor Rank Weight Adaptation
formula_latex: W_s = W_{0,s} + \alpha\,B\,G_s^{\top}A^{\top}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector form: } Y = XW_s + \alpha\,XAG_sB^{\top}),\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{shared by all layers } s,\ G_s\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{layer-specific};\ \delta\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{G}\times_1A\times_2B

name: FacT

mergeable_reason: Each slice \(\Delta W_i\) is a dense \(d\times d\) matrix that can be added to the corresponding frozen weight.

Box by box it maps into LoRA\(_r\), landing in the stratum \(\mathrm T_B\) because \(V_0=0\).

name: FLoRA (Tucker core)

paper_title: LoRTA: Low Rank Tensor Adaptation of Large Language Models

name: QuanTA
paper_title: QuanTA: Efficient High-Rank Fine-Tuning of LLMs with Quantum-Informed Tensor Adaptation
formula_latex: y = W_0x + \mathcal{T}_{\theta}x - \mathcal{S}x,\quad \mathcal{T}_{\theta}=\prod_{\alpha}T^{(\alpha)},\ T^{(\alpha)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{m}d_{n}\times d_{m}d_{n}}\ \text{acting on axes } (m(\alpha),n(\alpha)) \text{ of } x \text{ reshaped to } d_1\times\cdots\times d_N,\ \textstyle\prod_n d_n=d;\ \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{T}_{\theta_0}\ \text{frozen}

locus: linear layers of LLMs (attention projections)
structure: Circuit-shaped tensor network: the hidden vector is viewed as an \(N\)-qudit state and a sequence of two-axis 'gates' is applied (an einsum of small tensors); by the universality and rank-representation theorems it can express full-rank updates.

identity_at_init: A frozen copy \(S\) of the initial gates is subtracted (\(T_\theta x - S x = 0\) at step 0, Eq. 8); because \(S\) is fixed it can be folded into the base weight, \(W_0' = W_0 - S\) (the paper's Eq. 9 prints \(W_0 + S\), a sign slip relative to Eq. 8).

results_note: Improves over LoRA and DoRA on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning with LLaMA-family models while using fewer trainable parameters.

Its high rank is a cut statement about the circuit (Thm II.10), bought with an imposed reshape \(\Pi_\otimes\) of the hidden wire.

name: MoRA
full_name: High-rank updating with a square matrix
paper_title: MoRA: High-Rank Updating for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: h = W_0x + f_{decomp}\big(M\,f_{comp}(x)\big),\quad M\in\mathbb{R}^{\hat r\times\hat r},\ \hat r=\big\lfloor\sqrt{(d_{in}+d_{out})\,r}\big\rfloor;\ \text{reshape variant: }\Delta W=I_{d/\hat r}\otimes M=\mathrm{diag}(M,\dots,M);\ \text{RoPE variant: }\Delta W=\mathrm{diag}(P^{1},\dots,P^{n}),\ P^{i}=M\ \text{rotated by block rotation } R_{\theta,i}

results_note: Outperforms LoRA on memory-intensive tasks (UUID memorization, continual pretraining) and is comparable on instruction tuning and math reasoning.
categorical_reading: MoRA is a linear method: the trainable square \(M\) is pushed into weight space by fixed linear operators, e.g. \(\Delta W=I_{d/\hat r}\otimes M\), a subspace of dimension \(\hat r^2\) in a transported frame. Its 'high rank' is a cut property of that frame (rank up to \(d\)), not an increase of \(d(M)\) beyond \(|M|\).

name: MELoRA
paper_title: MELoRA: Mini-Ensemble Low-Rank Adapters for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{diag}(B_1A_1,\dots,B_nA_n)=W_0+\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}B_iA_i,\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d_{in}}{n}},\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_i,B_i\ \text{trained}

locus: attention/MLP linear layers (as LoRA)
structure: Block-diagonal direct sum of \(n\) independent mini-LoRAs acting on disjoint feature slices; rank is the sum of block ranks, so rank \(r\) is reached with \(n\) times fewer parameters than LoRA.
mergeable_reason: The block-diagonal \(\Delta W\) is a dense matrix of \(W_0\)'s shape.
identity_at_init: \(A_i\) Gaussian and \(B_i = 0\), as in LoRA.
key_idea: Concatenating mini-LoRAs along the diagonal adds their ranks instead of sharing a bottleneck, trading cross-block interactions for rank per parameter.

It keeps rank \(r\) at \(1/n\) of the budget by giving up every update that is not block-diagonal, and its rebasing closure is the block-diagonal subspace, not \(\Theta\).

name: DSEE
paper_title: DSEE: Dually Sparsity-embedded Efficient Tuning of Pre-trained Language Models
formula_latex: W = W_0\odot\mathcal{M} + UV + \mathcal{P}_{\Omega}(S),\quad U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \Omega=\text{top-}c\text{ entries of the sparse residual } S'\text{ of a robust-PCA (GreBsmo) split } W_0\approx AB+S',\ \mathcal{M}\ \text{optional pruning mask on the pretrained weights, chosen from } |\Delta W|\ (\text{unstructured) or head scores (structured)};\ U,V,S|_{\Omega}\ \text{trained, then re-tuned after pruning}

Its pruning stage is a base change \(\kappa(\theta)=\theta\odot\mathcal M\) that moves the base point (Def V.1(b)).

name: Sine-LoRA
paper_title: Efficient Learning With Sine-Activated Low-rank Matrices
formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{1}{g}\sin(\omega\,BA),\quad \sin\ \text{entrywise},\ \omega\ \text{(frequency)},\ g\ \text{(gain) fixed},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained}

results_note: Improves LoRA and DoRA at equal parameter count across ViT, LLM (e.g. LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning, GLUE), NeRF and 3D-shape tasks.

It keeps LoRA's apex, gauge and first-order image at \(\theta_0\), while globally it trades the rank bound for the box \(|\Delta W_{ij}|\le1/g\) and loses every covariance except signed permutations.

formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Big(\sum_{j=1}^{l}\beta_j B_j\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i A_i\Big),\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen pseudo-random (generated from a seed, optionally shared across layers)};\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{k},\ \beta\in\mathbb{R}^{l}\ \text{trained}
